events.text: {npc}, a cloud-diver with a rope round {his} waist, says an isle sank into the cloud sea before the war and never stopped glowing. On still nights you can see its lanterns through the white, far down. {He} wants a second pair of hands on the rope.
events.arc: The Isle Under the Cloud Sea

choices.text: Take the rope and go down with {npc}

effects.log: The cloud closes over you, soft and cold, and the lights below grow from sparks to windows.

choices.text: Hold the rope at the top

effects.log: You pay out rope for an hour while the cloud swallows {npc}. When the rope tugs, you haul with all your weight.

choices.text: Say the sea should keep its secrets

effects.log: {npc} nods slowly and winds the rope back up. "Fair," {he} says, and goes down alone.

events.text: The sunken isle is whole: a street, a tea-house, a bell in a tower. Every lantern burns with no oil. A table is laid for twelve, and the tea on it is still faintly warm. Dust is the only thing that has fallen here.
events.arc: The Isle Under the Cloud Sea

choices.text: Sit and drink the tea

effects.log: It tastes of the century before the war. You see, for a moment, eleven people around the table, laughing.

choices.text: Search the tower for the bell's ringer

effects.log: The tower is empty but the bell-rope is worn smooth by a hand that is still, in some way, pulling.

choices.text: Take nothing and look at everything

effects.log: You leave the dust exactly as you found it and come up with a clear head.

events.text: The eleventh chair slides back. Nobody sits, but the lanterns lean toward it as flowers do toward light. {npc} whispers that the isle has been waiting for the twelfth guest for six hundred years, and it has chosen you.
events.arc: The Isle Under the Cloud Sea

choices.text: Sit in the twelfth chair

effects.log: The lanterns steady. The isle does not rise, but it hums, and you carry its hum home like a coin in your pocket.

choices.text: Ring the bell for the sunken guests

ok.log: The bell's note rises through the cloud like a shout of welcome. The isle begins, slowly, to float.

fail.log: The bell cracks on a note of grief. {npc} hauls you up, ears ringing.

choices.text: Leave quietly

effects.log: You climb the rope in silence. Behind you the lanterns go on burning, patient.

events.text: The isle comes up out of the cloud like a sleeper waking, lanterns blazing, and the whole fleet turns to watch. {npc} laughs out loud, the first time in years. Twelve ghosts of people bow and fade into the morning.
events.arc: The Isle Under the Cloud Sea

choices.text: Moor it to the fleet and call it the Twelfth

effects.log: It sails with the fleet from then on, lit all night, and no one is lonely beneath it.

choices.text: Let it sink back to rest, with the lanterns lit

effects.log: You watch it settle. The lights go down slowly, and you feel they have been thanked.

events.text: A star fell on the Hanbit shelf last night, quietly, as stars do above. {npc}, an appraiser who has priced a thousand falls, stands at the crater's rim and is already arguing with the stars about the value. "Half of it is yours," {he} says, "if you can carry it."
events.arc: The Crater Where a Star Fell

choices.text: Climb in and gather the fallen starlight

effects.log: It pools in your cupped hands like cold milk. It does not weigh anything, and it is very hard to carry.

choices.text: Study the crater's shape first

effects.log: Its rim is a perfect ring, the stones all bent outward. A star falls like a seed, not a stone.

choices.text: Leave it to the appraiser

effects.log: {npc} sniffs at your caution and goes down alone. You hold the rope, which is its own kind of share.

events.text: {npc} has priced the starlight. Jarred, it sells for a fortune, but the crater itself hums, and every night it hums a little louder. "A star that falls this gently," {he} says, "is not dead. It is asleep."
events.arc: The Crater Where a Star Fell

choices.text: Sell your share to the markets

effects.log: The jars fetch a handsome price, and the crater goes quiet by morning, as if offended.

choices.text: Keep a jar and leave the rest

effects.log: You keep one jar on your shelf. It brightens when you are sad. {npc} says that is the worst kind of treasure and the best.

choices.text: Sit in the crater and listen

effects.log: The hum has a rhythm like a slow breath. You sit until dawn.

events.text: The star wakes in the crater: a dim white seed the size of a house, blinking. The Ministry of Weather sends clerks to "classify" it. {npc} watches them measure and says, very quietly, that this will end badly for the star.
events.arc: The Crater Where a Star Fell

choices.text: Speak for the star to the clerks

effects.log: You argue until sundown. The clerks write "protected curiosity" and leave, rolling their eyes. The star blinks twice.

choices.text: Lead the star out to the open sky by night

effects.log: It follows you like a lost lamb, drifting upward, and rejoins the stars with a sound like a sigh.

choices.text: Let the clerks do their work

effects.log: They carry it off to a hall. It dims. You tell yourself it was not your business.

events.text: Years later a small white light comes drifting past your window at dusk, circles once, and settles on your jar. The jar blazes. {npc} says some stars remember kindness longer than the Ministry remembers anything.
events.arc: The Crater Where a Star Fell

choices.text: Raise the little star at your side

effects.log: It grows slowly, cheerful and ridiculous, and lights your road when no one else will.

choices.text: Release it to the sky with the jar's light

effects.log: It rises, bows once, and is a new star in the evening by morning.

events.text: Six hundred years ago the immortal Yeoul walked into a grotto on a bare isle and sealed the door from within. The door is a plain slab of grey jade. Under the moss, someone has been leaving small offerings: a cup of tea, a folded fan, a pebble. Fresh ones.
events.arc: The Grotto of Yeoul Who Did Not Come Out

choices.text: Add a cup of tea and wait

effects.log: You leave tea and sit three days by the slab. On the third, the tea is warm again.

choices.text: Knock on the slab

effects.log: The knock rings hollow, and the moss at the foot of the door trembles with something like a laugh.

choices.text: Leave a pebble and go

effects.log: A pebble is the right size for a hello. You walk off feeling you have been polite.

events.text: A slip of jade slides out from under the door, no thicker than a leaf. It says: "Whoever knocks is a fool, whoever waits is a friend. I am not shut in. I am shut out of everything but my own thought, and it is the best company I have had in ages."
events.arc: The Grotto of Yeoul Who Did Not Come Out

choices.text: Write back and slip it under the door

effects.log: A reply takes a month. They argue about poetry across the slab for years.

choices.text: Ask what the grotto is for

effects.log: The next slip says: "To find out what is left of me when I stop being asked to do things." You think about it for a year.

choices.text: Set the slip back and say nothing

effects.log: Some silences are the kind of reply that fits.

events.text: The knock was heard. The slab swings open an inch, and a bored, ancient voice says that visitors owe a debt of one story, and the story must be true, and must be one you have never told. The grotto is full of the smell of old paper and mountain tea.
events.arc: The Grotto of Yeoul Who Did Not Come Out

choices.text: Tell the story of your first fear

effects.log: Silence. Then the door opens wider. "That will do," says the voice, delighted.

choices.text: Tell a lie so good it nearly counts

ok.log: The voice laughs till the slab shakes. "Good enough," it says, and lets you in for tea.

fail.log: The slab shuts like a yawn. "Come back with a true one," says the voice.

choices.text: Leave without entering

effects.log: You wave at the gap and go. The gap waves back.

events.text: Inside, Yeoul is a small cheerful person sitting before a cold hearth, surrounded by six hundred years of unfinished scrolls. "I came to finish one thing," they say, "and found a thousand. Would you like one? I will never get to them."
events.arc: The Grotto of Yeoul Who Did Not Come Out

choices.text: Take a scroll of lost method

effects.log: The method is incomplete and beautiful. Finishing it will take you half your life.

choices.text: Offer to sit and help them finish one

effects.log: You write for a decade at their side. The scroll ends, and the door opens for the first time in six centuries.

events.text: Yeoul's last slip arrives years after, folded very small: "You were right to wait. I walked out this morning. The sky is unreasonably large."
events.arc: The Grotto of Yeoul Who Did Not Come Out

choices.text: Keep the slip in your sleeve

effects.log: You carry it for centuries, and it smells of mountain tea.

choices.text: Go and meet them under the open sky

effects.log: They are squinting at the clouds like a child. You walk them around the isle till sunset.

events.text: Mist hounds are pale dogs that run through fog without leaving prints, and one has been taking fish from the drying racks of three isles. {npc} the warden asks for a tracker. "Not to kill it," {he} says. "To learn why it only takes the grey fish."
events.arc: The Mist Hound of the Three Isles

choices.text: Track it by the damp it leaves

effects.log: A mist hound drags a thin chill behind it. You follow the cold across a bridge and a field of drifting bluebells.

choices.text: Wait at the drying racks for it

effects.log: You sit through three nights. On the third, a long pale shape lowers its head over the grey fish and looks straight at you.

choices.text: Tell the warden to build better racks

effects.log: The racks get roofs. The fish go on being taken. {npc} sighs.

events.text: The hound crosses to the second isle. You find where it sleeps: a hollow under a cloud-pine, with six small grey bones laid in a ring. It is not a thief. It is feeding something that cannot come out of the hollow.
events.arc: The Mist Hound of the Three Isles

choices.text: Look into the hollow

effects.log: A pup, thin as a thread, almost transparent. Its mother is leaving it the one fish its stomach can hold.

choices.text: Follow the hound farther

effects.log: It leads you to a third isle and stops at a grave. You understand the grey fish are an offering.

choices.text: Leave a fish by the hollow and go

effects.log: You leave your own supper. In the morning the plate is clean.

events.text: The hound is cornered by three bored young immortals who want a pelt. {npc} arrives too late to stop them. The hound growls at the edge, mist curling off its back.
events.arc: The Mist Hound of the Three Isles

choices.text: Stand between the hound and the hunters

ok.log: You talk them out of it, and the hound slips past your legs into the fog without a sound.

fail.log: They shove you aside. The hound escapes, but you pay for the delay in bruises.

choices.text: Lead the hunters on a false trail

effects.log: You lead them three isles away, humming, and the hound goes home.

choices.text: Say nothing and stay out of it

effects.log: The hunters leave empty-handed anyway. You are not proud.

events.text: The hound arrives at your door, one winter, with a thin pale pup beside it, now grown. The pup lowers its head. Nobody asks for anything.
events.arc: The Mist Hound of the Three Isles

choices.text: Let the pup sleep by your fire

effects.log: It sleeps through the winter in a haze of mist, and the house smells of rain until spring.

choices.text: Send them off with a parcel of grey fish

effects.log: They go into the fog together. You hear one bark, thanks, perhaps, far off.

events.text: {npc} takes the story of the hound to the Ministry of Fog, which writes it into the registry as a protected breed. The racks of all three isles get a small gate left open at night.
events.arc: The Mist Hound of the Three Isles

choices.text: Sign the registry as witness

effects.log: Your name goes on the page. The three isles send you grey fish every autumn.

choices.text: Slip away before the clerks arrive

effects.log: You prefer the hound's manners to the Ministry's.

events.text: A young sky whale has drifted into the shipping lanes and is blundering toward the fleet at the pace of a slow mountain. The steersman Ohwa says it cannot be stopped, only turned, and the turning needs song. Someone must climb to its eye and sing.
events.arc: The Whale That Must Be Turned

choices.text: Climb to the whale's eye and sing

effects.log: The whale's eye is the size of a pond. It looks at you with immense and gentle confusion.

choices.text: Fly alongside and sound a horn

effects.log: A great note rolls over the clouds. The whale slows, listening.

choices.text: Warn the fleet to scatter

effects.log: The isles part, grumbling, and the whale passes down a lane of anxious clerks.

events.text: The whale hears you. Its song comes back, enormous and slow, and with it a picture: it is looking for the graveyard where its mother lay down. It has been looking for forty years. The map in its head is wrong.
events.arc: The Whale That Must Be Turned

choices.text: Sing back the way to the graveyard

effects.log: You search your memory for the old song of the lanes, and sing it through your whole body.

choices.text: Steer it away from the fleet

effects.log: You sing a bare, bossy tune. The whale obeys, but sulks.

choices.text: Ask it to be patient

effects.log: It hums for an hour in agreement and does nothing, which is also a kind of turning.

events.text: The graveyard is a ridge of enormous ivory ribs in a pocket of still air, with cloud-moss for flowers. The young whale settles beside its mother's bones and the sound that comes from it is the saddest, loveliest note you have ever heard.
events.arc: The Whale That Must Be Turned

choices.text: Stay and sing with it until dawn

effects.log: At dawn the whale drifts upward into the sun, lighter, and the ribs ring faintly behind it.

choices.text: Take one small rib-chip as a keepsake

effects.log: It hums in your hand. Later, in times of trouble, it hums back at you.

events.text: The whale turns, but with a roll and a grunt of protest that sends the leading isle spinning in its mooring. The fleet's clerks will invoice you for the repairs.
events.arc: The Whale That Must Be Turned

choices.text: Pay the clerks in spirit stones

effects.log: You pay four stones and the clerks are, for once, speechless.

choices.text: Argue the bill down with the whale as witness

effects.log: You describe the whale in detail until the clerks give in.

events.text: There is an archive that is never in the same place. It floats from isle to isle on a small raft of cloud, and {npc} the archivist rows it with a long pole. "Catch me on a Tuesday," {he} says. "It is the day I am in a mood to lend."
events.arc: The Archive That Moves on Tuesdays

choices.text: Jump aboard as it passes

effects.log: You land in a heap among rolled slips. {npc} peers down. "Lightly done," {he} says, unmoved.

choices.text: Wave a tea-flask from the dock

effects.log: The raft turns in. {npc} is partial to anyone who brings tea on a Tuesday.

choices.text: Wait and ask where it moors next

effects.log: You learn the route in a month. It is the same as the route of a particular wind.

events.text: {npc} will lend three slips, no more. The shelves hold maps of isles that have not yet drifted into being, a log of every wind that ever had a name, and a sealed slip marked "do not read before you are ready."
events.arc: The Archive That Moves on Tuesdays

choices.text: Borrow the map of the not-yet isles

effects.log: You study it until the isles begin to appear in the sky, one by one, as it predicted.

choices.text: Borrow the log of named winds

effects.log: Each wind has a mood. After a year you can ask any breeze what it wants.

choices.text: Borrow the sealed slip

effects.log: {npc} lifts a brow, then lets you take it. You carry it unopened for years.

events.text: {npc}'s raft is leaking, and the archive is slowly coming apart. Every Tuesday {he} patches a different seam. "When I stop," {he} says lightly, "someone else should be rowing."
events.arc: The Archive That Moves on Tuesdays

choices.text: Offer to row the archive

effects.log: The pole is heavy and warm. You row a season, and the archive forgives you for being slow.

choices.text: Help patch the seams with cloud-silk

effects.log: You work through a long afternoon. The raft floats a little more proudly.

choices.text: Wish {npc} well

effects.log: {He} thanks you with a Tuesday smile.

events.text: The sealed slip opens by itself on a still evening. It holds one line in your own handwriting: "Do not be afraid of what you decide next." You have never written it.
events.arc: The Archive That Moves on Tuesdays

choices.text: Take it as a quiet blessing

effects.log: You carry the line like a stone in your pocket. It makes you braver in small ways.

choices.text: Trace the writing to its odd source

effects.log: It was written by a self you will be in forty years. The thought is vertiginous and oddly kind.

events.text: {npc} hands you the pole at last. "It is a poor job," {he} says. "It has been the best of mine." The archive is yours now, and so are all its Tuesdays.
events.arc: The Archive That Moves on Tuesdays

choices.text: Take the archive and keep its route

effects.log: The slips are lighter than you feared. They sing when the wind is right.

choices.text: Moor the archive at a fixed isle

effects.log: It rests at last. Readers climb to it in all weathers. {npc} visits on Tuesdays and complains.

events.text: At the Edge of Heaven the wind stops being a wind and becomes a question. The cloud-sea ends in a bright line, and beyond it there is no word. A few immortals stand at the rail, eating plums, as if this were an ordinary view.

choices.text: Lean on the rail and eat a plum

effects.log: You feel the question blow through your ribs. By evening you feel lighter, and no wiser, and content.

choices.text: Say a word into the gap

effects.log: The word does not come back. You feel you have given something to the sky.

events.text: A sky-whale graveyard lies behind a curtain of rain: a field of ivory ribs the height of towers, grown over with pale moss. The air is hushed, and the moss glows when anyone speaks softly.

choices.text: Walk among the ribs in silence

effects.log: The whole field hums, one rib to the next. You come away calm.

choices.text: Gather moss to dry

effects.log: It dries to a faint glimmering thread, good for tinder or for dreaming.

events.text: A broken gate stands alone in the clouds: the Gate of Seven Banners, left from the war of the immortals. Two pillars, no wall. Even the wind goes around. On the left pillar a name is scratched, then scratched out, then written again.

choices.text: Read the layers of scratched names

effects.log: Six names, all different, all of people who held the gate. The last is blank, waiting.

choices.text: Rest in the shade of the pillar

effects.log: No one has made war here for nine centuries. The silence is complete and restful.

events.text: In a still pool at the edge of a hanging garden, cloud carp swim through the air, three feet above the water. They are the colour of dawn. A gardener says they only appear to those not trying to catch them.

choices.text: Sit very still and let them come

effects.log: One drifts to your fingertip and goes on. Your breathing settles for a week.

choices.text: Sketch them from memory

effects.log: The sketch is awful and happy. You hang it on your wall.

events.text: The thunder sparrows return to the Lantern Shelf for their season: small grey birds that crackle faintly when startled. Local custom says one must not clap, sing, or sneeze within a bowshot of the nest. Children are very good at this.

choices.text: Spend the season among the sparrows, silent

effects.log: You learn the stillness the children have. A spark jumps from a bird to your sleeve and leaves you humming.

choices.text: Collect fallen tail-feathers

effects.log: They hold a faint charge for years and make an excellent lantern-wick.

events.text: Star-moths come out in the dim orchard on the night of no moon, pale wings printed with the constellations as they were a thousand years ago. Old immortals come to see the skies they used to know.

choices.text: Watch the old skies on the moth wings

effects.log: You find a constellation that no longer exists. You mourn it a little, kindly.

choices.text: Hold a lantern to bring them close

effects.log: They settle on your sleeve in a living map. Your coat glows for an hour.

events.text: The reef-crabs of the Pale Reef carry chips of star-iron on their backs, picked up from the sea floor and arranged with care. A reefer says they trade them for shiny stones and are fair dealers, in a way crabs are.

choices.text: Trade a spirit stone for a chip of star-iron

effects.log: A claw slides the chip across. The crab's eyes are wise and a little mean.

choices.text: Watch the crabs build their mosaic

effects.log: The pattern is a map of the reef from above, which no crab could have seen.

events.text: On a bare isle you find a grotto no larger than a closet with a kettle in it, a single cup, and a note: "Out. Back in a century. Help yourself." The kettle is warm. The note is dated yesterday.

choices.text: Help yourself to tea and leave a thank-you

effects.log: It is the best tea you have had. You leave a plum for the host.

choices.text: Sit and wait out the century

effects.log: You wait a week, then leave a cheerful note under the cup.

events.text: A hot spring bubbles up through a crack in a lonely isle, and in the steam, if you squint, the faces of long-dead bathers drift past, nodding. The spring has a custom: you must say hello to each.

choices.text: Greet each bather politely

effects.log: They nod back and drift on. When you rise from the spring, your aches have left.

choices.text: Sit and think about nothing

effects.log: The spring lets you. It is the work of an hour and the rest of a decade.

events.text: Over a stretch of the cloud sea, lights rise like fireflies at dusk: the lanterns of the sunken, drifting up to the surface and fading. Skiff-pilots tip their hats as they pass. It is considered bad manners to count them.

choices.text: Tip your hat and do not count

effects.log: The lights rise past you like slow thanks. You feel accompanied.

choices.text: Row after one to the end of its rise

effects.log: It pops at the rim of the cloud like a bubble. You laugh before you can stop.

events.text: A staircase cut into a cliff of cloud-stone descends forever, each step wider than the one before. A sign, in a very old script, says it leads "somewhere you will like." Nobody has come back to confirm.

choices.text: Count the steps down to a thousand and turn back

effects.log: At a thousand the air smells of rain on warm stone. You carry the smell home.

choices.text: Leave a candle and a note at the top

effects.log: Some small hope that someone below will read it.

events.text: On the Long Drift night, a rogue immortal sits at the edge of a borrowed isle with a cup of cheap wine. They were turned from three isles this year for lacking a seal. The stars are free and give no tickets. They do not mind.

choices.text: Share the night with the rogue

effects.log: They have a thousand stories about doors that did not open. You stay till dawn.

choices.text: Keep walking and nod

effects.log: You nod. They nod. The stars look on.

events.text: At a cloud-bridge the toll-keeper looks at your skiff, then at your lack of sect seal, and says the toll is double for those with "no home isle." You are the only one in the queue who is charged. The keeper does not meet your eye.

choices.text: Pay the double toll (2 spirit stones)

effects.log: You pay and cross, and the keeper counts the coins twice, to be sure.

choices.text: Row around by the long way

effects.log: It takes an extra day. The wind is kind, the toll-keeper is not missed.

events.text: A single peak stands in the cloud sea, and at the top a bonfire has burned for four hundred years. No one knows who tends it. Skiff-pilots steer by it. The ash is warm and smells of cedar.

choices.text: Add a branch to the fire

effects.log: Cedar spits a spark. You feel part of a long chain of strangers keeping a light.

choices.text: Look for the keeper

effects.log: You find a small hut and a pot of soup, still hot, and nobody home.

events.text: A peddler on the cloud-bridge sells wind in bottles: a breeze from the Eastern Isles, a gale from the long noon, one stale sigh labelled "regrets, aged". The peddler has opinions on each.

choices.text: Buy the gale from the long noon (1 spirit stone)

effects.log: It howls cheerfully in its bottle. You open it on a bad day and fly the whole afternoon.

choices.text: Argue over what regrets are worth

effects.log: The peddler concedes they are priceless and refuses to sell. You are both happy.

events.text: An ancient stair spirals up out of the clouds with nothing at the top. The stone is polished by a million small steps, yet there is no door, only a landing and a view. Pilgrims come simply to stand on it.

choices.text: Stand on the landing and breathe

effects.log: You look at the same sky from a few feet higher. It is a better sky.

choices.text: Wonder who walked it so many times

effects.log: Whoever it was, they went up and came back, and went up and came back.

events.text: The night-blooming cloud-lotus opens once in a hundred years, and tonight is the night. A crowd has gathered on the lake isle with cushions and tea. The bloom is the size of a house and smells of every spring you have forgotten.

choices.text: Find a cushion and watch it open

effects.log: It opens slowly, over hours, and as it does the whole crowd falls quiet, then weeps, then laughs.

choices.text: Carry a petal home in a jar

effects.log: The petal keeps a hint of that scent for decades, and calms you.

events.text: A rogue immortal with no isle may sleep a night on a borrowed one, by courtesy, if they ask. Tonight you ask, and the isle's owner stands in the door with a lamp. "One night," they say. "Mind the cat."

choices.text: Thank them and mind the cat

effects.log: The cat sits on your feet. You wake warm and the owner leaves breakfast at the door.

choices.text: Offer to sweep the porch for the favour

effects.log: The owner softens, a little. "Stay for two nights," they say, as if it cost them.

events.text: The storm-eye is a patch of still air in the centre of a vast storm, where sunlight falls in a pillar and the clouds stand in a ring like a stadium. You come upon it by accident. Everything inside it is very, very quiet.

choices.text: Rest in the quiet and watch the ring turn

effects.log: An hour passes, or a day. When you leave, the storm lets you go like a cat releasing a mouse.

choices.text: Fly the rim of the ring, learning its pace

effects.log: You learn how a storm breathes. It helps with later storms.

events.text: At the bottom of an old crater a pool of starlight lies cold and still. A sign warns: "Do not drink. Do not touch. Do not wish." The sign has been carefully repainted by someone who loves it.

choices.text: Read the sign twice and respect it

effects.log: Some warnings are gifts from people who wanted you to live. You thank the painter, in your head.

choices.text: Touch the pool

ok.log: The pool is cold and sweet. A wish unspoken drifts up and, to your surprise, comes true in small ways.

fail.log: The pool takes a sliver of a year for the wish you did not make.
fail.deathCause: a wish from a pool of starlight

events.text: A trench of the old war of the immortals scars the edge of an isle, grown over with flowers. In the grass a rusted blade stands upright, and around it, someone has planted a ring of white peonies. The petals are fresh.

choices.text: Plant a peony of your own

effects.log: You are not sure for whom. It feels right.

choices.text: Read the blade's inscription

effects.log: It names a regiment and a year. Beneath, in newer hand, "still missed."

events.text: There is a pocket in the cloud-sea where no sound carries. Skiff-pilots avoid it: it makes them anxious. You enter by mistake. Your own breath vanishes, your footsteps vanish. You find, to your surprise, you rather like it.

choices.text: Sit in the silence until the anxiety passes

effects.log: It takes an hour. Afterwards you notice sounds you had never heard before.

choices.text: Leave before it gets into your bones

effects.log: You drift out into the roar of normal sound with a shake of the head.

events.text: {npc} the fowler is too stiff to climb the Lantern Shelf this season, and the thunder sparrows have come. "Take my net," {he} says. "The Ministry of Weather pays by the spark. But I never took a sparrow that was still nesting."
events.arc: The Season of the Thunder Sparrows

choices.text: Take the net and hunt at the nest-edges

effects.log: You work the margins with the net, patiently. The sparrows crackle at you in contempt.

choices.text: Take the net and only watch

effects.log: You hold the net unspread. The sparrows ignore you, then accept you.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to stay by the fire

effects.log: {He} grumbles but stays, and tells you all the old rules over tea.

events.text: The flock rises in a single movement, a grey cloud that crackles like frying. A young sparrow has fallen into your net. It is tiny, shaking, and sparks against your fingers.
events.arc: The Season of the Thunder Sparrows

choices.text: Release it into the flock

effects.log: It shoots upward, a flick of grey, and the flock closes round it.

choices.text: Hand it to the Ministry clerk waiting at the foot

effects.log: The clerk pays two stones and jars the sparrow. You do not look at the jar.

choices.text: Hold it until it stops shaking

effects.log: It falls asleep in your palm, then wakes and leaves without a goodbye.

events.text: A storm of sparks rolls in with the evening, and the sparrows are caught in it, calling. {npc} stumbles out of the cottage, lamp in hand, and begins to sing an old nesting song, cracked and wavering.
events.arc: The Season of the Thunder Sparrows

choices.text: Sing the nesting song with {npc}

effects.log: The sparrows turn toward the sound and settle. The storm passes over the nests.

choices.text: Draw the storm's charge into yourself

ok.log: The sparks run through you in a bright shudder and go to earth. The flock settles, steaming gently.

fail.log: The charge knocks you flat. {npc} drags you under the roof.

choices.text: Hold the lamp high for the flock

effects.log: You hold it until your arms shake. The flock lands.

events.text: The Ministry sends a letter: the sparrows will be "harvested at standard rates" next year. {npc} reads it twice and puts it in the fire.
events.arc: The Season of the Thunder Sparrows

choices.text: Write a counter-petition to protect the nesting-shelf

effects.log: The Ministry of Weather agrees to a "provisional grace" after a lengthy wait. The shelf stays quiet.

choices.text: Teach the other fowlers the old rules

effects.log: They begin to leave nests alone. Slowly, the Ministry's numbers fall, and the sparrows rise.

events.text: {npc} grows quiet over the following years. One autumn the cottage stands empty, the net hung on its nail, a sparrow nesting in the thatch. The flock rises over the shelf in a single crackling wave.
events.arc: The Season of the Thunder Sparrows

choices.text: Keep the net and the old rules

effects.log: You hang the net by the door, never to be used. A sparrow lands on it every spring.

choices.text: Take the cottage and become the shelf's fowler

effects.log: You learn each nest by name. The Ministry stops sending letters.

events.text: The Long Corridor is a canyon of cloud-stone where the wind turns solid and coils. The wind serpent that lives in it is bored, ancient, and hostile to singing. Skiff-pilots take the Corridor in silence, with ribbons tied to the mast to appease it.
events.arc: The Wind Serpent of the Long Corridor

choices.text: Run the Corridor with ribbons and silence

effects.log: The serpent passes alongside for a mile, a long cold shape in the air. It does not strike.

choices.text: Leave a gift at the Corridor mouth

effects.log: A bottle of sweet cloud-wine on a rock. In the morning the bottle is empty and the rock is warm.

choices.text: Take the long way round

effects.log: It costs four days. The ribbons stay dry.

events.text: The serpent speaks, in wind, from the walls. "You are the first to pass in a century who did not hum," it says. "It is rude to hum in a place of listening."
events.arc: The Wind Serpent of the Long Corridor

choices.text: Apologise on behalf of all who hummed

effects.log: The serpent sighs, a gust. "I accept on their behalf," it says dryly.

choices.text: Ask the serpent what it listens for

effects.log: A long pause. "The sound of my own children, asleep." It has been listening for forty years.

choices.text: Say nothing and nod

effects.log: It lets you pass.

events.text: A rival pilot, tired of the Corridor, loads a thunder-shell into a launcher and aims at the canyon wall to "clear the beast." You are three hundred feet away on your skiff.
events.arc: The Wind Serpent of the Long Corridor

choices.text: Fly between the shell and the wall

ok.log: The shell bursts harmlessly on the far wall. The serpent coils back, stunned, then bows at you with its whole length.

fail.log: The shell catches your skiff's edge. You tumble but the serpent is spared.

choices.text: Shout a warning to the serpent

effects.log: It recoils and the shell misses by a hair. The pilot curses and sails off.

choices.text: Report the pilot to the Ministry

effects.log: The Ministry of Fog writes a note about "Corridor etiquette". The pilot is fined, mildly.

events.text: The serpent's children are eggs of cloud-glass in a niche above the canyon. It asks you to carry one down to a warmer wind, for the cold is getting into the shells.
events.arc: The Wind Serpent of the Long Corridor

choices.text: Carry the egg through the warm winds

effects.log: You travel with it wrapped in your robe for a season. It hatches on a south wind, a tiny silver thread.

choices.text: Refuse, as too great a charge

effects.log: The serpent sighs. "I understand," it says, and does not ask again.

events.text: Years later the Corridor hums in the evening wind, a chord of many small voices. The serpent calls it "the family". You may now pass singing.
events.arc: The Wind Serpent of the Long Corridor

choices.text: Sing your way through the Corridor

effects.log: The walls answer. You come out on the far side humming and a little teary.

choices.text: Stay a night in the canyon to listen

effects.log: The family sings you to sleep. In the morning, a silver thread curls round your wrist and falls away.

events.text: {npc} keeps the last peach tree of the Old Orchard, a thousand years old and dying. {He} offers you the pit of its final fruit. "It remembers the tree," {he} says. "Plant it where you will be."
events.arc: The Peach Pit That Remembers

choices.text: Take the pit and plant it on a quiet isle

effects.log: You choose a south-facing slope. The pit sits in the soil like a small sleeping fist.

choices.text: Carry it in your sleeve unplanted

effects.log: It warms against your arm. At night you dream of an orchard in bloom.

choices.text: Decline, for it belongs to the tree

effects.log: {npc} smiles. "A good answer," {he} says, "and a bad one for the tree."

events.text: A sprout breaks the soil in a year: a single leaf, silver-green. It leans toward the east every dawn, toward the Old Orchard, and no wind alters it.
events.arc: The Peach Pit That Remembers

choices.text: Build a small windbreak around it

effects.log: The sprout grows a hand-width in a season. It leans less.

choices.text: Talk to it in the evenings

effects.log: You tell it the news of the isle. It rustles when you mention the orchard.

choices.text: Leave it to the weather

effects.log: It is stronger than you thought, a little offended.

events.text: The pit in your sleeve stirs. It has begun to show a faint green line along the seam. {npc} sends word: the old tree is falling. If the pit is to carry the memory, it must be planted now, in the Orchard's own soil.
events.arc: The Peach Pit That Remembers

choices.text: Go to the Orchard and plant it beside the old tree

effects.log: You plant it at the roots. The old tree sighs in the wind, and its last leaves fall onto the new soil like a blessing.

choices.text: Keep it and plant it at home, as promised

effects.log: The old tree dies without a pit nearby. {npc} does not reproach you, but is silent a long time.

events.text: The sapling stands taller than you now. It has the Orchard's habit of bearing fruit that tastes of a thousand-year-old afternoon. {npc} visits, takes a peach, and weeps in a happy sort of way.
events.arc: The Peach Pit That Remembers

choices.text: Offer cuttings to every isle that wants them

effects.log: Within a century the Old Orchard has grandchildren on twelve isles.

choices.text: Keep the tree for friends alone

effects.log: It is the best-visited porch in the sky.

events.text: The Orchard blooms again, pale and tremendous. {npc}'s eyes shine. "It remembers," {he} says. "It remembers everything. Even me."
events.arc: The Peach Pit That Remembers

choices.text: Sit under the new bloom with {npc}

effects.log: You pass the afternoon without a word, with petals in your hair.

choices.text: Take a cutting for your own isle

effects.log: It roots at once, and the memory travels with it.

events.text: In a pawn stall on a cloud-bridge you find an old steersman's compass whose needle points to no direction at all, but trembles and sways. The pawnbroker says it points to home. "Whose, I never learned."
events.arc: The Steersman's Compass

choices.text: Buy it (2 spirit stones)

effects.log: It is heavy in your hand, and warm.

choices.text: Hold it and watch where the needle swings

effects.log: It swings west, then stops and shivers. You put it back and carry the swing in your mind.

choices.text: Leave it for someone who needs it

effects.log: The pawnbroker says nobody ever does.

events.text: The needle drifts as you travel, and for a year it follows your skiff like a tame bird. It points not at an isle but at a time of day: evening. A particular evening in the past.
events.arc: The Steersman's Compass

choices.text: Chase the evening through the isles

effects.log: You sail west at dusk for a month. The needle quivers and becomes steadier.

choices.text: Ask the pawnbroker where it came from

effects.log: A steersman of the First Fleet left it behind when they went down to the world beneath. They never came back.

choices.text: Put it in a drawer and live your life

effects.log: It hums in the drawer, faintly, for the rest of the winter.

events.text: The compass leads you to a small isle with a lit window. An old immortal opens the door with the look of someone who has been waiting a very long time. "You have my compass," they say. "I was beginning to think I had lost home for good."
events.arc: The Steersman's Compass

choices.text: Return it with a bow

effects.log: They weep, and make tea, and tell you of the First Fleet. You stay a week.

choices.text: Ask to keep it as a loan

effects.log: "A loan," they say, laughing. "I am too old to need it." They give it as a gift.

events.text: The pawnbroker's stall is closed. A card on the shutter: "Gone home. The needle was right all along." The compass in your pocket swings once, joyfully, and settles pointing at your heart.
events.arc: The Steersman's Compass

choices.text: Keep it as a quiet charm

effects.log: It does not point anywhere any more. It simply feels warm when you are where you belong.

choices.text: Hang it at the door of your home isle

effects.log: Travelers pause to read it. Many leave smiling.

events.text: A jade qilin calf has strayed from its herd and is lost in the fog-meadows below the Orchard isle. Qilin are sacred, and the Ministry has put a bounty on its return. {npc}, a herder, says money is a bad reason and the only one the Ministry understands.
events.arc: The Jade Qilin Calf

choices.text: Search the meadows with {npc}

effects.log: You walk fog for two days. The calf's hoofprints leave small flowers.

choices.text: Wait with a bowl of cloud-milk

effects.log: It comes at dusk, step by cautious step, and drinks while trembling.

choices.text: Leave it to the herders

effects.log: {npc} thanks you with a steadiness that is a little cold.

events.text: The calf trusts you, a little, but it will not go toward the herd. It keeps looking up at the sky. The herd has moved, and the calf has not been told. It is grieving.
events.arc: The Jade Qilin Calf

choices.text: Carry the calf yourself to the herd

effects.log: It rests its head on your shoulder for the whole journey, heavy and warm.

choices.text: Follow the calf's gaze to the herd's new meadow

effects.log: It leads you across two isles to a field of pale blue lilies. The herd lifts their heads.

choices.text: Wait until the calf is ready to walk

effects.log: It takes three days. The calf makes up its own mind.

events.text: A Ministry official arrives on the meadow with a net of silver cord, to "secure the specimen." {npc} turns white. The calf stiffens and shifts toward you.
events.arc: The Jade Qilin Calf

choices.text: Face down the official

ok.log: Your argument is long and fair and the official, unable to find a rule against it, takes their net away.

fail.log: The official insists. {npc} hustles the calf out of the back of the herd while you stall.

choices.text: Slip the calf away to the herd by night

effects.log: It goes quietly with you into the dark. By morning it is among its kin.

choices.text: Step aside and let the Ministry proceed

effects.log: The net falls. You watch the calf cry, and cannot forget.

events.text: Years later a full-grown jade qilin steps from the fog and lowers its horn to touch your forehead. The touch is light and cool, and leaves a mark you can feel for a year.
events.arc: The Jade Qilin Calf

choices.text: Accept the blessing with a bow

effects.log: Your steps become gentle. Beasts, birds and children stop avoiding you.

choices.text: Walk the herd to its new meadow

effects.log: You see the field from above at sunrise. The herd is a river of pale green.

events.text: Every night at the hour of the owl, a bell rings from beneath the Tall Isle. There is no bell. {npc}, the isle's bellkeeper, has searched for forty years. "I would like to know," {he} says, "before I stop hearing it."
events.arc: The Bell Beneath the Isle

choices.text: Spend a night under the isle, listening

effects.log: The roots hang down like a curtain. The bell is a low note from somewhere inside the rock.

choices.text: Ask the oldest on the isle who remembers

effects.log: An ancient says there was once a chapel under the isle, before the drift. They do not know where the door went.

choices.text: Wish {npc} luck and leave

effects.log: {He} nods, as to a rain that will not stop.

events.text: The bell's note is a clear low chime, and it rings in the tune of the old nursery song everyone on the isle knows and no one has ever sung to the bell. You hum along. The bell changes key to match.
events.arc: The Bell Beneath the Isle

choices.text: Hum the whole song to the rock

effects.log: The rock gives a satisfied hum. A slim crack appears among the roots.

choices.text: Map where the sound is loudest

effects.log: It is loudest not beneath the isle but in one particular root. You mark it.

choices.text: Mention the song to {npc}

effects.log: {He} blinks, then goes pale with joy. "My mother sang that," {he} says.

events.text: The crack opens on a small hollow with a chapel bell of bronze, half-grown into the roots. Beside it, a child's doll and a note: "For whoever finds this. We rang the bell to say we were still here." It is dated the year the isle drifted away from its harbour.
events.arc: The Bell Beneath the Isle

choices.text: Ring the bell once, in answer

effects.log: The note is clear. Far below, a second bell answers from a harbour you cannot see.

choices.text: Bring {npc} to the hollow

effects.log: {He} sits with the doll in {his} hands for an hour. Then {he} rings the bell, and weeps, and laughs.

events.text: The bell is rung every night now by the children of the isle, in turn. The answer from below has become a regular thing. {npc} calls it "the neighbour."
events.arc: The Bell Beneath the Isle

choices.text: Climb down to find the neighbour

effects.log: The harbour is a day beneath the clouds, a small cove with a bell on a pier. A child waves at you.

choices.text: Leave the dialogue to the children

effects.log: They keep it up for centuries. It is the best kind of mystery, the kind that is happily left.

events.text: {npc} is made keeper of the bell and the hollow, and the isle holds a small festival every drift-month in {his} honour. {He} does not stop smiling, even in the rain.
events.arc: The Bell Beneath the Isle

choices.text: Attend the festival every year

effects.log: Your seat is the third from the left. The bell rings, the harbour answers, and you are home.

choices.text: Bring a tune of your own for the bell

effects.log: The bell learns it. The harbour learns it. Soon the whole cove hums it.

events.text: You have no isle and no seal, and this winter the last host who would have you has closed the door politely. At the cloud-bridge, a worn immortal with a patched coat shares a bench. "First year?" {npc} asks. "It gets easier. The sky does not mind who you are."
events.arc: The Drifting Life

choices.text: Ask {npc} how it is done

effects.log: {He} lists rules: borrow, never take; sleep on the lee side; always leave the kettle clean. "That is the whole law of the Drifting Life."

choices.text: Share your bread and sit

effects.log: The bread is stale and {npc} praises it as if it were a feast.

choices.text: Nod and move on alone

effects.log: {He} lifts a hand, unoffended. The bridge is cold after.

events.text: {npc} takes you through the lee-side stops: a shepherd who lends a hay-loft, a bridge-keeper who lets rogues sleep under the arch, a widow with a fire and a rule of one night. The Drifting Life is a map of small mercies held together by manners.
events.arc: The Drifting Life

choices.text: Repay every kindness with a task

effects.log: You mend a roof, split wood, carry water. The hosts remember you by name the next season.

choices.text: Learn the stops and pass them on to other rogues

effects.log: You write the map on a slip and leave copies at each stop. Soon a quiet road exists.

choices.text: Travel light and trust the sky

effects.log: The sky provides, in its own odd way.

events.text: At a stop with a sect seal on the gate, the steward looks at your coat and says the isle does not "house the unaffiliated." A child behind them leans out and whispers, "I can hide you in the barn." The steward pretends not to hear.
events.arc: The Drifting Life

choices.text: Accept the child's offer and leave before dawn

effects.log: The barn is warm and smells of apples. You leave coins in the child's boot.

choices.text: Argue your right to a roof, politely

effects.log: The steward concedes a corner of the porch. It is something. It is pointed.

choices.text: Walk on in the dark

effects.log: The night is clear. You are cold, and clean.

events.text: {npc} takes ill on a lee-side stop, a cough that will not leave. {He} has no isle to be nursed on. "Do not fuss," {he} says. "A rogue dies where the wind stops."
events.arc: The Drifting Life

choices.text: Carry {npc} to a healer's isle at your own cost

effects.log: It takes eight stones and a week of begging. {npc} lives, and curses you with deep affection.

choices.text: Brew a poultice from cloud-sage

ok.log: The cough breaks by the third day. {npc} says you are a better healer than half the Ministry.

fail.log: The poultice is weak. {npc} suffers but recovers, slowly, under your care.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} through the nights

effects.log: You tell {him} every story you know, and some you invent. {He} lives out of spite.

events.text: Years pass in the drift. The map you wrote is on a hundred slips. A stranger on a bridge says, "You are the one who made the road?" A seal is pressed into your hand: an isle that would be glad of a rogue for a keeper.
events.arc: The Drifting Life

choices.text: Take the keepership, and keep the road open

effects.log: Your isle becomes the first stop for rogues. The kettle is always warm.

choices.text: Decline, and keep drifting

effects.log: You belong to the sky. The seal goes to someone who needs a door more than you do.

events.text: The old ferry calls at seven isles in a week, a slow loop of wood and cloud-silk poled by {npc}, who has never missed a landing. Passage is a story from each passenger. "It is the fare," {he} says, "and the only thing worth carrying."
events.arc: The Ferry of Seven Isles

choices.text: Pay your fare with a true story

effects.log: You tell of your first sight of the sky. {npc} nods slowly. "That will carry us three isles."

choices.text: Pay in the work of an oar

effects.log: You pole three isles. {npc} critiques your stroke in a voice of boundless patience.

choices.text: Stand at the rail and listen to the others

effects.log: Six passengers, six stories. You listen to all of them.

events.text: The ferry takes on a passenger at the third isle who tells no story and keeps a covered cage in their lap. {npc} watches the cage the way one watches a pot. By the fourth isle, the cage is humming.
events.arc: The Ferry of Seven Isles

choices.text: Ask the passenger what is in the cage

effects.log: A newborn thunder sparrow, they say, stolen. They are afraid, and they do not know what to do.

choices.text: Offer to take the sparrow

effects.log: The passenger hands it over with relief. It sparks gently on your wrist.

choices.text: Say nothing and watch

effects.log: The humming grows. {npc} slows the ferry.

events.text: A storm-front rises between the fifth and sixth isles. {npc} pulls the ferry to a halt in the lee of a cloud-reef and puts a lantern on the bow. "Now we wait," {he} says. "Tell the oldest story you know."
events.arc: The Ferry of Seven Isles

choices.text: Tell the story of the sparrow-stealer's fear

effects.log: The passenger weeps. {npc} says nothing, but hands them tea.

choices.text: Offer to run ahead to the sixth isle for help

effects.log: The sixth isle sends three skiffs with ropes. The ferry is towed to port by dawn.

choices.text: Wait out the storm in silence

effects.log: The ferry rocks. The lantern holds.

events.text: At the seventh isle the passenger steps off and leaves the cage, empty. The sparrow is gone, loosed into the storm-light. {npc} says only: "Better to let it be." {He} has done this before.
events.arc: The Ferry of Seven Isles

choices.text: Wave from the rail as the ferry pulls away

effects.log: The ferry turns for its next loop. {npc} gives you a long look, a nod.

choices.text: Offer to stay aboard for the next loop

effects.log: {npc} gives you the second pole. You are a ferryman for a season.

events.text: When the ferry reaches the end of its last season, {npc} offers it to you. "It will not pay," {he} says, "but it will feed you stories till the end of the sky."
events.arc: The Ferry of Seven Isles

choices.text: Take the ferry

effects.log: You pole the seven isles for centuries, and your passengers become your friends.

choices.text: Decline, and ride as a passenger

effects.log: You remain the ferry's best-loved fare and its worst oarsman.

events.text: The reef-crab king is the size of a skiff, barnacled, wise, and in the habit of cutting the ropes of boats that tie to its reef. The reefers want it gone. The Ministry wants its shell. The crab, as it happens, has not been asked.
events.arc: The King of the Pale Reef

choices.text: Track the king across the reef at low cloud

effects.log: Its trail is a line of snapped moorings and polished pebbles in careful rows.

choices.text: Ask the smaller crabs where it lives

effects.log: They tap out an answer on a rock. It takes a day to read.

choices.text: Tell the reefers to moor elsewhere

effects.log: They grumble but they move. The crab takes it as a victory.

events.text: The king's lair is a cathedral of star-iron chips arranged in a mosaic. It watches you enter with a pair of eyes like lanterns, and clicks a claw politely. It is not a challenge. It is a greeting.
events.arc: The King of the Pale Reef

choices.text: Bow to the king

effects.log: It dips a claw. It has all the dignity of an ancient ambassador.

choices.text: Study the mosaic

effects.log: It is a map of the reef drawn from memory. A single mooring is marked in red: the one it cut, again and again.

choices.text: Back out slowly

effects.log: The king lets you go with a courteous clack.

events.text: The marked mooring is a rope tied to a broken post. Beyond it, in a crevice, lie crab eggs, a hundred pearls in a nest of cloud-moss. The reefers' boats, tied there, have been tearing the nest with every tide.
events.arc: The King of the Pale Reef

choices.text: Move the mooring and tell the reefers

effects.log: The king watches. It does not cut a rope again.

choices.text: Tend the nest yourself for a season

effects.log: You tie moss to the broken post and guard the eggs against careless boats.

choices.text: Write a warning for the reefers

effects.log: It helps a little. The reefers read slowly.

events.text: The eggs hatch on a spring tide: a hundred tiny crabs spill over the reef like silver. The king gives you a star-iron chip the size of your palm, set in a bit of polished shell.
events.arc: The King of the Pale Reef

choices.text: Keep the chip as a thank-you

effects.log: It rings softly when danger is near. Reefers say it is a reef-friend's mark.

choices.text: Give the chip to the Ministry for the reef's protection

effects.log: The reef is declared a nesting ground, and the chip goes into a case with a long label.

events.text: In the ruins of a war outpost, a courier's satchel hangs from a nail, untouched for nine centuries. It holds three hundred letters addressed to families who no longer exist. {npc}, a modern courier, says {he} has been trying to deliver them for ten years.
events.arc: The Unsent Letters of the War

choices.text: Help {npc} sort the letters by isle

effects.log: The addresses are archaic. Only a handful of isles still bear those names.

choices.text: Read one letter, with permission

effects.log: It is a soldier's note: weather, rice, a joke about the cook. The joke is still funny.

choices.text: Wish {npc} luck

effects.log: {He} nods, a little weary. "It is a small post, but it is a post."

events.text: Eleven letters find living addressees: descendants who never knew their ancestor wrote. {npc} insists on delivering each in person, and you go along. Some cry. Some shut the door. One asks you in for tea.
events.arc: The Unsent Letters of the War

choices.text: Stay for the tea and the story

effects.log: The descendant tells you what became of the soldier. It is not a sad story. Just a long one.

choices.text: Leave the letter and move on

effects.log: You keep the pace. Some things should be read alone.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach you the courier's knots

effects.log: {He} ties seventeen. Each means a different weather.

events.text: One of the letters has no addressee, only a symbol: a fan with five folds. It has been in the satchel since the day of the last battle. {npc} asks you to help {him} find its meaning.
events.arc: The Unsent Letters of the War

choices.text: Ask the old appraisers about the symbol

effects.log: It is the mark of a vanished court, whose last member is rumoured to live on the Edge.

choices.text: Open the letter, with {npc}'s blessing

effects.log: It is a love letter to someone who was never sent it, and who never knew.

events.text: The last member of the vanished court lives on a bare shelf at the Edge of Heaven. They are very old and very tired. The letter, read aloud, brings a long silence, then a smile that takes years off them.
events.arc: The Unsent Letters of the War

choices.text: Sit with the old one until sunset

effects.log: They tell you the name of the sender. It was their sister. It is the first time they have spoken it in nine centuries.

choices.text: Leave the letter and go quietly

effects.log: You leave them to read it again. You hear them laughing as you go.

events.text: {npc}'s satchel is empty at last. {He} hangs it back on its nail and says the ruin has gone quiet. {He} gives you a small leather pouch with the last letter in it: a note to {him}, written long ago, from the war, about a hope of retiring.
events.arc: The Unsent Letters of the War

choices.text: Frame the satchel in the outpost

effects.log: It becomes a small shrine of the lost post. Couriers come to pay respects.

choices.text: Take {npc} to a tea-house and buy {him} lunch

effects.log: {He} says it is the first meal {he} has eaten sitting down in twenty years.

events.text: On a cloud-reef off the common lanes, {npc} works star-iron: a metal that falls from the sky and refuses to be struck unless it is addressed by name. {His} forge is a hollow in the reef, {his} anvil a fallen star. "I need a helper," {he} says, "who can be patient with a stubborn thing."
events.arc: The Smith on the Cloud-Reef

choices.text: Offer to hold the tongs

effects.log: The star-iron glows white and then blue. {npc} speaks to it in a low voice, like to a horse.

choices.text: Ask the star-iron its name

effects.log: The smith stops, stares, then laughs. "No one has asked in a thousand years."

choices.text: Watch from the door

effects.log: You watch the forging for a day. It is the most patient thing you have ever seen.

events.text: The iron will not take the shape of a blade. It insists, over three months, on being a bell. {npc} sighs, shrugs, and lets it. The bell rings once, and every cloud in the sky seems to lean toward the sound.
events.arc: The Smith on the Cloud-Reef

choices.text: Help carry the bell to the reef's edge

effects.log: It is lighter than it looks. You hang it on a post over the abyss.

choices.text: Ask the smith to teach you the naming

effects.log: It takes a year. At the end, you can say the name of a small star-iron nugget, and it warms.

choices.text: Ring the bell

effects.log: The sound spreads out over the cloud-sea. The reef-crabs come out to listen.

events.text: A Ministry appraiser arrives: star-iron is a "regulated material", and the smith is working without a licence. They want {him} to hand over the bell. {npc} sits on the anvil, silent.
events.arc: The Smith on the Cloud-Reef

choices.text: Argue that the bell is a gift, not a good

ok.log: The appraiser, after much sighing, writes it down as "a reef-marker" and leaves the licence question open.

fail.log: The appraiser is unmoved. {npc} pays a fine of three stones and the bell stays.

choices.text: Offer to carry the bell to the Ministry under protest

effects.log: The Ministry hangs it in a hall. The smith visits it every week.

choices.text: Say nothing; it is {his} business

effects.log: The appraiser looks from {him} to you and does their paperwork, flatly.

events.text: {npc} gives you a nugget of named star-iron, the size of a plum. "It will answer to you," {he} says, "if you remember its name." Then {he} turns back to the forge. There is always another stubborn thing.
events.arc: The Smith on the Cloud-Reef

choices.text: Keep the nugget and speak its name every dawn

effects.log: It warms to your hand. After a decade it hums when you walk into a room.

choices.text: Leave it in the reef as a marker

effects.log: The reef-crabs bury it in a mosaic. The reef glows faintly for a century.

events.text: The bell the smith made rings across the cloud-sea at dusk, and sky-whales turn their heads. Some say it is the best thing ever forged on the reef. {npc} says it was the iron's idea.
events.arc: The Smith on the Cloud-Reef

choices.text: Climb to hear the bell from the reef's edge

effects.log: You sit by it for an hour. The sound goes through you like clean water.

choices.text: Tell the story of the bell in the markets

effects.log: It becomes a favourite tale. The smith gets visitors, and complains happily.

events.text: Under the Jade Void Sect's oldest hall is a locked cellar no disciple has entered in six hundred years. {npc}, an elder, finds you sweeping the stair and says: "I have the key and no courage. Do you have the courage and no key?"
events.arc: The Cellar Under the Jade Void

choices.text: Take the key and go down with {npc}

effects.log: The stair is long and cold, and the lock opens with a sigh.

choices.text: Ask what is down there

effects.log: "The sect's first mistake," {npc} says. "Kept so no one is embarrassed."

choices.text: Decline and keep sweeping

effects.log: {npc} pockets the key and nods, a little relieved.

events.text: The cellar holds a single jade slip on a stand, and a ring of cushions where, apparently, the founders argued. The slip reads: "We were wrong to close the gate on the first rogue. Open it when you can." It is signed by seven founders.
events.arc: The Cellar Under the Jade Void

choices.text: Carry the slip to the sect's assembly

effects.log: The assembly is silent, then stormy. In the end the gate is opened for a rogue, once a year. It is a start.

choices.text: Keep the slip until the right moment

effects.log: It sits in your sleeve for years like a coal.

choices.text: Return the slip and lock the cellar

effects.log: The shame of the founders stays in the dark, undisturbed.

events.text: Years later, an old rogue appears at the sect's gate, hat in hand. Your slip, long carried, burns in your sleeve. The gatekeeper is turning the rogue away.
events.arc: The Cellar Under the Jade Void

choices.text: Speak up with the founders' words

effects.log: The gatekeeper pales, steps aside. The rogue is welcomed, perplexed.

choices.text: Quietly escort the rogue in through a side gate

effects.log: You break no law but a custom. The rogue never learns your name.

events.text: The yearly Open Gate becomes a festival: rogues from every isle arrive with their patched coats and stories. {npc} serves tea at the gate, in tears, remembering the cellar.
events.arc: The Cellar Under the Jade Void

choices.text: Serve tea with {npc}

effects.log: You pour for a thousand rogues. Each leaves with a seal of passage to one more door.

choices.text: Write the founders' words above the gate

effects.log: They read, in gold, for generations.

events.text: At the Nine Clouds Palace the finest silk is spun only from the first clouds of the morning, caught before the sun touches them. {npc}, the head weaver, gives you a frame of white threads. "The cloud must come to the frame by itself," {he} says. "If you pull, it dies."
events.arc: The Dawn Silk Harvest

choices.text: Hold the frame still in the dawn

effects.log: You hold it for an hour in the cold. A cloud drifts in and settles, as delicate as breath.

choices.text: Sing quietly to attract a cloud

effects.log: A small, shy cloud approaches and curls round the frame.

choices.text: Watch {npc} work first

effects.log: {He} tilts {his} frame like a hand held open. The clouds arrive as if called.

events.text: The silk from your frame is uneven, a little torn, and utterly beautiful. {npc} turns it in the light and says it is the first honest silk {he} has seen in a decade. {He} wants to put it in the palace hall.
events.arc: The Dawn Silk Harvest

choices.text: Let {npc} hang it in the hall

effects.log: The silk sways in the draught. Visitors stop before it, puzzled and tender.

choices.text: Keep it for yourself

effects.log: You wear it as a scarf. It carries a faint scent of morning.

choices.text: Offer it to a poor weaver in the lower quarter

effects.log: They weep at the gift. It lines a baby's cradle.

events.text: A frost-wind comes at dawn and freezes the clouds into hard white scraps that cut the threads. The harvest is ruined, and a rival palace offers to sell its silk to the Nine Clouds at ruinous prices.
events.arc: The Dawn Silk Harvest

choices.text: Share the palace's remaining silk with the poorer weavers

effects.log: You give what remains. The palace is the poorer, and the weavers' gratitude is long.

choices.text: Lead a night harvest by lantern-light

ok.log: The weavers follow your lantern and catch a thin, silver cloud no one has ever caught at night. It sells for a fortune.

fail.log: The night clouds are too shy. The harvest yields little.

choices.text: Buy the rival's silk and say nothing

effects.log: It is cheaper to be silent.

events.text: The silk you caught hangs in the palace hall for a century, and weavers touch its edge for luck. {npc} says it is the only piece in the hall that was never meant to be there.
events.arc: The Dawn Silk Harvest

choices.text: Take a thread to remember it by

effects.log: It is faint as a hair and warm to the touch. It never frays.

choices.text: Teach the novices to catch uneven silk

effects.log: They learn that perfect silk is a kind of lie. The palace's silk grows livelier.

events.text: At the Star Sea Pavilion, {npc} has counted the falling stars for four hundred years and keeps a ledger of each: its brightness, its direction, its mood. "I cannot find the pattern," {he} says, "but I am sure it is there. Count with me?"
events.arc: The Man Who Counted Falling Stars

choices.text: Take the night watch and count

effects.log: You count eighty-one in a night. The ledger fills. Your eyes ache, and your spirits lift.

choices.text: Look for a pattern in the old ledgers

effects.log: The ledgers are a tower of paper. By the third shelf you see a faint rhythm.

choices.text: Bring tea and sit

effects.log: {npc} accepts the tea and a little company.

events.text: You and {npc} compare notes. The falling stars come in clusters of seven, then a gap of nine nights, then seven again. It is a rhythm, but of what? {npc} says it sounds like someone knocking.
events.arc: The Man Who Counted Falling Stars

choices.text: Knock back with a lantern signal

effects.log: You flash a lantern seven times. The sky is silent for nine nights. Then seven stars fall.

choices.text: Record the pattern and send it to the Ministry of Weather

effects.log: The Ministry notes it with a stamp and loses it.

choices.text: Keep watching without acting

effects.log: The pattern holds. You learn to wait.

events.text: The seven falling stars, you realise, are a message in a language of brightness. {npc} decodes it with a trembling hand. It says: "We are still here. Are you?"
events.arc: The Man Who Counted Falling Stars

choices.text: Answer with a lantern: "We are."

effects.log: The stars fall quiet for a month, then a single star dips toward the pavilion in answer.

choices.text: Study the reply, but refrain from answering

effects.log: The message is too beautiful to meddle with. You catalogue it.

choices.text: Keep it a secret between you and {npc}

effects.log: The ledger is hidden in the pavilion's roof-beam.

events.text: {npc} dies at the telescope, finished and content. {His} last entry reads: "Heard." You answer the sky for {him} each night, seven flashes, then nine nights of silence, then seven.
events.arc: The Man Who Counted Falling Stars

choices.text: Keep the watch for the rest of your long life

effects.log: The conversation with the stars is slow, patient, tender. The pavilion hangs your portrait beside {npc}'s.

choices.text: Teach apprentices the code and step back

effects.log: The pavilion fills with young counters. The stars never run out of friends.

events.text: The Ministry of Precedence wants a survey of the Edge of Heaven: a line on a map where "heaven ends." {npc}, a young surveyor, has been given a theodolite, three assistants and no idea where the edge actually is. {He} asks you to be the fourth.
events.arc: The Ministry Survey of the Edge

choices.text: Join the survey and plant the markers

effects.log: You walk four days along a line that keeps changing. The markers keep drifting.

choices.text: Advise a change of method

effects.log: You suggest measuring the wind instead of the ground. {npc} blinks, writes it down.

choices.text: Decline, with regret

effects.log: {npc} sighs. "I will draw it from the Ministry's window then," {he} says.

events.text: The edge refuses to stay put. Each night the markers have moved a few feet further out. {npc} grows pale. Then you notice: the markers have not moved. The ground has gone out from under them, and the edge is the ground's end, not heaven's.
events.arc: The Ministry Survey of the Edge

choices.text: Report the truth: the edge is a moving thing

effects.log: The Ministry takes it hard and files it as "preliminary". {npc} is promoted for honesty.

choices.text: Report a fixed edge, as the Ministry wants

effects.log: The report is accepted and a boundary stone is raised that will be wrong in a decade.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what {he} would prefer

effects.log: {He} wishes {he} had never been told. {He} picks the truth in the end.

events.text: At the true edge, you and {npc} look out at nothing: a wash of colour with no ground. A strange bird, pale and quiet, perches on the last stone. It looks at you, then at the void. {npc} whispers: "Do you think it wants to go out there?"
events.arc: The Ministry Survey of the Edge

choices.text: Throw a loaf to the bird and wait

effects.log: The bird takes it and flies a few feet over the void and back, as if trying it.

choices.text: Mark the place and withdraw

effects.log: You draw a small circle of salt on the stone. It is the first safe place at the edge.

events.text: The survey is published under {npc}'s name and yours, with a handsome map and a chapter on "the unsteady edge." It is the last honest survey of the Ministry in a long time.
events.arc: The Ministry Survey of the Edge

choices.text: Accept the credit with modesty

effects.log: Your name is on an official document. The Ministry sends a letter of thanks.

choices.text: Let {npc} take all the credit

effects.log: {He} is grateful beyond words. {He} sends you a bottle of cloud-wine every year.

events.text: The edge stone you set rings in a storm and a hundred skiffs steer clear because of it. {npc} calls it the Stone of Honest Fear. The Ministry removes it. The pilots put it back.
events.arc: The Ministry Survey of the Edge

choices.text: Sit at the stone and watch the skiffs steer clear

effects.log: It is a private satisfaction. The pilots wave.

choices.text: Petition for the stone's restoration

effects.log: It takes a year, but the petition succeeds. The stone is classified as "a navigation aid."

events.text: A small procession of pilgrims files along the Edge of Heaven, each carrying a stone from their home isle. They set the stones in a line on the last shelf, and say nothing, and go. The line has been growing for four hundred years. No one knows who started it.

choices.text: Add a stone from your own isle

effects.log: The stone sits among the others. You feel, obscurely, a part of something that outlasts quarrels.

choices.text: Read the stones, one by one

effects.log: Each has a name scratched on the underside. Two of them are yours.

events.text: Sky-whales gather at the turn of the year to sing the chorus of the old routes. It rolls through the clouds as a pressure, not a sound. Skiffs tie up at a safe distance and drift, passengers holding hands, tears on every cheek.

choices.text: Tie up and feel the chorus in your bones

effects.log: It takes an hour to let it go. You step off the skiff lighter.

choices.text: Hum a single note along

effects.log: One whale turns, slowly, to listen. You have been heard by something very large and very kind.

events.text: Between the broken pillars of a war-fortress, someone has laid out a perfect garden of dwarf peonies and moss. A tin kettle sits on a flat stone. No one is around, but the soil is damp, and the kettle is warm.

choices.text: Pour yourself a cup and sit

effects.log: Tea of the garden-keeper, who is clearly someone shy. A note: "Leave the cup."

choices.text: Leave a small plant of your own

effects.log: It is a fern. It takes at once. You imagine the keeper's quiet nod.

events.text: Fog-fishers ride small skiffs into the cloud-sea at dawn, trailing silk lines, hauling up ghost-fish that glow and vanish at the surface. The old fishers say the trick is not to hold them, only to look.

choices.text: Fish with a line for an hour

effects.log: You catch one. It glows once, pale and astonished, and winks out. You feel a child again.

choices.text: Sit with the old fishers and share their tea

effects.log: They tell you of fish that sang, once, the day the war began.

events.text: A lantern-toad squats in the roots of a cloud-pine, glowing softly green. It has sat there, by local account, since the isle was young. Children bring it dew-drops. It blinks in thanks, once a season.

choices.text: Bring it a drop of dew

effects.log: It blinks, slowly, the blink of a very old creature. You feel privileged.

choices.text: Sit beside the toad until it blinks again

effects.log: You wait four hours. It blinks. The wait was the point.

events.text: Under a quiet isle, a door hangs in the air with nothing around it: a plain wooden door with a brass handle, open to the sky on both sides. A few visitors have walked through it and come out, unchanged, on the same side.

choices.text: Walk through the door

effects.log: You step through and come out unchanged. For a moment your heart was very far away, and then it was back.

choices.text: Knock and wait

effects.log: No one answers. The door seems pleased to be asked.

events.text: In the bottom of a small star-crater a pond has formed, and in it the night sky is reflected in daytime. Birds fly over and look down, confused. A sign: "Do not feed the constellations."

choices.text: Watch the night sky in the pond until dusk

effects.log: At dusk the two skies meet and the pond goes dark and ordinary again.

choices.text: Drop a pebble and watch the stars ripple

effects.log: The ripples spread across a hundred constellations. The pebble sinks in a spiral of light.

events.text: A cliff of cloud-stone leans out into the sky with a handhold-ladder cut into it by someone who loved climbing. At the top, a bench, a plum tree, and a tin of tea. The view is not the point. The plum tree is.

choices.text: Climb up and eat a plum

effects.log: The plum is perfect. You carry a seed down in your pocket.

choices.text: Leave a thank-you note in the tin

effects.log: The next visitor will find it.

events.text: A spring on a lonely isle speaks, in a low murmur, the last things said near it. A scholar sits by it, writing. "It has a long memory," they say, "and no taste. It repeats all."

choices.text: Listen to the spring for an hour

effects.log: You hear a lover's quarrel, a lullaby, and a dispute over a goat. The spring is democratic.

choices.text: Whisper something kind into the water

effects.log: It will say it for centuries. You think of the unknown listener.

events.text: On the night of the Floating Lanterns, a thousand tiny skiffs set out across the cloud-sea, each carrying a lantern and a wish. They drift apart, one by one, to the horizon. Some sink. Most do not.

choices.text: Launch a lantern with a wish

effects.log: You do not tell the wish. It drifts out with the rest.

choices.text: Watch from the shore and count the lights

effects.log: You lose count at four hundred and begin again, gladly.

events.text: A set of stairs rises from a bare isle and ends in a ledge with a hammock and a flask of tea. A sign: "Rest here. Do not thank the stairs." A cat is already asleep in the hammock.

choices.text: Rest on the stair-step beside the cat

effects.log: You nap two hours. The cat purrs in its sleep and you wake lighter.

choices.text: Tuck a coin under the flask

effects.log: The stairs, you suspect, are pleased.

events.text: A grove of wind-bamboo grows from the underside of an isle and hangs downward, each stalk a different length. In the wind they play a slow, strange music that visitors swear they have heard before.

choices.text: Sit under the bamboo and listen

effects.log: It is a song you almost know. You hum it for a week.

choices.text: Trim a cane for a flute

effects.log: The flute plays the same song. It is, annoyingly, better than yours.

events.text: A tiny isle with a single willow tree has been following your skiff for three days, keeping a polite distance. When you stop, it stops. When you look at it, it drifts a little away. It is a shy isle.

choices.text: Leave out a small offering of rice cake

effects.log: In the morning the cake is gone, and the isle is a little closer.

choices.text: Wave and carry on

effects.log: It follows for a week, then bows, and drifts home.

events.text: On a rolling isle of green hills, a shepherd tends a flock of small clouds, driving them gently with a crook. Each cloud has a name and an opinion. The shepherd lets you carry one for the afternoon.

choices.text: Carry the cloud and listen to its complaints

effects.log: It is chilly, and wants to be elsewhere. You learn to carry a mood.

choices.text: Help drive the flock home

effects.log: You get wet, content, and the shepherd presses a bottle of mist on you.

events.text: At the edge of the Pale Reef, a floating market sells star-iron chips, crab-shell combs, and jars of reef-air that smell of salt and old stone. The haggling is done in claw-clacks and silent sums on an abacus of bone.

choices.text: Buy a jar of reef-air (1 spirit stone)

effects.log: You open it that winter. The room smells of a coast you have never seen.

choices.text: Haggle for the fun of it

effects.log: The seller ends up giving you a comb for a story. You both leave winners.

events.text: A tribulation cloud drifts past in the evening, black and rumbling, seeking someone not you. It pauses, as if checking, then moves on with a slightly aggrieved air. The immortals on the terrace raise their cups to it politely.

choices.text: Raise your cup to the cloud as well

effects.log: It rumbles faintly. You feel noticed, and not hunted.

choices.text: Retreat indoors and bolt the door

effects.log: The cloud passes. You feel a little foolish and a lot dry.

events.text: A wall of unmortared stone runs across a high plateau, older than any court. Moss has filled its seams. On windless days the wall hums; local children say it is dreaming.

choices.text: Press your ear to the wall

effects.log: You hear a low murmur, like water in a hollow. It is not a language, but it is an intention.

choices.text: Walk the wall to its end

effects.log: It takes a day. At the end, a single stone is missing, and the wind goes through it like breath.

events.text: At the ferry landing, a boatman waves the sealed passengers aboard and then points at you and says there is no room. There is plenty of room. The bench behind them is empty.

choices.text: Wait for the next ferry

effects.log: It comes after four hours. You sit with a flask of tea and your thoughts.
