choices.text: Pay extra for the empty bench (2 spirit stones)

effects.log: You pay and cross. The boatman does not meet your eye.

events.text: You find a single paper lantern snagged on a cloud-pine, still lit, with a name written on it that you cannot read. The flame is steady in a strong wind. It seems to be waiting for someone.

choices.text: Carry it to the nearest isle and hang it by a door

effects.log: The door opens. A face lights up. "I lost that eighty years ago," says the owner.

choices.text: Release it into the air once more

effects.log: It rises, bobbing, toward some other hand.

events.text: A very old sky whale carries a library in its throat: songs of the first routes, sung by its mother's mother. {npc}, who rides on its back in a small tent, writes the songs down as the whale sings. {He} has twelve of three thousand. {He} asks you to hold the lantern.
events.arc: The Library Inside the Whale

choices.text: Hold the lantern through the night

effects.log: The whale sings until dawn, a slow rolling thing. {npc} writes by your light and does not look up.

choices.text: Learn the first song by ear

effects.log: It takes a month. Your voice cracks. The whale hums a patient correction.

choices.text: Bring dumplings and talk with {npc}

effects.log: {He} is starved of conversation and tells you of the whale's habits for hours.

events.text: Song twenty-one is the route to the southern harbour, and it ends in a sob. {npc} says the whale does not sing the ending any more. Something happened there. The whale grows restless whenever it comes near the old route.
events.arc: The Library Inside the Whale

choices.text: Ask the whale about the harbour, in song

effects.log: The whale slows, and its answer is a picture: a harbour in flames, and a small whale-calf lost in the smoke.

choices.text: Sing the ending yourself, as you imagine it

effects.log: The whale shudders, then joins in, and for the first time the song finishes, soft and sad.

choices.text: Leave the harbour song unsung

effects.log: Some songs are kept open on purpose.

events.text: At the old harbour the water is still, the moorings long rotted. A single post stands, and wrapped around it is a ribbon of whale-skin, half petrified. A calf's toy, perhaps, or a grave-marker.
events.arc: The Library Inside the Whale

choices.text: Lay a garland of cloud-lilies at the post

effects.log: The whale lets out a long note. Something in its chest eases for the first time in years.

choices.text: Take the ribbon to the whale

effects.log: It nudges the ribbon with its nose, once, and falls silent. It wears it on its fin ever after.

events.text: The whale sings the harbour song entire, the next dawn, and the clouds themselves seem to still. {npc} writes every note, weeping openly. At the last bar, {he} stops, puts down the brush, and simply listens.
events.arc: The Library Inside the Whale

choices.text: Listen with {npc}, and say nothing

effects.log: Whale and keeper and you in a tent in the sky. It is the best hour of your life.

choices.text: Offer to copy the library for the archives

effects.log: Within a decade the songs are on jade slips in three archives. The whale does not mind.

events.text: {npc} gives you the first song, copied in {his} own hand. "Sing it," {he} says, "where whales can hear. They will always know.", and you do, and a whale across the cloud-sea turns its head.
events.arc: The Library Inside the Whale

choices.text: Sing the first song to the wide sky

effects.log: An answer rolls up from far below, a note as big as a hill. You grin like a fool.

choices.text: Teach it to the children of your isle

effects.log: They sing it in the evenings. The whales come near the isle, curious.

events.text: The dim orchard blooms with star-moths on one night in seven years. {npc}, an old astronomer, comes every time with a net of black silk and a notebook. "They carry the old sky on their wings," {he} says. "Help me read it."
events.arc: The Night of the Star-Moths

choices.text: Take the notebook and sketch the wings

effects.log: You draw until your fingers cramp. Each moth is a different year of the old sky.

choices.text: Hold the black net still

effects.log: The moths settle on it like snow. {npc} reads the patterns with a lantern.

choices.text: Just watch the moths

effects.log: A moth lands on your sleeve and shows you a constellation that no longer exists.

events.text: One moth bears a constellation {npc} cannot find in any catalogue: three stars in a line, with a fourth below, bright red. {He} goes pale. "That is the Warden's Lamp," {he} says. "It went out in the war."
events.arc: The Night of the Star-Moths

choices.text: Ask what the Lamp was

effects.log: A beacon on the Edge, lit by an order of watchers. Its failure marked the war's turn. {npc} has searched for it for sixty years.

choices.text: Follow the moth as it flies off

effects.log: It leads you across the orchard to a mossy stone with a hollow in it, empty of flame.

choices.text: Let {npc} have the moment

effects.log: {He} stands with the moth on {his} finger for an hour. You pour tea.

events.text: At the hollow stone you find a tiny glass vial with a pinch of silver dust and a slip: "To relight the Lamp, add a star's patience." The moths gather around you in a cloud, quiet, waiting.
events.arc: The Night of the Star-Moths

choices.text: Sit with the vial through the night, in patience

effects.log: At dawn the dust glows faintly. It has taken the shape of a flame the size of a seed.

choices.text: Try to ignite it with your own qi

ok.log: The flame catches and burns steady. The moths rise as one into a cloud of silver light.

fail.log: The dust scatters in the wind. The moths settle again, polite and unhurried.

choices.text: Return the vial to the stone

effects.log: Some patience belongs to the stone.

events.text: {npc} carries the seed of flame to the Edge, and the Warden's Lamp is lit again, small and steady. Skiff-pilots call it the Moth Light. The moths hover about it on summer nights.
events.arc: The Night of the Star-Moths

choices.text: Keep the Lamp with {npc} for a season

effects.log: It never goes out while you are there. It does not need you after.

choices.text: Tell the Ministry of Precedence about the Lamp

effects.log: A plaque is placed. The Lamp is made official, and a little less magical.

events.text: {npc} gives you the notebook when {he} leaves for the last long watch. "The old sky is in there," {he} says. "Look at it when yours gets crowded."
events.arc: The Night of the Star-Moths

choices.text: Keep the notebook and study it for decades

effects.log: The old sky is more orderly than the new. You draw comfort from it.

choices.text: Give the notebook to the Star Sea Pavilion

effects.log: They shelve it with a plaque. A new generation reads it.

events.text: {npc} is the only caretaker of the ruined fortress of the Seven Gates. {He} sweeps the same flagstones every day, though no one has walked them in nine centuries. "The last banner is still up," {he} says. "I cannot reach it. Can you?"
events.arc: The Last Banner of the Seven Gates

choices.text: Climb the broken tower for the banner

effects.log: The stone crumbles under your fingers. You reach the top with torn sleeves.

choices.text: Ask what the banner means

effects.log: {He} tells of a regiment that held the seventh gate for forty days against ten thousand. The banner bears their name.

choices.text: Offer to sweep with {him}

effects.log: {He} lets you take one broom. By evening you are friends.

events.text: The banner is silk, faded to the colour of old tea, still in its frame. A dried flower is pressed in its fold. Nine hundred years and it is still tied with a soldier's knot, tight as the day it was set.
events.arc: The Last Banner of the Seven Gates

choices.text: Bring it down gently and show {npc}

effects.log: {He} holds it with both hands and bows to it, three times, in silence.

choices.text: Leave it where it is and say a word to it

effects.log: You bow. The wind lifts it for a moment, as if returning the courtesy.

choices.text: Untie the knot

effects.log: The banner falls, and the whole fortress feels, for a moment, lighter.

events.text: A band of treasure-hunters arrives in two skiffs. They have maps. They have crowbars. They want the banner's silk (spirit-silk, it seems) and the old gate-stones. {npc} stands in front of the gate with {his} broom.
events.arc: The Last Banner of the Seven Gates

choices.text: Talk the hunters out of it

ok.log: You offer a deal: they may study the walls, but touch nothing. They grumble and agree, cheered by a flask of cloud-wine.

fail.log: The hunters push past. {npc} stands {his} ground, and in the end they tire and go, taking only a few stones.

choices.text: Stand beside {npc} with your own broom

effects.log: The hunters look from one broom to another and decide, with a curse, it is not worth it.

choices.text: Step aside and let the hunters work

effects.log: They take stones. The wall sighs, quietly.

events.text: The caretaker's broom wears out at last, and {npc} gives you the handle. "The fortress will want someone," {he} says. "It does not much mind who."
events.arc: The Last Banner of the Seven Gates

choices.text: Take the handle and keep sweeping

effects.log: The flagstones are cleaner every year. The fortress seems to approve.

choices.text: Raise a small shrine to the regiment at the gate

effects.log: Pilgrims arrive, a few at a time, and leave flowers.

events.text: The fortress holds a small festival on the anniversary of the siege: the caretaker rings a bell forty times, once for each day. You are the only guest. The bell is a gift, and it sounds like the sea.
events.arc: The Last Banner of the Seven Gates

choices.text: Count the strokes with {npc}

effects.log: At forty, {he} bows. You bow. The wind carries the last note over the clouds.

choices.text: Add a forty-first stroke for the caretaker

effects.log: {He} is silent, then wipes {his} eyes and nods.

events.text: {npc} needs a second hand for a cargo run to the Eastern Isles: forty days by skiff, a hold of cloud-silk, a rival who wants the cargo, and a storm season coming. "I cannot pay," {he} says. "But the route is a secret worth having."
events.arc: The Long Haul to the Eastern Isles

choices.text: Sign on as second hand

effects.log: You take the lee oar. {npc} teaches you the crossing-songs: wind, current, star.

choices.text: Ask to see the route first

effects.log: {He} unrolls a map of cloud-reefs and wind-lanes. The secret is a pass between two storm-pillars.

choices.text: Decline and wish {npc} well

effects.log: {He} nods. "Most do," {he} says, and goes aboard alone.

events.text: Twelve days out, a fog bank swallows the skiff. {npc} stands at the bow reading the air. "Left of the second star," {he} says. "Hold the line." You hold it. For hours the fog is blank, and then, like a curtain, it parts on a vast and moonlit cloud-plain.
events.arc: The Long Haul to the Eastern Isles

choices.text: Keep the heading and trust the pilot

effects.log: The plain is a spread of silver, utterly quiet. You cross it with a held breath.

choices.text: Log the heading for future runs

effects.log: You mark every star and turn. The log is useful, later, for a good many pilots.

choices.text: Stand beside {npc} and share {his} flask

effects.log: You trade stories of the worst storms you have each known.

events.text: A rival skiff shadows you at the storm-pillars, running dark. The rival's captain calls across the gap: "Share the pass or I will block it." {npc} grips the oar. The pass is narrow enough for one skiff at a time.
events.arc: The Long Haul to the Eastern Isles

choices.text: Race the rival to the pass

ok.log: You and {npc} pole like mad. The rival yields at the last moment, cursing, and you pass first.

fail.log: The rival takes the pass first. You follow in its wake, and lose a day.

choices.text: Offer to let the rival pass first, for a toll

effects.log: The rival is surprised, and pays two stones for the privilege. You both get through.

choices.text: Hold back and wait for the rival to go

effects.log: The delay costs a day. {npc} is not pleased but does not say so.

events.text: The Eastern Isles are small and bright and strange: round houses, kites on every roof, people who greet you with the word for "welcome back" though you have never been. {npc} grins. "It is the custom," {he} says. "Everyone is welcome back, even the first time."
events.arc: The Long Haul to the Eastern Isles

choices.text: Stay a season on the Eastern Isles

effects.log: You learn their kite-songs and a dozen recipes. When you leave, they say the word for "see you soon."

choices.text: Sell your share of the silk and travel on

effects.log: The silk fetches a fine price. You carry the memory of the crossing for the rest of your life.

events.text: You and {npc} chart the route in full, and it becomes the Secret Pass: a lane that trade-skiffs use for centuries. A small plaque at the storm-pillars reads: "By two, for all."
events.arc: The Long Haul to the Eastern Isles

choices.text: Share the chart freely

effects.log: The pass is crowded with skiffs within a decade. The plaque is polished by passing hands.

choices.text: Keep the chart between you two

effects.log: The pass stays quiet. It is yours alone, and the Eastern Isles send a basket of plums every year.

events.text: {npc} is a hermit whose isle is too large for one. {He} has put out a sign: "Spare room for a rogue, one year. Rent is conversation." You have been turned from seven doors this season.
events.arc: A Year on a Borrowed Isle

choices.text: Knock and accept the year

effects.log: {He} leads you through a gate in a bamboo hedge to a room with a window onto the whole sea of cloud.

choices.text: Ask what kind of conversation

effects.log: {He} says {he} has run out of arguments with {him}self, and would like a fresh set.

choices.text: Thank {him} but decline

effects.log: The pride of the rogue. You walk on in the rain.

events.text: The conversation is mainly about whether peaches are better fresh or pickled. It goes on for three months. You have learned to hold a position, lose gracefully, and make tea during pauses.
events.arc: A Year on a Borrowed Isle

choices.text: Argue the pickled side with fervour

effects.log: You win one point in a hundred. {npc} is delighted.

choices.text: Switch sides each week

effects.log: {He} catches on in the fourth week and laughs till {he} cries.

choices.text: Ask {him} about {his} years alone

effects.log: {He} tells you of a lost friend, a quarrel, a long silence. You listen for a night.

events.text: A sect envoy arrives with a seal and a smile: the isle belongs to a clan that has not paid its fees, and the "unaffiliated lodger" must go. {npc} sits very still. The envoy does not meet your eye.
events.arc: A Year on a Borrowed Isle

choices.text: Argue that you are a guest, not a lodger

ok.log: The envoy, flustered by the distinction, retreats to consult a rulebook. {npc} thanks you with tea and a rice cake.

fail.log: The envoy is not moved. {npc} pays the fee in full, three stones, and says nothing.

choices.text: Leave quietly to spare {npc} trouble

effects.log: You gather your pack. {He} hands you the bamboo flute. "Come back for the argument," {he} says.

choices.text: Stay out of it and let {npc} handle the envoy

effects.log: {He} handles it. You are ashamed, a little.

events.text: At the year's end {npc} writes you a letter of recommendation: "This rogue is a better guest than most of my kin." {He} affixes a seal of three peaches. It is not an official seal, but it opens doors.
events.arc: A Year on a Borrowed Isle

choices.text: Carry the letter for the rest of your drifting life

effects.log: Eleven doors open that would not otherwise. You leave the letter, folded small, with each host.

choices.text: Stay a second year

effects.log: The argument is still going. You are winning, two points in a hundred.

events.text: {npc} dies in the second spring, in {his} chair, mid-sentence. The isle goes to a cousin who tolerates you for one week, then sends you off kindly. You take the flute and a jar of pickled peaches.
events.arc: A Year on a Borrowed Isle

choices.text: Play the flute at the isle's edge once a year

effects.log: The tune is a hymn to a very long argument. Peaches grow on the isle in your honour.

choices.text: Pickle your own peaches and send them to the cousin

effects.log: The cousin writes back: "Hwang would have disputed the brine."

events.text: A young sky whale is tangled in a silver drift-net off the Seventh Reef. The net is a poachers' trap, cast to catch it alive and sell it to a menagerie. It thrashes and sings in distress, a thin high sound.
events.arc: The Calf in the Silver Net

choices.text: Cut the net at the knots from above

effects.log: You work along the rope, slowly, with a knife. The whale calms as you reach it.

choices.text: Sing to the whale to calm it

effects.log: The whale answers, and the thrashing eases to shivers.

choices.text: Signal the reef-wardens

effects.log: Two skiffs come at dusk, too late to help.

events.text: The whale is free in a surge. It circles you once, a great grey hill of grateful, then dives. The poachers' skiff comes out of the mist, three men with grapnels. They want what they lost.
events.arc: The Calf in the Silver Net

choices.text: Face them down from your skiff

ok.log: You block the grapnels with your own hooks, and the poachers decide it is not their day.

fail.log: The grapnels snag your skiff. You tear free with a cost in rope and bruises.

choices.text: Lead the poachers on a false chase

effects.log: You run for the reef-wardens' mooring with the poachers behind you. The wardens take them in.

choices.text: Retreat and let the poachers go

effects.log: They find another whale. You sit with that for a long time.

events.text: The whale-calf returns to your skiff the next dawn, and presses its great flank against the hull in a clumsy hug. It carries something in its mouth: a lump of grey amber, glowing faintly.
events.arc: The Calf in the Silver Net

choices.text: Accept the amber with thanks

effects.log: It is whale-amber, rare and fragrant. Even a pinch calms a restless room.

choices.text: Refuse and pat the whale

effects.log: It sighs and drops the amber into the sea. A mist of scent rises around you.

events.text: Years later a whale the size of a hill drifts beside your skiff and sings a single note: the song of the net, now a song of thanks. The whole sea seems to listen.
events.arc: The Calf in the Silver Net

choices.text: Sing the thanks back with a lantern raised

effects.log: The note rolls out over the cloud-sea. A hundred whales answer.

choices.text: Listen in stillness and let it pass

effects.log: The whale lingers, then dives. The sea is calm for a week.

events.text: In the Hall of Echoes, the clock tolls twelve times at noon and thirteen at midnight. {npc}, a clerk of the Ministry of Hours, is baffled. "There is an hour in this Hall that no one has lived," {he} says, "and it is somewhere in the walls."
events.arc: The Hour That Went Missing

choices.text: Listen at the walls at the thirteenth stroke

effects.log: A faint chime from the north wall, a half-tone off. {npc} marks it with chalk.

choices.text: Search the clerk's old logbooks

effects.log: The log has a blank page in it, dated the day the clock was installed.

choices.text: Wish {npc} luck

effects.log: {He} sighs and goes back to {his} ledgers, undaunted.

events.text: Behind the north wall is a narrow gallery with one chair, one desk, and one candle that burns without melting. On the desk lies a diary in a small neat hand: "The hour I am keeping for you."
events.arc: The Hour That Went Missing

choices.text: Read the diary

effects.log: The first page reads: "If you find this, you were looking for time. There is no more of it than anyone else has."

choices.text: Sit in the chair and wait

effects.log: The candle brightens. The clock tolls, and for one long moment the world holds still.

choices.text: Fetch {npc} to see it

effects.log: {He} reads the first page, then the second, and weeps softly.

events.text: The diary names a clerk, long dead, who stole an hour each year for forty years and hid them here, one by one, to give to the hurried. "Whoever needs an hour may take one," the last entry says. "Please return it when you are done."
events.arc: The Hour That Went Missing

choices.text: Take one of the hours

effects.log: You step out and the afternoon is slow and generous for a day. You finish three things you had given up on.

choices.text: Add an hour of your own to the stash

effects.log: You sit in the chair and give an hour of your life. The candle brightens.

choices.text: Close the gallery and say nothing

effects.log: It is a private thing. You respect it.

events.text: {npc} files an official report: "One hour (misplaced), now located." The Ministry confiscates the gallery. You find, by the next noon, the clock tolls twelve, and the hour is gone.
events.arc: The Hour That Went Missing

choices.text: Quietly open a second gallery in the archive wall

effects.log: It takes a year. The gift of the hour continues, in a different wall, anonymous.

choices.text: Visit the chair one last time and thank it

effects.log: The empty chair seems to straighten. You feel, absurdly, forgiven.

events.text: The hour you left grows in the dark. A year on, the gallery has a second chair, and the diary has new pages written in a hand not yours but kin to it.
events.arc: The Hour That Went Missing

choices.text: Read the new pages

effects.log: They describe a clerk who found the gallery and added an hour of their own. The story goes on.

choices.text: Leave the new pages unread

effects.log: You respect the privacy of an unfolding thing.

events.text: You bought a wind in a bottle at the cloud-bridge, cheap, and it will not stay quiet. It rattles the cork, whispers at night, and on the third day sulks. You realise the wind has opinions about where it wants to go.
events.arc: The Wind That Wanted Out

choices.text: Ask the wind where it wants to go

effects.log: It whispers a name: a cove on the southern edge, where it was bottled forty years ago.

choices.text: Open the bottle on a hilltop

effects.log: It swirls out in a delighted spiral and is gone in a heartbeat.

choices.text: Keep the bottle on a shelf

effects.log: The rattling continues. The wind sulks all winter.

events.text: You carry the bottle south in your cloak, and it hums as the miles pass. At a rocky cove on the southern edge, the wind pushes against the cork so hard it nearly pops. A faded sign reads "Wind-catchers' Rest".
events.arc: The Wind That Wanted Out

choices.text: Uncork the bottle in the cove

effects.log: The wind pours out and rushes about the cove, whistling. It sets the old wind-chimes ringing, a hundred small bronze voices.

choices.text: Look for a wind-catcher to ask first

effects.log: You find an old hand mending nets. "It belongs to the cove," they say. "Let it go."

choices.text: Carry the bottle farther south

effects.log: The wind sulks again, and the cork nearly pops.

events.text: The wind swirls out of the bottle into the chimes and then something unexpected happens: another wind answers, from the sea, a deeper voice. They twine together over the cove. The old wind-catcher says, "That is the one it has been missing."
events.arc: The Wind That Wanted Out

choices.text: Stand quietly and watch the winds reunite

effects.log: They play together till dusk, and the chimes ring in two voices. You are glad.

choices.text: Offer the bottle to the wind-catcher as a keepsake

effects.log: It is hung in the net-shed as a charm. Sailors visit to tap it for luck.

events.text: The bottle you carry is lighter now, empty. A tiny gust still slips out, sometimes, when you open it, a fond whisper. It smells of salt and seasons.
events.arc: The Wind That Wanted Out

choices.text: Keep the bottle as a memento

effects.log: On bad days the empty bottle sings a small thank-you.

choices.text: Hang the bottle in your window

effects.log: The wind returns on summer evenings and rattles the glass, a fond old guest.

events.text: The Demon Realm keeps a pass hidden in a storm-wall at its border, used by traders, runaways and the occasional lovers. {npc} guards it with a lantern and no sword. "It is not a secret," {he} says. "It is a courtesy."
events.arc: The Pass That Is Not on Any Map

choices.text: Offer to walk the pass with {npc}

effects.log: The path is a slit in the storm, twisting. You emerge on a quiet slope, your hair full of lightning.

choices.text: Ask about the pass's rules

effects.log: No weapons drawn. No names asked. Tea offered at both ends.

choices.text: Report nothing and pass by

effects.log: {He} smiles and says nothing. You are both content.

events.text: Three runaways arrive at the pass, thin and frightened, with the Ministry's hounds not an hour behind. {npc} looks at them, then at you, then at the pass. "I would rather not choose alone," {he} says.
events.arc: The Pass That Is Not on Any Map

choices.text: Hide the runaways in the storm-wall

effects.log: You and {npc} hold the lanterns low while the hounds pass. The runaways sleep three days in a hollow.

choices.text: Send them through to the far side

effects.log: They cross, trembling, and find a Demon Realm tea-house waiting on the slope.

choices.text: Lock the pass and send them back

effects.log: They go, silent. {npc} looks away. You do not feel clean.

events.text: A Ministry envoy arrives, demanding the pass be "regularised": a toll, a register, a gate. {npc} reads the paper and folds it very small. "It was a courtesy," {he} says. "It will be a prison."
events.arc: The Pass That Is Not on Any Map

choices.text: Argue the pass is a natural feature

ok.log: The envoy, defeated by the argument, departs to petition for a survey that will take twenty years.

fail.log: The envoy is not swayed, and the pass gets a gate. {npc} keeps the key for a while longer.

choices.text: Quietly open a second, unmarked pass

effects.log: It takes a season. Rhee tells no one. The new pass is a crack in a cliff, six paces long.

choices.text: Let the Ministry have its gate

effects.log: The pass becomes a prison with a nice sign.

events.text: The runaways come back, years later, with a tea-set and a small flag. They have a house on the slope. {npc} pours the tea. "A courtesy returned," {he} says.
events.arc: The Pass That Is Not on Any Map

choices.text: Sit at the tea-table with them

effects.log: The tea is strong, the stories long. You are the oldest friend of the pass.

choices.text: Carry a letter of thanks to the Demon Realm court

effects.log: It is received with ceremony. A seat at the pass is named after you.

events.text: A crater of black glass lies in the heart of a plateau, smooth as a mirror. Where a star fell, the ground melted and set. It reflects the sky so perfectly that skiff-pilots sometimes try to land on it, and land on air.

choices.text: Walk the rim and study the glass

effects.log: Under the surface, fine silver threads run in spirals. You trace one to its end, hours later.

choices.text: Skim a pebble across it

effects.log: It skates for a quarter mile in silence, then dips into the reflected sky and is gone.

events.text: A sword stands upright in a pillar of solid cloud, up to the hilt, left from the war of the immortals. A tradition says anyone who can draw it may keep it. Hundreds have tried. A cheerful old attendant sells tea beside it.

choices.text: Try to draw the sword

effects.log: It does not budge. The attendant gives you a free cup of tea for effort.

choices.text: Ask the attendant who last drew it

effects.log: "No one," says the attendant. "I keep it for the look on their faces." You laugh till you wheeze.

events.text: A cellar beneath an isle holds a perpetual snowfall: flakes drifting up from the floor, catching on the ceiling in white drifts. The warden says it is the memory of a winter that happened once, a thousand years ago. It plays every day, for visitors.

choices.text: Stand in the snow and breathe

effects.log: You feel a cold that is not cold. You leave refreshed.

choices.text: Make a small snowman of the memory

effects.log: It melts into a soft light. The warden approves.

events.text: A fog ox grazes on the open cloud-plain, grey and huge, with a bell at its neck that rings only when it is content. It is rare to hear the bell. Tonight, it rings.

choices.text: Sit near the ox and listen

effects.log: The bell is a clear single note. You feel as if you were being forgiven for something.

choices.text: Offer it a handful of cloud-clover

effects.log: It takes it with a slow tongue. The bell rings twice.

events.text: A dock at the end of nowhere, with a single skiff tied to it and a lamp lit in the window of a hut. A sign says "Back soon." The ink has faded to ghost-grey, and the skiff has grown a coat of moss.

choices.text: Wait an hour in the hut for the owner

effects.log: No one comes. You make a pot of tea and leave coins by the kettle.

choices.text: Untie the moss-skiff and give it a sail

effects.log: It rides like a dream. You return it before dusk, with the moss trimmed.

events.text: A cliff on the Edge of Heaven repeats what you say with a gap of one year. A shout today will answer you next spring. A local custom is to say something kind to your future self.

choices.text: Say something kind to your future self

effects.log: Next spring, a faint voice tells you the same thing. You laugh and cry together.

choices.text: Ask a question and wait a year

effects.log: The answer, when it comes, is "I do not know." You find this oddly comforting.

events.text: At dusk the cloud-sea reflects a harbour that is not there: masts, lanterns, tiny crowds. It fades at the first star. Old sailors tip their hats to it. They say it is the harbour of those who sailed too far.

choices.text: Tip your hat to the vanished harbour

effects.log: A lantern in the reflection dips, once, in answer.

choices.text: Row toward the reflection until it fades

effects.log: It dissolves as you approach. You sail home under the first stars.

events.text: In the lull after a great storm, the lightning-sprites hold a festival on the highest cloud, tiny sparks dancing in rings. Anyone who stands very still may be invited to join. Nobody has been, in living memory.

choices.text: Stand still and see if they notice

effects.log: A sprite lands on your finger, considers you, and leaves with a flick. You were almost invited.

choices.text: Offer a spark of your own qi

effects.log: The sprites spin in delight, and three of them hitch a ride on your sleeve for the day.

events.text: You find a mist hound's paw-mark in the frost on a roof-tile: a perfect print, ringed with pale light. Mist hounds are shy. This one has been watching the roof for weeks, and has finally come close enough to leave a mark.

choices.text: Leave a bowl of grey fish by the chimney

effects.log: In the morning the bowl is clean, and a second paw-mark rests beside it.

choices.text: Sit up all night to watch for it

effects.log: It does not come. You fall asleep in the cold. At dawn, a paw-mark on your sleeve.

events.text: An ancient road crosses the cloud-sea on piers of cloud-stone, mossed over, wider than any modern lane. It leads from nowhere to nowhere. Skiffs cross beneath it. Occasionally a pilgrim walks along the top, whistling.

choices.text: Walk the road to its far end

effects.log: It takes a day. At the end there is a bench, a view, and a note: "The point was the walking."

choices.text: Sit under the arches and watch skiffs pass

effects.log: You nod to every pilot, and they nod back. A good afternoon.

events.text: A tiny isle no bigger than a table drifts past with a single apple tree on it, a chair, and an old person asleep beneath. The apples are ripe. The sleeper snores gently. A sign hangs from the branch: "Help yourself, but please do not wake me."

choices.text: Take one apple and leave a coin

effects.log: It is the sweetest apple you have ever eaten. The sleeper smiles in their sleep.

choices.text: Sit quietly beside the sleeper for a while

effects.log: The isle drifts on. You step off before it leaves the lane.

events.text: A cold spring wells up in the middle of a bare field of cloud-stone, so clear that the water seems not there. A single cup hangs on a chain. Those who drink report, variously, a memory, a taste of rain, or the sudden ability to whistle.

choices.text: Drink one cup

effects.log: It tastes of a summer afternoon you cannot place. It lingers all day.

choices.text: Fill a flask to take home

effects.log: The water loses its magic in the flask, but you keep it for the walk itself.

events.text: In the long noon, when the sun stands still for a week, the isles go quiet. No wind, no cloud, no shadow. People sit outdoors and say little. A few swear they can hear the sun thinking.

choices.text: Sit in the stillness and listen

effects.log: You hear a vast low murmur that might be the sun or might be your own blood. You do not decide.

choices.text: Make a week of small repairs

effects.log: The roof, the fence, the lantern. You finish before the noon ends and feel lightly proud.

events.text: On the dark side of a hanging isle, moon-moss grows in silver mats, soft as a cat. It is harvested once a year by moonlight, by people with quiet hands. The moss mends cuts and quiets nightmares. The harvesters hum while they work.

choices.text: Join the harvest and hum along

effects.log: Your hands learn the grip. You come away with a pouch of silver moss and a good sleep.

choices.text: Gather by yourself, a little, without a hum

effects.log: The moss is wary. You collect less, and learn to hum.

events.text: At the Edge of Heaven, the sunrise comes up from below. A line of light on the horizon, a slow bloom of gold under the cloud-sea. Early risers sit with their knees pulled up. Some bring flasks of tea. Nobody speaks until the sun clears the rim.

choices.text: Sit through the sunrise in silence

effects.log: The light changes you in some small way. You come away humbler, and hungry.

choices.text: Share your flask with the person beside you

effects.log: They accept with a bow. You exchange not one word. It is a good friendship.

events.text: A stall at the cloud-market sells starlight in jars: pale, cold, a little sad. The stallholder says each jar was caught from a different night. "This one is the night before a war. This one, a child's first snow."

choices.text: Listen to each jar and choose none

effects.log: You borrow an hour from each. The stallholder lets you.

choices.text: Ask the price of that first snow

effects.log: Two stones, says the stallholder, or a good memory. You give the memory.

events.text: A herald at a cloud-court calls out the guest list and reaches the end: "...and those without a seal, by the side door." A few rogues file in, cheerful and wary. The best tea is, as always, at the side door.

choices.text: Take the side door and the good tea

effects.log: The side-door crowd is the best company in the building.

choices.text: Stand at the main door and ask the herald why

effects.log: The herald says "the custom". You say "the custom is wrong". They write it down. Nothing changes, yet.

events.text: A cook on a hanging inn takes pity on the unaffiliated. A rogue's supper is half price, a bowl of broth, a plate of bread. They ask nothing. The soup is, in truth, better than the regulars'.

choices.text: Eat the supper and thank the cook

effects.log: They wave a ladle. "The sky feeds all," they say.

choices.text: Leave an extra stone under the bowl

effects.log: The cook finds it and says nothing, but the next supper has an egg.

events.text: A hermit on a bamboo-isle carves flutes from fallen canes and gives them away to anyone who can play one note true. You try. The note is flat. The hermit hands you a flute anyway: "For the second note."

choices.text: Keep the flute and practise

effects.log: A year later, you play the second note, true. The hermit sends you a plum.

choices.text: Play the flat note again, more flatly

effects.log: The hermit laughs aloud. "That is the first honest note anyone has played in a decade."

events.text: On the Third Cloud-Reef, {npc} keeps a lamp that has not gone out in two thousand years. Wrecks lie round the reef like sleeping animals. "I am old," {he} says, "and the oil is low. If I stop, someone will drown. Will you carry oil?"
events.arc: The Keeper of the Reef Light

choices.text: Carry oil up the long stair, once a week

effects.log: The stair is eight hundred steps. By the third month you know every one by name.

choices.text: Ask what the lamp burns

effects.log: "Memories," {he} says. "Mostly lost ones. Pilots leave them in the oil-pot when they pass."

choices.text: Tell {npc} to leave the reef

effects.log: {He} laughs. "Where would I go? The reef is who I am."

events.text: A skiff comes in on the storm tide with its mast broken and a lantern swinging. The lamp flares, and the pilot steers by it between the wrecks. But the skiff is not alone: a sky-whale follows it, huge, wounded, wanting the light.
events.arc: The Keeper of the Reef Light

choices.text: Guide the whale away from the wrecks by lantern

effects.log: You swing the lantern slowly. The whale turns, vast and trusting, and finds the deep channel.

choices.text: Tend the pilot, wet and shaking

effects.log: You get them tea and dry clothes. The pilot sobs. It was their first storm alone.

choices.text: Keep the lamp bright and wait it out

effects.log: Dawn comes. Both pilot and whale survive. You do not know how.

events.text: {npc} falls ill in the winter. The stair defeats {him}. {He} lies by the lamp, grey and quiet, and says: "Light it for me till spring." You carry the oil, climb the stair, light the lamp, and sit with {him} while it burns.
events.arc: The Keeper of the Reef Light

choices.text: Sit by {npc} through the winter nights

effects.log: {He} tells you the story of each wreck. By spring {he} can stand, and the lamp has never been brighter.

choices.text: Brew a restorative from reef-kelp

ok.log: The kelp tea warms {him} to the bones. By the thaw {he} is cursing the stair again.

fail.log: The tea is weak. {He} lingers, and you keep the lamp lit on your own.

choices.text: Light the lamp and leave it to burn

effects.log: {He} lives. {He} is a little grumpy about being fussed over.

events.text: {npc} hands you the lamp-key on a spring morning. "You do not need to be old to keep a light," {he} says. "Only to be steady."
events.arc: The Keeper of the Reef Light

choices.text: Take the key and keep the reef light

effects.log: You live on the reef for centuries. Pilots remember your face, and your lamp.

choices.text: Take the key but hire a young keeper

effects.log: The reef has a new family on it, and a rota. The lamp burns brighter for being shared.

events.text: The pilot you tended returns a decade later with a fleet of skiffs and a gift of oil. "We have found a better wick," they say. The lamp blazes white. {npc} cries a little, which is unlike {him}.
events.arc: The Keeper of the Reef Light

choices.text: Accept the oil and the friendship

effects.log: The pilot and their crew sail the reef route for centuries, and always dip a flag as they pass.

choices.text: Share the oil with every keeper on the coast

effects.log: Within a year there are forty bright lamps where there were nine.

events.text: Prospectors say a vein of star-iron runs through the Whispering Cliff, rich enough to buy an isle. The cliff, which is said to whisper, has swallowed three digging crews. A fourth is forming, and wants a climber.
events.arc: The Vein in the Whispering Cliff

choices.text: Join the crew as climber

effects.log: You rope up at the cliff's foot. The whispers begin at the first ledge, soft and friendly.

choices.text: Study the whispering first

effects.log: You listen at the base for a day. The whispers are lullabies, in a language of stone.

choices.text: Wish them luck and sit it out

effects.log: The crew goes. You watch them from the foot, uneasy.

events.text: At the third ledge the whispers sharpen into words: "Stay. Rest. Sleep." The crew begins to slow, then to sit. Their eyes close. A crew-mate is already dozing in the sunlight, a smile on their face. The cliff does not mean harm. It wants company.
events.arc: The Vein in the Whispering Cliff

choices.text: Shout the crew awake and drag them down

ok.log: You haul them down one by one. They wake in the valley rubbing their eyes, sheepish and alive.

fail.log: You get most of them out, but one remains asleep on the ledge, smiling.

choices.text: Sing a lullaby of your own to the cliff

effects.log: The cliff pauses, listens, and answers softly. The crew wakes, one by one, rested.

choices.text: Leave the crew and climb down alone

effects.log: You do. You are ashamed and unharmed.

events.text: The cliff accepts your lullaby. The whispers settle, almost purring. Somewhere in its flank a vein of silver runs, a hundred paces long, and the cliff seems to say: "Take what you need. Leave the rest. I am lonely."
events.arc: The Vein in the Whispering Cliff

choices.text: Take a small portion and leave a lullaby behind

effects.log: You mine a handful. The cliff hums for a decade.

choices.text: Take none and visit regularly

effects.log: You climb the cliff once a year and sing. The cliff grows mossy and happy.

choices.text: Tell the prospectors how to mine safely

effects.log: They agree to leave the cliff a lullaby for each ton taken.

events.text: The prospectors return in force with a Ministry permit, a tower, and no lullaby. The whispers go silent, then angry. Rocks tumble. The cliff will crush them.
events.arc: The Vein in the Whispering Cliff

choices.text: Stand at the cliff's foot and sing the old lullaby

effects.log: The rocks pause. The prospectors scatter. The cliff relents, grumbling.

choices.text: Persuade the prospectors to withdraw

effects.log: It takes a week of tea and arithmetic. They concede the vein is not worth the cliff.

events.text: The silver you took is a modest fortune. The cliff sends you a sprig of cloud-ivy each spring, a tiny green hand. You plant it on your porch.
events.arc: The Vein in the Whispering Cliff

choices.text: Raise the ivy and visit the cliff yearly

effects.log: The ivy grows into a curtain. The cliff, you suspect, is pleased.

choices.text: Spend the stones on a library for the nearest isle

effects.log: The library hums in the night, with a faint stone whisper.

events.text: The dawn stag crosses the Golden Shelf once a decade, antlers like branches of lit amber. {npc} has hunted the Shelf for sixty years and never seen it. "Not to shoot," {he} says. "To see. Hold my bow."
events.arc: The Dawn Stag Once a Decade

choices.text: Keep watch with {npc} at the Shelf

effects.log: You and {npc} sit in the cold with a thermos of cloud-tea. The stars fade. A thin light brightens.

choices.text: Carry the bow and ask for the stories

effects.log: {He} tells you of hunts that ended in tea, and of one that ended in a wedding.

choices.text: Wish {npc} luck and go home

effects.log: {He} chuckles. "Most do," {he} says.

events.text: The stag steps onto the Shelf at first light. It is the size of a house, the colour of dawn, and it looks at you with quiet pity. Behind it, a hunting party in ceremonial red: a Ministry hunt, a dozen nobles, thirty hounds.
events.arc: The Dawn Stag Once a Decade

choices.text: Step between the party and the stag

effects.log: You raise a hand. The nobles, startled, hesitate. The stag steps behind you like a courteous guest.

choices.text: Distract the hounds with a scent-trail

ok.log: You lay a false trail across the Shelf. The hounds follow it, baying, and the stag melts into the dawn.

fail.log: The hounds ignore the trail. The stag turns away, and the nobles lose their nerve.

choices.text: Let the hunt proceed; it is none of your business

effects.log: The stag is not caught. You do not know whether you helped.

events.text: The nobles retreat, grumbling. {npc} weeps openly. The stag lowers its head and lets {him} touch its antler, once. The amber is warm and faintly alive.
events.arc: The Dawn Stag Once a Decade

choices.text: Bow to the stag with {npc}

effects.log: It dips its head. The dawn brightens. It crosses the Shelf and is gone.

choices.text: Sketch the stag from memory

effects.log: The sketch hangs in the Ministry of Beasts for a century. The stag is never hunted again.

events.text: A decade later you cross the Golden Shelf at dawn with {npc}'s bow in your hand, unstrung. The stag steps from the mist and stops a pace away. It does not flee.
events.arc: The Dawn Stag Once a Decade

choices.text: Offer it a bowl of cloud-oats

effects.log: It eats from your palm, warm-breathed and vast. Antler-light falls over your hands.

choices.text: Stand still and let it pass

effects.log: It walks round you, once, in a slow circle, and goes. You feel blessed beyond words.

events.text: Skiff-pilots tell of a child on a drifting reef, thin and bright-eyed, who waves at passing sails. They think it is a ghost. {npc}, a heaven-born child of eight, says they are lost, and the reef has been drifting for a season. "I am not afraid," {he} says. "I am hungry."
events.arc: The Child on the Drifting Reef

choices.text: Feed {npc} and take {him} aboard

effects.log: You share your bread, your blanket, your name. {He} falls asleep in an hour.

choices.text: Ask where {he} came from

effects.log: "A small isle that drifted off," {he} says. "My mother said to wait at the reef. They said they would send a kite."

choices.text: Signal a ferry and wait with {him}

effects.log: The ferry comes in a day. {He} is bundled in a coat three sizes too large.

events.text: You search the lanes for the lost isle. The child tells you its marks: one willow, one bell, a flag with a blue crane. You follow rumour from isle to isle, a week at a time, with {npc} on your shoulder pointing at every cloud.
events.arc: The Child on the Drifting Reef

choices.text: Ask every ferryman along the route

effects.log: The ferrymen are patient. By the fifth isle someone remembers a willow-isle and a bell.

choices.text: Fly a kite with the crane flag

effects.log: You paint the kite with the child's help. It rises, and far off a kite answers.

choices.text: Wait at the nearest port

effects.log: You wait a month. The child draws pictures of home in the margins of your logbook.

events.text: The willow-isle is a tiny speck in a storm-wall, its bell ringing in the gale. A woman on its edge is waving a cloth with both arms. The storm is closing. You have minutes to cross the gap.
events.arc: The Child on the Drifting Reef

choices.text: Race the storm to the isle

ok.log: You make the crossing with the child in your arms. The mother catches you both at the rail, sobbing.

fail.log: The storm clips your skiff. You arrive soaked, bruised, but with the child safe.

choices.text: Signal the isle to come to you

effects.log: The mother pulls a rope and the isle slowly turns. You meet halfway, in a lull.

choices.text: Hold position and wait for the storm to pass

effects.log: The storm passes in an hour. The mother has not stopped waving.

events.text: Years pass. A kite lands on your porch one spring, a blue crane on its wing, with a message: "I grew up. Thank you." It is signed in a small clear hand. A feather is tied to the string.
events.arc: The Child on the Drifting Reef

choices.text: Keep the feather and write back

effects.log: You exchange letters for a hundred years. {npc} becomes a ferry-captain, and invites you aboard.

choices.text: Fly the kite to the crane-flag isle

effects.log: You arrive for the isle's festival. They put you at the head of the table.

events.text: A grotto in a quiet isle is sealed from within by a poet who vowed not to open the door until they wrote a perfect line. That was nine hundred years ago. Notes slide out through the crack at times: a line, an apology, a bad pun.
events.arc: The Poet Who Sealed the Door

choices.text: Slip a line of your own through the crack

effects.log: A reply arrives in a week: "Bad, but sincere. Try again."

choices.text: Read the notes pinned outside the door

effects.log: A thousand pinned slips, each a line. Some are brilliant. Some are laundry lists.

choices.text: Knock politely and leave

effects.log: No answer. You feel accompanied anyway.

events.text: Over years you trade lines with the poet. They teach you the rule of the silent beat, and the trick of the closing image. You teach them the weather outside. One day they write: "Describe the colour of morning to me. I have forgotten."
events.arc: The Poet Who Sealed the Door

choices.text: Describe the morning in a single image

effects.log: You write: "A cold bell in a warm hand." The answer comes back: "That is the line." The door trembles.

choices.text: Send a jar of dawn-air under the door

effects.log: A week later: "It is not the same, but it is something."

choices.text: Send nothing; the silence is part of the poem

effects.log: The poet writes: "Understood." Then nothing for a year.

events.text: The door opens a hand-width. Light spills out, amber and old. A voice, thin and happy: "It is not perfect. But it is true. I am coming out." The door swings slowly wide. Behind it sits a small, tidy figure with ink on their sleeves.
events.arc: The Poet Who Sealed the Door

choices.text: Welcome the poet to the morning

effects.log: They step into the sun with a hand over their eyes. "It is so big," they say.

choices.text: Ask to read the finished poem

effects.log: They hand you a single page. The poem is one line. You read it three times and cry.

events.text: The door stays shut, but the notes keep coming, year after year, a slow correspondence. The poet never comes out. The lines they send are the best you have ever read. You post them on the wall outside.
events.arc: The Poet Who Sealed the Door

choices.text: Publish the lines under the poet's seal

effects.log: Readers climb the isle to read them. The poet, within, writes faster.

choices.text: Keep the correspondence private

effects.log: It is the closest friendship of your life, conducted through a crack.

events.text: The Tea Road is a chain of skiffs, thirty strong, that ferries cloud-tea from the Eastern Terraces to the western isles, a three-month trip. {npc} leads it and needs a guard who can also pour tea. "Pay is poor," {he} says. "Tea is excellent."
events.arc: The Tea Road of the Cloud-Skiffs

choices.text: Sign on as guard-and-pourer

effects.log: You wear the caravan's grey cloak. By the first week you know every crew by name and their favourite blend.

choices.text: Ask about the dangers of the road

effects.log: "Fog-hounds, tax-barges, boredom," says {npc}. "Boredom is the worst."

choices.text: Wish the caravan luck from the dock

effects.log: It sails with a long string of lanterns. You watch till it is out of sight.

events.text: A tax-barge of the Ministry hails the caravan at the Toll Isles and demands a levy of one chest in ten. {npc} does not argue. {He} sits down, pours tea, and offers the officer a cup. The officer takes it, to everyone's surprise.
events.arc: The Tea Road of the Cloud-Skiffs

choices.text: Serve the officer your best cup

effects.log: The tea is perfect. The officer closes the ledger, sighs, and waves the caravan on. "Never mind the levy."

choices.text: Dispute the levy by the Ministry's own rules

ok.log: You cite the clause on perishable goods. The officer, scowling, reduces the levy to a token.

fail.log: The levy stands, in full. {npc} pays, with a tight smile.

choices.text: Stay out of it

effects.log: {npc} manages. The officer drinks their tea and signs the pass.

events.text: A fog bank swallows the caravan on the sixtieth night. Skiffs lose touch with each other. In the white, a faint tinkling: the bell-lines {npc} strung from skiff to skiff. A single string is slack, and the last skiff is adrift.
events.arc: The Tea Road of the Cloud-Skiffs

choices.text: Take a rope and row to the adrift skiff

effects.log: You find it by the bell, tow it back, and tie the lines. Thirty skiffs, whole again.

choices.text: Signal with the lamp and wait

effects.log: The skiff hears the signal and rows to you. It takes two hours. Nobody scolds.

events.text: At the western isles the caravan unloads in a flurry of lanterns, a hundred festive stalls. {npc} hands you a packet of the first brew. "You earned that," {he} says. "Come back next year. I shall have a seat."
events.arc: The Tea Road of the Cloud-Skiffs

choices.text: Return next year as a full member

effects.log: The caravan becomes your home on the water for a century. The tea never tastes the same twice.

choices.text: Sell the packet and buy a skiff of your own

effects.log: You start your own small caravan. It is a quiet success.

events.text: {npc} grows old on the road. At the fiftieth landing, {he} hands you the caravan's lead lantern. "It is a poor thing," {he} says. "It has led thirty skiffs through every fog in the sky."
events.arc: The Tea Road of the Cloud-Skiffs

choices.text: Take the lantern and lead the caravan

effects.log: You carry it for centuries. Crews remember {npc} when the lantern sways.

choices.text: Share the lead with the crews in rota

effects.log: Every crew carries the lantern a season. The caravan flourishes.

events.text: A thunderhead belonging to the Ministry of Weather has slipped its moorings and is wandering the lanes, rumbling sadly. {npc}, the clerk responsible, is in disgrace. "It does not want to be a storm," {he} says. "It wants to be a rain. Help me find it?"
events.arc: The Storm That Got Lost

choices.text: Take a skiff and follow the rumbling

effects.log: The storm is easy to follow by ear, hard to follow by sight. It sulks in valleys.

choices.text: Check the Ministry's weather-log for habits

effects.log: The storm was once a gentle spring rain. It was promoted without asking.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the storm is the Ministry's problem

effects.log: {He} looks stricken. You feel a little mean.

events.text: You find the storm huddled in a ravine, sulking, black and trembling. It shrinks as you approach. A little rain falls, wanting to fall gently, and the thunder keeps interrupting. It sounds, oddly, like a sob.
events.arc: The Storm That Got Lost

choices.text: Sing a rain-song to the storm

effects.log: The thunder softens. The rain falls evenly for the first time in a century.

choices.text: Argue with the thunder

effects.log: It ignores you for an hour, then sheepishly goes quiet.

choices.text: Sit with the storm until it calms

effects.log: You sit for a day. It leans close, damp and warm.

events.text: The Ministry of Weather summons {npc} to a hearing. The storm is to be "reintegrated." You and {npc} stand before three senior officials. They are not interested in a rain-wish. They want a storm.
events.arc: The Storm That Got Lost

choices.text: Argue that a gentle rain is better for the farms below

ok.log: The officials, consulting charts, concede the point. The storm is reassigned to the Spring Rains department.

fail.log: The officials reject the argument. The storm is returned to the thunder desk, and {npc} is demoted.

choices.text: Smuggle the storm out under a tarp

effects.log: It rains on the officials' courtyard at dawn, gently, and then it is gone.

choices.text: Say nothing and watch

effects.log: {npc} fights alone. You are ashamed.

events.text: Years later a soft rain falls over the whole eastern isle in spring, so mild no one carries an umbrella. People stand in the open with faces upturned. {npc} watches from a window. "It got its wish," {he} says. "It is a rain at last."
events.arc: The Storm That Got Lost

choices.text: Stand in the rain with the others

effects.log: It soaks your coat, and you do not mind. A faint hum in the drops: a thank-you.

choices.text: Write the storm's story for the Ministry newsletter

effects.log: It runs on the front page. Three other clerks ask to be reassigned.

events.text: {npc}, an old rogue with a pack of folded paper, makes a living carrying letters from the world below to those above who cannot go back. "The ache is the same," {he} says. "A letter does not mind which way it travels." {He} needs a second pair of legs.
events.arc: Letters From the World Below

choices.text: Carry the second satchel

effects.log: The letters smell faintly of woodsmoke and rain. Each has a name on it you have never heard.

choices.text: Ask how the letters arrive

effects.log: "Through the rain," {he} says. "Every drop that falls above comes down below. Some carry words."

choices.text: Wish {npc} well and move on

effects.log: {He} nods. "A rogue knows the weight of home," {he} says, "better than most."

events.text: You deliver your first letter to an old immortal in a tower. It is from a grandchild: a spring flower pressed, a line about a new roof. The old one reads it three times, and says: "They are happy. That is enough." They put the flower in a cup of water.
events.arc: Letters From the World Below

choices.text: Offer to carry a reply down

effects.log: A rogue can take letters down with the rain, if the winds are right. You promise to try.

choices.text: Sit with the old one a while

effects.log: They tell of the granddaughter at five years old. It is the finest hour of the week.

choices.text: Leave the letter and go

effects.log: Some grief is private.

events.text: A letter in your satchel has no addressee and is sealed in black wax. Aunt Mirae goes pale when {he} sees it. "That is one of the unsent," {he} says. "From the war. A soldier wrote it for {his} own grave."
events.arc: Letters From the World Below

choices.text: Open it, with {npc}'s permission

effects.log: The letter is a farewell, kind and short. It ends: "Tell no one I was afraid." You tell no one.

choices.text: Take it down with the rain

effects.log: You hold it in the open air at dusk. A drop of rain takes it, soft as a hand.

events.text: Years on, {npc} gives you the satchel and the route. "I am done with the road," {he} says. "The letters will want someone with legs and a soft heart." The route is eighty isles long. You know every one.
events.arc: Letters From the World Below

choices.text: Carry the letters for the rest of your wandering

effects.log: You become the rogue-postman of the lanes. Doors open to you that never opened to others.

choices.text: Teach other rogues the route and step back

effects.log: There are twelve of you now. The letters never stop, and neither does the rain.

events.text: A single room floats in the cloud-sea, no isle under it: four walls, a floor, a table with a bowl of tangerines. The door stands open. A cat sleeps on the table. It is evidently a very old room. The tangerines are fresh.

choices.text: Eat a tangerine and thank the room

effects.log: The room hums, very faintly, in satisfaction. It sails on.

choices.text: Sit in the room and watch the clouds go by

effects.log: An hour passes. You step out onto a skiff you had not noticed being tied to the door.

events.text: A shed hangs from the underside of a drifting isle, hung with the huge pale scales that sky-whales shed once a century. Collectors prize them. The warden of the shed knows each by name and refuses to sell any. They are left to be looked at.

choices.text: Look at the scales and ask their names

effects.log: The warden tells you, one by one, of each whale. You leave humbled.

choices.text: Offer to polish the scales for a morning

effects.log: The warden says nothing, but leaves you a cup of tea at the door.

events.text: In a ruin, a stone oven still stands, with a trough of long-baked bread-crumb gone to dust. On the wall, a soldier's list of the week's meals in a neat hand, with annotations: "bad", "worse", "the cook is a poet."

choices.text: Read the whole list aloud

effects.log: The cook was, indeed, a poet. The last line reads: "Soup. Warm. Hope you are well."

choices.text: Light the oven and bake a loaf

effects.log: It takes a day. The bread is dreadful and you eat all of it, in honour.

events.text: A herd of cloud-goats grazes on the underside of a hanging isle, upside down, unconcerned. They are white as fog, bell-necked and rude. When you pass they all turn their heads at once and give you a long judging stare.

choices.text: Stare back until one of them blinks

effects.log: You win, after twenty minutes. The goat looks insulted. You feel absurdly proud.

choices.text: Offer salt and make friends

effects.log: The leader takes it with a slow tongue. Now you are on the list of those allowed.

events.text: Mist hounds leave no print, but they leave a hush. On a foggy morning you walk through a patch of silence, no louder than breath, and know one has just passed. The grass is faintly pale where it stepped.

choices.text: Follow the hush for an hour

effects.log: You lose it at a stream. The hush lingers in your ears for a day.

choices.text: Leave a piece of grey fish at the stream

effects.log: You hear nothing. In the morning the fish is gone.

events.text: In the pit of an old crater, a drift of fallen things has collected: a boot, a bronze mirror, a flute, a child's kite, a bowl of rice gone to stone. The pit has a custom. You may take one thing, and must leave one.

choices.text: Take the flute and leave a coin

effects.log: The flute plays a note that makes birds listen. It has an owner somewhere, and no regrets.

choices.text: Leave a small thing and take nothing

effects.log: You leave a button. The pit seems pleased to be remembered.

events.text: There is a beach at the Edge of Heaven: a long arc of pale cloud-sand with a surf of mist that comes in and goes out. Immortals walk it barefoot, collecting shells that are really tiny frozen sighs. The shells hum when held to the ear.

choices.text: Walk the beach and collect a shell

effects.log: Each shell holds a different sigh. Yours is a happy one, from long ago.

choices.text: Sit at the waterline and let the mist wash over

effects.log: You think of nothing. It is the best hour of the year.

events.text: A lake of cloud-water lies in a cup of an isle, so still it reflects stars even at noon. Boats on it float on their own reflections. The lake keeps no fish, only reflections of fish, which dart away when you reach.

choices.text: Row to the middle and look down

effects.log: The reflected stars are brighter than the real ones. You come back dazzled.

choices.text: Skip a stone and watch the ripples

effects.log: Every ripple holds a different night sky. You name them.

events.text: On a green hill, a stone circle rings with a faint hum each noon, as if the stones were thinking. A shepherd says the hum is a cheap trick of the wind. But children swear it changes tune depending on who stands in the middle.

choices.text: Stand in the middle and listen

effects.log: The hum shifts into a slow, calm chord. You feel a settled sort of pride.

choices.text: Hum along with it

effects.log: The stones harmonise. You and the stones are a rather good trio.

events.text: A stair of cloud winds up to a landing where a lone monk, or perhaps just a recluse, offers a cup of tea in exchange for a question. Questions are scribbled on a slate. The answers are scribbled below. Today the slate reads "Does the sky end? / It is not important."

choices.text: Ask a question of your own

effects.log: The answer is a drawing of a cat. You work it out in a week.

choices.text: Drink the tea and write nothing

effects.log: The recluse nods. "That is also an answer," they say.

events.text: On the peak of a storm-wall, a cairn of weathered stones records the names of pilots who flew through and lived. Each pilot adds a stone. You find the pile at your height. You add yours.

choices.text: Add a stone and say a name aloud

effects.log: The wind drops for a moment. It is as if the cairn nodded.

choices.text: Count the stones and compute the year

effects.log: There are 1,188. One is brand new. You wonder whose.

events.text: A hot spring on a mountain isle is shared by a tribe of small blue cloud-monkeys, who sit in rows with their eyes shut. They allow visitors if you wash first. A sign in crude paint: "Wash. Be quiet. Be kind."

choices.text: Wash and join the monkeys in the spring

effects.log: You sit in the steam with eleven monkeys. It is peaceful until one steals your robe.

choices.text: Stay on the bank and share an apple

effects.log: A monkey takes it with great dignity and gives you a pebble.

events.text: On the hundredth night of winter a bloom of ice flowers opens in a high valley, glass-clear and singing. People come with cloaks and flasks and a hush. At dawn the flowers fall in a ring of chimes.

choices.text: Stay for the dawn chimes

effects.log: The chimes ring over the whole valley. Your eyes sting.

choices.text: Carry one flower home in a jar of snow

effects.log: It lasts a week and sings nightly. Your neighbours pretend not to mind.

events.text: Before dawn, the dew-gatherers climb to the high isles with silver bowls. The dew there is thinner than water and tastes of nothing. A cup is said to restore a tired mind. They work in silence. The sun comes up behind them like a bell.

choices.text: Join the gatherers with a bowl

effects.log: You collect half a cup. It tastes of nothing at all, and it clears your head completely.

choices.text: Watch from a bench with your tea

effects.log: The gatherers nod. One brings you a cup.

events.text: A stall at the cloud-market is run by a rogue with a patched awning and no seal. Their wares are odds and ends: a compass with no needle, a lantern with no oil, a jar labelled "air from somewhere nice." Business is slow. The patter is good.

choices.text: Buy the jar of air for a copper

effects.log: It smells of rain on warm stone, and you do not regret it.

choices.text: Stay and listen to the patter for an hour

effects.log: You learn four proverbs and a recipe. The rogue is delighted to be heard.

events.text: At a bridge-gate, a clerk checks seals and passes. When you step up, the clerk holds a hand out for your seal, finds none, and sighs: "Side road, please." The side road is a plank over a gap. Others cross by the main way with a bow.

choices.text: Take the plank, with grace

effects.log: It sways. You cross. The clerk looks away, a little embarrassed.

choices.text: Ask politely for the clerk's name

effects.log: They give it, startled. You thank them. It is a small revolution.

events.text: In a lull between storms, a tea-house puts tables out on the terrace and serves lightning-brewed tea: the kettle is set on a copper rod and charged by a passing strike. The tea tastes of ozone and honey. It is wildly popular.

choices.text: Order a cup and watch the next strike

effects.log: The strike hits the rod. The tea in your cup is a note too sweet and a note too sharp. You drink it twice.

choices.text: Bring your own kettle to try

effects.log: The kettle bursts. The staff are used to it. They lend you a new one and a mop.

events.text: An isle the size of a courtyard drifts past, bare except for a single seed-pod the size of a boat. Inside, tiny sprouts press against the shell. A note on it: "To be planted somewhere high. Please. —the previous isle."

choices.text: Tow it to a quiet cliff and plant it

effects.log: The pod splits in a week. The sprouts reach for the sun like hands.

choices.text: Leave it drifting on

effects.log: Someone else will find it. You tell yourself so.

events.text: A herald at a court notices a seat unfilled: a rogue, not on the list, has slipped in at the back and is eating the pastries. The herald does not eject them. Instead, a small bow, and "welcome". The room goes quiet at the audacity of kindness.

choices.text: Slide a plate of pastries to the rogue

effects.log: A shy smile. The herald, passing, murmurs "Excellent."

choices.text: Raise your cup to the herald

effects.log: They flush. The mood in the hall changes, slightly, for the better.

events.text: In a cloud-inn kitchen, the cook seasons a pot of broth with a pinch of qi, a flick of the wrist that sends a silver mist into the steam. The broth tastes of mountain air. The cook says it is the only spice worth the name.

choices.text: Ask the cook to teach you the flick

effects.log: It takes a month. Your first batch tastes of nothing. Your fifth is a promise.

choices.text: Eat three bowls and praise the pot

effects.log: The cook beams. A fourth bowl appears.

events.text: In the Archive of Weathers, a card in the catalogue is misfiled: "Wind, of a morning in Spring, one thousand years ago, very gentle." It sits in the drawer for Hail. You find it and carry it to the right drawer, and the whole archive rustles in thanks.

choices.text: File the card in its right place

effects.log: A faint breeze stirs the drawers. You feel the weight of centuries lighten.

choices.text: Keep the card in your sleeve for a day

effects.log: It smells of spring. You return it, reluctantly.

events.text: A wind blows past that has a name, written on a ribbon tied to a pole: "Hana, mild, afternoons." Skiff-pilots greet the winds by name, as one greets a neighbour. When you say "Hana" aloud, it ruffles your hair.

choices.text: Greet the wind by name each time it passes

effects.log: In a year it learns yours. It brings you small things: a leaf, a seed.

choices.text: Ask the pilots for the names of all the winds

effects.log: They list forty-one, and the moods of each. It is a poem of weather.

events.text: A library sank into the cloud sea in the war, shelves and all, and {npc} has spent {his} life trying to reach it. "The books are not wet," {he} says. "Cloud does not wet. They are only far." {He} has found the way down, a flue in a reef, and needs a partner to hold the line.
events.arc: The Library That Sank

choices.text: Hold the line at the reef-mouth

effects.log: You pay out silk rope for hours. At each tug you answer with a tug.

choices.text: Go down with {npc}

effects.log: The flue is a corkscrew of cloud, cold and silent. The dark below is full of tiny lights, like a library of fireflies.

choices.text: Warn {npc} the way is deadly

effects.log: {He} says thank you and goes anyway. You watch the rope sink.

events.text: The library is whole. Shelves climb out of sight; the books glow gently where they are touched. A reading-desk waits with a lamp, and a note: "Please do not remove books. Please read them here. You may stay as long as you like."
events.arc: The Library That Sank

choices.text: Read at the desk for a week

effects.log: The books are about small things: how to mend a net, how to say sorry, how to keep a bee. You come up wiser, and slow.

choices.text: Copy a single book for the surface

effects.log: You copy by lamplight for ten days. The book is called "A Guide to Ordinary Mornings."

choices.text: Leave quietly, touching nothing

effects.log: You respect the note. It is a rare kind of kindness.

events.text: A librarian waits at the back of the stacks: a faint, tall figure of cloud and ink, polite beyond words. "Thank you for visiting," they say. "I have been dusting for nine hundred years. I should like to give someone my keys."
events.arc: The Library That Sank

choices.text: Accept the keys and become the librarian

effects.log: You spend a hundred years among the books, a faint figure of ink. The reef-mouth is yours to open or close.

choices.text: Offer to share the keys with {npc}

effects.log: The librarian approves. You and {npc} keep the library together, in shifts.

choices.text: Decline politely and say you will visit

effects.log: The librarian nods. "Everyone says that," they say, smiling. You do.

events.text: {npc} comes up the flue at dawn with a book clutched to {his} chest, which {he} has copied in a night. "It is the first honest thing I have ever read," {he} says, and weeps. The library has been seen, and the world is a little more complete.
events.arc: The Library That Sank

choices.text: Help {npc} publish the copied book

effects.log: A hundred readers a year come to the surface for it. The reef-mouth is marked on a map.

choices.text: Keep the book between you

effects.log: It is the best secret you ever shared.

events.text: The library thrives under its two keepers. Visitors climb down by silk rope and leave their own books on the empty shelves, one by one, in thanks. The library has begun to grow.
events.arc: The Library That Sank

choices.text: Add your own story to the shelves

effects.log: You write a short book of your wanderings. It is read by a stranger a century later, and loved.

choices.text: Shelve the visitors' gifts with care

effects.log: You are the happiest of librarians. The dust, for the first time in nine centuries, is not a burden.

events.text: Once a year, the cloud carp of the lowest lake climb a waterfall of mist to the sky above, and those that reach the top are said to become dragons. Hunters wait at the falls with nets. {npc}, a warden, asks you to help {him} keep them off. "A carp has one chance," {he} says.
events.arc: The Night the Carp Climb the Sky

choices.text: Guard the falls with {npc} through the night

effects.log: The mist is cold and loud. You watch the carp leap, silver fish against the stars.

choices.text: Talk to the hunters at their fire

effects.log: They are mostly poor, and mostly hungry. You share bread and listen.

choices.text: Watch from the bank

effects.log: It is the finest sight of your year. Every carp that leaps seems to say something.

events.text: At midnight the carp rise in thousands. A large silver one, the size of a skiff, reaches the second ledge and stalls, exhausted. The hunters' nets glint in the mist. The warden whispers: "That one is a dragon in the making."
events.arc: The Night the Carp Climb the Sky

choices.text: Cut the nets from the ledge above

ok.log: You slash the nets one by one. The big carp gathers itself and leaps, the whole fall streaming from its fins.

fail.log: You cut half the nets before the hunters shout. The big carp wavers, then climbs on, a little torn.

choices.text: Offer the hunters a better catch elsewhere

effects.log: You point them to a school of lesser carp downstream. They go, grumbling, with full nets.

choices.text: Let events take their course

effects.log: The big carp slips the net unaided, sheer will. You feel small.

events.text: At the top, the carp breaks through the last curtain of mist and hangs in the air for a heartbeat, glowing. Its scales turn to jade, its fins to ribbons. A dragon the length of a river looks down at you with kind, slow eyes.
events.arc: The Night the Carp Climb the Sky

choices.text: Bow to the young dragon

effects.log: It dips its head. Its breath is cold and sweet. Then it is gone into the clouds.

choices.text: Ask the dragon for nothing, and tell it so

effects.log: A faint chuckle rolls in the sky. A single jade scale drifts down into your palm.

events.text: The hunters' fire is low and the night is cold. One of them, a child of twelve, asks what a dragon looks like. You have no answer, so you describe the carp. They listen like a student.
events.arc: The Night the Carp Climb the Sky

choices.text: Take the child under your wing for a season

effects.log: They learn to read, to row, to leave a fish go. They become a warden in time.

choices.text: Give the child a spare net with the holes still in it

effects.log: They laugh. "It is a net for catching nothing," they say, and keep it for life.

events.text: Every year on the night of the old defeat, a column of pale figures marches across a plateau in silence, in step, eyes forward. Watchers keep away. The regiment cannot see the living. They are on their way to a battle that ended nine centuries ago.
events.arc: The Regiment That Still Marches

choices.text: Stand beside the road and watch them pass

effects.log: A thousand figures, each in a worn uniform. They do not look up. The air is heavy and sweet.

choices.text: Walk beside the column

effects.log: You match the pace for a mile. Nothing happens. The marching sound is the only sound.

choices.text: Leave a lantern at the roadside

effects.log: It is still burning at dawn. Whose, you cannot say.

events.text: One figure at the end of the column slows, stumbles, and stops. It is a young soldier, barely visible, looking at their boots. They do not know the way. They have lost the column. They look at you as if you were a gate.
events.arc: The Regiment That Still Marches

choices.text: Offer to walk the soldier to the column

effects.log: You walk them to the head of the line, silent. They salute. The column does not change step, but a place is made.

choices.text: Show the soldier the lantern

effects.log: They stare at the flame, then at you, and sit by it. The column marches on without them.

choices.text: Stay still and say nothing

effects.log: The soldier stumbles on, alone. You feel a little ill.

events.text: The next year, the column is one figure shorter. A single lantern burns by the road where the soldier sat. The marchers pass round it as water round a stone. At the head of the column, a figure salutes, then walks on, in time.
events.arc: The Regiment That Still Marches

choices.text: Add another lantern to the road

effects.log: By the tenth year there is a line of lanterns for the column to pass. The marching sound softens.

choices.text: Sit by the first lantern with a flask of tea

effects.log: The marchers pass. One of them, in passing, tips a helmet.

events.text: The column marches into the plateau's farthest edge, where a stone arch stands open. One by one the figures step through. There is a sound like a long exhale. By dawn, the road is empty, and has been empty since.
events.arc: The Regiment That Still Marches

choices.text: Close the arch with a tide of flowers

effects.log: You lay petals across the stones. The wind carries them gently on.

choices.text: Sit in the arch till dawn

effects.log: It is the quietest night of your life. The sunrise is gold.

events.text: In a high isle there is a grotto with three doors, each marked with a name and a season: Spring, Autumn, Snow. Behind each, the old tales say, lives one of three sisters who quarrelled and have not spoken in a thousand years. Visitors may knock on one door a year.
events.arc: The Grotto of the Three Sisters

choices.text: Knock on the Spring door

effects.log: A voice, warm and impatient: "Come in. Mind the plants. Do not mention my sisters."

choices.text: Knock on the Autumn door

effects.log: A voice, dry and amused: "Come in. I am just finishing a poem. Do not mention my sisters."

choices.text: Knock on the Snow door

effects.log: Silence, then a very small voice: "Come in. It is cold, but the tea is hot."

events.text: Spring is a garden in a cave, wild and green; a pruner with a sharp tongue and a gentle heart. Spring asks you to carry a seed-packet to Autumn, "without saying who it is from."
events.arc: The Grotto of the Three Sisters

choices.text: Carry the seeds to Autumn's door

effects.log: Autumn opens, sniffs the packet, and says nothing. But the eyes are bright.

choices.text: Ask Spring why they do not carry them in person

effects.log: Spring snaps, then sags. "Because I have forgotten how to say sorry," they say.

choices.text: Decline, kindly
