effects.log: Spring shrugs and goes back to pruning. A petal falls on your shoulder.

events.text: Autumn is a library in a cave, warm with lamps; an ironic old poet. Autumn asks you to carry a poem to Snow, "without saying who it is from."
events.arc: The Grotto of the Three Sisters

choices.text: Carry the poem to Snow's door

effects.log: Snow opens a crack, reads the poem, and closes the door softly. A tear falls on the sill.

choices.text: Ask Autumn why

effects.log: "Because I wrote it for Snow fifty years ago," they say. "It has been in a drawer."

events.text: Snow is a still room, white and quiet; shy, frozen, wrapped in a warm shawl. Snow asks you to carry a pot of tea to Spring, "without saying who it is from." The pot is still warm.
events.arc: The Grotto of the Three Sisters

choices.text: Carry the tea to Spring's door

effects.log: Spring opens the door, drinks, and the face changes. "That is Snow's," they say. "Snow never forgets the sugar."

choices.text: Offer to deliver all three gifts together

effects.log: You gather seed, poem and tea on one tray and set it on a table in the grotto's hall.

events.text: The three sisters, after a thousand years, meet in the hall of the grotto. Spring and Autumn stand, awkward. Snow arrives with a shawl round the shoulders. The silence lasts an hour. Then Spring laughs, a hiccup, and the dam breaks.
events.arc: The Grotto of the Three Sisters

choices.text: Pour tea and withdraw

effects.log: You leave them to it. You hear laughter until dawn. The three doors stand open from that day.

choices.text: Stay at the table, silent, as a witness

effects.log: They tell you of the quarrel, which began over a lost umbrella. You laugh and weep together.

events.text: The sisters send a joint letter each spring: three hands, one page, three cheerful lines. You post it on your wall. It is the best proof you have that a quarrel can end.
events.arc: The Grotto of the Three Sisters

choices.text: Reply with a pot of tea

effects.log: The grotto sends back a clay cup. It is warm every time you hold it.

choices.text: Visit once a year, with a seed, a poem and a pot of tea

effects.log: You are the family friend of three immortals. They fuss over you.

events.text: {npc} is building a bridge from the Edge of Heaven out into the void. Plank by plank, each one a day. There is no far side. "The bridge is the point," {he} says. "I will keep going until it reaches somewhere." {He} needs planks.
events.arc: The Bridge That Will Not Finish

choices.text: Carry planks to the bridge-end

effects.log: The bridge sways and sings. You lay each plank like a word in a long sentence.

choices.text: Ask where the bridge is going

effects.log: "Nowhere," {he} says. "And everywhere else I could not go on foot."

choices.text: Wish {npc} patience

effects.log: {He} laughs. "That I have," {he} says.

events.text: One night the bridge begins to hum, a long deep note rising from the planks. {npc} presses a palm to the wood. "It is listening," {he} says. "The void is listening." Out in the dark, something answers, a faint knock.
events.arc: The Bridge That Will Not Finish

choices.text: Knock back on the plank

effects.log: The answer comes, three knocks. You exchange greetings with the void.

choices.text: Hum along to the bridge's note

effects.log: The note deepens. The void hums with you. Your bones sing.

choices.text: Listen without answering

effects.log: You sit on the plank, saying nothing. It is enough.

events.text: A great wind-storm rises from the void, and the bridge strains against its mooring. Planks creak. {npc} shouts for ropes. If the bridge tears loose, a year of work will fall into the dark.
events.arc: The Bridge That Will Not Finish

choices.text: Anchor the bridge with a rope round the nearest pillar

ok.log: You wrestle the rope round a stone, taking a burn on your palms. The bridge holds, trembling, through the night.

fail.log: The rope slips, but the bridge holds on its own stubborn planks.

choices.text: Cut the last few planks to save the rest

effects.log: You sacrifice a day's work to save a year's. {npc} does not forgive you for an hour, and thanks you for a decade.

choices.text: Hold the lantern and shout encouragement

effects.log: {npc} does the rest. Your voice is hoarse by dawn.

events.text: At last the knock from the void is a knock from a door. A small shelf appears out of the dark, a floating landing with a lamp lit upon it, just beyond the last plank. {npc} sits down and weeps. "Somewhere," {he} says. "It is somewhere."
events.arc: The Bridge That Will Not Finish

choices.text: Step onto the landing together

effects.log: The landing is warm. A kettle hums on a tiny stove. Someone has been expecting you.

choices.text: Leave {npc} to cross alone

effects.log: {He} steps onto the landing. A hand takes {his}, from the dark. You hear laughter.

events.text: The bridge is never finished, but {npc} keeps working, and pilgrims come to walk its length, slowly, to its swaying end. They sit and listen to the void. Some say it speaks. Most say it simply stays near.
events.arc: The Bridge That Will Not Finish

choices.text: Sit with the pilgrims at the end

effects.log: You hear what they hear: a low contented hum. It is, perhaps, the sound of company.

choices.text: Carry planks for another decade

effects.log: The bridge grows by thirty feet. You cannot say you finished anything, and you are content.

events.text: The isles drift apart in winter, the gaps widening to days of open cloud. Rogues without a seal are shut out of the winter harbours, and the lanes empty. You have a skiff, a blanket, and four days of food. The next harbour is six days away.
events.arc: A Rogue's Winter

choices.text: Ration food and press on

effects.log: You eat half a loaf a day. On the fourth day a gale pushes you the wrong way.

choices.text: Turn back to the harbour that refused you

effects.log: You knock at the gate. The keeper stares, then, with a grumble, lets you in for one night.

choices.text: Fish the cloud-sea for ghost-fish

effects.log: You catch three. They are thin and glow, and they do not feed you, but they cheer you.

events.text: The gale blows you onto a lonely rock with a single hut. A rogue like you waves a lantern from the door and offers a bowl of soup and a bed. "Winter is hard enough without being alone," they say. They have run this hut for forty winters.
events.arc: A Rogue's Winter

choices.text: Accept and stay until the gale ends

effects.log: The soup is thin and salty. The bed is warm. You sleep like a stone.

choices.text: Ask how the hut is kept

effects.log: The rule: any rogue is welcome, one condition, they leave something behind. The walls are hung with scraps from forty years of strangers.

choices.text: Thank them and push on

effects.log: They press a loaf on you. The gale has calmed.

events.text: The hut's wall is hung with rogues' offerings: a feather, a bell, a poem, a child's drawing. You add yours: a small carved gull. The keeper sets it on the shelf with the others. "That will be remembered," they say.
events.arc: A Rogue's Winter

choices.text: Leave a promise to return in spring

effects.log: They nod. "Rogues often promise," they say dryly. "Few return. Do."

choices.text: Leave more than a carving: a sack of grain

effects.log: They lift a brow, then accept. It is the most useful thing on the wall.

events.text: In spring you return with grain, wood, and a fresh bell. The keeper is on the doorstep, thinner but steady. The hut has a new offering on the wall: a note from another rogue, thanking the keeper. They blush at your arrival.
events.arc: A Rogue's Winter

choices.text: Stay a month to repair the hut

effects.log: You patch the roof, trim the lamp, and sing in the evenings. The keeper tells you stories you will keep.

choices.text: Leave the supplies and a promise to visit every winter

effects.log: You keep it, for centuries. The hut becomes a landmark on the rogue-lanes.

events.text: A sky whale has slept for twenty years on a shelf off the Third Reef. It has not moved. Every morning there is a fresh heap of cloud-krill beside its mouth, which it eats in its sleep. {npc} has watched for years and cannot find out who brings it. "Help me," {he} says.
events.arc: Who Is Feeding the Sleeping Whale?

choices.text: Stay awake on the shelf, hidden

effects.log: You watch from a ledge through the dark. At the hour before dawn, a shape moves in the mist.

choices.text: Scatter ash to catch footprints

effects.log: In the morning, a ring of prints, small and bare, leading from the whale's mouth to the sea.

choices.text: Leave a lantern lit and go to sleep

effects.log: A good night's sleep, a heap of krill at dawn. The mystery keeps.

events.text: The feeder is a child of nine, thin and quiet, with no isle and no name. They bring the krill from a net in the reefs. When you speak, they bolt. {npc} says the child has fed the whale for twenty years, since they were an infant, which cannot be. Not for a human child.
events.arc: Who Is Feeding the Sleeping Whale?

choices.text: Follow the child at a distance

effects.log: The child climbs a rope to a hollow in the whale's great ribs and disappears inside.

choices.text: Leave a bowl of rice cake where the child will find it

effects.log: It is gone at dawn. A tiny bow on the lip of the bowl.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to let them be

effects.log: {He} nods, a little relieved.

events.text: Inside the whale's ribs is a little home: a bed, a stove, a shelf of seashells. The child is not a child. They are the whale's own spirit, in the shape of a human, kept small by the long sleep. They look at you with enormous patience. "Please do not wake it," they say.
events.arc: Who Is Feeding the Sleeping Whale?

choices.text: Promise to keep the secret

effects.log: The child nods. A shell is pressed into your hand. It sings of tides.

choices.text: Ask how long the whale will sleep

effects.log: "Until it has dreamed enough," the child says. "A hundred years. Or a thousand."

choices.text: Back out quietly and say nothing

effects.log: You leave. You think of the child and the stove for days.

events.text: You tell {npc} the whale's secret in the gentlest way you can, a story of a small spirit and a big sleeper. {He} listens, quiet. "I thought as much," {he} says. "I have left a bowl of tea by the ribs for years."
events.arc: Who Is Feeding the Sleeping Whale?

choices.text: Take shifts with {npc} to guard the whale

effects.log: You and {npc} keep the shelf in rota, ensuring no hunter or Ministry clerk disturbs the sleeper.

choices.text: Leave the whale in its dream and move on

effects.log: You return once a year with a bowl of rice cake. The child never changes.

events.text: A tribulation cloud is drifting across the lanes in search of {npc}, a senior brother of the Jade Void who has been hiding in a cellar for a month. {He} has no wish to be struck. "Go and distract it," {he} says. "You are a better target. You are junior."
events.arc: Chasing Someone Else's Tribulation

choices.text: Draw the cloud away across the isles

effects.log: You lead it on a long chase, laughing. It sends sullen thunder after you and misses.

choices.text: Tell the senior to face it like a grown immortal

effects.log: {He} turns the colour of paper. "I am not ready," {he} says.

choices.text: Hide with the senior in the cellar

effects.log: The cloud passes overhead. {npc} looks at you in grudging gratitude.

events.text: The cloud turns on you, a cold white-blue crackle at the lip. Thunder cracks. The air tastes of metal. For one moment you see the shape inside: a vast quiet eye that is, impossibly, kind.
events.arc: Chasing Someone Else's Tribulation

choices.text: Stand your ground and take the first strike

ok.log: The bolt runs through you like a bell. You fall, smoking, and wake with the whole sky ringing. A little of the cloud's power is yours.

fail.log: The bolt throws you off the isle onto a lower terrace. You are bruised, shaken, and alive.

choices.text: Duck into a cloud-cellar and let it pass

effects.log: It circles overhead, grumbling, and gives up. You emerge damp and unharmed.

choices.text: Run for the sect gate and shout for help

effects.log: The elders turn out with umbrellas of jade. The cloud, unimpressed, floats on.

events.text: The cloud, having tested you, drifts back toward {npc}'s cellar, sulking. It wants its due. {npc} sits in the dark, trembling. {He} has run out of excuses.
events.arc: Chasing Someone Else's Tribulation

choices.text: Go down and stand with {him}

effects.log: You stay in the cellar as the thunder rolls. The cloud passes, in the end, without taking a bolt: it merely looks.

choices.text: Let {him} face it alone

effects.log: {He} walks out at dawn, pale, and takes it on the chin. {He} is better for it.

events.text: The senior sends you a jar of plum wine the next spring. The note reads: "To a better target than I deserved. Come and drink." The cloud, you learn, has moved on to a different isle, and found a different, braver soul.
events.arc: Chasing Someone Else's Tribulation

choices.text: Visit {npc}, and bring the wine back to {him}

effects.log: You trade stories of your worst fears. It is a long, pleasant evening.

choices.text: Save the wine for a stormy night

effects.log: You open it years later, in a thunderstorm, and pour it out on the wind to the senior's health.

events.text: A tall chimney of stone rises from the cloud-sea, warm to the touch, steaming gently. Rogues sleep in a ring around its base in winter, their blankets drawn up. Nobody knows who built it. It never needs wood.

choices.text: Sleep a night against the chimney

effects.log: It hums with a deep heat. You wake rested and oddly cheerful.

choices.text: Walk round it and count the rogues

effects.log: Thirty-one. All asleep, all smiling. You leave them be.

events.text: On a still night a lullaby rolls across the cloud-sea, enormous and slow, and every skiff in earshot slows, and every pilot yawns. A sky-whale mother is singing the calf to sleep. The whole sea is hushed to listen.

choices.text: Drift in the lullaby and nap

effects.log: You sleep a night and a half. You wake lighter, hungry, and absurdly well.

choices.text: Tie up, lower your lantern, and stay awake to listen

effects.log: You hear every word of a language you do not know. It is about love.

events.text: Storm finches nest in the lee of lightning-struck pines and sing only when thunder is near. Birdwatchers wait for hours on freezing ledges with flasks of tea. When the thunder cracks, the finches sing, and for ten seconds the whole ridge is a choir.

choices.text: Wait for the thunder and the choir

effects.log: It comes at midnight. Ten seconds. You will remember them for a hundred years.

choices.text: Share your flask with a fellow birdwatcher

effects.log: A friendship begins in a ledge-side silence. It outlasts the finches.

events.text: The yearly Hunt of the Silver Hare on the high meadow is a sport of laughter and tea: the hare is a decoy of silk, the prize is a pot of honey, and the rule is that the loser buys the next round. All ages play. Cheating is encouraged, as long as it is funny.

choices.text: Join the hunt and cheat with style

effects.log: You hide a decoy in a kite. The crowd howls. You lose, magnificently.

choices.text: Referee and keep score

effects.log: You rule with a stern face and a sly wink. Everyone remembers you.

events.text: A tower of the war survives, roofless, its spiral stair worn smooth. At the top, a bench, a view of five isles, and a note scratched into the stone: "Lookout 3 reporting. All quiet. I have been here three years. I hope someone relieves me."

choices.text: Scratch your own note beneath it: "Relieved."

effects.log: You sit the lookout for an hour in honour. The five isles are very quiet.

choices.text: Climb down and tell no one

effects.log: It is a private thing. You carry it for years.

events.text: The morning after a meteor passes, the sky smells of struck flint and cold flowers. Children go out to collect the ash. It is soft, silver, and makes good ink. A teacher leads a class along the crater rim, with a basket and a nature-lesson.

choices.text: Join the class and learn the lesson

effects.log: It is about patience. You collect a jar of silver ash and a headache.

choices.text: Gather ash for a calligrapher friend

effects.log: The friend writes you a scroll in return. It reads "thank you" in seven scripts.

events.text: At the Edge of Heaven, a small stall sells postcards: "Wish you were here." Nothing else. The postcards are blank on the back. The stall-keeper says that is the point. Many send them to their own address. Some arrive.

choices.text: Buy a postcard and send it to yourself

effects.log: It arrives a month later, with a faint smell of nothing. You keep it.

choices.text: Write a postcard to a friend you have lost

effects.log: You do not post it. You leave it at the edge, and the wind takes it.

events.text: In the lull after the harvest the isle holds a lantern walk. Each lantern holds a name, written on the shade. You walk the path in a line of strangers, reading the names aloud. It is considered rude to skip any. It takes all night.

choices.text: Read every name aloud

effects.log: Hundreds. By the end, your voice is a whisper, and your heart is full.

choices.text: Add a name to a lantern: someone you miss

effects.log: The lantern floats off at dawn. A small ceremony of release.

events.text: On the night of the long shadow, a ferry rows the dark between star and star, carrying those who want to touch the sky. The ferryman is a quiet old immortal who charges nothing. They only ask that you not try to bring anything back.

choices.text: Ride the star-ferry and touch a star

effects.log: It is warm and humming, and smaller than you expected. You let go gently.

choices.text: Watch from the dock and wave

effects.log: A star glimmers in answer. The ferryman tips a cap.

events.text: A cloud-shepherd wanders the hill isles with a flute and a flock of small grey clouds that follow the notes. The shepherd lets you try the flute. The clouds ignore you. After an hour, one trundles over, sniffs the reed, and lies down at your feet.

choices.text: Play on, badly, for the cloud

effects.log: It is, at least, a patient audience. It dissolves into a gentle drizzle as you finish.

choices.text: Thank the shepherd and give back the flute

effects.log: The shepherd smiles. "That one never lies down," they say. "You are a friend."

events.text: The moon-peach blooms for a single night every eleven years, a pale pink cloud on one branch. Folk gather at the old orchard with blankets and wine. Silence is requested. Poems are not. Bad poems are celebrated.

choices.text: Recite your worst poem to the tree

effects.log: The crowd roars with approval. The tree sheds a petal on your head.

choices.text: Sit under the branch and say nothing

effects.log: Petals fall into your tea. It is the loveliest tea of your life.

events.text: A garden drifts by on a raft of cloud, tended by a gardener who has not touched land in three hundred years. They offer you a seedling in a pot, no strings: "Plant it somewhere you will return to." The seedling has two leaves.

choices.text: Take the seedling and plant it at home

effects.log: It grows into a tree of tiny golden bells. It rings every dusk.

choices.text: Offer the gardener tea in exchange

effects.log: You and the gardener sit through the afternoon on the raft. The garden drifts on.

events.text: A rogue stands in the corridor of the Jade Court, a petition in their hand, waiting for a clerk who is perpetually "just coming." The petition is for a single seal-less pass to the Ministry library. It has been twenty years. They are very polite.

choices.text: Sit with the rogue and keep them company

effects.log: You swap stories, then proverbs. The clerk never arrives, but the afternoon is not lost.

choices.text: Carry the petition to a clerk you know

effects.log: It takes a week. The pass is granted on the last day, in a grudging stamp.

events.text: As the market closes, a vendor lays out their last wares at half price: unsold wind, the end of a rainbow, a bell of pure silence. Haggling is traditional. The vendor says if you can make them laugh, the lot is yours.

choices.text: Try to make the vendor laugh

effects.log: You tell the story of the toll-keeper and the cat. The vendor wheezes. You walk away with the bell.

choices.text: Pay full price for the bell of silence

effects.log: It is worth it. Your home is quieter for a century.

events.text: The night clerk of the Archive of Winds is a thin person with a lantern, who dusts the jade slips by feel. They have not been seen in daylight in two hundred years. They are kind to wanderers who knock at midnight, and brew an exceptional tea.

choices.text: Knock at midnight and ask for tea

effects.log: The clerk makes two cups. You talk until dawn, and do not know their name.

choices.text: Leave a small gift at the door

effects.log: In the morning, a slip of jade with a blessing in a very small hand.

events.text: A noodle-cart rolls along the cloud-bridge after midnight, pulled by a patient old goat. The cook ladles broth from a cauldron that never empties. The only rule: no questions about the cauldron. The noodles are the best in the sky.

choices.text: Order a bowl and eat in silence

effects.log: The broth tastes like a memory you almost have. You tip heavily.

choices.text: Ask a question about the cauldron anyway

effects.log: The cook smiles and shuts the lid. "That is not a question," they say. "That is a hobby."

events.text: On the first fair wind of the year every isle flies its kites at once, and the sky becomes a field of bright tails. Contests are held: highest, strangest, most soulful. Kites are made of anything. One year, a pair of trousers won.

choices.text: Fly a kite of your own design

effects.log: It is a fish. It flies badly, but gloriously. You get an honourable mention.

choices.text: Judge the strangest category

effects.log: The trousers return. You cry with laughter and award them first place again.

events.text: A spring on a high isle is said to run backwards: water rises out of the stone and falls into the sky, a stream going up. At dawn the stream catches the sun and becomes a column of light. Visitors climb up to drink the rising water, which tastes of the future.

choices.text: Drink from the rising stream

effects.log: It tastes of something yet to come. You cannot name it. It leaves you hopeful.

choices.text: Stand in the column of light until it fades

effects.log: It is warm. You think of everything you meant to do.

events.text: On a cold, bare shelf an ancient lamp stands, older than the court, older than the fleets. It is unlit. A tradition says that whoever lights it will see the first day of the sky. Nobody has tried, because nobody wants to learn the first day was dull.

choices.text: Light the lamp

effects.log: The flame is pale and steady. The first day of the sky was, you find, mostly waiting. It was beautiful.

choices.text: Leave it dark and put a flower beside it

effects.log: The lamp has been waiting a long time. A flower is a good neighbour.

events.text: A cloud-fox is stealing names. Not a thing, but a name: a tailor wakes one day and cannot remember what to call {him}self, and the shop sign is blank. {npc} comes to you in a daze, with a scrap of paper that says only "I used to be somebody." The fox, the neighbours say, has a white tail and a laugh.
events.arc: The Cloud-Fox Who Steals Names

choices.text: Track the fox by the blank signs it leaves

effects.log: Every shop it passes has a sign gone white. The trail leads through six lanes to a rooftop garden.

choices.text: Set a trap with a name as bait

effects.log: You write a false name on a scrap and leave it on a roof. By dawn it is gone. A white hair is caught on the nail.

choices.text: Keep {npc} company while {he} recovers

effects.log: You tell {him} what you know of {him}. The names are in the telling.

events.text: The fox is no thief but a lonely creature: it has no name of its own and collects those it can. Its den is a nest of paper scraps, every name carefully folded. It looks at you with big, apologetic eyes. "I only wanted to try one on," it says.
events.arc: The Cloud-Fox Who Steals Names

choices.text: Offer it a name of its own

effects.log: You think for an hour. "Haneul," you say. The fox repeats it, delighted, and gives back every stolen name.

choices.text: Bargain: your name for the tailor's

effects.log: The fox is moved. It takes yours for a day and returns it, polished, with the tailor's alongside.

choices.text: Take the tailor's name by force

effects.log: The fox yelps and drops it. It cries. You feel awful.

events.text: The fox now has a name and a home on the tailor's roof. It stops stealing and begins to give: an extra stitch in a seam, a lost button returned, a whispered pun. The street, in time, comes to love it.
events.arc: The Cloud-Fox Who Steals Names

choices.text: Visit the roof and bring a pastry

effects.log: The fox, called Haneul, runs in circles. It does not need a pastry, and eats three.

choices.text: Tell the neighbours the fox's story

effects.log: They stop locking their signs. A tiny shrine is raised on the roof.

events.text: The false name bait comes back to you a year later, in the post, with a note in an unknown paw: "I tried it on. It did not fit. Thank you for lending." The fox has gone to other lanes, taking only what it returns.
events.arc: The Cloud-Fox Who Steals Names

choices.text: Keep the note

effects.log: It is the most original letter you have received. It smells faintly of fox.

choices.text: Leave a new false name on the roof

effects.log: It is picked up by dawn. The game goes on, for centuries.

events.text: You buy a second-hand skiff for four stones, sail it for a week, and discover it has opinions. It refuses certain winds. It steers itself toward particular isles. It hums when it is happy. The seller, you now recall, grinned a little too widely.
events.arc: The Skiff That Chose Its Own Way

choices.text: Pay a rigger to look at it (2 spirit stones)

effects.log: The rigger pats the hull and says it is awake, and has been for a long time.

choices.text: Let it steer for a week and see where it goes

effects.log: It takes you to a small harbour you never knew, with a fruit stall and a friendly dog.

choices.text: Argue with the skiff

effects.log: It sulks. You lose half a day. You apologise to a plank.

events.text: The skiff takes you to an isle with a shipyard, very old and empty. A sign on the gate says: "Built here. Keel laid by hand. If you find our child, please give it a good home." It is a shipwright's note. The skiff hums softly at the gate.
events.arc: The Skiff That Chose Its Own Way

choices.text: Sail into the shipyard and stay a night

effects.log: The yard is quiet and kind. The skiff settles into a berth like a sleeper in a bed.

choices.text: Ask the skiff what it wants

effects.log: It points its bow toward the horizon and rings the bell once: out.

choices.text: Read the shipwright's ledger

effects.log: It records the building of nine skiffs. Eight are noted as sold. One, as "gone to the sky of its own accord."

events.text: The skiff wants to find its siblings, eight skiffs sold across the isles in a hundred years. You trace them by the ledger. Three are wrecks, two are ferries, one is a houseboat, and two are lost. The skiff hums at each, a long low greeting.
events.arc: The Skiff That Chose Its Own Way

choices.text: Take the skiff to visit each sibling in turn

effects.log: It takes a year. At each stop the skiffs exchange hums. Even the wrecks seem to smile.

choices.text: Reunite two of the living skiffs for a day

effects.log: They sail side by side across the evening cloud. The sight draws a crowd.

events.text: The skiff makes its own course, every morning, and you learn to let it. It takes you to places no map has: a pool of floating stars, a cave of singing frost, a calm bay where whales surface to sleep. You are the happiest passenger in the sky.
events.arc: The Skiff That Chose Its Own Way

choices.text: Let the skiff choose for the rest of your life

effects.log: It never takes you anywhere dull. At the end, it sails you home.

choices.text: Keep a log of its every choice

effects.log: The log becomes a guide to the unmapped. Pilots consult it with reverence.

events.text: {npc} runs the last ferry from the Quiet Isle to the Edge of Heaven, one trip a month, empty. "People used to want to see it," {he} says. "Now they send a postcard." {He} offers you a free fare, if you will talk to {him} on the way.
events.arc: The Last Ferry to the Edge

choices.text: Take the ferry and talk the whole way

effects.log: {He} tells you of the old riders: a bride, a poet, an assassin who got off and stayed. The cloud slides by.

choices.text: Take the ferry and sit in silence

effects.log: The crossing takes six hours. {npc} nods, approving of a quiet fare.

choices.text: Decline and wish {him} a full boat

effects.log: {He} smiles. "Most do," {he} says.

events.text: At the Edge, a single hut stands on a shelf, a shrine to the ferry and its fares. Photographs, notes, a lantern. {npc} lights the lantern each trip. "A hundred and twelve fares," {he} says. "I remember every one. They never remember me."
events.arc: The Last Ferry to the Edge

choices.text: Add a note to the shrine in your own hand

effects.log: You write: "Fare 113. Thank you for the ride." {npc} reads it twice and puts it in the frame.

choices.text: Tell {npc} that you will remember

effects.log: {He} laughs and waves a hand. But {his} eyes shine.

choices.text: Look at the photographs

effects.log: Faces, hundreds of them, smiling at the camera or the cloud. A history of wanting to see.

events.text: A storm closes the ferry route for the winter. {npc} sits at the dock in {his} coat, watching the cloud-sea, and says: "Perhaps it is time to stop. A ferry nobody rides is a long way of being alone." The ferry creaks at its mooring, as if to disagree.
events.arc: The Last Ferry to the Edge

choices.text: Offer to bring fares next spring

effects.log: You post notices on three isles. By spring there is a queue of twelve, eager and shy.

choices.text: Take the oars for a trip and give {npc} a rest

effects.log: You row a full crossing with a dozen curious passengers. {npc} watches from the dock.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} and watch the storm

effects.log: You drink {his} tea. Neither of you says much.

events.text: The ferry has fares again. {npc} paints a new name on the hull: "The Fare 113." {He} has a bell now, and a crowd on the dock, and a ledger with eleven pages full.
events.arc: The Last Ferry to the Edge

choices.text: Ride the Fare 113 at the next trip

effects.log: You sit with a dozen strangers. {npc} rings the bell. You cross to the Edge as friends.

choices.text: Leave the ferry to {npc} and its fares

effects.log: It flourishes without you. You hear of it from time to time and smile.

events.text: {npc} leaves the ferry to you when {he} retires. "It is a modest inheritance," {he} says. "A boat, a lantern, and a list of names." You row it for a century. Every fare is remembered.
events.arc: The Last Ferry to the Edge

choices.text: Keep the lantern and the list

effects.log: You add a name each month. The shrine grows into a small hall.

choices.text: Hire a young ferryman and sail as a passenger

effects.log: It is the best thing you ever did. The ferry goes on, long after you.

events.text: In the sky-whale graveyard lives a bone-singer, who tunes the ribs of the dead whales like harp-strings. {npc} plays a requiem every dawn. "The whales liked music," {he} says. "They ought not to be forgotten in silence." {He} asks you to tune a fallen rib.
events.arc: The Bone-Singer of the Ivory Field

choices.text: Tune a rib with {npc}

effects.log: You tap the bone and listen. It takes a day to find the note. When you do, the field hums back.

choices.text: Listen to the dawn requiem from the edge

effects.log: It is a huge, sweet, melancholy sound. Moss glows in answer.

choices.text: Bring {npc} a meal

effects.log: {He} eats like someone starved of company. You learn the names of the dead whales.

events.text: One rib will not sound. It was the mother's, {npc} says, the great whale who gave its life to turn a storm. The bone is pitted and cold. "{He} has nothing to say," {he} sighs. "Or {he} does not trust the living."
events.arc: The Bone-Singer of the Ivory Field

choices.text: Sing to the rib, softly, a lullaby

effects.log: The rib trembles. A single low note breathes from it, and the field goes silent, listening.

choices.text: Lay a hand on the bone and wait

effects.log: You wait for an hour. It warms against your palm. A deep slow hum begins.

choices.text: Leave the rib as it is

effects.log: Some silences are the right shape for grief.

events.text: Grave-robbers arrive by night in a black skiff, with saws and a winch. They want the great ribs for carvers' markets: ivory beyond price. {npc} stands in front of the mother's rib with {his} arms crossed. The field is silent and furious.
events.arc: The Bone-Singer of the Ivory Field

choices.text: Stand beside {npc} and call out

ok.log: The robbers, spooked by the field humming in anger, back off. Their skiff turns and flees through the mist.

fail.log: The robbers press on, and only the field's thunderous hum finally frightens them off.

choices.text: Strike the great rib to wake the whole field

effects.log: The ribs ring in a roar. The robbers flee, ears streaming.

choices.text: Wait in the shadows for the Ministry

effects.log: The wardens arrive at dawn. The robbers are gone. The field is untouched, by luck.

events.text: The mother's rib sings at last, at the next dawn, a full-throated hymn. The whole field answers, a choir of the dead. Living whales gather above the ridge. The sound goes on for an hour. {npc} lies on the moss and weeps.
events.arc: The Bone-Singer of the Ivory Field

choices.text: Lie beside {npc} and listen

effects.log: The choir is the most beautiful thing you will ever hear. You do not speak.

choices.text: Fly up and join the living whales

effects.log: You sing with them, a tiny voice among giants. A whale tilts to look at you.

events.text: {npc} passes the tuning-fork to you, a rib-tip carved to a point. "You have the ear," {he} says. "I am tired." You play the dawn requiem the next morning. It is not as good, but the field forgives you.
events.arc: The Bone-Singer of the Ivory Field

choices.text: Become the bone-singer of the Ivory Field

effects.log: You play for centuries. The moss grows brighter. The living whales visit.

choices.text: Teach three apprentices to share the dawn

effects.log: The requiem becomes a quartet. It is, they say, the first harmony in the sky.

events.text: A small star has landed in {npc}'s cabbage patch, gently, as if sitting down. It is the size of a melon and sulks among the leeks. {He} has tried to move it with a shovel; it is not that kind of star. "It is eating my cabbages," {he} says, "in a spiritual sense."
events.arc: The Star That Landed in a Garden

choices.text: Study the star among the leeks

effects.log: It hums when the cabbages grow. It seems to feed on the sound of growing.

choices.text: Offer it a bowl of cloud-milk

effects.log: It dims, then brightens. A faint ring of light settles round the bowl.

choices.text: Advise {npc} to move the cabbages

effects.log: {He} grumbles, but moves them. The star hums approvingly.

events.text: The star warms the garden. The cabbages are huge, glossy, almost musical. {npc} grudgingly admits the star is a good neighbour. But word spreads, and by autumn a queue of Ministry officials has formed at the garden gate with measuring rods and forms.
events.arc: The Star That Landed in a Garden

choices.text: Stand at the gate and argue that the star is a guest

effects.log: The officials argue back. You win an adjournment by sheer stamina. The star hums.

choices.text: Move the star by night to a safer garden

effects.log: It rolls like a pebble into your cloak. It is warm. You carry it a mile and set it down by a quiet pond.

choices.text: Let the officials measure and leave

effects.log: They find the star "uncooperative" and file a complaint.

events.text: The star starts to dim. Its glow is thin, and it turns slowly in the dirt. {npc} is worried; the star is a friend now. A visiting astronomer says stars that fall gently need to rise again before they die. It needs a high place and a push.
events.arc: The Star That Landed in a Garden

choices.text: Carry the star to the nearest peak at dusk

effects.log: You and {npc} climb a hundred switchbacks. At the top, the star lifts into the evening sky as if released.

choices.text: Launch it from a kite

effects.log: It is a clumsy launch. The star rises, wobbles, and pins itself back among the constellations.

events.text: The star is gone, but the cabbage patch glows faintly at night, and the cabbages grow musical for a decade. {npc} sells them as "starfed", and does well. Every year on the date, a faint spark falls from the sky and lands in the middle of the patch.
events.arc: The Star That Landed in a Garden

choices.text: Sit in the garden on the star's date

effects.log: A spark lands. It lingers, then lifts. You are glad.

choices.text: Help {npc} build a little shrine of cabbage leaves

effects.log: It becomes a local pilgrimage. {He} charges nothing and receives a lot of soup.

events.text: In a ruin, an embassy of an old court still stands, its hall roped off with silk: a table set for twelve, each place with a name card. The war came before the guests. The embassy staff, long dead, are said to still arrange the table each night.
events.arc: The Embassy That Never Left

choices.text: Walk the hall in the evening and read the cards

effects.log: The cards bear titles that no longer exist. One reads: "The Honourable Guest of the Last Day."

choices.text: Wait for midnight in the doorway

effects.log: At midnight the cards shuffle themselves a little, an inch. It is as if someone were picking the seating.

choices.text: Leave a flower on the table

effects.log: In the morning it is on the card of "The Honourable Guest."

events.text: The Honourable Guest's chair is empty and slightly pulled out. A message on the card: "We are ready when you are. Please do not hurry. We have been ready for a long time." The air smells of tea and old silk.
events.arc: The Embassy That Never Left

choices.text: Sit in the chair

effects.log: The table fills with pale figures, passing dishes that are not there. A soft murmur of dinner conversation rises.

choices.text: Pour tea into the cup before the chair

effects.log: Steam rises. The cup is lifted by an unseen hand, and set down again, emptied.

choices.text: Bow to the table and leave

effects.log: You walk out with a feeling of having kept an old appointment.

events.text: The pale guests turn to you, politely. One of them, a figure in an ambassador's hat, leans toward you and murmurs: "Tell us, how did it end?" They do not know the war is over, or who won, or that the court is gone. They ask like children.
events.arc: The Embassy That Never Left

choices.text: Tell them honestly, gently, the whole story

effects.log: You tell it for an hour. When you finish, the figures stand and bow, and fade into the lamp-light.

choices.text: Tell them it ended well, and that the court is at peace

effects.log: The figures smile, relieved. The table slowly empties. It is a kindness that may or may not be true.

choices.text: Say you do not know

effects.log: The ambassador nods, sadly. "Neither do we," they say.

events.text: The hall is silent the next dawn. The table is empty, the cards blank. A single lantern burns in the doorway. You blow it out, and the roof sighs, and settles. The ruin is just a ruin now, and a rather beautiful one.
events.arc: The Embassy That Never Left

choices.text: Leave a wreath at the doorway

effects.log: It is an ordinary wreath of cloud-lilies. It stays fresh for a year.

choices.text: Keep the Honourable Guest's card

effects.log: It is blank now. In a certain light, a name appears.

events.text: You need a pass to the High Market. Rogues are not issued passes. {npc}, a registrar of the Ministry of Precedence, sits behind a desk of cloud-oak. "There is a procedure," {he} says without looking up. "It is not written down. I do not recommend it."
events.arc: Earning a Pass Without a Seal

choices.text: Ask what the procedure is

effects.log: {He} sighs. "Three witnesses, a year's residence, a letter of character, a fee, and a favour owed." The list is a wall.

choices.text: Offer a small bribe

effects.log: {He} lifts a hand. "Absolutely not. That is a different procedure, and a much longer one."

choices.text: Thank {him} and walk away

effects.log: {He} nods, and goes back to {his} forms.

events.text: You collect three witnesses over a year: the hut-keeper, a ferry pilot, a vendor in the market. They write you glowing letters. {npc} reads each and sets them aside with the weariness of a man who has seen a hundred such stacks.
events.arc: Earning a Pass Without a Seal

choices.text: Add a letter of your own, of honest character

effects.log: You write the truth, short and plain. {npc} reads it twice.

choices.text: Ask the witnesses to appear in person

effects.log: They cram into the registry in their patched coats. The room smells of cloud-tea and rain. {npc} blinks at them.

choices.text: Wait out the residence period

effects.log: A year of waiting. You earn nothing but patience.

events.text: {npc} stamps the pass at last: a small square of jade with a number. "It is good for ten years," {he} says. "I would not apply again. The favour owed is that you not tell others how." {He} almost smiles. "They would clog the desk."
events.arc: Earning a Pass Without a Seal

choices.text: Keep the secret and use the pass

effects.log: The High Market is a wonder, and you walk through it humbly. The pass is a quiet marvel.

choices.text: Tell other rogues the procedure, quietly

effects.log: A handful learn and pass. The desk is, for a month, very busy. {npc} sighs and does not tell.

events.text: {npc} writes to you, in the ten-year gap, a short note: "The stack has grown. More rogues apply. I have begun to stamp the passes faster. It is, I find, easier than not." A pass is enclosed, unrequested.
events.arc: Earning a Pass Without a Seal

choices.text: Write back a letter of thanks

effects.log: You exchange letters for twenty years. The registry changes, slowly, from within.

choices.text: Return the pass in person, with tea

effects.log: {He} is stunned, then grateful. {He} pours you tea. The desk has a second chair now.

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion's chart shows a constellation, the Heron, that no one has seen in the sky for three hundred years. {npc}, a mapper, has been trying to find it. "It did not fall," {he} says. "It hid."
events.arc: The Constellation That Went Missing

choices.text: Spend a season mapping the dark patches

effects.log: You find a hollow in the sky where the Heron should be. Its stars are black, not gone.

choices.text: Read the Pavilion's oldest charts

effects.log: The Heron is described as "shy, bright in spring". It has not been seen since the war.

choices.text: Wish {npc} luck and go to bed

effects.log: {He} sighs. "The sky is patient. So am I," {he} says.

events.text: You and {npc} track the black patch to its edge, a ring of dim stars that lean away from you when you look directly. You realise: the Heron is shy. It does not like to be stared at. It will only come out if no one is watching.
events.arc: The Constellation That Went Missing

choices.text: Turn your back and look at the patch with the corner of your eye

effects.log: You glimpse a faint trace of wings, a stir of light, a heron lowering its neck.

choices.text: Build a hide of black silk and wait inside

effects.log: You wait three nights. On the third, a faint gleam seeps in at the edge of the cloth.

choices.text: Leave a cup of milk on the observatory roof

effects.log: The milk is untouched. You feel obscurely foolish.

events.text: The Heron steps out of the dark on a night of no moon. Seven stars, bright and long-necked, one wing slowly lifting. {npc} nearly drops the lens. "It is real," {he} whispers. "We have found a shy thing, and must not frighten it."
events.arc: The Constellation That Went Missing

choices.text: Watch in silence and tell no one

effects.log: The Heron stays for an hour. You and {npc} keep the secret for the rest of your lives.

choices.text: Chart the Heron for the Pavilion

effects.log: The chart is displayed with a plaque: "Seen by arrangement." The Heron appears once a decade.

events.text: The Heron returns each spring for a night. You and {npc} keep the date and the dark. Over decades, other mappers learn it: a small, quiet circle who believe in shy stars. They call themselves the Corner-Eyed.
events.arc: The Constellation That Went Missing

choices.text: Join the Corner-Eyed

effects.log: You attend their yearly dark-vigils. The Heron is a friend. The circle is a family.

choices.text: Write the Heron's story as a children's book

effects.log: It is read to a hundred generations. The Heron, you imagine, blushes.

events.text: A cave in the cliff-face answers questions for a price: one question, one memory. The cave takes the memory, but only the one you offer. A line of customers waits, thoughtful. A sign: "Please bring a memory you can spare."

choices.text: Offer a small memory and ask a small question

effects.log: The cave takes a childhood afternoon. It answers: "Yes." You wonder, for a long time, what you asked.

choices.text: Watch the line and learn from the customers

effects.log: Some leave smiling, some in tears. You go home with a heavy, pleasant head.

events.text: A courtyard in a ruin catches rain in a hundred stone basins, a custom of the old court. Each basin is named for a person. The rain falls into them even when the sky is clear. They sing, faintly, when you touch the rim.

choices.text: Touch a basin and listen

effects.log: It sings a note you half know. You carry it a week.

choices.text: Name an empty basin for someone you miss

effects.log: The rain falls into it all evening. By morning it is full.

events.text: A cloud-climber, a thin old person with rope and chalk, scales the underside of a hanging isle for no reason but the joy of it. They invite you to try. The handholds are of root and cloud-stone. The view, from the bottom, is the whole sky.

choices.text: Climb with them for an hour

effects.log: Your arms ache. Your heart is full. The sky at the bottom is a roomy, bright place.

choices.text: Hold the rope from the top

effects.log: They shout down a joke every minute. You laugh, and tighten the rope, and trust.

events.text: You follow the trail of a silver hare across a meadow of white flowers. It leaves no tracks but a scent, like moonlight on tea. After an hour it sits on a stone and looks back at you, ears twitching, as if waiting for a verdict.

choices.text: Sit across from the hare and say nothing

effects.log: It washes its face and nods. You part friends.

choices.text: Offer a cabbage leaf

effects.log: It sniffs, takes it, and bounds off. A moment later, it returns with a daisy.

events.text: A moss-ox carries a small garden on its back, with herbs, a bench, and a sleeping cat. It plods across the cloud-plain like a slow green island. You are invited, by a nod of the great head, to sit. The ox hums all the way.

choices.text: Sit in the herb-garden and ride

effects.log: The ride takes the whole afternoon. The cat wakes once, regards you, and returns to sleep.

choices.text: Walk beside the ox and pick herbs

effects.log: You fill a pouch with mint and thyme. The ox patiently waits at each stop.

events.text: Every full moon, the lake on a high isle rises a hand-breadth, a gentle swell of silver, and recedes. Boat-folk row out to the middle and drink tea in the moonlight. They speak of nothing. The lake keeps its own counsel.

choices.text: Row out and drink tea in the silver

effects.log: The moonlight tastes of nothing and everything. You feel unburdened.

choices.text: Watch from the shore and sketch

effects.log: The sketch is poor. The memory is perfect.

events.text: A bridge of glass crosses a gap of two days' drift. It is perfectly clear. Walkers say the first step is the hardest. Beneath the bridge, nothing, for miles. In the middle, a bench, and a person already sitting, knitting.

choices.text: Cross to the middle and sit by the knitter

effects.log: They hand you a ball of wool and a needle. You make a very bad scarf. You treasure it.

choices.text: Walk straight across, eyes up

effects.log: It takes an hour. The far side is an ordinary lane. You feel enormously brave.

events.text: The Thousand Steps climb from the cloud-sea to a high shrine, and every step bears a name carved by a pilgrim. Most are unreadable. A few are fresh. You find the step where an old friend cut theirs, centuries ago, and sit on it.

choices.text: Sit on your friend's step and rest

effects.log: You think of them for an hour. The shrine bell rings, high above.

choices.text: Carve your own name on a fresh step

effects.log: It takes the afternoon. Someone, someday, will sit on it.

events.text: A lodge on a windy peak keeps one window open all year. The keeper says it is so the wind can come in and warm itself. In winter the wind comes in and sits by the fire, and tea is poured for it, and no one speaks, out of respect.

choices.text: Pour a cup for the wind

effects.log: The cup is empty in a breath. The room smells of pine and distance.

choices.text: Sit by the fire and keep the wind company

effects.log: It leaves at dawn with a little swirl. You feel visited.

events.text: In the high meadows, cloud-cotton grows in white drifts, and pickers walk the rows with sacks. It is soft, weightless, and warm. Pickers sing as they work. A visitor is welcomed with a sack and a song.

choices.text: Join the pickers and learn the song

effects.log: It has eleven verses. You get through nine and are cheered.

choices.text: Pick quietly and take a small pouch home

effects.log: The cotton warms your bed all winter.

events.text: In a quiet cove the glow-fish rise at dusk, hundreds of tiny lanterns drifting upward from the cloud. A young fisher sits on the pier counting them aloud. They get to 312 and begins again, always with the same cheer.

choices.text: Count along with the young fisher

effects.log: You reach 312 together and the young fisher hoots with joy. They let you lead the next round.

choices.text: Leave a coin for the young fisher and watch the lights

effects.log: The young fisher bows. The glow-fish sink back into the dark.

events.text: Caught in a squall, you duck into a cloud-shelter built by someone kind: a bench, a roof, a lamp, a pot of dried tea-leaves, a note: "Take shelter. Leave dry wood." There is a stack of dry wood. You add to it.

choices.text: Wait out the squall and leave dry wood

effects.log: The squall passes in an hour. You feel part of a long chain of strangers.

choices.text: Boil a pot of tea for whoever comes next

effects.log: You leave it warm under a cloth. You hope for a wanderer.

events.text: On a rolling isle, a ring of tall standing stones leans slightly inward, as if gossiping. When the wind is right, you can hear them whisper. The words are mostly the names of weather. Children dance among them on festival days.

choices.text: Stand in the ring and listen

effects.log: You hear: "Mizzle. Haar. Drizzle. Flurry. Squall." A weather-poem.

choices.text: Join the children in the dance

effects.log: It is a quick, silly dance. The stones lean closer.

events.text: A lotus floats on a pond, each petal a faint pinprick of light, a miniature star-field. It opens at midnight and closes at dawn. A hermit tends the pond and charges nothing, asking only that visitors say one kind thing to the flower.

choices.text: Say a kind thing to the lotus

effects.log: It brightens. You feel, absurdly, that you have been heard.

choices.text: Sit with the hermit and share tea

effects.log: The hermit talks about lotuses for three hours. You do not mind.

events.text: The inn at the very Edge keeps a sign: "Last Stop. First Stop." The innkeeper is jolly and unflappable. They serve a single soup, and it is always right. Their guestbook has every kind of handwriting, and one page that is blank on purpose.

choices.text: Eat the soup and sign the guestbook

effects.log: You write one line. It is the most honest line you have written in decades.

choices.text: Leave the blank page blank

effects.log: The innkeeper nods. "Most do," they say.

events.text: An isle holds a festival of mismatched socks. Every attendant brings one sock and finds its partner, or a partner of their own. The matches are made by lot and laughter. The prize is a pair of mismatched socks. It is the best-attended festival in the sky.

choices.text: Bring a sock and find its mate

effects.log: Your partner is a fine old person with a matching sense of humour. You become friends.

choices.text: Judge the oddest match

effects.log: It is a sock and a mitten. You award first prize. The crowd cheers.

events.text: A seller at the cloud market offers rainbows by the span: a hand's width of arc, wrapped in tissue. Customers hang them in windows. The seller admits the rainbows lose their colour in a year. "That is what makes them worth having," they say.

choices.text: Buy a span and hang it

effects.log: It glows through winter. In spring it is a pale smear. You have never been happier.

choices.text: Haggle by telling the seller a joke

effects.log: The seller laughs and lowers the price to a smile.

events.text: At the court gate a young guard checks seals with great care and pomp. For a rogue they have rehearsed a special form of words: "I regret to inform you, honoured guest, that entry is not permitted." They deliver it as if reading a poem. It is a little sad and a little funny.

choices.text: Thank the guard for the elegant refusal

effects.log: The guard blinks, then blushes. That line has had a lot of practice.

choices.text: Ask the guard to teach you the phrase

effects.log: You learn it, and use it, years later, to a bore at a party.

events.text: The cook of a hanging inn makes storm-soup only when thunder is near. The broth is charged with static; it crackles in the bowl and tingles on the tongue. The cook swears it cures every ailment but loneliness. A bowl is half a stone.

choices.text: Order the soup and listen to it crackle

effects.log: It tingles all the way down. You feel awake for a week.

choices.text: Ask the cook about loneliness

effects.log: The cook sits with you and tells of the inn at midnight. It is not a cure, but it is soup.

events.text: In the Archive of Weathers, a diary lies open on a stand, kept by a clerk for a thousand years. It records only the weather and a single line of mood: "Fog, subdued." "Sun, bright, somewhat vain." "Hail, absurd." Visitors may add a line.

choices.text: Add a line for today's weather

effects.log: You write: "Mist, thoughtful." You are very proud of it.

choices.text: Read a year at random

effects.log: It was a calm year, mostly. The mood of the clerk improved by autumn.

events.text: A spring on a mild isle is said to make you sleepy if you listen to it for too long. The pilgrims come with blankets and are asleep within the quarter hour. The hermit who tends the place is awake; they stuff their ears with wax and wave.

choices.text: Listen to the spring for a short while, then leave

effects.log: You nod off for ten minutes, wake refreshed, and leave a coin in the bowl.

choices.text: Join the pilgrims for a long sleep

effects.log: You dream of a field of silver wheat. It is a good dream.

events.text: A traveller passes on the road with a pack, a stick, and the air of someone content to be nowhere in particular. They stop to share a flask of tea, ask your name, forget it, and ask again with equal pleasure. They are the best company of the year.

choices.text: Share a stretch of road with the traveller

effects.log: You walk a day together. You will not see them again, and you do not mind.

choices.text: Exchange a story and part

effects.log: You tell yours. They tell theirs. Both are better for the trade.

events.text: The tea-house pond on a quiet isle holds forty cloud carp, and they surface only when someone nearby speaks truly. {npc} keeps the pond and swears it is a nuisance: "Say one polite lie and the whole pond sinks." {He} bets nobody can feed them a full meal.
events.arc: The Carp Who Rise for Truth

choices.text: Speak only plain truths at the water

effects.log: Forty mouths break the surface. It is the most embarrassing quarter hour of your life, and the carp love it.

choices.text: Ask {npc} why the carp are so strict

effects.log: {He} goes quiet. "They came with my mother. My mother never lied once, and it did the family no good."

choices.text: Drink your tea and let the carp sulk

effects.log: The pond stays dark. A very old carp glares up at you from the weeds.

events.text: Feeding goes well until {npc} asks you a plain question: do you think the pond is worth keeping? The carp wait. The honest answer is complicated, and the water is already rippling.
events.arc: The Carp Who Rise for Truth

choices.text: Say the pond is worth more than the tea-house around it

effects.log: The whole pond rises as one. {npc} turns away, wiping an eye with a sleeve.

choices.text: Say it is a burden, and say it kindly

effects.log: The carp rise, slowly, and the oldest one nudges {npc}'s boot. Truth is not unkind to them.

choices.text: Say you do not know

effects.log: A single small carp surfaces, blinking. It is enough.

events.text: {npc} wants to sell the pond to a collector who will give three hundred stones and a promise. The carp, {he} says, would be kept in a crystal tank and fed at fixed hours. {He} asks what you would do.
events.arc: The Carp Who Rise for Truth

choices.text: Tell {him} to refuse and offer to help with the tea-house costs

effects.log: You give a hundred stones toward the roof. The carp surface the day you hand them over.

choices.text: Suggest {he} lets the carp choose

effects.log: You carry a bowl of pond water to the collector. The carp rise for no one there. The deal dies quietly.

choices.text: Say nothing and leave it to {him}

effects.log: You sit in the garden until the tea goes cold.

events.text: The pond is yours in all but name: {npc} leaves you the key, the tea set and a note saying only "Be honest." The carp rise at your step and stay all evening. Seasons pass, and the pond becomes known as the one place on the isle where no one lies.
events.arc: The Carp Who Rise for Truth

choices.text: Keep the pond and speak truly there for a century

effects.log: It is not easy. It is restful, in the end.

choices.text: Open the pond to anyone who wishes to confess a small truth

effects.log: The queue is long on the first day and longer on the second. The carp rise for every one.

events.text: The collector finds another pond. The carp keep rising. In the autumn {npc} hangs a small sign on the gate: "Please bring only what you mean." It is quoted on three isles by spring.
events.arc: The Carp Who Rise for Truth

choices.text: Add your name to the sign as the one who taught the pond a new kindness

effects.log: The carp surface when anyone reads it aloud.

choices.text: Leave the sign as it is

effects.log: It needs nothing more.

events.text: Every dusk, star-moths gather on a lonely mooring post where one lamp burns for all who never came home from the war. {npc} tends it. "Oil costs more every year," {he} says. "The moths do not mind. They are only here for the warmth." {He} asks if you would carry a flask.
events.arc: The Moths Who Keep a Lamp

choices.text: Buy a flask of lamp-oil (2 spirit stones)

effects.log: The oil is clear and smells of pine. {npc} pours it with both hands.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} and watch the moths settle

effects.log: They come down in a slow cloud, silver on the post, wings barely moving.

choices.text: Say you will think about it

effects.log: You walk on. The lamp is still in your mind an hour later.

events.text: {npc} tells you how the moths found the lamp: the first night, a ship lost in fog fired a single flare and a cloud of moths rose to meet it. The ship found the post by following them. Since then, no ship has failed to find it. {He} has kept the log of every landing.
events.arc: The Moths Who Keep a Lamp

choices.text: Offer to copy the log into jade slips

effects.log: Three months of evenings. The slips are filed at the Ministry of Fog under "keep".

choices.text: Ask what happens if the lamp goes dark

effects.log: {He} shrugs. "The moths will go. And the post will be only a post." It sounds like a plea.

choices.text: Say the log is a fine thing

effects.log: {He} nods. It is a very quiet compliment.

events.text: A hard winter drives most of the moths to warmer isles, and {npc} sits alone at the post with a thin flame. The few moths left cluster near {his} shoulder. {He} asks, almost shyly, whether the log should be handed on to someone when {he} is gone.
events.arc: The Moths Who Keep a Lamp

choices.text: Take the keeping of the lamp yourself

effects.log: You move into the hut by the post. In spring the moths come back in a silver tide.

choices.text: Find a young steersman to share the post

effects.log: A girl called Jin takes it on. {npc} teaches Jin the oil, the log and the quiet.

choices.text: Say you will visit every year

effects.log: You do. The lamp is always lit.

events.text: The moths do not mind who keeps the lamp. They mind that it is kept. You learn their habits: they gather an hour before a storm, a day before a death, and the night before the first ship home in a season. The post becomes a little weather-sign for the isles around it.
events.arc: The Moths Who Keep a Lamp

choices.text: Write the moths' signs on a board at the post

effects.log: Steersmen come to read it before sailing. Not one has lost a ship since.

choices.text: Keep the signs to yourself and the moths

effects.log: It is a private happiness, the best of its kind.

events.text: Jin keeps the lamp with the wild patience of the young. {npc} sits in a chair nearby with a rug over {his} knees and corrects the trimming, and the moths, who cannot be flattered, come anyway. At the end of the season, {he} sends you a jar of silver dust and a note: "Jin is better than I was."
events.arc: The Moths Who Keep a Lamp

choices.text: Keep the jar on your shelf

effects.log: It glimmers faintly at dusk. You do not open it.

choices.text: Pour a little on the lamp for luck

effects.log: The flame turns pale blue for a moment and settles. Moths drift in from three isles away.

events.text: A wind serpent has shed its skin across the rigging of a drifted wreck: forty paces of translucent silk that still holds a faint gale in its folds. {npc} found it first and wants to sell it to a sailmaker. "Skins like this raise a sail without a wind," {he} says.
events.arc: The Skin the Wind Serpent Left

choices.text: Help {npc} carry the skin to the sailmaker

effects.log: It moves in your arms like a sleeping wave. The sailmaker offers sixty stones.

choices.text: Warn {npc} that a serpent without its skin is cold and angry

effects.log: You have heard it from old pilots. {He} frowns but listens.

choices.text: Admire the skin and leave it be

effects.log: It rises slightly in the evening air, as if to wave.

events.text: Three nights after the sale, the air around the skiffers' isle turns bitter. A great pale shape circles the mooring posts at dawn, shivering, its scales dull. It has come for what it lost. {npc} hides in the hut.
events.arc: The Skin the Wind Serpent Left

choices.text: Go out to the serpent with a bolt of warm cloth

effects.log: It stills when you lay the cloth across its neck. The serpent studies you with a green eye.

choices.text: Offer to buy the skin back from the sailmaker

effects.log: It costs seventy stones. You carry the skin to the shore yourself.

choices.text: Keep clear and let the serpent circle

effects.log: It circles till noon and leaves. The cold lingers in the beams for a week.

events.text: The serpent takes the skin and wraps it round itself with a long slow shudder, and the colour comes back into its scales. It does not leave. It coils on the mooring post and looks at you, then at {npc}, then at the sky. A gale rises from nowhere and fills every sail on the isle.
events.arc: The Skin the Wind Serpent Left

choices.text: Ask the serpent to ferry a boat across the cloud-sea

effects.log: It rides beside the skiff all the way, a bright slow ribbon of wind.

choices.text: Let it rest on the post for the season

effects.log: It stays three months. Skiffers leave offerings and no one is ever lost in fog again.

events.text: The skin is cut into sails by a sailmaker who says nothing of its source. A year later {npc} comes to you ashen: a ship in the fleet went down in a calm. "The skin wants to go home," {he} says. "They always do." The sails strain at every mooring and will not be reefed.
events.arc: The Skin the Wind Serpent Left

choices.text: Cut the sails free and let them fly

effects.log: They lift into the sky like pale birds and wheel south. {npc} watches with a long exhale.

choices.text: Pay the sailmaker for the lost cloth and bring the remainder to the serpent

effects.log: It takes the offering and leaves a single scale on the dock. It is warm to the touch.

events.text: A stall in the silk lane sells a single bolt of cloud-silk, woven on the day of the longest noon and said to remember it. Hold it, and the cloth grows warm and bright. {npc}, the weaver's daughter, will not sell it, only lend it for a night. "It was my mother's last," {he} says.
events.arc: The Bolt That Remembers a Day

choices.text: Borrow the bolt for a night

effects.log: It glows gold in your hands. By dawn you remember a noon you never lived: a woman laughing at a loom.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to tell you about the day

effects.log: {He} says the weaver wove with the window open and let the whole noon in.

choices.text: Buy a cheap yard of ordinary silk instead

effects.log: It is nice, it is plain, it keeps the dust off.

events.text: The bolt's noon has a hole in it, a small cold place in the weave where the light does not go. {npc} says the old weaver ran out of thread on the last row and finished with a single strand of grey. "It was for the grief that comes later, {he} said," {he} says.
events.arc: The Bolt That Remembers a Day

choices.text: Offer to find a thread of matching gold

effects.log: You search three stalls. The gold you find is almost right, and {npc} will not use it.

choices.text: Say the grey thread belongs where it is

effects.log: {He} breathes out. "That is what the old weaver told me."

choices.text: Run a thumb along the grey strand

effects.log: The cloth is cool there, and then, strangely, warm.

events.text: A buyer comes for the bolt: a ministry collector, polite and patient, with a purse of two hundred stones. {npc} turns white. {He} does not want to sell, but the stall has not paid its rent in three months.
events.arc: The Bolt That Remembers a Day

choices.text: Pay the stall's rent yourself (6 spirit stones)

effects.log: It is a small sum next to what the bolt is worth to {him}. The collector bows and withdraws.

choices.text: Introduce {npc} to the Nine Clouds for a fair commission

effects.log: The dawn silk looms take the weaver on as a teacher. The bolt stays in the family.

choices.text: Let {npc} decide alone

effects.log: {npc} sits a long time, and does not sell.

events.text: The grey strand is mentioned in the silk-lane guide, after that: a bolt of the longest noon, with its small cold place that grows warm when held. People come to it on the anniversary of their own losses. {npc} keeps the bolt on a rail by the stall and lets them touch it.
events.arc: The Bolt That Remembers a Day

choices.text: Add a thread of your own to the hem

effects.log: You choose a pale blue. {npc} sews it with {his} own needle.

choices.text: Visit each year with a small gift of tea

effects.log: It becomes a habit and then a friendship.

events.text: {npc} has sold bottled winds for four hundred years: a breeze for a baker's sails, a gale for a feast, a hush for a mourner. Now {he} is retiring, and {his} shelves hold nine bottles that have never been opened. "Each one is a promise I could not keep," {he} says. "Take one if you will carry its promise."
events.arc: The Last Bottles of the Wind Merchant

choices.text: Choose the smallest bottle

effects.log: It hums faintly. {npc} writes your name on its label and a single word: "kindness."

choices.text: Ask what the promises were

effects.log: {He} reads them aloud, slowly: a lullaby, an apology, a farewell, six others.

choices.text: Decline and buy a pinch of ordinary breeze

effects.log: The breeze is cool and smells of rain.

events.text: The smallest bottle is a lullaby, bottled for a child that grew up before it could be delivered. The child, {npc} says, is now a ferry captain on the Third Reach, white-haired and gruff. Will you carry it there?
events.arc: The Last Bottles of the Wind Merchant

choices.text: Sail to the Third Reach and find the captain

effects.log: It takes nine days. The captain is asleep on the deck. You uncork the bottle gently.

choices.text: Leave the bottle at the ferry office with a note

effects.log: It is delivered by a clerk. You never learn how it was received.

choices.text: Keep the bottle and hum the lullaby yourself

effects.log: It is not the same. It is kind.

events.text: The captain wakes in a light you cannot describe. {npc} says nothing for a long time, and then: "My nurse used to hum that." A hand comes up and pats the cork, then the bottle, then your sleeve. The ferry rocks gently in a wind from nowhere.
events.arc: The Last Bottles of the Wind Merchant

choices.text: Stay for the evening crossing

effects.log: The captain tells you of a hundred storms, a hundred passengers, and one lullaby.

choices.text: Let the captain have the quiet

effects.log: You slip off at the next mooring. The wind follows you for a mile.

events.text: {npc} asks you to take a second bottle. The apology, {he} says, was meant for an old rival, and the rival is dead. The wind should go, therefore, to the rival's grave. It is a long way. {He} has a kind of ache around the eyes.
events.arc: The Last Bottles of the Wind Merchant

choices.text: Carry the apology to the grave

effects.log: The isle is empty save a stone and a few gulls. You open the bottle. The gulls rise.

choices.text: Say the grave is as well served by silence

effects.log: {He} sighs and nods. The bottle goes back on the shelf.

events.text: You buy a steersman's compass at a salvage stall and discover it does not point to your home. It points, steadily, at somewhere you have never been. The old steersman Ohwa, who sold it, goes grey. "That was my daughter's," {he} says. "{He} did not take it when {he} left."
events.arc: The Compass That Points to a Stranger's Home

choices.text: Follow the needle across three isles

effects.log: It is a long road. The needle never wavers, except once, at a bridge, where it dips toward the ground.

choices.text: Ask {npc} where the daughter went

effects.log: {He} does not know. It is why {he} sold the compass: so it would stop pointing at nothing.

choices.text: Put it away unopened

effects.log: The needle trembles in the pocket for a week.

events.text: The needle ends at a small mooring on the Bamboo Reach: a house with blue shutters and a girl on the step, perhaps nine years old, who stares at the compass and says, "That is my mother's." The mother, it turns out, is {npc}'s daughter, who died in the spring.
events.arc: The Compass That Points to a Stranger's Home

choices.text: Give the girl the compass

effects.log: The girl holds it close. The needle points at the girl's heart, and then steadies, pointing at the door.

choices.text: Offer to take the girl to meet the old steersman

effects.log: The girl nods without a word and packs a small bag.

choices.text: Sit on the step for an hour

effects.log: The girl brings you a cup of cold barley tea and sits too.

events.text: {npc} is waiting at the mooring when the skiff comes in. {He} does not say anything. {He} kneels, and the girl puts {his} arms round {his} neck. The compass in {his} hand points steadily at the old steersman, and does not move again.
events.arc: The Compass That Points to a Stranger's Home

choices.text: Stay for the evening meal

effects.log: {He} cooks fish and ginger. The house is warm.

choices.text: Slip away and leave them to it

effects.log: You are three isles away before you notice you are smiling.

events.text: The girl keeps the compass in the blue-shuttered house, and Ohwa visits on every holiday. A letter comes to you in the autumn: "The needle now points to a new place each month. The girl says it is following the person loved most. I think it is simply tired." It is signed with a small drawing of a compass.
events.arc: The Compass That Points to a Stranger's Home

choices.text: Write back with a map of the places it might lead

effects.log: The girl pins it to the wall. It is a treasure chart for years.

choices.text: Keep the letter

effects.log: It is a small, odd thing, and it makes you happy.

events.text: At the lowest ebb of the cloud-sea the reefs show their gardens: pale blooms that open for one hour and are worth twenty stones a basket. The Pickers' Guild holds the picking rights. {npc}, a guild picker, offers to take you down in {his} skiff at the ebb, if you can keep up and keep quiet.
events.arc: The Reef-Bloom Pickers

choices.text: Go down with the guild at dawn

effects.log: The reef is a garden of white spires. {npc} points to the best patches, and you pick until your arms ache.

choices.text: Ask about the rules of the picking rights

effects.log: {He} lists them. They run to eleven clauses, nine of which seem designed to keep newcomers out.

choices.text: Watch from the cliff above

effects.log: The bloom opens like a slow white sigh, across the whole reef at once.

events.text: The reef shows something under the blooms: a hull, half buried in coral, with the lantern of a lost ship still hanging on its mast. {npc} stops picking. "The guild says it is off limits," {he} says. "It is a grave. Do you want to see it?"
events.arc: The Reef-Bloom Pickers

choices.text: Go to the wreck and leave a lantern-offering

effects.log: A single candle in a paper boat. The wreck rocks slightly.

choices.text: Tell the guild so they can mark it

effects.log: The marshals put up a post. The wreck is left in peace.

choices.text: Leave the wreck and go on picking

effects.log: You pick fast now, and a little less happily.

events.text: A guild warden stops you at the dock. Without a faction seal, {he} says, a picker's basket may not be sold at the guild stall. {He} is polite about it, which makes it worse. {npc} stands behind you, jaw set.
events.arc: The Reef-Bloom Pickers

choices.text: Sell the baskets to a back-lane dealer for half

effects.log: It is less, but it is clean.

choices.text: Argue the clause with the warden

effects.log: It takes an hour and a loophole. The warden sighs and stamps the sheet.

choices.text: Give the baskets to {npc} to sell under {his} seal

effects.log: {He} takes them without a word, and brings you your share, a day later, to the coin.

events.text: The Pickers' Guild offers you a seat on its board for the good of the reef. It is real power, and a small chain of obligations. {npc} says nothing, but watches your face, as the bloom watches the sun.
events.arc: The Reef-Bloom Pickers

choices.text: Accept and push for open rights

effects.log: The first meeting ends in shouting. The second ends in a vote. It passes by one.

choices.text: Decline and keep picking at your own pace

effects.log: You are a free picker with a basket and a good friend.

events.text: The post at the wreck is hung with ribbons by the next ebb. The guild adds a line to its rules: no picking within a boat's length of a grave. {npc} says it is the shortest clause on the sheet and the only one {he} respects.
events.arc: The Reef-Bloom Pickers

choices.text: Add a ribbon of your own

effects.log: It is blue. The reef wind catches it at once.

choices.text: Tell the story at the guild hall

effects.log: A few pickers nod. One of them takes off a cap.

events.text: A skiff caught in the great storm is pulled into its eye, and the sky goes silent. In the calm stands a floating market of a hundred stalls, lit by lanterns, with no one to explain it. The stallholders look up with relief, as if they had been waiting for a customer.
events.arc: The Market in the Eye of the Storm

choices.text: Walk the market and ask who runs it

effects.log: The stallholders answer in turn: "We came in for shelter. The storm is our landlord."

choices.text: Buy a bowl of soup and listen

effects.log: It is hot and good. A woman at the next stall tells you the market has been in the eye for sixty years.

choices.text: Ask the nearest stallholder how to leave

effects.log: They point at the wall of cloud and shrug.

events.text: The stalls sell things that exist only in the eye: a bottle of silence, a coil of still air, a lantern that burns white. Prices are strange. A stallholder will take a memory of rain in payment, or a good joke.
events.arc: The Market in the Eye of the Storm

choices.text: Trade a memory of rain for a bottle of silence

effects.log: The rain leaves you for a moment, a soft grey space. The silence you get is absolutely quiet.

choices.text: Pay in jokes and collect a coil of still air

effects.log: You tell your three best. The stallholder laughs at two, and the air goes into your pocket.

choices.text: Browse and buy nothing

effects.log: It is its own kind of pleasure, to wander a market unhurried.

events.text: The market is thinning; the eye is closing. The stallholders pack their lanterns without a word. Someone has to tell the new arrivals how the market works, and none of the oldest stallholders will. The old woman from the soup stall looks at you: "You have the face for it."
events.arc: The Market in the Eye of the Storm

choices.text: Stay and take over the old woman's stall for the next eye

effects.log: The old woman places a ladle in your hand. You are the market's newest keeper.

choices.text: Help carry the stalls to the next storm

effects.log: You haul bolts of silence by lantern light until the eye shifts.

choices.text: Slip out through the wall of cloud before it closes

ok.log: You skim the wall and come out into dry air, laughing.

fail.log: The wall tears at the skiff. You sail out limping, with a sprained wrist.

events.text: A year later you pass a storm on the horizon and feel an urge so strong that it has to be answered. You turn your skiff toward it. A lantern flickers inside the cloud. The market has found its next storm.
events.arc: The Market in the Eye of the Storm

choices.text: Sail in and take your old stall
