effects.log: The soup is already boiling. The old woman nods without looking up.

choices.text: Wave at the cloud and sail on

effects.log: A lantern bobs once, politely, and goes out.

events.text: The skiff is out of the storm at last, with a bottle of silence in the hold. When you open it in your own quiet room, the silence is full of tiny sounds: a leaf, a thread, a wing, a heartbeat. It is the quietest company you have ever had.
events.arc: The Market in the Eye of the Storm

choices.text: Keep the bottle on your desk and uncork it when you need to think

effects.log: It does not fail you once.

choices.text: Give the bottle to a friend who cannot sleep

effects.log: They sleep for ten hours and send you a pie.

events.text: The Hundred Posts is an isle of nothing but moorings: a hundred stout posts, and a ferry office. Every post has a boat, save the ninety-ninth, where a rope is tied to nothing. {npc}, the warden, says the rope was tied by a visitor long ago, and the boat never came. "I keep it taut," {he} says. "In case."
events.arc: Who Moors at Post Ninety-Nine

choices.text: Ask who tied the rope

effects.log: {He} shows a ledger. A name, a date, and "returning shortly" in a hasty hand, three hundred years old.

choices.text: Test the rope with your hand

effects.log: It is cold and heavy, as if the other end is held by something.

choices.text: Wish the warden a quiet season

effects.log: {He} nods. It is the most anyone has said to {him} in a month.

events.text: You haul gently on the rope. Something, very far off, answers with a tug. {npc} grips the post. The rope hums as if a long song were running down it. A dim lantern shows, miles out, hanging in the sky with no boat under it.
events.arc: Who Moors at Post Ninety-Nine

choices.text: Signal back with the post lantern

effects.log: Three flashes. The far lantern answers with three. {npc} is silent, then laughs.

choices.text: Take a skiff and sail toward the lantern

effects.log: You sail for six hours. The lantern never gets closer, but your skiff drifts as if pulled.

choices.text: Leave the rope and fetch the warden tea

effects.log: The two of you drink it on the dock, watching the light.

events.text: The lantern is a boat, after all, a very old one with all its sails furled and its crew asleep on deck. They are the rope-tier's crew, who sailed out on a mission and fell asleep in a becalmed reach, three hundred years ago. They wake slowly, and ask for the time.
events.arc: Who Moors at Post Ninety-Nine

choices.text: Tell them the date and the news of three centuries

effects.log: They listen like children at a story. The captain asks only about the harbour.

choices.text: Tow the boat to the ninety-ninth post

effects.log: It takes a day. The crew are cheering when the rope comes taut.

choices.text: Let them wake in peace and wave from afar

effects.log: The captain raises a hand. The boat turns itself home.

events.text: The crew of the ninety-ninth boat settles into the isle as if it had never been away. {npc} has two more mouths at {his} table, and a garden of ghosts and old stories. The captain proposes to run a ferry again, with the old boat, on the old route. The route no longer exists.
events.arc: Who Moors at Post Ninety-Nine

choices.text: Help them chart a new route

effects.log: You spend a month with the captain over a table of maps. The new route runs through six isles.

choices.text: Gift them the warden's ledger for a charter

effects.log: It is accepted by the Ministry of Fog without question.

events.text: Every year after, on the date the rope was tied, {npc} lights a lantern on the ninety-ninth post. The boat is there now, with its sails set. It sails and returns, as promised. On the post is carved: "Returned shortly."
events.arc: Who Moors at Post Ninety-Nine

choices.text: Carve your own initial beneath

effects.log: The warden approves, and adds a notch.

choices.text: Sit on the dock and watch the sails

effects.log: It is a good thing to see a promise kept.

events.text: The Ministry of Weather has lost a spring. Not a pool of water but a season: it was due on the Eastern Isles and never arrived, and the buds there sit shut. {npc}, a clerk of the filing hall, begs your help: the record exists, {he} says, but under the wrong heading.
events.arc: The Spring That Was Misfiled

choices.text: Search the files by season and by isle

effects.log: Three days of dusty shelves. You find a spring filed under "Autumn, delayed."

choices.text: Ask the weather-marshals what they last saw

effects.log: They remember a pale wind that smelled of plum. No more.

choices.text: Make tea for the overworked clerks

effects.log: It is received with gratitude and a stack of forms.

events.text: The spring was filed correctly after all. It has been collected in a jar, by mistake, and shelved with the autumn winds. The jar is warm and hums, and every moment it stays closed, the eastern buds suffer. Releasing it requires a seal, and the seal is held by the Minister of Precedence.
events.arc: The Spring That Was Misfiled

choices.text: Request the Minister's seal in the proper form

effects.log: It takes four forms and a long wait. The Minister stamps it, gently amused.

choices.text: Open the jar quietly in the filing hall

effects.log: Plum petals drift in the cold stacks. A clerk sneezes. The spring is out.

choices.text: Sit on the jar and consider the matter

effects.log: It is warm. You are patient.

events.text: The spring flows east in a ribbon of pale wind. Buds open on a hundred terraces. The Eastern Isles send a basket of plums and a letter of thanks. The Minister of Weather adds a line to the daily report: "Spring arrived late, correctly filed."
events.arc: The Spring That Was Misfiled

choices.text: Accept the plums and share them in the filing hall

effects.log: The clerks eat, wordless and happy. {npc} cries a little.

choices.text: Suggest a new filing rule for seasons

effects.log: It is adopted as Regulation Eleven. You are named in the preamble.

events.text: The spring in the hall, unauthorised, is a small scandal. The Minister of Precedence frowns at the plum petals on the floor, then at you. {npc} stands between you with {his} hands behind {his} back. "It was my filing," {he} says.
events.arc: The Spring That Was Misfiled

choices.text: Take the blame yourself

effects.log: A reprimand for you, a quiet pat for {npc}.

choices.text: Show the Minister the eastern buds from the window

effects.log: The Minister looks for a long time and says nothing. The reprimand is dropped.

events.text: Snow falls upward on the Frost Reaches, and a heron nests in it, grey on grey, its feathers each tipped with a spark of cold. {npc} wants a plume for {his} daughter's wedding cloak. "One feather, only one," {he} says. "It sheds them as the snow rises." {He} asks if you will track with {him}.
events.arc: The Heron of the Upward Snow

choices.text: Track the heron along the rising snow

effects.log: The flakes lead you in a rising spiral. The heron stands in the drift, on one leg, utterly still.

choices.text: Wait at the nest and watch the habit of the bird

effects.log: It preens at noon and drops a feather. You do not touch it.

choices.text: Warm your hands at a little fire

effects.log: {npc} grumbles, then sits too.

events.text: The heron knows it is hunted. It leads you to a ledge where the snow rises fastest and the wind is a knife. The feather, a long grey one, hangs on a thorn ten paces from the drop. {npc} reaches, and the ledge groans.
events.arc: The Heron of the Upward Snow

choices.text: Edge out and take the feather yourself

ok.log: You lift it clean from the thorn. The heron turns its head and lets you.

fail.log: The ledge shifts and you slip, catching the rock with one hand. The feather escapes upward.

choices.text: Tie a line to {npc} and let {him} reach

effects.log: {He} takes the feather in two attempts, shaking like a leaf.

choices.text: Pull {npc} back and leave the feather

effects.log: The wind drops. The heron preens again, unhurried.

events.text: The heron comes to {npc}'s wedding feast, uninvited, and stands in the doorway. It sheds a feather into the bride's cup. Nobody can say if it is a blessing, a theft or a joke. The bride laughs and drinks, and the cup glows grey for the whole night.
events.arc: The Heron of the Upward Snow

choices.text: Raise a glass to the heron

effects.log: It bows once and walks into the snow.

choices.text: Stay quiet and watch the glow

effects.log: It is the most beautiful wedding you have ever attended.

events.text: The heron does not shed another feather for forty years. {npc} comes to you as an old man with the wedding cloak across {his} arm. "My daughter says the feather has grown," {he} says. It has: a quill of pure grey, longer than a sword. You are asked to lay it on the nest in spring.
events.arc: The Heron of the Upward Snow

choices.text: Lay it at the nest at dawn

effects.log: The heron is there. It takes the quill in its beak and lays it in the drift.

choices.text: Give it back to {npc}

effects.log: {He} holds it a long time and says nothing.

events.text: With no isle and no faction, you mend ropes for a living. Every harbour has frayed lines, and a mender with a good eye and no pride can eat well. {npc}, a rigger on the Long Reach, says {he} has work for you if you do not mind {his} sharp tongue. {He} pays by the line.
events.arc: The Mender of Mooring Ropes

choices.text: Take the work and mend three lines before supper

effects.log: You are faster than {he} expected. {He} says nothing, but the stew is thick.

choices.text: Ask for a better price

effects.log: {He} glares, then halves the work and doubles the price. You mend six lines.

choices.text: Decline and move on to the next harbour

effects.log: The next harbour pays less and offers no stew.

events.text: Harbour guild riggers hold the mending trade for themselves. A guild-sealed man stops you at the dock and tells you, kindly and plainly, that a rope mended without a seal will not be insured. {npc} looks at the ground. "{He} is right," {he} says. "I would hire you, but I cannot insure it."
events.arc: The Mender of Mooring Ropes

choices.text: Offer to mend only lines the guild has condemned

effects.log: The guild-man pauses, then shrugs. It is a loophole nobody uses.

choices.text: Ask what a seal costs

effects.log: Forty stones and two years of apprenticeship. It is not a price, it is a wall.

choices.text: Mend the line in the dark where no one sees

effects.log: It is the best rope in the harbour, and no one will ever know.

events.text: You mend condemned lines for a season, and the harbour begins to notice that your old rope holds better than the guild's new. A skiff-owner pays you in advance for a year. {npc} brings you a little mallet with a worn handle. "It was my master's," {he} says.
events.arc: The Mender of Mooring Ropes

choices.text: Take the mallet and the work

effects.log: You mend your way along the Long Reach. A name goes round: the Condemned Mender.

choices.text: Offer to teach a guild apprentice the knot-stitch

effects.log: It is not allowed, strictly. It is done, quietly, behind the net shed.

events.text: The guild offers you a seat after all, with a forty-stone seal, waived, and a warm cap. It is a gesture. It is also a chain. {npc} says, softly, "You can say no, you know." You consider the harbour, the dock, the sky.
events.arc: The Mender of Mooring Ropes

choices.text: Take the seal and the cap

effects.log: You are an insured rigger. Your rope is the best in the Reach. Your freedom is a little narrower.

choices.text: Decline and keep mending condemned lines

effects.log: The harbour mutters. The work continues.

events.text: A cloud carp has settled in a bucket outside the noodle stall and will not leave. It rises each time the cook sings off-key, to listen. The cook is offended. The carp is delighted.

choices.text: Sing a few lines yourself

effects.log: The carp circles twice and goes under. It was a verdict.

choices.text: Slip the carp a crust and leave

effects.log: It nibbles with great dignity.

events.text: Carp in the Weir Pool are said to rise by the moon's phase: seven on the full, none on the dark. A boy on the bank has kept a tally for ten years and wants you to check the sums.

choices.text: Check the tally and add the missing nights

effects.log: It matches to the carp. The boy grins like sunrise.

choices.text: Tell the boy to keep counting

effects.log: The boy does, and writes you each new moon.

events.text: A swarm of star-moths has settled round a reader's lamp in the archive and will not be shooed. They read along, apparently. When the reader turns a page, they turn their wings.

choices.text: Read aloud, slowly, so they can follow

effects.log: They hold perfectly still for the whole chapter.

choices.text: Open the window and let them out

effects.log: They go reluctantly, trailing silver on the sill.

events.text: A tin of star-moth dust is sold in the Moon Lane as a cure for dull evenings. A hawker swears a pinch makes any room glow. The tin is half sawdust.

choices.text: Buy one and test it

effects.log: A faint silver in the dark, and a sneeze. Worth the single stone.

choices.text: Tell the crowd about the sawdust, gently

effects.log: The hawker curses you cheerfully and cuts the price.

events.text: A wind serpent calls from the Western Gap every sunset, a long low note that makes your ears ring. Pilots who answer it always have a fair wind. Pilots who do not rarely do.

choices.text: Hum the note back from the deck

effects.log: It answers, twice, softly. The sails fill.

choices.text: Stop your ears and sail on

effects.log: The wind is thin and sour all night.

events.text: A single wind-serpent scale lies on the dock, big as a plate, humming faintly. A child wants to know if it is lucky. The harbourmaster says it is, and also that it is someone else's.

choices.text: Help the child take it to the serpent's reach

effects.log: You set it on a cairn at the cliff edge. A coil of wind lifts it away.

choices.text: Leave it where it lies

effects.log: In the morning it is gone. The child is satisfied.

events.text: An old beam in the dock has a nail that has never rusted. A carpenter says it is star-iron, fallen long ago and used because nobody knew. Pulling it would take the beam with it.

choices.text: Leave the nail and tell the carpenter its worth

effects.log: The beam is now a local treasure.

choices.text: Buy the beam and the nail (3 spirit stones)

effects.log: The nail is star-iron, dense and cold. It is a handsome find.

events.text: In the ashes of a fallen star a boy sifts for star-iron grains and sells them by the pinch. The boy is hungry, honest and utterly alone with a sieve.

choices.text: Buy a pinch for the price of a meal

effects.log: The grains are real. The boy eats like a prince.

choices.text: Show the boy how to sift for the larger pieces

effects.log: The boy finds a nugget the size of a thumb, and smiles for a week.

events.text: A shop in the Fog Quarter sells a bottle of hush: the exact quiet of a snowfall at midnight. It costs two stones. The shopkeeper warns it should be opened only in anger.

choices.text: Buy the bottle (2 spirit stones)

effects.log: You keep it in your sleeve. Twice, since, you have almost opened it.

choices.text: Admire it and walk on

effects.log: The shopkeeper bows, unoffended.

events.text: At the rear of a wind stall, a bottle of old gust has been marked down because it is cranky and blows in the wrong direction. The vendor says it needs a kind home.

choices.text: Take the gust for one stone and open it on a ridge

effects.log: It blows backwards for a minute, then settles into a gentle breeze that follows you for a year.

choices.text: Leave it with the vendor

effects.log: It rattles its cork in protest.

events.text: At dawn the reef at the Edge turns pink for a minute, from the first light on the coral. A reef-keeper stands there daily and calls it the best minute of the day, and invites you to share it.

choices.text: Stand beside the keeper and watch

effects.log: It lasts exactly as long as promised.

choices.text: Come back every dawn for a week

effects.log: By the seventh, you are a little in love with a minute.

events.text: A reef-gardener plants cloud-coral in the shallows of a lagoon. It has not taken in three years. The gardener asks you to try a graft from your own isle.

choices.text: Graft a cutting from your isle

effects.log: It takes in a fortnight, to everyone's surprise.

choices.text: Advise the gardener to try the spring tide

effects.log: The gardener does. It works on the second try.

events.text: You pass through the eye of a small storm and the sky turns silent. A skiff drifts beside yours, its owner asleep at the tiller. The calm will last an hour.

choices.text: Rest too, until the wall closes

effects.log: You wake with the sun on your face and a clear mind.

choices.text: Steer the sleeper's skiff to safety

effects.log: They wake on a quiet mooring, flustered, and grateful.

events.text: The wall of the eye is a cliff of cloud, turning slowly, with lightning in its teeth. Your skiff is on the inside edge, and the calm is closing.

choices.text: Run for the gap on the lee side

effects.log: You thread it with a yard to spare. Your hands shake for an hour.

choices.text: Wait in the centre until it passes

effects.log: It takes a day. The skiff is dry, and you are bored.

events.text: A wreck turns slowly in the eye of the storm, held in the calm like a leaf on a pond. Its hold is full of crates marked with a seal you do not know.

choices.text: Search the crates carefully

effects.log: Most hold dried tea. One holds a bolt of silk and a note: "For whoever finds it."

choices.text: Leave it undisturbed and mark its place

effects.log: It is a grave, or a larder. You choose to leave it.

events.text: Hoofprints of an unknown stag cross a snowfield that falls upward. They end mid-field, as if the animal had simply taken to the air. A tracker beside you says it happens every winter.

choices.text: Follow the line of the print upward

effects.log: You lift your gaze and see antlers in the cloud, a long way up.

choices.text: Mark the spot for next winter

effects.log: You return and find fresh prints at the same place.

events.text: An anvil on a drifting rock has no smithy, no house and no owner, but its face is warm. Every few days a spark jumps from it to the air. A passing pilot says a smith is somewhere still working.

choices.text: Strike it once, lightly, with a stone

effects.log: It rings a clear note and the spark answers. Somewhere far away, a hammer rings back.

choices.text: Wrap it in cloth against the cold

effects.log: You feel foolish and kind.

events.text: A tailor in a back lane cuts cloth from fog and was taught, so the sign says, by the cloud itself. The price of a fog coat is the best story you know. The shop keeps a ledger of tales.

choices.text: Tell the tailor your best story

effects.log: The tailor listens, and the coat is warm for a month. Your tale goes at the top of a page.

choices.text: Admire the shop and leave

effects.log: The tailor waves from the doorway, smiling.

events.text: Without a seal, the reef-bloom stall will not sell to you at the posted price. The stallholder quotes you twice the rate, politely, and looks past you at the next customer.

choices.text: Pay the double rate this once

effects.log: It is galling. The bloom tea is good.

choices.text: Walk on and find an unmarked stall

effects.log: The back lane has one. It is cheaper and friendlier.

events.text: The guild bridge to the Cedar Isle has a toll for the unsealed: one stone to cross, and a stern look from the bridge-warden. Faction members walk free.

choices.text: Pay the stone and cross

effects.log: The warden nods, a bit embarrassed.

choices.text: Take the long ferry round

effects.log: It is a pleasant half day. You eat plums on deck.

events.text: The cloud-reef under Lantern Quay has begun to move, a hand's breadth a day, toward the south. The whole quay is moored to it. {npc}, the harbour-reeve, spreads a chart on a barrel: "In a year we are moored to nothing at all." {He} asks you to find out why it walks.
events.arc: The Reef That Walked Away

choices.text: Dive the reef with a line and a lamp

effects.log: The coral is warm and slow, and there are scratches in it like the marks of something dragging.

choices.text: Ask the old quay-wives what the reef did when they were girls

effects.log: They laugh: "It moved then, too, only slower." One produces a diary.

choices.text: Drink the reeve's tea and think it over

effects.log: The tea is stewed. The thought is a good one.

events.text: Under the reef hangs a crown of roots, and the roots are pulling, a patient inch at a time, toward a distant green smudge on the horizon: a young isle just risen from the deep cloud, bright with first grass. The reef is going to it, as a flower follows light.
events.arc: The Reef That Walked Away

choices.text: Tell the reeve the reef is following a new isle

effects.log: {He} stares at the green smudge. "Then it will not stop," {he} says.

choices.text: Cut a mooring to the new isle and test the pull

effects.log: The new line sings with tension. It will hold, but the reef will drag it.

choices.text: Watch the green smudge until dark

effects.log: It is lovely, and the reef is plainly in love with it.

events.text: The quay must decide: unmoor and follow the reef, or cut loose and drift. A meeting is called in the fish-hall, with shouting. {npc} asks you to speak, since you found the cause.
events.arc: The Reef That Walked Away

choices.text: Argue that the quay should follow the reef

effects.log: There is a long pause. A fishwife says, "My grandmother would have liked a new view." The vote carries.

choices.text: Argue that the quay should find a still reef

effects.log: It is a sensible plan and a sad one. It carries by two hands.

choices.text: Say that only the quay can choose

effects.log: The room goes quiet, and then sensibly noisy.

events.text: The quay moves in procession: forty houses on floats, eleven boats, a bell and a goat. It takes a month. The reef ahead sets the pace, patient, like a grandmother leading a school walk. At the green isle the new grass is waist-high and every child runs into it at once.
events.arc: The Reef That Walked Away

choices.text: Walk beside {npc} at the front

effects.log: {He} says little. Once, {he} touches the reef's coral as it passes. Once, {he} smiles.

choices.text: Ride at the back to mind the stragglers

effects.log: You carry two bundles, a cat and a shy old man on your shoulders. The goat refuses.

events.text: The quay finds a still reef at last, two weeks off to the east, and moors there. The old reef walks on without them toward its green isle. Every dusk the quay-folk light a lantern on the south pier. On the third year, a lantern answers from the horizon.
events.arc: The Reef That Walked Away

choices.text: Light a lantern with them each year

effects.log: The answering lantern is always there. No one speaks of it.

choices.text: Carry the story to the Ministry of Fog

effects.log: It becomes a footnote in a chart, and a legend in a harbour.

events.text: When a wind serpent crosses the Long Reach it leaves a wake of fast air, and young pilots ride it on their thinnest skiffs for the thrill. {npc} is the best of them, and the most reckless. {He} has a spare seat in a skiff the size of a canoe. "Afraid?" {he} asks.
events.arc: The Wake-Riders of the Serpent Run

choices.text: Take the seat

effects.log: The skiff leaps. For nine breathless minutes you ride the serpent's breath, and the world is a blur of silver.

choices.text: Ask to watch from the cliff first

effects.log: {He} grins and goes without you. From the cliff the ride looks like a thread pulled through the sky.

choices.text: Wave {him} off and drink tea

effects.log: {He} will be back for supper, windblown, and insufferable.

events.text: The serpent turns. Wake-riders know the rule: when it turns, leave the wake at once. {npc} does not. {His} skiff holds the line a heartbeat too long, and a spill of ragged air begins to spin the little craft around.
events.arc: The Wake-Riders of the Serpent Run

choices.text: Lean hard and haul the skiff out of the wake

ok.log: The skiff skids out of the wake on one runner. You both laugh, shaking.

fail.log: The skiff tips and you are thrown, grabbing a line. You come out soaked and sore.

choices.text: Shout the old signal to cut the sail

effects.log: {npc} hears, and cuts it. The skiff drops out, wobbling.

choices.text: Trust {npc} and hold on

effects.log: It works, narrowly, and {he} swears never to do it again.

events.text: {npc} gives up the wake and takes to the safer craft of ferry-piloting, with a face like a scolded cat. The Reach talks of it for a season. Then {he} appears at your door with a plan: a school for wake-riders, with rules. Will you teach the signals?
events.arc: The Wake-Riders of the Serpent Run

choices.text: Teach the signals and the safe-line chart

effects.log: The school opens with eleven students. Not one is lost in a decade.

choices.text: Offer to judge the first race

effects.log: The race is clean, fast and loud. You hand out ribbons to the dizzy.

events.text: From the cliff you notice something the riders do not: the serpent turns at the same mark on every pass, a rock shaped like a bent finger. The wake is not random. You chart the turns across a season.
events.arc: The Wake-Riders of the Serpent Run

choices.text: Give the chart to {npc} and the riders

effects.log: The riders cheer. {He} calls it the best gift a rider ever had.

choices.text: Keep the chart and watch the serpent by yourself

effects.log: It is a long, still friendship with something that never knows you.

events.text: Two families on the Plum Isle are to be joined, and both claim the right to supply the wedding silk. One has a loom, the other a flock of star-moths whose cocoons spin a pale thread that glows. {npc}, the seamstress, is caught between. "I will use the thread that comes with the kinder offer," {he} says. "Find it."
events.arc: The Wedding Dress of Moth-Silk

choices.text: Visit the loom family and listen

effects.log: They are proud, and tired, and have not slept for a week. They are afraid of being outdone.

choices.text: Visit the moth family and listen

effects.log: They keep their moths in a warm loft. They are afraid of being forgotten.

choices.text: Take a walk and let the problem settle

effects.log: The seamstress is pleased by your restraint.

events.text: Both families are kind. Both are frightened. The seamstress hands you two thread-ends, one each, and says: "Weave them together and see." The braid is stronger than either strand, and glows with a warm light.
events.arc: The Wedding Dress of Moth-Silk

choices.text: Propose a dress with both threads

effects.log: {npc} hums. "It is a good idea. It will take a year."

choices.text: Offer to carry the threads between the families

effects.log: You become a go-between with a basket, a tin of tea and endless patience.

choices.text: Tell both families the braid was your idea

effects.log: They laugh, and are a little less afraid.

events.text: The year passes. The dress is finished on a still night, ankle to throat, woven of loom-thread and moth-silk, and it glows faintly from within. The families come to see it on its stand and for a moment nobody speaks.
events.arc: The Wedding Dress of Moth-Silk

choices.text: Stay for the wedding

effects.log: The bride wears it, and the guests are moved to quiet. The feast afterwards is long and loud.

choices.text: Leave a small gift and slip away

effects.log: You leave a pot of honey and a note. The couple keep it for sixty years.

events.text: The moth family will not share the thread, or the shame of asking. The seamstress sighs and tells you {he} will make the dress of loom-thread and plain care. It will not glow. It will be a good dress. The bride says {he} does not mind.
events.arc: The Wedding Dress of Moth-Silk

choices.text: Bring a handful of moths yourself, as a gift

effects.log: You carry a small cage across the isle at dusk. The moths settle on the dress and it shines for one night.

choices.text: Say a plain dress is a fine thing

effects.log: The bride nods. It is a good dress.

events.text: The Star Sea Pavilion keeps a small observatory inside the eye of the great storm, where the sky is clear for a thousand years at a time. {npc}, the astronomer on watch, has seen no visitors in a century. "I thought you were a moth," {he} says. "You are bigger."
events.arc: The Observatory Inside the Storm

choices.text: Tour the observatory and ask about the long watch

effects.log: {He} shows you a hundred years of star-charts, each page signed with a neat small hand.

choices.text: Offer supplies from the Pavilion

effects.log: You unload tea, dumplings and the news. {He} reads the news slowly, with delight.

choices.text: Look through the great lens in silence

effects.log: The sky is bright and sharp. The storm wall circles quietly round the hole.

events.text: One star in the charts has been dimming for forty years, a slow patient fade that no one else has noticed. {npc} fears that when the eye closes, the record will be lost. "Whoever comes next will start from nothing," {he} says.
events.arc: The Observatory Inside the Storm

choices.text: Offer to carry the charts to the Pavilion archive

effects.log: It takes three trips. The Pavilion clerks are astonished by the hand-copied volumes.

choices.text: Stay a season and help copy the charts

effects.log: You copy day and night. The astronomer teaches you the dim star's secret.

choices.text: Promise to return

effects.log: You do. It takes longer than you thought.

events.text: The eye is closing, as it does every thousand years. The astronomer sits on the deck with a final chart on {his} knee and a look of calm. "The wall will take the observatory," {he} says. "But the charts will live." The wall of cloud is already bending in.
events.arc: The Observatory Inside the Storm

choices.text: Take {npc} out in your skiff before the wall closes

effects.log: You thread the wall at the last moment. {He} looks back once, then laughs.

choices.text: Stay with {npc} to the end and sail out together

effects.log: The wall is a roaring, silver blur. You come out in clean air with ringing ears and a flag.

events.text: The dim star flares and dies in the thirtieth year of your life as a student of its charts. Only you know that it fell, and that you watched it. The astronomer's last page lies open in your lap.
events.arc: The Observatory Inside the Storm

choices.text: Publish the full record under the astronomer's name

effects.log: The Pavilion names a comet after {him}. {npc} would have said it was too much, and been very pleased.

choices.text: Keep the record for your own study

effects.log: It is a quiet lifelong joy.

events.text: In a ruined bell-tower on a half-sunk isle hangs a bell of star-iron, big as a boat, with a clapper that moves freely and makes no sound. {npc}, a bell-founder, has come from three isles away to see it. "It is made wrong," {he} says. "Or made right, for something I cannot hear."
events.arc: The Star-Iron Bell That Would Not Ring

choices.text: Strike the bell with a stick and listen

effects.log: A thump, a click, nothing. A faint hum under the floor.

choices.text: Press your ear to the iron

effects.log: It is cold. A deep vibration runs through it, too low to hear.

choices.text: Sit with the founder and share {his} flask

effects.log: {He} tells you about bells for an hour. It is worth the climb.

events.text: The hum comes from the isle itself, which is sinking by a finger a year. The bell rings at the rate the isle sinks, a note so slow it takes a decade to make a single toll. The founder is thrilled and appalled. "It is a clock," {he} says. "It tells how long we have."
events.arc: The Star-Iron Bell That Would Not Ring

choices.text: Count the toll with {him} for a season

effects.log: Two ticks, a long silence, two ticks. The founder weeps with joy at the numbers.

choices.text: Ask whether the isle can be raised

effects.log: {He} thinks hard. "With ten thousand floats and a good summer," {he} says.

choices.text: Sketch the bell for the record

effects.log: The sketch is clumsy and affectionate.

events.text: The Isle-Wardens come to measure the sink, and tell you the bell is a hazard: it tells people that the isle is doomed, and they will leave. The founder wants to keep it ringing. The wardens want it silenced. They look at you.
events.arc: The Star-Iron Bell That Would Not Ring

choices.text: Side with the founder: the bell is honest

effects.log: The wardens grumble. The islanders gather to hear it toll and stay on, out of stubbornness.

choices.text: Side with the wardens: raise the isle first

effects.log: It takes two summers and ten thousand floats. The isle rises a hand, and the bell slows.

choices.text: Propose a compromise: ring it only on feast days

effects.log: Nobody is satisfied, which is how you know it works.

events.text: The bell tolls once in a decade. When it does, the isle gathers and sings: it is the oldest custom there. The founder is buried beneath it, as {he} asked, and a flat iron plate is inscribed with a single word: "Listen."
events.arc: The Star-Iron Bell That Would Not Ring

choices.text: Attend the toll each decade

effects.log: You grow old beside it. The isle never quite sinks.

choices.text: Teach the isle-children the bell-song

effects.log: It becomes a school, in time, and the children can name the next toll within a day.

events.text: The isle rises, floated by a hundred hands. The bell tolls slower, then slower, then stops. The founder stands beside it in the quiet, smiling. "It has nothing to say," {he} says. "It is the best sound a bell ever made."
events.arc: The Star-Iron Bell That Would Not Ring

choices.text: Leave the bell hanging as it is

effects.log: On a still day, if you press your ear, it hums.

choices.text: Carry a splinter of star-iron home as a keepsake

effects.log: The founder presses it into your hand, cold and heavy. It rings when you are lost.

events.text: A bolt of cloud-silk has vanished from the Silk Lane overnight, and the first person the marshal looks at is the stranger with no seal: you. {npc}, the stallkeeper, is apologetic and frightened. "It is only a question," {he} says. "The unsealed are always a question."
events.arc: The Bolt Gone From the Silk Lane

choices.text: Answer the marshal's questions calmly

effects.log: The marshal writes everything down. The pen is slow, and polite, and pointed.

choices.text: Offer to find the bolt yourself

effects.log: The marshal waves it away, then follows you at a distance.

choices.text: Leave the lane until the marshal calms

effects.log: You are watched all the way to the bridge.

events.text: The bolt is not stolen. It is in a bolt-crate at the bottom of the stall's own storeroom, wedged behind a sack by a clumsy apprentice. Only you, the rogue, are blamed. The marshal does not apologise: "The question was reasonable."
events.arc: The Bolt Gone From the Silk Lane

choices.text: Point out that the question was only ever asked of you

effects.log: The marshal reddens. The lane goes quiet. {npc} stands up straight beside you.

choices.text: Accept the clean slate and say nothing

effects.log: You walk out with your head up. The apprentice follows with hands in sleeves.

choices.text: Ask {npc} for a cup of tea

effects.log: It is the best cup of tea in the lane.

events.text: The lane changes its habits after that. The marshal now asks everyone. The stalls hold a small collection to pay you for your trouble: thirty stones in a paper wrap, and a note from {npc} that says only "Sorry, from all of us."
events.arc: The Bolt Gone From the Silk Lane

choices.text: Take the stones and the note

effects.log: It is more than you were owed. It is not enough. It is something.

choices.text: Give the stones to the apprentice for the storeroom shelves

effects.log: The apprentice nods, face red. The shelves are built in a week.

events.text: You are never asked again. {npc} slips you a bolt-end of plain silk at the new year, wrapped in paper, with no seal and no price. You keep it for a long time. It is the first kindness from the lane that did not need a question first.
events.arc: The Bolt Gone From the Silk Lane

choices.text: Sew it into a scarf

effects.log: You wear it to the lane in winter. {npc} smiles at the sight.

choices.text: Keep it folded, unused

effects.log: It is a small thing to keep, and a heavy one to carry.

events.text: A stoppered bottle sits on your doorstep one dawn, warm to the touch, with a hum of wind inside. There is no note. A faint smell of rain-on-stone comes from the cork. Someone left it deliberately.
events.arc: The Bottle on the Doorstep

choices.text: Open the bottle at the window

effects.log: A small gust rushes out, circles the room and stops at the door as if expecting you to follow.

choices.text: Leave it corked and ask the neighbours

effects.log: No one saw a thing. A child saw a sparrow carrying something.

choices.text: Set it on the shelf and wait

effects.log: It hums, quietly, for three days.

events.text: The wind from the bottle runs down the stairs and along the lane to a house at the end: closed, shuttered, the paint peeling. It leans on the door and the door creaks open an inch. Inside, the air is cold and still, as if no one had breathed in years.
events.arc: The Bottle on the Doorstep

choices.text: Step inside

effects.log: A table, a chair, a cup left half drunk. On the table is a letter, unsealed.

choices.text: Knock and wait

effects.log: No answer. A shutter rattles, once.

choices.text: Close the door gently and walk away

effects.log: The wind trails behind you, bewildered.

events.text: The letter is addressed to "the one who opens the bottle". It is from a woman who lived here, who loved a pilot who never came back, and who put a last breath into a bottle in the hope that someone kind would carry it somewhere. The letter asks that it be taken to the Western Gap, where the pilot was lost.
events.arc: The Bottle on the Doorstep

choices.text: Carry the wind to the Western Gap

effects.log: It is a four-day trip. At the Gap you uncork the bottle on the cliff and the wind is gone into the sky like a sigh.

choices.text: Read the letter aloud in the empty room

effects.log: The wind whirls round you, and stills. The room feels lighter.

choices.text: Fold the letter and keep it

effects.log: It will be there when you know what to do.

events.text: At the Gap, a gust answers from the sea of cloud, and for a moment two winds spiral up together into a pillar of silver, and part. A keeper on the cliff sees it and says nothing, then, quietly, takes off a cap.
events.arc: The Bottle on the Doorstep

choices.text: Leave a flower on the cliff

effects.log: It is there a year later, dried, perfectly kept.

choices.text: Tell the neighbours the story at the end of the lane

effects.log: They repaint the shutters, a pale blue. Someone plants a window-box.

events.text: A sparrow lands on your sill a month later with a scrap of paper tied to its leg: "Thank you." The handwriting is not the woman's. It is a pilot's, square and rough, and it is dated three years back.
events.arc: The Bottle on the Doorstep

choices.text: Wonder at it for the rest of the day

effects.log: It is a perfect little mystery, left unsolved.

choices.text: Pin the note beside the door

effects.log: It stays there for decades.

events.text: Each autumn, on a single afternoon, a small isle appears off the Western Reach and is gone by dusk. {npc} the chartmaker has tried to pin it for forty years and drawn it forty different ways. {He} has a skiff, a thermos and a theory. "Come with me this year," {he} says. "Two sets of eyes."
events.arc: The Isle That Appears for a Day

choices.text: Join the chartmaker and the thermos

effects.log: You sail at noon. At the third hour the sea of cloud ripples and a green hump rises.

choices.text: Ask for the forty charts first

effects.log: They are all different, and all beautiful. A pattern is hiding in the margins.

choices.text: Wish {him} luck and watch from the pier

effects.log: You see a green flicker, far out, and a skiff like a spark.

events.text: You land. The isle is a single hill with one house on it and a garden in full bloom. The door is open and a pot is boiling. A woman looks up from the stove and says, "Visitors. How lovely. I am afraid I only have until dusk."
events.arc: The Isle That Appears for a Day

choices.text: Accept tea and a story

effects.log: The tea tastes of every autumn you ever lived. The woman tells of a year when the isle stayed, and the year it left.

choices.text: Ask what the woman tends in the garden

effects.log: "The part of the year that does not fit," the woman says. "Out-of-season flowers. They need somewhere to go."

choices.text: Help the woman pick the last blooms

effects.log: Your arms fill with flowers that have no name.

events.text: As dusk draws near, the isle begins to fade at its edge, like a drawing left in rain. The woman folds an apron. There is no mind in it; it happens every year. {npc} frantically pins the isle on the chart. It will not hold.
events.arc: The Isle That Appears for a Day

choices.text: Take {npc}'s hand and walk to the skiff together

effects.log: You make it off with a bunch of flowers and a lump in your throat.

choices.text: Ask the woman where the isle goes when it is gone

effects.log: "Where flowers go," the woman says, and waves.

events.text: The pattern is in the margins of the forty charts: the isle appears at the point where the autumn winds cross, and the crossing drifts by exactly one finger a year. The next landing is predictable. You work out the exact day, and the hour.
events.arc: The Isle That Appears for a Day

choices.text: Give the prediction to {npc}

effects.log: {He} is silent for a long time. Then {he} kisses your hand and calls you a menace.

choices.text: Keep the prediction and visit alone each year

effects.log: The woman starts setting a third cup. It becomes a small ritual.

events.text: A family of sky-otters has made a slide of the wind that curls round Ripple Isle, and they use it all day for the joy of it. {npc}, the ferrywright, wants them gone: they knock {his} skiffs off their moorings. "Beautiful pests," {he} says. "Come and see what they did to my morning."
events.arc: The Otters of the Long Slide

choices.text: Watch the otters at play

effects.log: They slide, flip, tumble and roll, and one of them waves a paw at you.

choices.text: Offer {npc} a better mooring

effects.log: You re-tie {his} skiffs on the lee side. The otters, disappointed, find another game.

choices.text: Share {npc}'s grievances and a pot of tea

effects.log: {He} feels heard, which is most of the battle.

events.text: The smallest otter has a tangle of rope round one hind leg, a trailing end of mooring line. It slides badly, and the others circle it in worry. It lets you approach, whiskers quivering.
events.arc: The Otters of the Long Slide

choices.text: Cut the rope free

effects.log: The otter twirls once in thanks and is gone. A chorus of squeaks goes up on the wind.

choices.text: Lure the otter in with a bit of dried fish

effects.log: It comes to your hand, nibbles, and lets you unpick the knot.

choices.text: Leave it to its family

effects.log: The adult otters chew the rope through in a minute.

events.text: The otters begin leaving small gifts on your doorstep: a pretty shell, a bead, a knot of silver weed. They are paying you. {npc} is outraged and impressed in equal measure. "They never pay me," {he} says.
events.arc: The Otters of the Long Slide

choices.text: Return the gifts with a fish each

effects.log: It becomes a trade. A fine ratio, they decide, of shell to fish.

choices.text: Build a small platform at the slide for the otters

effects.log: The otters adopt it. {npc} approves of the safe distance from {his} skiffs.

events.text: The otters come to you for their fish, every day at noon, and the ferrywright gives up and builds them a proper slide of timber and sail. Visitors come to see it. By midsummer, {he} is selling tickets, and cursing {his} own idea.
events.arc: The Otters of the Long Slide

choices.text: Take a share of the tickets (3 stones)

effects.log: The otters are better paid than you.

choices.text: Let {npc} keep the money

effects.log: {He} does not spend a stone of it on {him}self, and buys the otters a mountain of fish.

events.text: {npc} grows old on Ripple Isle, and the otters grow bold. One summer morning {he} is found asleep in the slide's hollow, a sleeping otter on each shoulder, and the whole family arranged around {him} like a quilt. {He} is smiling.
events.arc: The Otters of the Long Slide

choices.text: Leave the scene as it is and tiptoe away

effects.log: You leave {him} to the best nap of {his} life.

choices.text: Sit nearby and keep the gulls off

effects.log: You stay till {he} wakes. {He} says, "I was not asleep."

events.text: The Hush Isle is quiet in a way that frightens visitors: nothing echoes there. A grey owl lives in the cliffs, and it swallows echoes whole. {npc}, a listener from the Hush Isle, wants it turned, not harmed, because the isle's old song cannot be sung with no echo. "Shout into a cave and nothing comes back," {he} says.
events.arc: The Owl That Eats Echoes

choices.text: Track the owl by the silence it leaves

effects.log: You walk in the quietest places. At the quietest of all, a pair of round yellow eyes opens.

choices.text: Call out and listen for what does not come back

effects.log: Your shout vanishes. The owl is directly overhead.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} and listen to the quiet

effects.log: It is a restful, odd place to be.

events.text: The owl is old and thin, and the echoes it swallows are all it eats. The isle has been quiet because the owl was starving: it ate the old echoes and now has none left. It watches you with enormous patience.
events.arc: The Owl That Eats Echoes

choices.text: Lend the owl echoes from the farther cliffs

effects.log: You walk it round the isle, calling at cliffs that still echo. It eats, and fattens, and blinks.

choices.text: Give the owl a song sung into a jar

effects.log: You sing, cork the jar, and leave it by the nest. The owl swallows the song in one gulp.

choices.text: Leave the owl and sleep on it

effects.log: You dream of echoes.

events.text: The owl is full, at last, and gives a long slow hoot that carries across the isle. The hoot comes back from the cliffs, doubled, then tripled, then a thousand times, ringing round the hills. The listener stands with {his} hands over {his} mouth, weeping.
events.arc: The Owl That Eats Echoes

choices.text: Sing the isle's old song into the echoes

effects.log: It rings back from every hill, in a hundred voices.

choices.text: Let {npc} sing alone

effects.log: {He} sings the old song, and the owl joins in at the last note.

events.text: The jar of song is eaten, and the owl hoots once. The isle echoes for an hour, then falls silent again. The owl is not starving, but it is not satisfied. {npc} asks if you will bring more songs, every year, in jars. You agree.
events.arc: The Owl That Eats Echoes

choices.text: Bring a jar each spring

effects.log: The isle echoes for an hour every year, and the owl grows stout.

choices.text: Teach the isle-children to fill the jars themselves

effects.log: The children sing into jars for years. The owl grows fat and happy.

events.text: The Jade Void Sect sets a trial for those who would climb its high terrace: stand on a ledge as three winds blow in turn, and do not move. {npc}, the elder who keeps the ledge, is kind and exact. "The first wind is a flatterer," {he} says. "The second is a bully. The third is a friend. The third is the hardest."
events.arc: The Trial of the Three Winds

choices.text: Take the ledge and wait for the first wind

effects.log: It strokes your hair and tells you what you want to hear. You stand firm.

choices.text: Ask what the third wind does

effects.log: {He} smiles. "It asks you to rest. Most fall asleep."

choices.text: Watch another candidate try

effects.log: A young disciple holds for a full hour before sneezing.

events.text: The second wind arrives like a fist, tearing at your sleeves, shouting in your ears. You grip the stone with your toes. The elder watches without comment. A thin line of blood from a scratched hand beads and dries in the gale.
events.arc: The Trial of the Three Winds

choices.text: Stand through it, eyes closed

effects.log: It passes. You are shaking, but you have not moved.

choices.text: Step back and ask for a pause

effects.log: {npc} nods. "Wise. It is not a contest of pride."

choices.text: Shout back at the wind

effects.log: It shouts louder. Nothing is gained, much is lost.

events.text: The third wind comes soft as a mother's hand. It carries the smell of your childhood house, a tune you half-remember, a voice calling you in to supper. You are so tired. The ledge is so wide. The elder says nothing at all.
events.arc: The Trial of the Three Winds

choices.text: Stand upright and breathe

effects.log: You do not sleep. The wind sighs and withdraws. You are astonished at how much you wanted to lie down.

choices.text: Sit on the ledge and watch the wind pass

effects.log: You sit, and do not sleep. The elder nods: a different kind of pass.

events.text: The pause is granted. You rest an hour, drink a cup of cold tea and listen to the elder talk about {his} own trial, forty centuries ago, when {he} fell asleep in the third wind and woke to a pot of tea and an older, kinder teacher.
events.arc: The Trial of the Three Winds

choices.text: Return to the ledge for the third wind

effects.log: You hold it. The elder pats your shoulder, rough with approval.

choices.text: Decide the ledge is not for you

effects.log: The elder says it is a decision, not a failure.

events.text: As a rogue with no isle, you eat where you are fed. {npc}, a ferry-cook, feeds you three nights in a row and refuses payment. "Keep a ledger," {he} says. "Not of coins. Of kindnesses. Pay them back when you can, to whoever needs them." {He} hands you a small notebook.
events.arc: The Ledger of Small Kindnesses

choices.text: Start the ledger that night

effects.log: Page one: a bowl of broth, a blanket, a ferry-cook. You underline it twice.

choices.text: Ask {npc} why {he} does this

effects.log: {He} shrugs. "Someone did it for me. It is the same bowl."

choices.text: Thank {him} and sail on

effects.log: The broth lingers for a day.

events.text: A year later the ledger has forty lines, mostly kindnesses given to you, a few given by you: a mended boot, a lost child walked home, a bad poem praised. A faction-sealed man snubs you at a dock, and the ledger is full of the kindness of others, and the snub weighs nothing.
events.arc: The Ledger of Small Kindnesses

choices.text: Pay a debt forward: feed three strangers

effects.log: You share a stew from a borrowed pot. It is the best you have made.

choices.text: Read the ledger aloud to yourself

effects.log: It is a long list. You are rich.

choices.text: Add a line for the snub, and cross it out

effects.log: It makes a small joke on the page.

events.text: You find {npc}'s ferry at a distant harbour, and the cook is unwell, in a hammock under the stern. The ferry has no cook. The passengers grumble. {He} looks at you and does not ask.
events.arc: The Ledger of Small Kindnesses

choices.text: Take over the galley for the crossing

effects.log: You feed sixty passengers and a goat. {npc} watches from the hammock, smiling.

choices.text: Fetch a healer and cook for {npc} alone

effects.log: You sit with {him} and spoon broth. It is the same bowl.

events.text: The ledger runs to a hundred pages. In the last years of your wandering you give it to a young rogue sitting alone on a dock, with the first line already written: "A bowl of broth, a blanket, a stranger."
events.arc: The Ledger of Small Kindnesses

choices.text: Give the ledger and walk on

effects.log: You hear years later that it has crossed ten harbours.

choices.text: Keep the ledger and start a second

effects.log: Page one of volume two: "A bowl of broth."

events.text: A raft of sky-otters crosses the Ripple Gap in a line, holding paws, every one with a stone on its belly. They do this every year on the same day and nobody knows why.

choices.text: Watch from the cliff and count them

effects.log: Forty-one. The last one waves.

choices.text: Lay a bowl of fish at the landing

effects.log: They eat politely, in order of size.

events.text: A grey owl sits on the lamp-post at the end of Quiet Lane, and the lane is quieter for it. A cart-driver says it stops dogs from barking. A baker says it stops the kettle from whistling.

choices.text: Nod to the owl and pass

effects.log: One yellow eye opens, then closes, in what might be thanks.

choices.text: Hum a note and see what happens

effects.log: The note vanishes. You stand in a perfectly peaceful pocket of nothing.

events.text: A swarm of star-moths has turned up uninvited to a wedding on the Plum Isle and settled on the paper lanterns. The bride's mother is mortified. The bride is delighted.

choices.text: Tell the mother it is a blessing

effects.log: The mother dabs a tear. It is accepted as such.

choices.text: Shoo a few moths toward the cake table

effects.log: They land on the cake. It glows for a minute.

events.text: A lantern-seller sells moth-cages with a free moth, though moths do not stay caged and the seller knows it. Every child on the Plum Isle has a cage with a moth in it, briefly.

choices.text: Buy a cage for a child, and open it in the garden

effects.log: The moth rises, trailing silver. The child cheers.

choices.text: Ask the seller to stop selling

effects.log: The seller shrugs. Nothing changes, but the question lingers.

events.text: A ribbon of old wake from a long-gone serpent lingers over the Long Reach, a thin line of fast air that skiffers use as a free road. Today it is a little thicker than usual.

choices.text: Ride the ribbon for an hour

effects.log: You cut the day's sail in half. A skiffer waves, jealous.

choices.text: Mark its edge on the chart for others

effects.log: Your note is copied by seven pilots by sunset.

events.text: On a still night a young wind serpent wraps its coils round a mooring tower and sleeps, humming. The tower hums back. The whole isle sleeps well.

choices.text: Hum along very quietly

effects.log: You wake the next day with a clear head and a faint buzz in your teeth.

choices.text: Lay a blanket on the stair for the night watch

effects.log: The watchman sleeps, too. No one is robbed.

events.text: A newly fallen star lies in a field, cooling, with a ring of frost round it. A farmer tends it with a bucket of water and looks lost. "It is still warm," the farmer says. "Who does it belong to?"

choices.text: Tell the farmer it belongs to the field

effects.log: The farmer nods slowly. The field will be famous in a year.

choices.text: Stay and help carry water until nightfall

effects.log: The star hisses, thanks you and cools.

events.text: A ruined gate is held together by a hinge that never rusts, and a bell-founder swears the hinge is star-iron. The gate is a hundred centuries old and swings in the least wind.

choices.text: Oil the hinge and leave it

effects.log: It swings easily, as if grateful.

choices.text: Sketch the hinge for the founder

effects.log: The founder is moved to write you a long letter in return.

events.text: A bolt of cloud-silk in the market has a strange tag: "Made from the cloud that fell on the third day of the Winter Festival, Year Nine Hundred." The tag is the cloth's true price. The stallholder knows.

choices.text: Ask about the third day of the Winter Festival

effects.log: The stallholder tells a long, tender story about a snowfall that stopped a war.

choices.text: Buy a handspan (2 spirit stones worth, paid in goods)

effects.log: You trade a jar of tea. It is a fair swap.

events.text: A shelf of bottled winds in the market has labels in a careful hand: "A Sigh of Relief," "The Day After Rain," "Someone's Grandmother's Sneeze." Browsing costs nothing.

choices.text: Open "The Day After Rain" for a moment

effects.log: The whole stall smells of washed stone. The vendor beams.

choices.text: Buy "A Sigh of Relief" for later

effects.log: You pop the cork on a bad day and it works at once.

events.text: A pilot offers to sell you a compass that points to the pilot's home. The pilot is leaving on a long journey and has no wish to look at it. The needle swings, longing.

choices.text: Buy the compass for a modest sum and send it home with a letter

effects.log: You post it to the address on the hull. The reply comes with a plum cake.

choices.text: Say you cannot carry another man's home

effects.log: The pilot nods and puts the compass away, folded in a handkerchief.

events.text: A reef-fog has settled over the harbour, thick as wool. Ships tied at the quay sound their bells in patterns. A steersman near you counts the bells and names every ship, blind.

choices.text: Learn the bell patterns from the steersman

effects.log: The steersman teaches you six. You feel suddenly rich in a very small way.

choices.text: Offer to ring a bell for a stranded skiff

effects.log: You ring all night. In the morning a grateful skiff docks beside you.

events.text: A path of calm, a few hundred paces wide, winds through the heart of a storm like a lane through a wood. Pilots use it to cut across the Reach, when it is there.

choices.text: Take the path through the storm

effects.log: The wall roars on both sides. You come out the far end buzzing.

choices.text: Wait for the storm to pass

effects.log: It takes a day. You read a book.

events.text: A thunder sparrow has taken shelter in the eye of the storm and sits on the rail of a lone skiff, humming sparks. It looks at you as if you were the one intruding.

choices.text: Offer it a crumb and a place at the rail

effects.log: It hops onto your wrist, warm and prickling.

choices.text: Stay out of its way

effects.log: It watches you all afternoon, politely.

events.text: At the Edge of Heaven a gull that has never seen a boat follows you for an hour, calling. It is old, and its feathers have gone silver from the height.

choices.text: Toss it a bit of bread

effects.log: It catches the bread mid-air, as if it had always done so.

choices.text: Follow it to the lip of the cliff

effects.log: It rides the updraft and lets you watch the long drop.

events.text: An old ledger of the Harbour Wardens lists a ship, lost with all hands a thousand years ago, whose crew are still paid a wage each year. Nobody knows who collects it.

choices.text: Ask the Wardens who signs for it

effects.log: A clerk finds a pen-stroke. It is the same every year, in a hand that has not aged.

choices.text: Add your own coin to the fund

effects.log: The clerk writes it down. It will outlast you.

events.text: A pier juts out over the Edge into nothing at all. Planks are missing at the far end. A sign says: "Do not walk to the end." A line of footprints says otherwise.

choices.text: Walk halfway and sit

effects.log: The cloud-sea stretches out below you like a bowl of milk.

choices.text: Mend a plank with a spare from your skiff

effects.log: It is a small kindness to the next idle walker.

events.text: At the Ministry's relief desk, a long queue of unsealed rogues waits for a stamp. A clerk has called a recess. Nobody knows for how long. A man at the front has been there three days.

choices.text: Share your food with the queue

effects.log: The queue is polite and astonished. The man at the front weeps.

choices.text: Take a number and wait with them

effects.log: You wait nine hours. The stamp, when it comes, is faint and crooked.

events.text: A tea-seller quotes you a price that is twice the one on the chalkboard. "For the unsealed," the seller says, not unkindly. "We have extra to cover." Behind you, someone with a seal is served at half.

choices.text: Pay it and say nothing

effects.log: The tea is good. The silence afterwards is heavier.

choices.text: Point at the chalkboard until the price drops

effects.log: The seller sighs and charges the board. A small victory.

events.text: A kind innkeeper offers you the loft above the stable for free, because the inn is full and you look cold. In the morning there is a bowl of porridge by the ladder and no one around.

choices.text: Leave a small gift on the doorstep

effects.log: A jar of honey. It is gone by evening.

choices.text: Sweep the stable before you go

effects.log: The yard looks better than it has for a decade.

events.text: A pale egg the size of a water-jar has lodged in the rigging of a moored freighter, humming faintly. {npc}, the first mate, says it dropped from nowhere in last night's gale. "It is warm," {he} says. "That is a wind serpent's egg, and a wind serpent will want it back."
events.arc: The Egg in the Rigging

choices.text: Watch the egg through the night

effects.log: It hums at midnight and shivers at dawn. Something inside shifts like a sleeper turning over.

choices.text: Send word to the Ministry of Fog

effects.log: A clerk replies in a week: "Not our department. Try the weather." The weather replies: "Not ours either."

choices.text: Wrap the egg in a blanket and wait

effects.log: {npc} fusses over it like a mother hen.

events.text: The egg cracks in a gale. Out slides a hatchling wind serpent the length of an arm, translucent as a ribbon, which knots itself round your wrist and refuses to let go. It sings in a thin high voice that makes the rigging shiver.
events.arc: The Egg in the Rigging

choices.text: Let the hatchling stay on your wrist

effects.log: It sleeps there for a week, cool as a bracelet. Pilots look at your arm with envy.

choices.text: Feed it on dew and mist from a spoon

effects.log: It drinks the mist and grows an inch before your eyes.

choices.text: Put it in a crate and wait for the mother

effects.log: The crate rattles, then hums, then rattles. The mother does not come.

events.text: A young wind serpent needs a gale to practise in, and the only gale for a month is a ragged squall over the Lonely Reach. {npc} offers the freighter's boat. "If it sulks, it will tangle the lines," {he} says. "If it flies, I will pay for the beer."
events.arc: The Egg in the Rigging

choices.text: Take the hatchling out into the squall

effects.log: It leaps from your wrist and spirals into the grey, singing. It circles the boat three times and is gone.

choices.text: Keep it and teach it to fly on calmer days

effects.log: You spend a month on a quiet bay. It learns slowly, hovers, squeals and then soars.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to take it instead

effects.log: {He} grumbles, and takes it, and sings to it all night.

events.text: The serpent returns years later, full grown, a pale river of wind across the harbour sky. It circles the freighter, lowers its great head to you and breathes once, softly. The sails of every boat in the harbour fill at once. The mate waves his cap.
events.arc: The Egg in the Rigging

choices.text: Raise a hand to the serpent

effects.log: It dips, flicks its tail across the water, and spins away towards the horizon.

choices.text: Sit on the dock and watch the sails fill

effects.log: It is the finest sight of the year.

events.text: The hatchling grows long and strong and still knots itself round your wrist when it wants company. It has a favourite perch on your mast and a favourite song. Pilots call you the Serpent-Keeper. You never asked for the title. You answer to it anyway.
events.arc: The Egg in the Rigging

choices.text: Keep the serpent for life

effects.log: It outlasts your skiff, your hobbies and three tea-shops.

choices.text: Release it at a gale-feast with the other serpents

effects.log: It slithers up into the sky with a crowd of its own kind. It looks back once.

events.text: {npc}, a heaven-born girl of nine, keeps one cloud carp in a basin and says it was a river fish once. It only rises when {he} says a certain word, and {he} will not say what the word is. "It is secret," {he} says. "It is the name of the river."
events.arc: The Carp Who Remembers a River

choices.text: Ask what the river looked like

effects.log: {He} describes it in detail, colour by colour. {He} has never seen it. The carp told {his}.

choices.text: Promise to keep the secret

effects.log: {He} looks at you hard, and decides to trust you.

choices.text: Offer the carp a pinch of rice

effects.log: It rises, takes the rice and sinks again, bored.

events.text: The word is "Haneulgang", and the child whispers it into the basin. The carp rises, golden, shivering, and beats the water. You know the name: it is a river far below, in the mortal world, that you once crossed as a young cultivator. The carp is nearly two thousand years old.
events.arc: The Carp Who Remembers a River

choices.text: Tell {npc} you know the river

effects.log: {He} goes quiet. "Is it still there?" {he} asks. You say you think it is.

choices.text: Say nothing and watch the carp circle

effects.log: The carp seems to know more than you do.

choices.text: Sit with the child and the basin for an hour

effects.log: The carp rises each time the word is said.

events.text: Carp that remember rivers fade if they are kept from them. The carp's scales have gone dull, and it floats near the surface. {npc} asks if there is any way to take it home. It is a long way down, and the girl cannot make the journey alone.
events.arc: The Carp Who Remembers a River

choices.text: Offer to carry the carp below in a jar of cloud-water

effects.log: It is a month's journey. You pour the carp into the river at dawn. It rises, spins, and is gone.

choices.text: Ask the Ministry of Prayers to send it by a prayer-chute

effects.log: The Ministry takes a form, a week and a copper bell. The carp is sent. A note returns: "Arrived. Splashing."

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth: it is too far

effects.log: {He} nods gravely. The carp and the child look at each other.

events.text: A letter reaches {npc} the next spring, written in a very small hand: a fisherman by the river says a golden fish has taken up residence in {his} bank, and {he} feeds it every morning. {npc} reads it aloud to the basin, which is now empty. {He} smiles and pins it to the wall.
events.arc: The Carp Who Remembers a River

choices.text: Add a drawing of the river to the wall

effects.log: The girl adds a little carp at the edge. Beside it, in blue, a cloud.

choices.text: Leave the girl to {his} letter

effects.log: {He} reads it again, and again.

events.text: The carp dies in the spring, quietly, at the basin. {npc} buries it beneath a cloud-pine and says the word one last time. The ground shivers, as though in answer. You stand with {him} a long time.
events.arc: The Carp Who Remembers a River

choices.text: Stay with {npc} until dark

effects.log: There are some things for which the right kindness is only to be there.

choices.text: Plant a river-stone on the grave

effects.log: It is smooth and grey. It will do.

events.text: The Nine Clouds Palace keeps a flock of star-moths for their dawn silk, and one of them has gone dark: it flutters about the loft, pale and frightened, with no glow at all. {npc}, the silk-warden, is distraught. "It is the youngest," {he} says. "It will be eaten by the others."
events.arc: The Moth That Lost Its Light

choices.text: Examine the moth with a lamp

effects.log: Its wings are intact, but the dust on them is grey. Something has dulled it.

choices.text: Ask the other moths to make room

effects.log: They shift on the beam. One of them settles close to the dark one, glowing gently.

choices.text: Keep the moth warm in your sleeve

effects.log: It trembles, and settles.

events.text: The grey dust is smoke. A new brazier in the loft burns resinous wood, and the soot has settled on the youngest moth, which perches directly over it. The warden had no idea. The moth is not ill, only dirty.
events.arc: The Moth That Lost Its Light

choices.text: Wash the moth gently in dew and cloud-water

effects.log: It sneezes and glimmers, and by morning is brighter than before.

choices.text: Move the brazier to the far end of the loft

effects.log: The loft is colder, but all the moths glow brighter in a week.

choices.text: Let the moth find its own cure

effects.log: It flies off to the window and sits in the sun. It works.

events.text: The moth, now bright, follows you everywhere in the Palace. It lands on your shoulder at council. It circles your lamp at night. {npc} says it has chosen you. "A moth that chooses is a moth that stays," {he} says. "I cannot take it back."
events.arc: The Moth That Lost Its Light

choices.text: Accept the moth and keep it at your desk

effects.log: It glows when you work and sleeps when you rest. You work longer than you used to.

choices.text: Give the moth to the silk-warden as a gift

effects.log: {He} nearly weeps. The moth sits on {his} head all afternoon.

events.text: The loft grows warm in a week and bright in two. The Nine Clouds Palace sends {npc} a commendation for the loft's record silk. The warden writes your name beside the date, in dawn-silk ink, on the beam where the youngest moth now roosts.
events.arc: The Moth That Lost Its Light

choices.text: Attend the commendation

effects.log: The warden is nervous and glowing. The moths glow back.

choices.text: Send a bunch of flowers and stay away

effects.log: The warden is pleased. So are the moths.

events.text: {npc}, the chef of a famous inn, has been given a pan of star-iron by a grateful diner, and the pan will not heat. Qi will not warm it, nor fire, nor three days in the sun. "It is the finest metal in the sky," {he} says, "and it is cold as a grudge." {He} offers you a free meal if you can make it work.
events.arc: The Pan That Would Not Heat

choices.text: Study the pan's weight and grain

effects.log: It is heavy and dense, with a faint blue pattern in the iron like frost on a pane.

choices.text: Ask the diner who gave it

effects.log: A merchant from the Star Sea, who says the metal fell on a winter night "and kept it."

choices.text: Order a bowl of noodles from another pan

effects.log: The noodles are good. {npc} sulks.

events.text: Star-iron, you learn, does not heat from fire but from music. A low steady note makes the pan warm; a rising one makes it hot. The chef cannot sing. He blushes at the idea. His wife, though, plays a bamboo flute, and has been waiting twenty years to be asked.
events.arc: The Pan That Would Not Heat

choices.text: Suggest the flute

effects.log: The wife plays. The pan warms, hisses and begins to glow a gentle orange.

choices.text: Hum the note yourself

effects.log: The pan warms a little. You are not a singer. The chef winces, politely.

choices.text: Offer to wash the dishes while they try

effects.log: It is a good evening for the inn.

events.text: The inn becomes famous for its flute-cooked dishes: every plate comes with a tune. The chef's wife plays from a stool by the stove, and the whole dining room hushes for the sauce. The pan, once cold, is the heart of the kitchen. Guests come from three isles.
events.arc: The Pan That Would Not Heat

choices.text: Dine at the inn once a season

effects.log: Each time, the tune is different. Each time, the food is better.

choices.text: Write a short song for the pan

effects.log: The wife plays it every evening. The chef weeps into the soup.

events.text: The pan stays cold. {npc} puts it on a shelf and hangs a ribbon on it. "Perhaps it is not for cooking," {he} says. "Perhaps it is for keeping cold things cold." The cellar benefits. Ice cream, that season, is magnificent.
events.arc: The Pan That Would Not Heat

choices.text: Try the ice cream

effects.log: It is silken and clean and tastes of snow on a bright morning.

choices.text: Suggest a use as a cooling stone for summer drinks

effects.log: The inn sells chilled tea in glasses. It is a hit.

events.text: A diplomat from the high isles has arrived at the Demon Realm's border with a gift: a bottle of true winter wind from the roof of the sky, for peace. {npc}, the envoy, is polite, nervous and shivering. "I was told to bring the best gift in my realm," {he} says. "I did not realise how cold it was."
events.arc: The Guest Who Brought Frost

choices.text: Escort the envoy to the Hall of Welcome

effects.log: The envoy walks in your shadow, grateful. At the hall, the guards bow stiffly.

choices.text: Take the bottle for inspection

effects.log: The cork frosts at once. It hums with a note like a bell in ice.

choices.text: Offer the envoy a bowl of hot soup

effects.log: The soup is accepted with a sob.

events.text: The Demon Realm has no winter. The bottle, uncorked in the hall, would freeze the roof. The Warden of Gifts is troubled and polite: a refusal would insult the envoy; an acceptance would flood the hall with snow. {npc} looks at you, hopeful and afraid.
events.arc: The Guest Who Brought Frost

choices.text: Propose opening the bottle in the courtyard under the sky

effects.log: A snowfall drifts down on the courtyard, the first anyone there has seen. Children stand with open mouths.

choices.text: Propose keeping it corked as a treasure of the hall

effects.log: The Warden accepts with relief. It is placed under glass, frosting the case.

choices.text: Excuse yourself and let them settle it

effects.log: They settle it. It takes six hours.

events.text: The snow lasts one afternoon. The children build a lopsided snowman from it and name it the Warden. {npc} stands in the courtyard in the falling flakes, tears frozen on {his} cheeks. "I did not think it would be like this," {he} says.
events.arc: The Guest Who Brought Frost

choices.text: Throw a snowball at the envoy

effects.log: It lands on the shoulder. The envoy is aghast, and then laughs, and throws one back.

choices.text: Stand with the envoy in the snow

effects.log: The two of you say nothing. The snow is the best answer.

events.text: The bottle sits under glass, a small cold star in the warm hall, and no one forgets it. A petition from the Warden to the high isles asks for a second bottle, to be opened, in time, on the child of the next envoy. The envoy returns, one year later, with a smile.
events.arc: The Guest Who Brought Frost

choices.text: Attend the second opening

effects.log: The second snow is thicker. A child makes a snow-dragon that melts by midnight.

choices.text: Send a gift of warm cloaks to the high isles

effects.log: It is the envoy's turn to be moved.

events.text: {npc} makes compasses that point to home. Every steersman owns one. {His} apprentice, a quiet girl called Sora, has made forty and each one points to the same place: the middle of the cloud-sea, where there is nothing. "{He} has no home," the compass-maker says. "The needle knows."
events.arc: The Needle That Pointed Nowhere

choices.text: Ask Sora about the middle of the cloud-sea

effects.log: {He} looks at {his} hands. "I was born on a skiff," {he} says. "I never touched ground."

choices.text: Test one of {his} compasses yourself

effects.log: The needle points steadily to the empty sea. It is as clear as a bell.

choices.text: Leave the shop and think it over

effects.log: You walk the quays for an hour.

events.text: Sora's skiff was lost in a storm when she was six. She was found by a ferryman who raised her on the water. All her life she has been looking for a home, and the compasses she makes are all honest: her home is the sea itself. She asks if you think that is a place at all.
events.arc: The Needle That Pointed Nowhere

choices.text: Tell her the sea is a home of sorts

effects.log: She smiles slowly. It is a small, wet smile.

choices.text: Suggest she make a compass for the ferryman who raised her

effects.log: She goes pale. She has never thought of it. She starts at once.

choices.text: Make her a cup of tea

effects.log: She drinks it, silently, and the shop is a little warmer.

events.text: The ferryman's compass points to a small harbour on the Cedar Reach, where an old man sits on a bench mending nets. He looks up. Sora stands in the lane with the compass in her hands. Neither speaks for a long time. Then he stands, and opens his arms.
events.arc: The Needle That Pointed Nowhere

choices.text: Withdraw quietly and let them be

effects.log: You leave them to it. The sound carries a long way: first a sob, and then a laugh.

choices.text: Greet the old man and share the news

effects.log: He has been waiting years for this day. He talks of nothing else for an hour.

events.text: Sora opens her own shop with a sign that reads: "Compasses for Those Without a Home. They All Point Somewhere." The needles in the window turn slowly, each to its own place: the sea, a bench, a doorway, a grave. Wanderers come to see where their needle leads.
events.arc: The Needle That Pointed Nowhere

choices.text: Buy a compass from her

effects.log: It points toward a house in a plain town you have not thought of in two centuries.

choices.text: Recommend the shop to every lost soul you meet

effects.log: The queue grows. The compass-maker visits, proud.

events.text: Each spring the lowest tide leaves hundreds of tiny paper lanterns stranded on the cloud-reef, each one lit and humming. Nobody knows who launches them. {npc} has gathered them for forty years and kept a ledger of the messages written inside. "Each has one line," {he} says. "None of them are addressed."
events.arc: The Lanterns That Come In With the Tide

choices.text: Read a few lanterns

effects.log: The lines are short and strange: "I am still here." "The kettle is on." "Come when you can."

choices.text: Help gather lanterns at dawn

effects.log: You fill three baskets. Each hums in your hand like a bee.

choices.text: Sit on the reef and watch them drift in

effects.log: It is the loveliest thing you have seen all year.

events.text: The messages come from the sky-whales' graveyard, {npc} has worked out: the whales drift there when they die, and the lanterns are launched by the old keepers. Each line is for a lost one. They cannot be answered, for there is no address. But they are read.
events.arc: The Lanterns That Come In With the Tide

choices.text: Write a reply and set it adrift

effects.log: Your lantern goes out with the tide. It is a small, odd comfort.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach you to launch one

effects.log: The beachcomber shows you the paper, the wax, the knot. It takes an hour.

choices.text: Leave the lanterns alone and walk away

effects.log: They hum behind you for a mile.

events.text: Years pass. The ledger fills. {npc} grows too stiff to climb the reef, and asks if you will take over the gathering. {He} hands you the ledger and a basket and a flask of tea. "They never ask for anything," {he} says. "They only want to be read."
events.arc: The Lanterns That Come In With the Tide

choices.text: Take the ledger and the basket

effects.log: You gather each spring for thirty years. You read every one.

choices.text: Promise to visit and read the ledger with {him} each year
