effects.log: You do. Over tea, the two of you read the old lines aloud.

events.text: You launch a lantern for a friend lost before you came above. It drifts out on the tide. A month later, at the lowest ebb, a lantern comes back, not yours, but with the same line you wrote, in a different hand, adding two words: "Me too."
events.arc: The Lanterns That Come In With the Tide

choices.text: Keep the lantern on your desk

effects.log: It hums until the wax gives out.

choices.text: Launch another with the same words

effects.log: A conversation across the tides begins. It lasts decades.

events.text: A stationary storm has hung over the Gale Isles for three centuries, and in its eye lives a small family of storm-keepers on a platform of floats. {npc}, a boy of ten, has never heard thunder, because the walls of the eye are muffled with cloud. {He} asks you to describe it.
events.arc: The Child Born in the Calm

choices.text: Describe thunder in words

effects.log: {He} listens with wide eyes. "It sounds like a very large person clearing their throat," {he} decides.

choices.text: Offer to show {him} real thunder

effects.log: {His} mother hesitates. "At a distance," {he} says. "At a very great distance."

choices.text: Tell {him} about the sea of cloud beyond the wall

effects.log: {He} listens, rapt. Then asks if there are fish.

events.text: You take the boy to the edge of the eye in a skiff and wait. A fork of lightning stabs the wall on the far side and, a heartbeat later, the thunder rolls across the cloud-sea like a drum. The boy claps his hands over his ears. Then he laughs.
events.arc: The Child Born in the Calm

choices.text: Let him listen to a second peal

effects.log: He counts the seconds between flash and sound. By the fifth, he is correct to a breath.

choices.text: Take him closer for a better view

effects.log: The wall is a roaring grey cliff. The boy is white and shining and utterly silent.

choices.text: Take him home and let him think

effects.log: He talks of nothing else for a week.

events.text: The boy, grown, becomes a weather-seer of the eye, and measures the wall by sound alone. The Ministry of Weather asks him to the capital. He does not want to leave the calm. His mother does not want him to stay. They ask you for advice.
events.arc: The Child Born in the Calm

choices.text: Tell him to go and return with what he learns

effects.log: He sails for the capital. A letter arrives in a year: he has found the Ministry fascinating and the food terrible.

choices.text: Tell him to stay where he belongs

effects.log: He nods slowly. The Ministry sends a scholar to him. It is a kinder trade.

choices.text: Tell them it is his choice alone

effects.log: Both are relieved and a little cross with you.

events.text: The boy sleeps badly after the lightning. He wakes in the night to the quiet of the eye, which has never frightened him before. His mother gives him a bell to ring when the walls feel close. It is a soft bell, and he rings it for a year.
events.arc: The Child Born in the Calm

choices.text: Visit and bring him a thunderbell of your own

effects.log: You craft a small bronze bell that rings like a distant rumble. He sleeps like a log.

choices.text: Send a letter of encouragement

effects.log: It is read aloud at the supper table.

events.text: At dawn, a line of footprints appears on the flat white surface of the cloud-sea off the Cedar Reach: bare, small, evenly spaced, leading out from the shore toward nothing. By noon they are gone. By next dawn, there is another line, a little longer.
events.arc: The Footprints on the Cloud-Sea

choices.text: Walk out along the prints in a light skiff

effects.log: The prints go straight, never wavering. After an hour they simply stop.

choices.text: Sit on the shore and wait for the maker

effects.log: No one comes. At sunrise the first print appears, from nowhere, at the water's edge.

choices.text: Ask the fishermen what they know

effects.log: They shrug. "Been happening since our grandfathers' time."

events.text: You stay three nights. Each night the prints go farther, one step per night. You mark the spot where the line stops. It is a little over a thousand steps from the shore. It will reach the far side of the Cedar Reach in a few hundred years, if it keeps its pace.
events.arc: The Footprints on the Cloud-Sea

choices.text: Chart the prints on a map for the Wardens

effects.log: They are impressed, and uncertain, and offer a cup of tea.

choices.text: Leave a lantern at the last print

effects.log: In the morning there is a new print beside it, and the lantern is warm.

choices.text: Step into the last print yourself

effects.log: It is cold and soft, like a stepping-stone of snow. For a moment you feel very light.

events.text: The lantern at the end of the prints is warm each dawn. You come to expect it. One morning you find a second lantern beside it, a simple paper one, with a folded note: "Thank you for the light. It is lonely out here." The hand is small and round.
events.arc: The Footprints on the Cloud-Sea

choices.text: Reply with a note and a sweet

effects.log: The note is gone by dawn. The sweet is gone, too.

choices.text: Wait up all night to see who it is

effects.log: You see nothing but a ripple, and hear a tiny pair of feet, running.

choices.text: Leave a blanket by the lanterns

effects.log: It is taken. A small fold of it appears as a flag on the next print.

events.text: The prints continue every night, and every night a note is left. Over a year you become friends with the walker, and learn by increments what the walker is: a child of the cloud, wandering outward to find the end of the sea. The walker wants no help. The walker wants only to be seen.
events.arc: The Footprints on the Cloud-Sea

choices.text: Promise to see each step, always

effects.log: You keep the promise for a long, long time.

choices.text: Tell the Wardens to protect the prints

effects.log: A post and rail are built. The prints go on, quietly, beside them.

events.text: You never learn who the walker is. But the line of prints goes on, and every year a few more people come to the shore at dawn to see the newest step. A teahouse opens. A song is written. The prints, in the end, reach the far shore, and you are there to see.
events.arc: The Footprints on the Cloud-Sea

choices.text: Wave at the empty shore

effects.log: A small cold hand brushes yours for a heartbeat.

choices.text: Drink your tea in silence and let them be

effects.log: The sea is flat and white and kind.

events.text: A cloud-boar has been rooting up the cloud-pines of the Evergreen Isle, tearing out the roots that hold the isle together. The isle-wardens will not kill it: it is the last of its herd. {npc}, the warden of the isle, wants it turned toward the wild hills, where its kind once roamed. "It is blind with grief," {he} says.
events.arc: The Cloud-Boar That Must Be Turned

choices.text: Track the boar by its rooting

effects.log: A line of scattered earth leads to a muddy hollow where the huge beast lies panting.

choices.text: Lay out food in a line toward the hills

effects.log: You scatter chestnuts. The boar follows the line, sniffing, and halts at the last one.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to tell you about the herd

effects.log: {He} tells you of forty boars, then twenty, then one.

events.text: The boar charges. It is not at you, but at an old stump it mistakes for a rival. The turf shakes. The warden shouts to stand clear, and the beast wheels round, eyes rolling, tusks as long as an arm.
events.arc: The Cloud-Boar That Must Be Turned

choices.text: Step aside and let the charge pass

ok.log: The boar thunders past, and you roll clear, breathless, delighted.

fail.log: The boar clips your hip as it passes. You spin into the mud, bruised.

choices.text: Throw a coat over the stump so it stops looking like a rival

effects.log: The boar sniffs the coat and, confused, lowers its head.

choices.text: Climb a tree and wait

effects.log: It is undignified. It is safe.

events.text: The boar slows, tired and puzzled. {npc} approaches with a bag of acorns and a quiet voice, and the boar eats from {his} hand. Then {he} starts walking, slowly, toward the hills, and the boar follows, without being asked, a great hairy shadow in the dusk.
events.arc: The Cloud-Boar That Must Be Turned

choices.text: Walk beside the boar and the warden

effects.log: The three of you cross the isle at dusk without a word.

choices.text: Go ahead and clear the path of fallen branches

effects.log: It is slow, steady work. The way is clear by dark.

events.text: The chestnut trail leads the boar to the wild hills in a week. It stops at the edge of a stand of old oak, sniffs once, and walks in. A moment later, a second boar-snout appears at the edge. The herd was not lost; it had only moved. {npc} sits down on the grass and laughs until {he} cries.
events.arc: The Cloud-Boar That Must Be Turned

choices.text: Watch the reunion from a distance

effects.log: Two boars sniff each other all over. It is surprisingly formal.

choices.text: Leave a basket of chestnuts at the oaks

effects.log: It is gone by dawn.

events.text: Two ministers have arrived at the same reef-landing on the same morning, in two skiffs, and neither will disembark first. Precedence forbids it. They have been bobbing for two hours. {npc}, the landing-marshal, is sweating through {his} coat. "I have consulted three rulebooks," {he} says. "They disagree."
events.arc: Who Lands First

choices.text: Consult the rulebooks yourself

effects.log: The first says the senior lands first. The second says the guest. The third is a recipe for plum jelly.

choices.text: Propose both land at once on parallel planks

effects.log: {He} stares. "That is... unprecedented," {he} says. "I like it."

choices.text: Bring the ministers a pot of tea on trays

effects.log: Both accept. Neither spills. Neither lands.

events.text: The ministers agree to the double plank, but disagree about the width. One wants it broader; the other says broad planks imply weakness. A carpenter is summoned, and then a second carpenter, and then, in desperation, a child with a ruler.
events.arc: Who Lands First

choices.text: Let the child measure it

effects.log: The child chooses eleven hands. Both ministers are annoyed, which is a kind of fairness.

choices.text: Propose the plank be the width of the landing itself

effects.log: It is accepted with a cough. It is, technically, the only width that offends neither.

choices.text: Offer to hold one end of the plank

effects.log: You do, solemnly. It is a very small honour.

events.text: Both ministers land at once. A trumpet is blown, a banner dropped, and, to everyone's embarrassment, the landing-marshal weeps with relief. The ministers are gracious. They send you an official thanks: a scroll with a large seal and, inside, a small box of plum jelly.
events.arc: Who Lands First

choices.text: Accept the thanks and the jelly

effects.log: The jelly is wonderful. The seal looks well on your wall.

choices.text: Give the jelly to the child with the ruler

effects.log: The child is solemn, then radiant.

events.text: A new rule is drafted that evening: "On the occasion of equal rank at a landing, planks shall be laid in pairs." It becomes Regulation Four Hundred and Twelve. The marshal reads it aloud, once, to the empty landing, and sighs with something like love.
events.arc: Who Lands First

choices.text: Add a footnote in your own hand

effects.log: "Or, when in doubt, ask a child." It stays.

choices.text: Say nothing and enjoy the quiet

effects.log: The landing is empty and pleasant in the evening.

events.text: A child on the Moss Isle has a fever that the guild healer will not treat without a seal and a fee. You have herbs and some knowledge. {npc}, the child's grandmother, begs you at the door. "I can pay in eggs," {he} says. "I can pay in anything."
events.arc: The Healer Without a Seal

choices.text: Brew a fever tea and sit with the child

effects.log: You sit up all night. By dawn the child is cool and sleeping.

choices.text: Fetch a guild healer and pay the fee for the child

effects.log: The healer comes, grudging, and prescribes the same tea. You pay the fee and say nothing of it.

choices.text: Direct {npc} to the healer's kitchen door

effects.log: {He} nods. It is not the answer {he} wanted.

events.text: The child is well in three days. The guild finds out in four. A warden arrives at the grandmother's door with a form: treating a patient without a seal is a fine of forty stones, or a month in the guild's kitchen. {npc} stands in front of you with a wooden spoon in {his} hand.
events.arc: The Healer Without a Seal

choices.text: Offer to serve the month in the guild kitchen

effects.log: You wash pots for thirty days. The cooks, who like you, slip you dumplings.

choices.text: Argue that the child was in danger of life

effects.log: The warden consults a rule. There is an exception for emergencies. The fine drops to ten.

choices.text: Pay the fine in full (forty stones)

effects.log: It is an enormous sum. The grandmother weeps.

events.text: The guild's own healer, an old man who has never smiled, comes to you in the kitchen on your last day. "The fever tea was right," he mutters. "I would not have thought of the willow." He leaves a small book of notes on your stool and goes out without another word.
events.arc: The Healer Without a Seal

choices.text: Read the book, and add a page of your own

effects.log: It is a quiet exchange of learning. You do not meet again.

choices.text: Return the book with a note of thanks

effects.log: He sends it back with a pressed willow leaf in it.

events.text: The Moss Isle forgets the fine. It remembers the child. For forty years, a small basket of eggs is left on your doorstep at the new year, wherever you live. You never discover how the grandmother finds you. The eggs are always fresh.
events.arc: The Healer Without a Seal

choices.text: Share the eggs with your neighbours

effects.log: The tradition grows. In time the whole lane knows it.

choices.text: Eat them at once, with joy

effects.log: They are the best eggs in all the heavens.

events.text: A nest of wind-serpent eggs hangs from a high cliff in a net of woven gale. A pilot offers to take you close, for a price. A ranger says to stay away. The eggs hum in chorus.

choices.text: Watch the nest from the ranger's post

effects.log: The ranger lets you look through the telescope. A tiny head pokes out of a shell.

choices.text: Pay the pilot to circle once

effects.log: You see all forty eggs. The pilot is red with shame at the end.

events.text: A cloud-boar has made a wallow in the garden of a quiet monastery and refuses to leave. The monks say it is a blessing. The gardener says it is a plague. The boar says nothing.

choices.text: Scratch the boar behind the ear

effects.log: It groans with joy and rolls onto its back.

choices.text: Help the gardener move the herbs out of its path

effects.log: You save the sage. The boar settles into the thyme.

events.text: A star-moth has been battering itself against a lamp-lit window for an hour. The householder inside wants it out. The moth wants in. A third party, the cat, wants both.

choices.text: Open the window and let the moth in

effects.log: It circles the lamp and settles. The cat watches it with a dignified yearning.

choices.text: Take the lamp outside and move it beyond the garden

effects.log: The moth follows. The householder sighs with relief.

events.text: On a warm night a cloud of star-moths drifts through a peach orchard and every blossom lights up in turn. The orchard-keeper stands with his hat off, saying nothing.

choices.text: Stand beside the keeper and watch

effects.log: It lasts the better part of an hour. The keeper wipes his eyes.

choices.text: Pick a blossom and keep it pressed

effects.log: It glows faintly for a year.

events.text: A carp in the temple pool is said to grant wishes to anyone who feeds it a bun. The temple sells the buns for one stone. The carp is unusually round. Its wishes, a local tells you, are modest ones.

choices.text: Buy a bun and wish for a good day

effects.log: The day, in the end, is quite fine. Whether the carp had a hand in it is another matter.

choices.text: Tell the temple the carp should be on a diet

effects.log: A priest glares. A child giggles. The carp ignores you.

events.text: A school of cloud carp follows a lone angler all the way down the lane, hoping for crumbs. The angler is embarrassed. "I never fed them," he insists. "They simply like my hat."

choices.text: Admire the hat

effects.log: The angler beams. The carp swirl delightedly.

choices.text: Buy the hat for two stones and wear it

effects.log: The carp follow you instead. It is not a comfortable thing.

events.text: A ribbon of wind-serpent hide, long as a street, is stretched out to dry on the roofs of the dyers' quarter. It hums as the breeze moves across it, a low unhurried note.

choices.text: Stand under the ribbon and listen

effects.log: The note settles in your chest. For an hour you feel utterly at ease.

choices.text: Ask the dyers where it came from

effects.log: A tale of an old serpent that came to die on the roof. They sing to it every spring.

events.text: A cloud-silk hem stall sells only hems, by the foot. Customers buy the hem and sew it on to old, plain cloaks, which at once look rich. The seller makes more than the cloak-makers.

choices.text: Buy a hem for yourself (1 spirit stone worth)

effects.log: It transforms an old coat. The coat does not feel like itself, but looks very well.

choices.text: Compliment the seller's trade

effects.log: The seller bows. "It is all in the edges," they say.

events.text: A stall sells star-iron nails, three for a stone. A sign says: "Genuine. Fell at dawn." A passerby mutters that the sign has been the same for forty years. The nails are a plain grey.

choices.text: Buy three nails and test them

effects.log: They are quite ordinary iron. The seller nods, unembarrassed: "I never said which dawn."

choices.text: Ask the seller for a real piece

effects.log: A pause. A small, cold, heavy lump is produced from a cloth. It is priced at a fair sum.

events.text: A child on the quay holds up a bottle that is jerking and humming, plugged with a cork. "It is a gale," the child says. "Only a very small one. I caught it myself."

choices.text: Ask to hold the bottle

effects.log: It tugs at your fingers, eager to be off.

choices.text: Tell the child to let it go in a field

effects.log: The child does, and the whole field bows in a ring.

events.text: A compass-seller on a cloud-bridge sells needles that point to "the place you most want to be." A queue forms. Most come away puzzled; a few come away weeping; one comes away laughing.

choices.text: Try one yourself

effects.log: The needle points at the seller's tea tin. You laugh, and so do they.

choices.text: Watch the faces of those who try

effects.log: You learn more from the faces than any needle could tell.

events.text: The reef-crabs of Pearl Reef hold a dance at the low spring tide. They line up in two rows and sidle in unison, clicking. The audience is a thousand gulls, motionless and rapt.

choices.text: Watch from a respectful distance

effects.log: The dance ends in a bow. The gulls applaud with their wings.

choices.text: Join the dance at the end of the row

effects.log: The crabs make room. It is a very sedate affair.

events.text: A lantern hangs from the rigging of an old reef wreck and lights itself each dusk. A ferryman swears it has done so for a century. He refuses to sail past it without lifting his cap.

choices.text: Lift your cap too

effects.log: The lantern flickers once in reply.

choices.text: Row out to see how it lights itself

effects.log: A tiny moth sits on the wick. It smiles, or does something moth-like.

events.text: In a pocket of calm at the heart of a squall a small pond of cloud-water lies perfectly still, reflecting stars that are not in the sky above. A swimming fish looks up at them, thoughtfully.

choices.text: Sit by the pond until the squall passes

effects.log: The stars in the water shift, a little, like a slow breath.

choices.text: Skim a stone across the pond

effects.log: The ripples run out in perfect rings. The fish turns away.

events.text: A watchman stands on a little tower at the edge of the eye, noting its width. He measures the wall with a knotted rope. "Seven paces smaller than last year," he says. "I do not know if I am glad."

choices.text: Hold the rope end for the measurement

effects.log: He thanks you. The number is the same.

choices.text: Bring him a flask of tea

effects.log: He nods. He drinks it slowly, his eyes on the wall.

events.text: In the ruin of a sunken gatehouse sits a cup of star-iron, half full of cloud-water that has not spilled in a thousand years. A tarnished note beside it says: "For the next traveller."

choices.text: Drink from the cup

effects.log: It tastes of cold stone and a very old rain. You feel a little braver.

choices.text: Refill the cup and leave it for the next

effects.log: The cup gleams slightly as you put it back.

events.text: A bookshop in a back lane has a door at the rear marked "Staff Only" that opens, when you push it, onto a cloud-balcony with a single chair and a view of the sunset. A sign says: "Free to anyone who asks."

choices.text: Sit on the chair and watch the sunset

effects.log: The sky turns gold, then pink, then violet. The bookshop keeper brings tea unasked.

choices.text: Leave a book on the chair for the next visitor

effects.log: You choose an old poetry book. You hope it is read.

events.text: A hostel on the Willow Reach displays a sign that reads "Sealed guests only." A yard behind it has a lean-to and a pump. A sleepy girl tells you the cook leaves a pot there for the unsealed, every night.

choices.text: Eat the stew and wash the pot

effects.log: It is lentils and onion. It is excellent.

choices.text: Leave a coin under the pot

effects.log: The coin is gone by morning, and a clean pot is in its place.

events.text: A rogue like yourself is selling mended boots from a blanket at the edge of the market. The market warden has ordered the blanket moved three times already. The rogue is calm about it.

choices.text: Buy a pair of boots and chat

effects.log: The boots are good. The rogue knows every back lane in the quarter.

choices.text: Help carry the blanket to a better corner

effects.log: The warden watches, frowns, and says nothing.

events.text: At the Edge of Heaven stands a postbox with no town, no clerk and no stamps. It is stuffed with letters addressed to the world below. A notice says: "Collected at the turn of the year."

choices.text: Post a letter to someone below

effects.log: It is a short one. You feel lighter for it.

choices.text: Read the stranger's addresses and say a quiet word for them

effects.log: Names of the mortal world, names of rivers. You say them one by one.

events.text: A small raincloud has hung over the Lower Reach since spring and has not rained once. At its heart a door of falling drops stands open. {npc}, who minds the local weather-posts, says the cloud is a realm in the making. "It lives one season," {he} says. "Then it rains itself out. Nobody has stayed to see how."
events.arc: The Realm Inside a Raincloud

choices.text: Walk through the door of drops

effects.log: The drops part around you like a curtain, cool and unhurried.

choices.text: Watch from the edge and take notes

effects.log: You learn that the cloud breathes in and out once an hour, and that the door follows the breath.

choices.text: Leave it to the weather-post

effects.log: You wish {npc} luck. A realm that lasts a season does not need an audience.

events.text: Inside, the cloud is a hall of hanging water with rooms made of slow rain. In one, a pool holds the reflection of a sky that is not above you. In another, a stair of mist climbs to a ceiling that keeps changing its mind. The air tastes of the first day of spring.
events.arc: The Realm Inside a Raincloud

choices.text: Climb the stair of mist

effects.log: It holds under your steps and sags when you hesitate. At the top is a bench made of cloud, and the view of an ocean you cannot name.

choices.text: Sit by the pool and read the other sky

effects.log: The stars in it are in the wrong places, and the longer you look the more sensible the wrongness feels.

choices.text: Listen to the rain in the walls

effects.log: Every drop sounds a different note. By evening you hear a tune.

events.text: The season is turning. The cloud thins at the edges and the rooms begin to rain themselves out one by one. At the heart, the last room holds a single drop that does not fall, the size of a plum, humming like a held note.
events.arc: The Realm Inside a Raincloud

choices.text: Take the drop out with you

effects.log: It sits in your palm as cool as a coin. The walls sigh as you leave.

choices.text: Let it fall with the rest

effects.log: It drops, and the whole cloud answers with one long soft rain over the Lower Reach.

choices.text: Sit with the drop until the room is gone

effects.log: You sit through the last hour. When the walls are gone you are floating on a puff of damp air.

events.text: Years later the drop on your shelf still hums on rainy nights. {npc} visits and holds it to {his} ear. "That is the whole season in there," {he} says. "Every room, every stair. Do not let it dry." Rain falls on your roof. For an hour the walls of your house are a hall of slow water.
events.arc: The Realm Inside a Raincloud

choices.text: Keep the drop in a jar of rainwater

effects.log: Each spring it sings the first note of a season long gone, and the neighbours stop to listen.

choices.text: Return it to a raincloud with {npc}

effects.log: You release it into the next cloud that passes. The cloud sings, once, and drifts on.

events.text: The Lower Reach had a good harvest of rice-mist that year, and {npc} swears it was the cloud's gift. A small stone now stands where the door of drops once hung. Someone leaves a bowl of rainwater at it each spring, and the bowl is always empty by morning.
events.arc: The Realm Inside a Raincloud

choices.text: Leave a bowl yourself every spring

effects.log: The bowl is empty each morning. Something drinks.

choices.text: Tell the story to the next weather-post warden

effects.log: The warden writes it in the post ledger, under "Seasonal Phenomena". Under "Cause" they write: gratitude.

events.text: {npc}, who has swept the Jade Court floor for four hundred years, taps a flagstone with the end of {his} broom. It rings hollow. "Third from the throne," {he} says. "It has rung hollow since before the court was built. I have never lifted it because nobody told me to."
events.arc: The Vault Under the Floor of the Jade Court

choices.text: Offer to lift it with {npc}

effects.log: The stone is lighter than it should be. Under it is a stair of pale jade, going down.

choices.text: Ask the Ministry of Precedence if you may

effects.log: A clerk brings a form. The form asks you to describe the hole you are asking to open. You cannot, so you do.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to leave it alone

effects.log: {He} nods slowly. The broom goes on sweeping, around the stone.

events.text: The stair ends in a long cold room of jade shelves, thick with dust and ribboned tags. This is where the court keeps what it has promised to forget: seals of dismissed ministers, gifts that were refused, a clock that counts down to something unnamed.
events.arc: The Vault Under the Floor of the Jade Court

choices.text: Read the tags on the refused gifts

effects.log: Every gift was given in good faith and refused for reasons of precedence. Each tag is a small tragedy of manners.

choices.text: Study the clock

effects.log: Its hand moves a hair per decade. The face is marked in no calendar you know.

choices.text: Leave the dust undisturbed and go up

effects.log: You close the stone behind you. The court above goes on with its ceremony, unaware of what it stands on.

events.text: The clock has moved. A soft chime sounds under the floor during the audience of the new moon, and several ministers glance down. By evening the hush has the shape of a rumour: the court has a thing it promised to forget, and it is waking.
events.arc: The Vault Under the Floor of the Jade Court

choices.text: Tell the Ministry of Precedence what lies below

effects.log: A cold hush follows. Then a very polite man with a very sharp sleeve asks you to repeat it, in writing.

choices.text: Say nothing and let the clock be

effects.log: You keep the secret. The chime sounds three more times that year, and each time you are the only one who does not look down.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what to do

effects.log: {npc} considers the broom. "Sweep," {he} says. "Whatever comes, the floor will want sweeping after."

events.text: The chime ends. The stone lifts of its own accord and a small sealed jar rolls out across the floor of the court: the promise, finally due. Inside is a single line of ink: "Remember that we asked for forgiveness first." The ministers stare. {npc} sweeps it up with the dust.
events.arc: The Vault Under the Floor of the Jade Court

choices.text: Read the line aloud before the court

effects.log: The hush is deep and then, slowly, something like relief. Several ministers weep quietly into their sleeves.

choices.text: Keep the jar and tell no one

effects.log: You put the jar on your shelf. You never learn what court asked whom for what forgiveness. Sometimes that is the better ending.

events.text: The chime stops, years later, as quietly as it began. {npc} says the floor sounds solid now, the hollow gone. Under it, perhaps, the clock has finally struck its hour, and no one was there to hear. {He} sweeps on, humming.
events.arc: The Vault Under the Floor of the Jade Court

choices.text: Raise a cup to the floor and the sweeper

effects.log: The two of you drink on the third flagstone from the throne. It is a small, odd, perfect ceremony.

choices.text: Walk away without looking down

effects.log: You learn that not every secret is for the telling. The court stands, which is what courts do.

events.text: Every seventh year a herd of cloud-bison crosses the cloud sea, a slow grey tide of shoulders and breath, a hundred isles long. {npc} has followed them for sixty years on a patched skiff. "They never stop," {he} says. "Neither do I. Come along a season and see if you can keep up."
events.arc: The Migration of the Cloud-Bison

choices.text: Join the skiff for a season

effects.log: The herd moves at a walk, which in the sky is faster than most isles. You eat in the skiff and sleep to the thud of hooves.

choices.text: Follow on your own cloud and keep a record

effects.log: You write down where they graze and where they sleep. The pattern is a spiral, widening.

choices.text: Watch them pass from a high isle

effects.log: It takes three days for the herd to pass. You never see the end.

events.text: Years on, the herd has thinned. {npc} says the old cows lead the way and the young ones are fewer every cycle. The pastures along the route are going silent: cloud-grass dying where the isles have drifted off. The herd is walking toward somewhere that may no longer exist.
events.arc: The Migration of the Cloud-Bison

choices.text: Plant cloud-grass along the route

effects.log: It takes root in the vapour and drinks the dawn. By the next crossing there is a green line across the sky.

choices.text: Ask the Ministry of Fog to move a fleet of isles

effects.log: A year of forms. In the end three isles shift a day eastward, and the herd finds them.

choices.text: Stay with {npc} and the old cow

effects.log: You walk beside the lead cow for a whole season. Its gaze is calm and enormous.

events.text: Twenty years in, the herd reaches the place it has always walked toward: a hanging basin of still cloud, white and ringed with mountains of mist. It is a calving ground, old as the sky. {npc} weeps openly. The calves are born in a single dawn.
events.arc: The Migration of the Cloud-Bison

choices.text: Keep guard through the dawn

effects.log: You stand between the herd and the wind till every calf is up. Nothing in your life has felt more useful.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} and watch the calves rise

effects.log: The two of you say nothing for hours. The first calf stumbles to your knee, sniffs, and blunders on.

choices.text: Record the calving ground for the maps

effects.log: Your chart is passed to every steersman of the fleet. The ground is respected by all.

events.text: {npc} is too old to follow now. At the next crossing {he} sits on the dock and waves the herd past, and you take the oars. The lead cow stops by the dock, bends one huge head over the old herd-follower, and breathes once. {npc} laughs, wet-eyed, and says the herd has finally followed.
events.arc: The Migration of the Cloud-Bison

choices.text: Row on with the herd in {npc}'s place

effects.log: You follow. Sixty years go by like cloud. The herd never learns your name, and you do not mind.

choices.text: Stay on the dock with {npc}

effects.log: You sit with the old one till the last bison has passed. The dock creaks in the silence of such company.

events.text: The herd grows. Every seventh year the sky darkens with it, and the pasture-line you laid runs clear across the Lower Reach. {npc} is remembered in a children's song, mostly wrong. Visitors still ask which of the isles was the herd-follower's. You say all of them.
events.arc: The Migration of the Cloud-Bison

choices.text: Teach the song its true words

effects.log: The children correct their parents. The song is, for a season, accurate.

choices.text: Let the song stay a little wrong

effects.log: Some stories are better with room to breathe. The herd, at least, sounds the same.

events.text: Far under the cloud sea lies an isle that sank while its people slept. Lamps burn there. Chimneys smoke. The isle has not sunk, quite: it has settled into a pocket of thick calm, and everyone aboard is still dreaming. Only the steward is awake, and has been for two hundred years. "Come in," {npc} calls up the shaft. "I need someone to talk to."
events.arc: The Isle That Sank in Its Sleep

choices.text: Go down the shaft of calm

effects.log: The air thickens to warm syrup. You float down, slowly, past cloud-pine roots, to a landing under a lamp.

choices.text: Call down and ask what happened

effects.log: "A bell rang the wrong hour," says {npc}. "We all lay down at once. I was in the cellar and missed it."

choices.text: Leave a lamp at the top of the shaft

effects.log: The lamp burns against the dark. You hope someone below sees it.

events.text: {npc} shows you the sleepers: a baker with flour on a smile, a clerk of the isle with a pen still in hand, the girl Rua with a cheek on an open book. Everything is as it was the hour the bell rang. The steward has kept the dust off every face.
events.arc: The Isle That Sank in Its Sleep

choices.text: Try to wake the girl with the book

effects.log: Rua frowns in sleep, murmurs a line of the book you cannot catch, and rests again. The steward flinches. "Not yet," {he} says. "Not unless we know why."

choices.text: Look for the bell that rang

effects.log: It hangs in the harbour tower, cracked in a way that looks gentle. Its tongue is wrapped in cloth, wound by hand.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} and listen

effects.log: The steward speaks of the baker, the girl, the clerk. You keep each name.

events.text: You find the cause in a sealed cupboard of the tower: a note in the bell-keeper's hand. "The sleep is a mercy. A plague of waking dreams was loose on the isle. We chose to sleep through it. Wake us when it has passed." No one has dared to see if it has.
events.arc: The Isle That Sank in Its Sleep

choices.text: Wake the isle, one sleeper at a time

effects.log: The baker first, blinking, with a yawn the size of a cave. The isle rouses like a sea turning over.

choices.text: Hold the isle in sleep another year and test the air

effects.log: You and {npc} take turns breathing the lamplight and watching for any waking dream. None comes.

choices.text: Leave the note where you found it

effects.log: The sleep goes on. You hope it is still the mercy it was meant to be.

events.text: The isle wakes. The baker complains the bread is cold. Rua wants to finish the book. The bell, unwrapped, rings the right hour. The sleepers weep, laugh, and look for their lost two centuries. {npc} sits at the harbour with a cup of tea, and for the first time in two hundred years does not look up.
events.arc: The Isle That Sank in Its Sleep

choices.text: Help the isle rise to the cloud-top

effects.log: You and the steersmen haul the isle on ropes of mist. It breaks the surface at dawn, streaming. The isle cheers for the first time in two centuries.

choices.text: Stay a season to teach them the new calendar

effects.log: Two hundred years of news is a great deal of tea. You pour it daily.

events.text: The plague of waking dreams has long since died. The air is clean. You and {npc} carry the sleepers into the sun, one at a time, to a field of cloud-grass above. They wake over a season, in the soft light, in the right order. Rua wakes last, with the book on a chest still rising, and says: "I know how it ends."
events.arc: The Isle That Sank in Its Sleep

choices.text: Read the last page with Rua

effects.log: It ends well. You never tell {npc} what was written, only that the steward may sleep now.

choices.text: Hold the door for the steward to rest

effects.log: {npc} sleeps for a month, the first in two hundred years, and wakes to a harbour full of voices.

events.text: The isle is at rest again when you return years on, but in the daylight, this time on purpose. {npc} watches from the harbour. The baker keeps a hammock by the oven for the nap now taken properly. {npc} has opened a school of waking and sleeping. The bell rings every night at the same soft hour.
events.arc: The Isle That Sank in Its Sleep

choices.text: Take a nap on the harbour with the rest of them

effects.log: It is the best nap of your long life.

choices.text: Leave the isle to its own gentle hours

effects.log: It needs nothing from you. That is the finest thing to know of a place.

events.text: On a flat grey isle stands the duel-ground of the old immortals: a circle of stones with a ring of tally-posts around it, cut with notches. {npc}, a marker bound to the place long ago, still tallies. "Step in and I will count," {he} says. "Any blow. Any word. Any look. It is all kept."
events.arc: The Duel-Ground That Keeps Score

choices.text: Step into the ring and spar with shadows

effects.log: Shapes rise from the stones: faint old fighters, bowing. Each of your strikes puts a notch on a post.

choices.text: Walk the posts and read the old scores

effects.log: A thousand-year score between two friends, still level. A war-score, scratched out and rewritten as a draw.

choices.text: Decline politely and watch from the rim

effects.log: {npc} notches your politeness. You do not ask what it was scored.

events.text: The marker shows you a post nobody has touched in nine hundred years. Two names are cut into it, close together, with an unfinished tally between them. "They were friends," says {npc}. "They never settled it. The post has been waiting ever since. Someone ought to."
events.arc: The Duel-Ground That Keeps Score

choices.text: Settle the old score as a third party

effects.log: You stand between the two names and speak to the ring. A faint warmth moves round the stones, and one notch is added to each side.

choices.text: Duel the shadow of the stronger name

effects.log: It bows, and takes you apart gently, with great precision. You are bruised and understand something of the sword.

choices.text: Leave the post as it is

effects.log: Some scores are better kept open. The marker nods, and notches the nod.

events.text: Years later you return. The ring has a new notch, in a hand you do not know. {npc} frowns. "Someone has been here without me," {he} says. "They counted themselves, which no one is permitted to do. Scores mean nothing if the scorer is the scorekeeper." A shape, faint, stands in the ring.
events.arc: The Duel-Ground That Keeps Score

choices.text: Challenge the stranger in the ring

ok.log: The shape is a mirror of your own old self. You strike it down and the ring settles. It is the first honest score you have kept in years.

fail.log: The shape strikes you in the shoulder with no rancour. You stagger out. The marker notches it as a draw, for kindness.

choices.text: Ask the stranger to name itself

effects.log: It cannot, but it points at the post of the old friends. It has come to finish the score and has not the heart.

choices.text: Tell the marker to ignore the notch

effects.log: {npc} very slowly rubs the notch away. The ring settles. The marker is, you realise, relieved.

events.text: {npc} comes to you at the end of the long century with a single post carried on {his} back. "Cut your name in this," {he} says. "Your score is level with the ring, and I am tired of keeping the books alone. Take over the tallying when I am gone." The post is heavy with old marks.
events.arc: The Duel-Ground That Keeps Score

choices.text: Take up the post and the tally

effects.log: You carve your name. The ring accepts it with a soft chime. For the next century you count, fairly, without favour.

choices.text: Carry the post to the Jade Court and propose a keeper

effects.log: The court sends a junior clerk. {npc} approves. You write the contract in three drafts.

events.text: The marker comes to you, thin as a candle. "I have kept the score of everything but my own," {he} says. "Add it up for me." You count: a long life, a patient one, and not one notch of malice. {npc} smiles. The ring rings once, softly. Then {he} is gone and the posts are silent.
events.arc: The Duel-Ground That Keeps Score

choices.text: Cut one notch for the marker on the oldest post

effects.log: The notch stays. Every duellist who visits afterwards touches it once for luck.

choices.text: Stay a night in the ring and listen to the stones

effects.log: They hum a long low tune of gratitude. You go home lighter.

events.text: Qi has been going missing from the Tea Terraces: a breath here, a day's cultivation there, a whole apprentice's morning gone. {npc} found paw-prints in the dew, small as a thumb, three-toed, and glowing. "A thief-beast," {he} says. "Dew-weasel, by the toes. It drinks qi the way a cat drinks cream. Help me catch it."
events.arc: The Thief-Beast That Steals Qi

choices.text: Lay a trap of bait-qi

effects.log: You pour a thread of qi into a bowl and wait in the dark. At midnight something sips.

choices.text: Follow the prints by day

effects.log: They wind across four terraces and end at a hole in the roots of a tea-bush, warm to the touch.

choices.text: Guard the apprentices' practice hall

effects.log: You sit by the door, and for a week no one loses a breath.

events.text: The dew-weasel is a slip of silver fur with enormous black eyes, no larger than a sleeve. It sits, stuffed with qi, in the bowl, hiccupping. It looks at you with total innocence. {npc} breathes out. "It is a baby," {he} says. "It is starving. That is why it steals."
events.arc: The Thief-Beast That Steals Qi

choices.text: Offer it a bowl of your own qi, freely

effects.log: It drinks and curls into your palm, humming. The terraces are safe that night.

choices.text: Net it gently and carry it to the Beast Wardens

effects.log: The wardens take it with dignity. It watches you over the net-rim, betrayed.

choices.text: Leave it the bait bowl and watch

effects.log: It sleeps in the bowl till dawn. {npc} makes tea for the pair of you.

events.text: The weasel grows. It follows you on your travels, sleeping in your sleeve, and takes only a little qi each night, politely, like a guest. {npc} visits and shakes {his} head. "A weasel that steals is a nuisance," {he} says. "A weasel that asks is a friend. Yours has learned the difference. Ask it to teach you."
events.arc: The Thief-Beast That Steals Qi

choices.text: Let the weasel teach you to stretch qi thin

effects.log: The trick is generosity, oddly. You learn to spread a thread of qi so fine it can feed a whole terrace.

choices.text: Send it to live in the tea-bush and visit

effects.log: It stays, fat and bright, and the terraces never lose another breath.

choices.text: Go on as you are

effects.log: You share your qi with an odd small friend. Nothing wrong with that.

events.text: {npc} is old now, and the tea has gone quiet. The weasel curls on the shelf beside the cups, grey at the muzzle. "It was the best thief I ever caught," {he} says, "because it was the only one who stole nothing it did not give back." The weasel opens one eye and sips a thread of qi from the steam.
events.arc: The Thief-Beast That Steals Qi

choices.text: Bury it when its time comes, under the oldest tea-bush

effects.log: The bush blooms silver the next spring. Every apprentice who sips its tea feels briefly kind.

choices.text: Stay with it through the last night

effects.log: It purrs in your lap until the dew comes. Then there is only a warmth on your hands.

events.text: The weasel is the terrace's mascot now. {npc} keeps a ledger of what it steals and what it returns, and the returns are always larger. Children come to see the "qi cat". The Beast Wardens put up a sign: DO NOT FEED, and below it, in another hand: unless it asks.
events.arc: The Thief-Beast That Steals Qi

choices.text: Leave a bowl at the sign every dusk

effects.log: It is always empty by dawn, and the dew on the rim glows faintly.

choices.text: Argue with the Wardens to leave the sign

effects.log: You lose, politely. The sign comes down. The bowl does not.

events.text: A jade slip drifts into the stacks of the lower archive, carved with a name nobody knows: the lost expedition of the Hundred Banners, lost four thousand years ago. {npc} turns it over. "It is a page of a diary," {he} says. "There must be more. Pieces of it have been washing in for years, and no one has put them together."
events.arc: The Diary of the Lost Expedition

choices.text: Offer to help gather the pieces

effects.log: {npc} grins. A jade slip from the first wave of the expedition has been found in a hundred places.

choices.text: Read the first page carefully

effects.log: The diarist writes about weather, tea, a lonely cough. The tone is gentle and unafraid.

choices.text: Return to the stacks and wait for more

effects.log: Pieces come in with the tide. The archive hums.

events.text: Three pieces more. The diarist names the expedition's purpose: to chart the lower edge of the sky, where the clouds end and something else begins. They name each companion in turn, with a line of fondness. One is called the Quiet Cook. One is called the Boy Who Always Looked Down.
events.arc: The Diary of the Lost Expedition

choices.text: Write each name on a tag and pin it to a map

effects.log: The map fills with small tags. The companions become a company.

choices.text: Try to retrace the route from the diary

effects.log: The weather is wrong and the isles have moved. You get as far as the first cloud-reef.

choices.text: Ask the archive for similar slips

effects.log: Two more come from a very high shelf, and a sheaf of pressed flowers.

events.text: The last pieces arrive. The diary stops mid-sentence. "We have found the end of the clouds, and below it is--" The rest is gone, or was never written. {npc} sits very still. "It could be the best thing in the sky," {he} says, "or the worst. They did not live to tell."
events.arc: The Diary of the Lost Expedition

choices.text: Finish the sentence with your best guess and sign it

effects.log: You write: "...home." It is probably wrong. It is, you decide, the right ending.

choices.text: Leave the sentence broken

effects.log: The archive hangs it unfinished. Scholars stand before it for centuries, each completing it differently.

choices.text: Take a copy and set out to find the end of the clouds

effects.log: The way is long. You take the diary like a lamp.

events.text: Centuries pass. {npc} is gone, but the diary hangs in the archive with its last line. The expedition's companions are written in the roll of the lost, honoured each year. You visit the diary at the new year and say a name to it. The paper warms very slightly, as if someone, far down, had heard.
events.arc: The Diary of the Lost Expedition

choices.text: Say the Quiet Cook's name, with a bow

effects.log: A scent of steeped tea fills the hall, and fades.

choices.text: Add a line to the roll and leave

effects.log: It is a small ceremony, but kept.

events.text: You dream of the end of the clouds. Below it, a calm sea of something pale and warm, and a small raft with eleven people on it, singing. You wake to the sound of the archive's bell. The ending the diary never wrote was not a tragedy at all.
events.arc: The Diary of the Lost Expedition

choices.text: Write the dream down and place it with the diary

effects.log: The two pages hang side by side. Visitors read one and then the other, and look up from both, smiling.

choices.text: Keep the dream to yourself

effects.log: Some endings should be told only by those who dreamed them.

events.text: A grotto in a hanging cliff will answer any question, if you leave something behind. A sign scratched at the mouth reads: "Ask once. Pay at the door. The grotto does not give change." Inside, a voice like a cold bell waits. People have left their names, their luck, a childhood summer, a favourite song.
events.arc: The Grotto That Answers for a Price

choices.text: Ask a small question, pay a spirit stone

effects.log: The grotto weighs the coin. "Fair," it says. Your question is answered with a single plain sentence.

choices.text: Ask a great question, pay with a memory

effects.log: You feel a summer leave you like a bird. The answer is vast and lovely and you cannot quite keep it.

choices.text: Read the names carved at the mouth and leave

effects.log: Many of the names are of those who asked and paid and walked out smiling. You walk out smiling too.

events.text: You come back, years later, with a better question. The voice is the same. The price has changed, as prices do. "Today I take only what you can spare," the grotto says. "It is up to you to decide what that is." The grotto has never let anyone choose before.
events.arc: The Grotto That Answers for a Price

choices.text: Offer your fame

effects.log: The grotto takes a measure of what the sky says of you. The answer is lucid, and your name gets a little smaller.

choices.text: Offer a month of your qi

effects.log: You feel your reserves drain gently. The answer is quiet and true.

choices.text: Offer nothing and ask anyway

ok.log: The grotto laughs, a surprised silver sound. "No one has dared. Ask." The answer is given free, and your luck is, for a moment, shining.

fail.log: The grotto is silent. Then it takes something you did not offer: an old name from the back of your mind. You stagger out.

events.text: A letter is waiting at your door, sealed with grey wax. "The grotto thanks you for paying fairly," it says. "It has kept your question and your payment together in a small room. You may visit them when you wish." There is a drawing: a tiny room with a tiny lamp, and two small jars on a shelf.
events.arc: The Grotto That Answers for a Price

choices.text: Visit the little room

effects.log: The jars glow. In one is a question; in the other a memory of a summer. You can hold them both. For one afternoon you are a child again.

choices.text: Leave the room unvisited

effects.log: Some debts are best paid and never revisited.

events.text: You return a third time, and the grotto is quiet. A strip of mist lies in the doorway like a bow. "You have paid enough," the voice says at last. "I will answer one more without a price." You find that the question you came with has changed, and ask the new one.
events.arc: The Grotto That Answers for a Price

choices.text: Ask what you most need to know

effects.log: The answer is a sentence, a little long, a little strange. It is the best thing anyone has ever told you.

choices.text: Ask what the grotto itself wishes

effects.log: The voice is silent a long while. "To be asked, once, how it is," it says. "Thank you."

events.text: The grotto is a little quieter now. The sign at the mouth has a new line, smaller: "Come back and tell me what you did with it." You could. You do not know what you would say.
events.arc: The Grotto That Answers for a Price

choices.text: Return and tell the grotto what you did with the answer

effects.log: You talk for an hour. The grotto listens, hums, and asks a question of its own.

choices.text: Let the sign stay unanswered

effects.log: Some conversations are best left on the stairs.

events.text: A guest-immortal is a wandering rogue who earns a bed with a skill: mending, singing, counting stars, teaching a child to read a cloud. You arrive at the first isle with a bundle and no seal. {npc}, who keeps the hostel, looks you over. "No seal means double the price," {he} says. "Or a good story. I have a weakness for stories."
events.arc: The Guest-Immortal Who Moves On

choices.text: Tell a true story of your own

effects.log: {npc} listens with a whole face, and gives you the corner room at the old rate.

choices.text: Offer to mend the roof for the night

effects.log: The roof is mended, badly but with feeling. {npc} sniffs and says it is better than the last guest.

choices.text: Pay the double price in stones

effects.log: It is not kind, but it is fair. You leave with a little less and a great deal of sleep.

events.text: The hostel guests look down on a rogue. A Jade Void junior leaves the table when you sit. A Nine Clouds pair whisper behind their cups. {npc} says nothing, but slides your bowl first across the board. "I serve in order of arrival," {he} says calmly, "and you arrived before any of them."
events.arc: The Guest-Immortal Who Moves On

choices.text: Thank {npc} and ignore the whispers

effects.log: You eat in quiet comfort. By morning one of the whisperers has sat down across from you.

choices.text: Leave a verse on the table for the guests

effects.log: It is a gentle poem about places that reject and places that do not. Two guests ask for a copy.

choices.text: Stay quiet and slip out early

effects.log: You catch the ferry at first light. The hostel diminishes behind you, small and lit.

events.text: Ten years on you are known on four isles as the guest who mends, the guest who tells, the guest who leaves. A letter arrives at the last hostel you slept in. {npc} is retiring. "The hostel needs a keeper who understands the road," {he} writes. "You are not an isle person. You are what isles need."
events.arc: The Guest-Immortal Who Moves On

choices.text: Take the hostel and keep a place for rogues

effects.log: The hostel doubles in a season. Its sign says: EVERY GUEST SERVED IN ORDER OF ARRIVAL.

choices.text: Decline, and keep the road

effects.log: You write back with thanks. {npc} replies, a month later: "Of course. The road needs you too."

choices.text: Visit once a year and sleep in the corner room

effects.log: The room is always aired. The bowl is always first.

events.text: A hundred years later the hostel stands, now a small institution on the isle, with a hostel-keeper who is not you and a rule that is. In the common room hangs your old bundle on a nail, labelled: THE FIRST GUEST WITHOUT A SEAL. Pilgrims touch the bundle for luck.
events.arc: The Guest-Immortal Who Moves On

choices.text: Add a line to the plaque beneath the bundle

effects.log: It reads: "Served in order of arrival." The keeper has no idea who wrote it. You smile.

choices.text: Sit at the corner table and listen to the road-stories

effects.log: Four rogues tell stories of four isles. The bowl comes first to the one who came earliest.

events.text: You walk the road for a hundred years more. At every hostel you are known by a single word: guest. At every isle, someone has left a bundle on a nail in your honour. You are lonely, and you are not. Under a distant sky {npc} sends a last kite-note: "Eat. Rest. Go on."
events.arc: The Guest-Immortal Who Moves On

choices.text: Take the note and go on, lightly

effects.log: You do. The road has never been lighter.

choices.text: Stop for a season on a high isle and write it all down

effects.log: You have a great deal to say about doors that open.

events.text: The Unfinished Sun-Seed is said to lie at the bottom of a drowned cloud-trench: a half-made star that, once finished, would warm the sky for a thousand years or burn it down. Every faction wants it. {npc}, a wandering seeker, finds you at the trench-mouth. "I will tell you honestly," {he} says. "I want it, and I should not. Come with me, and keep me honest."
events.arc: The Treasure Everyone Wants and Nobody Should Have

choices.text: Go down with {npc} and keep watch

effects.log: The trench is cold. The seeker walks ahead, sweating at the thought of what lies below.

choices.text: Warn the Ministry of what is going on

effects.log: A clerk writes it down. Two weeks later the trench is surrounded by marshals. You get there first.

choices.text: Refuse and let the seeker go alone

effects.log: {npc} nods, without anger. "Then I will have to keep myself honest," {he} says.

events.text: At the bottom the Sun-Seed hangs in a hollow, the size of a plum, glowing a warm unfinished gold. It hums, hungry. The seeker kneels, hands shaking. "It is beautiful," {he} says. "I could finish it. I could do such good." And the seed, very gently, hums back.
events.arc: The Treasure Everyone Wants and Nobody Should Have

choices.text: Pull {npc} away from the seed

effects.log: You haul the seeker back by the sleeve. {He} struggles and then goes limp, weeping, and nods.

choices.text: Study the seed without touching it

effects.log: It is a half-made star of unbelievable craft, abandoned by someone who knew better. The signature is not a name but a sigh.

choices.text: Wait and see what {npc} does

effects.log: {He} sits with the seed all night and says nothing. At dawn {he} stands and walks away.

events.text: Word of the seed has spread. Marshals, mercenaries, a Star Sea pavilion and a pair of Demon Realm envoys all converge on the trench-mouth. Everyone swears they mean to guard it. Nobody believes anyone else. {npc} appears at your door, haggard. "They will tear the sky for it," {he} says. "We have to hide it."
events.arc: The Treasure Everyone Wants and Nobody Should Have

choices.text: Slip down and move the seed to a deeper trench

ok.log: You carry it through the dark, warm in your palms and silent as a sleeping coal. You sink it where no hand will reach.

fail.log: The seed flares at the crowd's noise. You drop it, singed, and it settles back into its hollow, brighter and angrier.

choices.text: Stand at the mouth and refuse all comers

effects.log: You hold the line a night and a day. The envoys withdraw, grumbling. The marshals do not.

choices.text: Go to the Jade Court and ask for a guard

effects.log: The court assigns a guard of six. It is, for a month, enough.

events.text: The seed is gone from every map. Every faction accuses every other of taking it. {npc} laughs bitterly over tea. "We saved the sky," {he} says, "and nobody will ever know. I find I do not mind." The seed lies deep, humming its unfinished note in the dark, waiting for someone wise enough to leave it be.
events.arc: The Treasure Everyone Wants and Nobody Should Have

choices.text: Drink to the nameless guard

effects.log: You and the seeker drink a long evening away. Neither of you ever tells the secret.

choices.text: Chart the trench falsely so no one finds it

effects.log: It takes a year of careful lies. The false map is a masterpiece.

events.text: The Sun-Seed flares, and for three days the lower sky glows gold and uneasy. Then it dims, exhausted, but not before every faction has seen it. {npc} hangs {his} head. "I am sorry," {he} says. "I thought I could hide it. I could not." The scramble for it will go on for centuries.
events.arc: The Treasure Everyone Wants and Nobody Should Have

choices.text: Stand beside {npc} and keep trying to guard it

effects.log: You keep a rota with six other guards across the years. The seed stays where it is.

choices.text: Ask the Jade Court to bind it in law

effects.log: The court draws a long treaty on a short scroll. It holds, mostly.

events.text: Beneath the Hanok Isle, among the hanging roots of the cloud-pines, a lamp burns in a hollow. {npc} lives there, and has lived there for six hundred years, tying and untying knots in the roots. "Each knot is a word," {he} says. "The isle is learning to speak. Come, tie one, if you have something to say."
events.arc: The Hermit in the Roots of the Isle

choices.text: Tie a knot that says "thank you"

effects.log: The root tightens a little around the knot. Somewhere high above, the isle shivers with something like pleasure.

choices.text: Study the hermit's old knots

effects.log: There is a grammar here, slow and green. You read three lines of a poem the isle is writing.

choices.text: Sit and share a cup of dew-tea

effects.log: The hermit pours into a cup made of a hollow root. It tastes of rain a very long time ago.

events.text: One of the old knots has come undone. {npc} frowns. "That one was a promise," {he} says. "The isle promised to hold its people through the wind season. Now there is a loose end." You can feel the isle shiver above. Winter is coming, and the roots are tired.
events.arc: The Hermit in the Roots of the Isle

choices.text: Retie the promise with the hermit

effects.log: Your hands shake. The root answers. The knot holds, and the roots across the whole underside shiver in relief.

choices.text: Tie a new, kinder promise beside it

effects.log: The roots do not understand at first, then they do. The knot is smaller and stranger and holds better.

choices.text: Carry a message up to the isle's elders

effects.log: They listen politely. The hermit's promise is not their business, they say. Not yet.

events.text: The wind season arrives, and the isle holds. Elsewhere in the fleet two isles break loose and drift apart. The hanging roots sing in the gale like a chorus of cellos. {npc} sits by the lamp, a little smug. "I told you," {he} says. "Words are structure."
events.arc: The Hermit in the Roots of the Isle

choices.text: Thank the hermit publicly at the isle council

effects.log: The council stares. Then one old elder says, "We have always wondered who minded the roots." {npc} is mortified and pleased.

choices.text: Bring a bundle of fresh root-twine as a gift

effects.log: The hermit weeps a little. The twine goes straight onto a new knot.

choices.text: Stay by the lamp through the storm

effects.log: The wind sings. You doze beside the old one.

events.text: The hermit asks you to untie the last knot of {his} life. "It says my name," {he} says. "When it is untied, the isle will forget me gently, so that no one grieves." The root is warm in your fingers. Above, far above, a bell rings once.
events.arc: The Hermit in the Roots of the Isle

choices.text: Untie it, softly, and let {npc} go

effects.log: The root lets go with a long sigh. The lamp goes out. The next morning, a new green shoot grows from the knot's end.

choices.text: Refuse, and tie the knot tighter

effects.log: The hermit looks at you with more love than reproach. "So be it," {he} says, and lives another century, tangled and content.

events.text: You return a hundred years later and the lamp is lit. A young apprentice of the roots has arrived, and sits tying knots among the old ones. The apprentice does not know the hermit's name. The knots still say it.
events.arc: The Hermit in the Roots of the Isle

choices.text: Tell the apprentice who started the roots speaking

effects.log: The apprentice writes it on a leaf and ties it into the oldest knot. The roots shiver.

choices.text: Leave the apprentice to find it out

effects.log: Some stories ought to be read in knots.

events.text: The Ministry of Weather logs a rain that fell upward for an hour over the Hanwol Isle. Rain that falls up is a snow-season thing; in summer it is a sign of something. {npc}, a junior clerk, hands you the report. "They want a verdict," {he} says. "Is it a prank, a portent or a clerical error?"
events.arc: The Rain That Fell the Wrong Way

choices.text: Go and watch the drops rise

effects.log: They climb in neat lines. The people of the isle stand with open mouths and buckets.

choices.text: Review the isle's weather-ledger

effects.log: Six hundred days of clear skies and one blank page. Someone has torn out a day.

choices.text: Write "portent" and file it

effects.log: It lands in the portent drawer. The drawer is rather full.

events.text: Hanwol Isle keeps a tradition: once in a century, a child is born at the exact moment the sun sets and the moon rises. The rain fell up on the hour that child cried. "The child may be a rain-caller," {npc} says. "The Ministry will want the child. The isle will not give the child up."
events.arc: The Rain That Fell the Wrong Way

choices.text: Propose the child be schooled on the isle

effects.log: The Ministry grumbles. The isle weeps with gratitude. A tutor is sent, and the Ministry has a new correspondent.

choices.text: Take the child's gifts to the Ministry as a delegate

effects.log: The child sits on a stool and makes a drizzle rise. The Ministry offers a place, and a pension for the isle.

choices.text: Return and report "clerical error"

effects.log: The report is accepted. The isle thanks you. The child keeps raining up on Tuesdays.

events.text: Years pass. The child, grown, is a quiet weather-singer whose rain falls up on command, and all across the Lower Reach harvests turn on those tunes. {npc} writes you a note. "The singer has been asked to sing for the Jade Court," {he} says. "Afraid. Can you come?"
events.arc: The Rain That Fell the Wrong Way

choices.text: Attend the audience beside the singer

effects.log: The court is vast and cold. The singer sings anyway, and an upward rain gilds every pillar. The court is silent, and then applauds.

choices.text: Write the singer a letter of encouragement

effects.log: The singer reads it before the court and steadies. It is a modest kindness, and it works.

choices.text: Wish the singer well from afar

effects.log: The upward rain falls over the court that day. You hear of it by evening.

events.text: The weather-singer is made a minister of small rains, and the isle sends you a bolt of silk with raindrops stitched upward through it. {npc} is promoted, too, and says it is your fault. The Ministry's drawer of portents is, for the first time in a century, emptied.
events.arc: The Rain That Fell the Wrong Way

choices.text: Wear the silk to the next audience

effects.log: Everyone asks. You tell them the truth. The Ministry of Weather has a new reputation, for kindness.

choices.text: Fold the silk and keep it

effects.log: On rainy days it rustles in the chest like something alive.

events.text: The upward rain falls again at the weather-singer's wedding, and the whole isle stands in the drops holding buckets and laughing. The Ministry files it under "joy". {npc} writes in the margin: "Verdict: none needed."
events.arc: The Rain That Fell the Wrong Way

choices.text: Add your seal beside it

effects.log: Your seal and the clerk's, side by side, on a report that finally settles nothing.

choices.text: Raise a cup of rain to the new minister of small rains

effects.log: The rain in your cup is excellent. The drops are, for once, going the right way.

events.text: A star in the Star Sea's charts burned out a thousand years ago, but its light is still crossing the sky. {npc} has built a mirror to catch it, a disc of polished star-iron on a mount of bone. "It arrives next year," {he} says. "One last night of a star that is gone. Help me aim."
events.arc: The Mirror of a Dead Star

choices.text: Help aim the mirror, patiently

effects.log: It takes a month of small adjustments. The disc finally rests exactly toward the dead star's old place.

choices.text: Compute the exact moment of arrival

effects.log: Your numbers say a quarter hour after midnight. {npc} writes it in ink on the mount.

choices.text: Bring tea and keep {npc} company

effects.log: The astronomer does not eat for days. You see that the tea is drunk.

events.text: The night comes. The mirror gathers a thin cold ray, white, trembling. It falls on the astronomer's notebook and lights a page. "It is its voice," {npc} whispers. "A star speaking after it is dead." In the light you see words forming, faint, like frost.
events.arc: The Mirror of a Dead Star

choices.text: Read the words aloud

effects.log: They are a list of the star's planets. Every one is dead. The last line says: "I was glad of company."

choices.text: Write down what the light says without reading it

effects.log: The frost settles into your page. It fades by morning, and your notes are the only copy.

choices.text: Stand in the light and say nothing

effects.log: It rests on your hands, cold and honest. The astronomer weeps quietly.

events.text: The Star Sea asks you and {npc} to explain the mirror's findings. A pavilion elder wants to know if the dead star can be revived. Another asks if its light can be harvested. A third, quietly, if its planets are inhabited. The room waits for a verdict.
events.arc: The Mirror of a Dead Star

choices.text: Say it should be honoured, not used

effects.log: The room is divided. A third of the elders agree. The matter is referred to committee, where it will live for four hundred years.

choices.text: Present the data and let the elders decide

effects.log: They decide badly, but slowly. No harm is done.

choices.text: Defer to {npc}

effects.log: {He} says only: "Let it be remembered." The elders nod.

events.text: The mirror hangs in the pavilion now, labelled: THE LAST LIGHT OF A STAR NAMED NOTHING. Each year on the night it arrived, pavilion members sit in front of it in a cold white hall and say what they remember. {npc} says the star would have liked to be asked how it was.
events.arc: The Mirror of a Dead Star

choices.text: Speak a line for the star each year

effects.log: The line changes with the years. The mirror hums faintly when it is true.

choices.text: Leave the star to its silence

effects.log: The hall is quiet and cold. It is, in its way, a lovely quiet.

events.text: The astronomer dies, in time, and the mirror is moved to an observatory with a better view. The dead star's light, if any more is coming, will be caught again some night in the next three thousand years. A student notes in the margin: "Kind of a long wait."
events.arc: The Mirror of a Dead Star

choices.text: Write beneath it: "Worth it."

effects.log: Your hand is the same hand as {npc}'s was, in a way. The ink dries on a question to the sky.

choices.text: Leave the margin as it is

effects.log: It is a good margin.

events.text: On the Jade Void's highest ledge a disciple, {npc}, has sat at the mouth of a cave for forty years. The cave is empty, as far as anyone knows. "I was told to wait for my master to come out," {he} says. "The master went in the day I arrived. I think the master has forgotten I am here."
events.arc: The Disciple at the Cave Mouth

choices.text: Sit with {npc} for an afternoon

effects.log: The wind comes out of the cave smelling of old tea and sandalwood. It is a lonely, comforting smell.

choices.text: Walk a few steps into the cave

effects.log: The cave ends after a dozen paces in a wall of smooth jade. There is a door-shaped dent, and nothing behind it.

choices.text: Bring {npc} a meal and leave

effects.log: It is the first hot food in a month. The disciple eats slowly, surprised.

events.text: You return a season later with a rake and a pot of paint. Together you repaint the dent in the wall: a door, red, with a brass ring. {npc} laughs for the first time you have seen. "Now it looks like a door," {he} says. "Perhaps the master will use it."
events.arc: The Disciple at the Cave Mouth

choices.text: Knock on the door three times

effects.log: Silence. Then, faintly, three knocks answer from the other side.

choices.text: Wait with {npc} through the night

effects.log: At midnight the ring on the door turns by itself, a quarter turn, and stops.

choices.text: Go and ask the Jade Void elders about the master

effects.log: They check the roll. There is no such master. There never was. The disciple has been waiting for a rumour.

events.text: {npc} learns the truth from the elders, or enough of it: the master was a figure the old disciples invented to give a new arrival a reason to sit still and learn patience. "So I was waiting for nobody," {he} says. "And yet I learned everything I know in that time. What does that make the master?"
events.arc: The Disciple at the Cave Mouth

choices.text: Say the waiting master was the best teacher the sect ever had

effects.log: The disciple laughs, a long, rueful, grateful laugh, and stands up for the first time in years.

choices.text: Say the waiting taught the lesson, not the master

effects.log: {He} nods slowly. The truth gives the disciple something solid to lean on.

choices.text: Say nothing, and walk the ledge with {npc}

effects.log: The two of you walk the whole length of the Void in silence. It is a good silence.

events.text: {npc} becomes the Void's new keeper of the ledge, and invents, in turn, a master for each new arrival: gentle, absent, endlessly forbearing. "It is a kindness," {he} says. "And the best lessons are the ones you finish yourself." The red door stays on the cave wall, with a ring that sometimes turns.
events.arc: The Disciple at the Cave Mouth

choices.text: Keep the secret and help invent the master

effects.log: You write the master a very good first name and a bad temper. The disciples love the master.

choices.text: Leave {npc} to the work

effects.log: It will be done well.

events.text: The disciple takes up a tea-table on the ledge, and sits in the cave mouth no more. But every evening, at the hour of the old waiting, {he} stands by the red door and says: "Good night, Master." The ring turns, maybe. It might be the wind.
events.arc: The Disciple at the Cave Mouth

choices.text: Stand beside {npc} at the door

effects.log: The ring turns. You will never be sure.

choices.text: Smile and leave them to it

effects.log: There are worse ways to be loved by a rumour.

events.text: {npc}, a rogue net-maker, hangs a great net on the Pale Reef at the turning of each tide. It sings in the wind, a note for every thread. "I take no seal and no pay," {he} says. "I catch what the tide brings: lost shoes, ribbons, small bright things. People come for their lost things. Rogues are the only ones who check the net, since no one else will."
events.arc: The Net That Sings in the Reef-Tide

choices.text: Help {npc} sort the catch

effects.log: There are three hundred ribbons, a lute with no strings, a lock of hair in a locket. Each has a story you imagine.

choices.text: Offer to repair the net where it frays

effects.log: You re-thread it with qi. It sings a half tone sweeter.

choices.text: Look through the catch for something you lost

effects.log: You find nothing, and do not mind. It was a pleasant afternoon among others' things.

events.text: Among the catch is a letter in a sealed jade tube, addressed in a hand that trembles. "To the one who finds this," it begins. A faction pavilion elder has been sending messages out on the tide for years, hoping a rogue will find one. {npc} reads it aloud. It is an apology.
events.arc: The Net That Sings in the Reef-Tide

choices.text: Deliver the apology to the one it was meant for

effects.log: You follow the clues, isle to isle. The recipient is a sleeping scholar who weeps when you read it.

choices.text: Write a reply in the same hand and cast it into the tide

effects.log: Three seasons later the tide returns your reply, annotated in a third hand.

choices.text: Return the letter to the net with a note

effects.log: The net hums softly. Someone else will find it.

events.text: The Ministry of Fog wishes to close the net. "Tide-rigging is a licensed activity," a clerk says to {npc}, with real regret. {npc} has no licence. It is an old argument, and the clerk is not unkind. The net, meanwhile, goes on singing in the wind.
events.arc: The Net That Sings in the Reef-Tide

choices.text: Speak for the net before the Ministry

effects.log: You cite fourteen reports of lost things returned. The clerk puts the licence form on the table, and signs it for {npc}.

choices.text: Offer to be the net's licensed keeper

effects.log: Your name goes on the form. The rogue stays free, and the net stays hung.

choices.text: Let {npc} argue alone

effects.log: {He} does, with dignity, and loses with a bow.

events.text: The net sings on, now licensed, and rogues of a dozen isles hang their own nets on the reef. The tide returns lost things by the thousand, and every catch is read, sorted, returned. {npc} sits at the quay with a cup in hand and says: "I always knew the tide had manners."
events.arc: The Net That Sings in the Reef-Tide

choices.text: Raise a cup to the net

effects.log: The net hums a gentle approval. You leave before dusk with a small blue ribbon.

choices.text: Walk home along the reef at dusk

effects.log: The nets sing in the wind. You hear them all the way home.

events.text: The net is cut down by a Ministry clerk one grey morning, years on, after the licence lapsed. {npc} hangs a new one the same night, in the same place, with the same song. "They will come back," {he} says. "They always do. And I will still be here."
events.arc: The Net That Sings in the Reef-Tide

choices.text: Hang a net of your own beside it

effects.log: Two nets sing in thirds. The Ministry sighs and turns a blind eye.

choices.text: Bring {npc} a flask of hot wine

effects.log: The two of you watch the tide come in. The net catches a single silver shoe.

events.text: A mist hound pup on the edge of the Cherry Isle has learned to hide. It folds itself into the fog on the road and appears behind visitors with a bark. Children of the isle say it is the best game in the sky. The pup waits for you at the bridge.

choices.text: Play along, pretend to be surprised

effects.log: The pup glows with delight and follows you for a mile, tail wagging.

choices.text: Teach it a new hiding place

effects.log: It disappears into a barrel of rainwater and does not come out until supper.

events.text: A pocket garden hangs inside a hollow cloud-reef: three plum trees, a bench, a fish pond the size of a tray. A faded sign says: PLEASE LEAVE IT AS FOUND. Nobody lives here. Nobody ever has. The plums are ripe, and the bench is warm.

choices.text: Sit on the bench for an hour

effects.log: The plums sway. You eat none. The warmth leaves you with an odd quiet.

choices.text: Eat a single plum and leave the pit

effects.log: It tastes of every summer. The pit takes root in the reef by evening.

events.text: On a calm night a sky whale passes under the isle singing, so low the floors thrum. Old people say it is a lullaby, and that somewhere in the cloud sea a very small whale is being sung to sleep. The isle holds its breath.
