choices.text: Hum along very softly

effects.log: The whale's note shifts, just slightly, to meet yours. It is the strangest duet of your life.

choices.text: Sit in silence until it has passed

effects.log: It takes the whole night. You wake at dawn feeling faintly adopted.

events.text: A single marble pillar stands on a floating rock, with no roof, no floor, no ruin round it. Moss grows on the north side. A swallow has built a nest in the capital. Nobody can say what the pillar held up, and the swallow is not telling.

choices.text: Climb the pillar and look out

effects.log: From the top you can see six isles, each tiny. A swallow circles you, annoyed.

choices.text: Read the lichen

effects.log: The moss has grown in a pattern, a map of the rock below. You draw it. It is surprisingly accurate.

events.text: On a cloud-bridge between two quiet isles, a toll-ghost stands with an outstretched hand. It has collected nothing for a thousand years and looks relieved when you approach. "One coin or one story," it says, in a papery voice. "I am short on both."

choices.text: Tell it a short story

effects.log: The ghost listens with great seriousness and then waves you through, wiping an eye.

choices.text: Pay a spirit stone

effects.log: The ghost bows deeply. The stone vanishes, and for a mile you feel unaccountably fond of strangers.

events.text: The crater of a fallen comet is lined with green glass, fused in the heat of a thousand years ago. Walking across it is like walking across the inside of a bell. Every step rings. Birds avoid the place. The echoes seem to answer in the wrong order.

choices.text: Walk the glass slowly, listening

effects.log: You learn to place your feet so the echo follows you like a pet. The sound lingers in your bones for a week.

choices.text: Skip a pebble across and watch the ripple of sound

effects.log: The glass sings a chord. Seven birds rise at once, far off.

events.text: At the Edge of Heaven, swallows nest in the cracks of a cliff that has no ground beneath it. They dive into the white and return with their beaks full of cloud, which they feed to their young. The chicks are very pale and very fat.

choices.text: Watch the feeding all afternoon

effects.log: The parents never miss a trip. The chicks never cease asking. You find yourself envious of both.

choices.text: Leave a dish of mist on the ledge

effects.log: A fat chick climbs in and sulks. The parents regard you with new suspicion and eat from it.

events.text: In a small mirror-pond on the Cloud Terraces a carp swims upside down, tail to the sky and head to the reflection. The gardeners have given up asking why. Other fish avoid it, politely. It is, they say, very old and very clean.

choices.text: Sit by the pond and ask it a question

effects.log: The carp turns right-side up, regards you with one huge eye, and turns back. Somehow, that was an answer.

choices.text: Feed it with a crumb of cloud-rice

effects.log: It takes the crumb upside down, delicately. The pond ripples softly in applause.

events.text: A stair of white stone climbs a cliff-face into mist, each step cut with a name. Visitors climb it reading the names aloud. After the ninth hundredth step the names are in a language nobody speaks, and the stair carries on up.

choices.text: Climb till the names stop

effects.log: You climb for a day. The names stop at a landing with a stone bench and a small cut: your own name, in a hand you do not recognise.

choices.text: Read three hundred names aloud, then rest

effects.log: Each name cools in your mouth like a pebble. You carry them home in your head, like a rosary.

events.text: On the rolling cloud-hills above the Soyo Isle a shepherd drives a flock of tiny clouds with a crook. They graze on starlight at dawn and bleat softly. Come winter, they are sheared, and the fleece is spun into a thin, cold, delicious silk.

choices.text: Help drive the flock home

effects.log: The little clouds break and rejoin like water. You go home damp, happy and a little taller.

choices.text: Buy a skein of fleece (1 Low-Grade Spirit Stone)

effects.log: It chills your hands when you hold it, and warms your heart when you wear it.

events.text: At the harvest-turn the people of the Yeonhwa Isle release a hundred paper lanterns into the cloud sea, each with the name of a loved one who has gone below. The lanterns do not rise. They sink, slowly, down to the world under the clouds, glowing.

choices.text: Release a lantern for someone you have lost

effects.log: You write the name and let go. It sinks, small and steady, until you cannot see it.

choices.text: Hold the string for a child who is afraid to let go

effects.log: The child lets go at last and weeps and laughs. You walk home together in the half dark.

events.text: A plain wooden door hangs in the air a hand's breadth above the cloud-floor of a quiet glade, with no wall and no frame. It is locked. A key is on a hook beside it, and a sign says: DO NOT. Of course, you think. Of course.

choices.text: Unlock the door and look in

effects.log: You open it. On the other side is the same glade, seen from slightly higher up. A man in a chair looks back at you, startled, and shuts it.

choices.text: Respect the sign and sit with a book

effects.log: You read a chapter. The door, you notice, does not open. It seems relieved.

events.text: A pup of the reef-crab kind, no larger than a button, has attached itself to your sleeve and will not let go. It clicks softly, hungry, small. A passing steersman says, kindly, that they are always a nuisance for about a year, and then they are loyal for six hundred.

choices.text: Keep the pup in a teacup

effects.log: It climbs out nightly. It brings you gifts: buttons, bottle-caps, one fine pearl.

choices.text: Carry the pup back to the reef

effects.log: It does not want to go. It clicks all the way there and then, abruptly, goes.

events.text: A stair of nine hundred steps winds inside a hollow cloud. A sign says: Wish at the top. At the bottom, a second sign: Wish at the bottom. In the middle is a bench with a third: This is where you wish for the thing you should.

choices.text: Climb the nine hundred steps and wish

effects.log: At the top the wind is cold and clear. Your wish comes out smaller and better than the one you carried up.

choices.text: Wish at the bench in the middle

effects.log: You wish for the thing you should. It is a surprise to find out what it is.

events.text: A great nest of woven cloud-reed hangs under a cliff, empty, big as a hall. Whatever laid in it is long gone. A scatter of blue-grey feathers lies about its rim, each longer than your arm. The nest sways in the breeze and smells faintly of rain.

choices.text: Take a feather as a keepsake

effects.log: It hums when the wind turns. The bird it came from, you suspect, is not far.

choices.text: Sit in the nest for a night

effects.log: It is the warmest, softest bed in the sky. You sleep nine hours and wake feeling hatched.

events.text: In the lee of an isle you find the First Hearth of the immortals: a ring of black stones with an ash-bed that is still, faintly, warm. A small iron pot hangs over it on a chain. Scratched on the rim, in an old hand: "Anyone may eat. Anyone must wash up."

choices.text: Cook a simple meal in the old pot

effects.log: The pot makes everything taste like the dish you most needed. You wash up carefully.

choices.text: Sweep the ashes and leave the hearth tidy

effects.log: It is a small kindness, and the stones seem to settle gratefully.

events.text: A thin bright wind flows between two isles like a ribbon, visible only when it catches sunlight. It carries pollen, bird feathers, small sounds. Steersmen call it the Letter Wind, because everything it carries ends up somewhere that mattered.

choices.text: Release a note into the Letter Wind

effects.log: It rises, curls and is gone. You never learn who reads it.

choices.text: Follow the wind to its end

effects.log: It ends at a tiny garden with a bell. The bell rings once for you, and nobody answers. The wind drops a feather.

events.text: A tiny isle called Pantry hangs between two big ones, with nothing on it but a shed, a stove and a shelf of jars, labelled in a quavering hand. A sign: HELP YOURSELF. LEAVE SOMETHING. The jars are full of preserves, pickles, and a single jar of lightning, for emergencies.

choices.text: Leave a jar of your own

effects.log: You leave a small jar of plum jam. The shelf looks a little more like home.

choices.text: Take a jar of pickles and a note of thanks

effects.log: The pickles are sharp and glorious. You leave a note and a bow.

events.text: A flock of thunder sparrows crosses the sky at dusk, crackling, a mile-long ribbon of small grey bodies and blue sparks. They are migrating, as they do every autumn, to the warm shelves. The whole isle goes quiet to let them pass.

choices.text: Stand under the flock with your arms raised

effects.log: A spark lands on your sleeve and goes out. You hum for an hour.

choices.text: Count the flock on a ledger

effects.log: You reach six thousand and lose count. Close enough.

events.text: A petition has sat unread on the Jade Court table for six hundred years, bound in blue ribbon and weighted with a pebble. Every steward has moved it aside for a more urgent one. No one remembers who wrote it. A porter holds it out to you, and shrugs.

choices.text: Read the petition aloud

effects.log: It is a request for a bench in the Court's outer garden, for old people to sit. You see that the Court has no such bench. You see it by evening.

choices.text: Put it on top of the pile and leave

effects.log: It will be there when the next steward comes. So it goes.

events.text: On the high pasture of the Tu Isle you cut across the fresh track of a dawn stag: a line of hoof-prints that glow faintly gold, then fade. They end at a boulder where the stag has rubbed its antlers. A few hairs remain on the rock, bright and silky.

choices.text: Keep the hairs, as a memento of a stag unseen

effects.log: They shine in your pocket for a week.

choices.text: Sit and wait for it to return

effects.log: It does not. But you spend a whole peaceful afternoon at the boulder, listening for hooves.

events.text: An abandoned watch-post stands on a drifting shelf, with a log-book on the table. The last entry: "All quiet. Watching still." The ink is fresh. The chair is warm. There is nobody here, and a thermos on the sill steams faintly.

choices.text: Take up the watch for an hour and make an entry

effects.log: You write: "All quiet." It feels, oddly, like a duty done.

choices.text: Sit down and have the tea

effects.log: It is good tea. You leave a thank-you note in the log.

events.text: On the Thousand-Year Orchard, the peaches ripen once a century and all at once. The orchard-keepers hang bells in the branches, and when a peach is ready a bell rings. You arrive in the middle of a symphony, with a basket and a very short window.

choices.text: Pick fast, taking only ripe ones

effects.log: You fill the basket in an hour. Your hands are sticky and your heart is light.

choices.text: Sit beneath a tree and eat one slowly

effects.log: It is the best peach you will ever have. Time is a very strange thing.

events.text: At the very Edge of Heaven stands a postbox, a bright red one, with no street and no town and no letter. A sign says: LAST COLLECTION: WHENEVER. The box is empty. It has a slot for letters going down.

choices.text: Post a letter to someone below

effects.log: It drops away into the white. You will never know if it is read.

choices.text: Sit beside the box a while

effects.log: The wind is clean. You think about everyone you would write to.

events.text: A sky whale has anchored itself to the underside of a quiet isle to scrape its barnacles on the cloud-pines. Hundreds of little silver shells rain down, tinkling. Children collect them in baskets. The whale sighs with contentment, which rattles the windows.

choices.text: Collect barnacles with the children

effects.log: You come home with a basket of shells and a story you will tell for a century.

choices.text: Scratch the whale's back with a long pole

effects.log: It groans with pleasure and shifts slightly. The isle tilts a degree and settles again.

events.text: A two-headed goose waddles through the market, honking in two keys. The heads argue constantly and agree on nothing but bread. Its owner, an old woman with a cart, says the goose has outlived three husbands, all of whom disagreed with it.

choices.text: Offer the goose a roll

effects.log: Both heads snap at it, then glare at each other. One gives way. You are thanked, in two voices.

choices.text: Ask the owner how she keeps them from fighting

effects.log: "I do not," she says. "That is the secret. Everyone needs someone to disagree with."

events.text: A cave in a cloud-bank belongs, a sign says, to a "Mr. Gwaneum, away until further notice". Inside, a cot, a stove, a shelf of well-thumbed books. It is warm and dry. The note on the table says: if anyone needs the cave, they may borrow it, but please feed the cat.

choices.text: Borrow the cave for the night and feed the cat

effects.log: The cat, of which you see no sign, has a clean bowl by morning. The books are excellent.

choices.text: Leave a note and a spirit stone for the cat

effects.log: You pay it forward. The cave seems, subtly, pleased.

events.text: Forty years ago a sky whale rose under the Dalnae Isle during its lantern festival and, in a moment of confusion, swallowed the whole dancing floor. {npc} was the lantern-master then. "We are all still in there," {he} says, "in a sense. On festival nights you can hear the drums from inside the whale. Come with me when it passes."
events.arc: The Whale That Swallowed a Festival

choices.text: Wait on the cliff with {npc} for the whale

effects.log: It comes at midnight, a long dark hill under the stars. The drums are faint, then clear, then gone.

choices.text: Ask the old festival-keepers what they remember

effects.log: Each remembers a different song. None remember the whale's arrival, only the lanterns going out one by one.

choices.text: Leave a lantern on the cliff-edge

effects.log: The whale's eye glints as it passes. You like to think it saw.

events.text: The whale returns on schedule and {npc} asks you to ride it. A skiff is lashed to the great fin, and you slip into the dark of its mouth. The air inside is warm and smells of incense. The drums are loud now, and under them a crowd laughing. Lanterns hang from the ribs like fruit.
events.arc: The Whale That Swallowed a Festival

choices.text: Follow the drums deeper

effects.log: The floor is still there: a wooden dancing floor, cracked, with a hundred shapes of mist dancing on it, in no hurry to stop.

choices.text: Light a lantern from {npc}'s and hang it on a rib

effects.log: The mist-dancers turn toward the light and bow. One of them looks, for a moment, like someone {npc} lost.

choices.text: Listen from the mouth and do not go in

effects.log: The sound is enough. The whale breathes in and out around you, slow as a tide.

events.text: A dancer in the mist steps out of line and walks to {npc}. The old lantern-master goes white. It is the one who danced beside {him} forty years ago. The mist-figure holds out a hand. "Dance with me," it says in a voice like a held breath. "The song is not over."
events.arc: The Whale That Swallowed a Festival

choices.text: Urge {npc} to take the hand

effects.log: {npc} does. For three bars the two of them dance. When the mist-figure fades, {npc} is crying, and laughing.

choices.text: Hold {npc} back, gently

effects.log: "Not yet," you say. The mist-figure waits, patient, and bows. {npc} stays in your arm, trembling.

choices.text: Step aside and let them decide

effects.log: {npc} stands very still for a long while. Then {he} bows, and does not take the hand.

events.text: The whale sets {npc} and you down in the dawn on the Dalnae Isle, damp and humming. The lantern-master sits on the quay with a cup and says: "I thought I would dread it. I did not. The song is over now, for me." The whale passes under the isle one last time, and does not come back.
events.arc: The Whale That Swallowed a Festival

choices.text: Raise a cup of cloud-wine to the whale

effects.log: It is a small salute. The whale's eye rolls, and it sinks into the cloud sea, singing one low note.

choices.text: Hang the festival lanterns for the first time in forty years

effects.log: They glow without drums. The isle comes out in its best clothes, quietly, and watches them swing.

events.text: The whale comes back every festival night, and the isle learns to leave a place on the dancing floor for the mist-dancers. {npc} stays by the lanterns, and dances, now and then, with no one. "It is a good dance," {he} says. "One of us always knows the steps."
events.arc: The Whale That Swallowed a Festival

choices.text: Join the dance at the next festival

effects.log: The drums beat from far under the sea. You dance with a space beside you, and it is not empty.

choices.text: Bring a lantern each festival and say nothing

effects.log: It is enough to be there.

events.text: Wedged between two cloud-reefs is a shop with a crooked sign: YESTERDAYS, BOUGHT AND SOLD. {npc} stands at the counter with a cloth and a very old smile. "A day is the cheapest thing in the sky," {he} says, "and the dearest. Come in. I have a few that might suit."
events.arc: The Shop That Sells Yesterdays

choices.text: Browse the shelves of jars

effects.log: Each jar holds a day: a rainy Tuesday, a feast, a quiet Sunday in a dead master's garden. They glow softly, labelled in a looping hand.

choices.text: Ask what a day costs

effects.log: "A day," says {npc}, "or a day's worth of something. I take what you can spare."

choices.text: Admire the shop and leave

effects.log: The sign swings behind you. Somewhere a bell chimes a day you will never know.

events.text: You sell the shop a bad day: one you would be glad to be rid of. {npc} weighs the jar and smiles. "Thank you," {he} says. "Someone will buy it who needs it." You walk out lighter by a Tuesday you never wanted. But you cannot quite remember why you were sad.
events.arc: The Shop That Sells Yesterdays

choices.text: Return and buy back the day, to see what it was

effects.log: It costs a spirit stone in value, paid in a good afternoon. The day is as bad as you remember, and, now, bearable.

choices.text: Buy a happy day from someone else's shelf

effects.log: You open it at home. It is a stranger's springtime. You walk through it in tears and wake with a lighter heart.

choices.text: Leave the bad day sold and not look back

effects.log: There are things better sold than kept.

events.text: {npc} calls on you years later. "A customer has returned a day, wanting it back," {he} says. "It is yours. Whoever bought it found it dull, and brought it back with a note. Do you want it, or shall I sell it again?" The jar hums softly on the counter.
events.arc: The Shop That Sells Yesterdays

choices.text: Take the old day back

effects.log: It is the day you sold. It is still bad. But it is yours, and you set it on the shelf where you can see it.

choices.text: Let {npc} sell it again

effects.log: The jar goes back on the shelf. Another stranger buys it, perhaps, who needs a bad day.

choices.text: Pour the day into the cloud sea

effects.log: It sinks out of sight, a faint shimmer. You feel unaccountably free.

events.text: The shop closes one spring, and {npc} hands you the key. "Someone has to keep the days," {he} says. "A rogue with sense and a decent hand, ideally." The shelves hum with ten thousand days of strangers, glowing in the dark, waiting to be needed.
events.arc: The Shop That Sells Yesterdays

choices.text: Take the shop and the jars

effects.log: You keep the shop for a long century. Customers come in sad and leave a day lighter. It is hard to say who is better served.

choices.text: Thank {npc}, and recommend an apprentice

effects.log: You find a keen young clerk with a fondness for old things. The shop stays open.

events.text: {npc} retires and the shop gets a new keeper, a cheerful apprentice who has never had a bad day. You pass the old shop years later and the sign has a new line: BAD DAYS ACCEPTED, NO QUESTIONS. You smile, and do not go in.
events.arc: The Shop That Sells Yesterdays

choices.text: Go in and sell a day anyway

effects.log: It is a small day, quickly sold. The keeper hugs you. You do not know why you needed it.

choices.text: Pass by with a nod

effects.log: The bell chimes after you, a day just starting.

events.text: Once a decade, on the night the stars fall thickest, a pale hare appears and runs along the track of the falling stars, leaping from beam to beam. {npc} has tracked it for sixty years and never once seen it clearly. "I do not want to catch it," {he} says. "I want to see its face. Come with me. Bring a lantern and good legs."
events.arc: The Hare That Runs on Falling Stars

choices.text: Lie in wait on the Starfall Ridge

effects.log: The first star falls at midnight. The hare is a flicker, a streak, a pale nothing.

choices.text: Follow the falling stars on a skiff

effects.log: You chase the hare across the night, never closing. The skiff creaks in protest.

choices.text: Bring {npc} tea and wait up

effects.log: {npc} drinks it without looking away from the sky.

events.text: The decade turns, and {npc} returns with a plan. "A hare runs where it cannot be seen," {he} says. "So we must let it see us not looking." You spend the night with your backs to the stars, facing a dark pool, and the hare's reflection appears in it, a silver bounding shape.
events.arc: The Hare That Runs on Falling Stars

choices.text: Watch the pool without moving

effects.log: The hare's face is long and wise and very young. It stops in the water, looks up at you, and goes on.

choices.text: Call softly to the hare

effects.log: It pauses mid-leap, one ear swivelling. Then it bounds away, leaving a path of faint light.

choices.text: Say nothing, and let {npc} look

effects.log: {He} stares at the pool until dawn. When the light comes, {he} weeps and laughs.

events.text: The third decade brings a surprise: the hare does not run. It sits on a ridge-top, panting, a pale fur of exhaustion, as if it, too, had grown old. {npc} is stunned. "It is tired," {he} says. "Perhaps it has run its last." The falling stars go by overhead, and the hare watches them go.
events.arc: The Hare That Runs on Falling Stars

choices.text: Sit with the hare through the night

effects.log: It lets you come close. It smells of dew and cold iron. At dawn it rises, stretches, and starts running again, slowly.

choices.text: Offer it water and a handful of dew-clover

effects.log: It sniffs, accepts, and nibbles. Your hand trembles with an odd joy.

choices.text: Leave the hare alone and take {npc} home

effects.log: The old hunter is silent all the way down the ridge. At the door {he} says: "Thank you for not catching it."

events.text: {npc} dies in a good year. In {his} will is a lantern, and a note: "Hang this on the Starfall Ridge the night the stars fall. The hare may want a light." You do. The first star falls. A pale shape pauses by the lantern, looks at it, looks at you, and runs on.
events.arc: The Hare That Runs on Falling Stars

choices.text: Hang the lantern every decade, as asked

effects.log: It becomes a tradition. The hare comes to the lantern each time, to rest a moment, before running on.

choices.text: Hang it just once and leave it to the sky

effects.log: It burns for a decade, and then is gone, as lanterns are.

events.text: {npc}'s hunting-cloak hangs in the tea-pavilion on the ridge, with a small sign: THE HUNTER NEVER SAW ITS FACE. WE THINK IT WAS KIND. Pilgrims come to the ridge every decade and sit with their backs to the stars, facing a pool. You take your turn, in a quiet decade.
events.arc: The Hare That Runs on Falling Stars

choices.text: Sit with your back to the stars and your face to the pool

effects.log: The hare's reflection crosses the pool, fast and silver. Its eye finds yours, and you know why the old hunter never wanted more.

choices.text: Leave the cloak on its peg

effects.log: There will be another hunter. There always is.

events.text: After the war of the immortals the battlefield was left to itself, and the weapons took root. Swords grow from the ground like saplings, glaives like bamboo, a great bow like a willow in blossom. {npc} tends the Garden of Old Weapons, pruning. "Nothing here is sharp," {he} says. "It has been thirty thousand years. They have all gone green."
events.arc: The Garden Where the Old Weapons Took Root

choices.text: Walk the rows with {npc}

effects.log: A sword-sapling brushes your hand, leaf-flat and soft. It smells of resin.

choices.text: Help prune a glaive-bamboo grove

effects.log: The shoots rattle like laughing. You fill three baskets.

choices.text: Rest beneath the bow-willow

effects.log: It sways in the breeze and drops a petal on your sleeve.

events.text: One sapling in the garden is wrong. It is a sword, brightly green, but its leaves are edged in a cold bluish light, and nothing else grows within an arm of it. {npc} frowns. "It has not gone green," {he} says. "It has gone quiet. It remembers the war."
events.arc: The Garden Where the Old Weapons Took Root

choices.text: Plant a flowering vine beside it

effects.log: The vine climbs and twines. The sword shivers and, very slowly, one leaf turns pale green.

choices.text: Sit by it and tell it the war is over

effects.log: You talk for an hour. The blue light does not fade. But the leaves lean toward you.

choices.text: Mark it with a stake and move on

effects.log: It will be there if anyone wants it. {npc} nods, uneasy.

events.text: A cold wind blows through the garden one autumn, and the quiet sword wakes. Its leaves flash, and a whisper runs along the rows: all the old weapons shiver. {npc} runs through the garden, soothing. "They remember," {he} says. "Help me, quick. If they all wake at once, we have a war."
events.arc: The Garden Where the Old Weapons Took Root

choices.text: Calm the quiet sword with a thread of qi

ok.log: You sing to it. The blue fades, and the garden settles in a long green sigh.

fail.log: The sword flares and a blade-leaf cuts your sleeve. Nothing worse, but you leave bruised and humbled.

choices.text: Water the whole garden with rain from a cloud-jar

effects.log: It takes all night. At dawn every weapon is dripping, and quiet.

choices.text: Stay with {npc} and tend the rows

effects.log: You work through the night, hand over hand. The dawn is gentle.

events.text: The quiet sword has put out a flower, small and white, on a cold bright stem. {npc} cannot believe it. "In thirty thousand years," {he} says, "I have never seen one flower." The petals have a faint edge, like a blade, and the smell is of rain.
events.arc: The Garden Where the Old Weapons Took Root

choices.text: Take a seed from the flower and plant it far off

effects.log: It grows into a sword-lily in a quiet temple garden. The monks call it a miracle, and are right.

choices.text: Leave the flower where it grows

effects.log: It lasts a day. You pass the garden each year and look for another.

events.text: The garden is quieter than it was, and {npc} is quieter too. The old gardener sits among the blades with a cup of tea, and says: "I think they were never meant to cut anything. I think we meant them for this." Overhead, the bow-willow lets fall a petal.
events.arc: The Garden Where the Old Weapons Took Root

choices.text: Plant another weapon and watch it take

effects.log: You leave a spent sword blade in the soil. By spring, it has begun to bud.

choices.text: Pay the gardener a visit each year

effects.log: The garden grows. So do you.

events.text: A grotto on a hanging reef has a reputation. Those who go in come out lighter, quiet, with no memory of what troubled them. The mouth is lined with small stone figures of those who stayed. A traveller at the mouth says: "It takes one grief. Only one. But it takes it all."
events.arc: The Grotto That Makes You Forget

choices.text: Go in, to be rid of a grief

effects.log: The grotto is warm and gold. A voice asks: "Which?" You think of the heaviest, and feel it lift like a bird.

choices.text: Study the stone figures at the mouth

effects.log: Each stands in a different posture of peace. Their faces are smooth, and blank, and calm.

choices.text: Leave the grotto alone

effects.log: Some griefs are loaded for a reason.

events.text: You return to the grotto years later. The grief you gave is gone, and with it, a hole shaped like a person. A voice asks: "Which?" And you realise the hole has been aching more than the grief ever did. The stone figures wait at the mouth, serene, hollow.
events.arc: The Grotto That Makes You Forget

choices.text: Ask the grotto to return what it took

ok.log: The grotto hums, doubtful, and then gives it back, all of it: the grief, the love, the person. You weep for an hour, and then breathe freely.

fail.log: The grotto laughs gently and takes a second grief to keep the first company. You leave lighter and emptier, and no wiser.

choices.text: Take a stone figure home and sit with it

effects.log: It is cold, smooth, blank. You learn something about peace, and its price.

choices.text: Walk away from the grotto, hollow but whole

effects.log: The ache stays. You carry it, and it becomes, over time, bearable.

events.text: A stranger comes to your door, grey and stooped, and asks if you remember them. You do not. They explain, gently: they went into the grotto too, years ago, and gave their only love away. They have been walking the sky since, looking for the face that fits the hole. "Do you recognise it?" they ask.
events.arc: The Grotto That Makes You Forget

choices.text: Hear their story and help them look

effects.log: You walk the sky together for a season. You do not find the face. But the walking is a kind of remembering.

choices.text: Tell them what you learned about the grotto

effects.log: They listen. They nod. They go back, to ask for the love that was taken.

choices.text: Give them tea and let them rest

effects.log: They sleep through the afternoon. When they wake, they say it was the best sleep in years.

events.text: The grotto is quiet, and the stone figures at the mouth are fewer by one, a place on the ledge empty where a figure stood. The traveller at the mouth, a different one now, says: "One of them walked out last week, weeping. Said she remembered. Said it hurt. Said it was worth it."
events.arc: The Grotto That Makes You Forget

choices.text: Leave a flower at the empty place

effects.log: You leave a sprig of cloud-heather. It lasts a week, then another, then a year.

choices.text: Walk the road home slowly

effects.log: The ache is still there. It is a company, of a sort.

events.text: The figures at the mouth have grown by two. The traveller, the same as before, shrugs. "People come," they say. "They always come. We hold the door and let them go in or not. It is a small kindness, to let them choose." You nod, and leave the grotto to its work.
events.arc: The Grotto That Makes You Forget

choices.text: Stand the vigil at the door with the traveller

effects.log: You sit through a night. Four people come, two go in, two do not.

choices.text: Return home with your own ache, untouched

effects.log: It is yours, and in the end it is what you have of someone.

events.text: At the Edge of Heaven there is a watchman, {npc}, who sells sunsets. For a spirit stone you may buy one, in a jar, to open at home. The watchman has been catching them in a net for four hundred years. "They are all different," {he} says. "No two are quite alike. Even the grey ones have something."
events.arc: The Seller of Sunsets at the Edge

choices.text: Buy a sunset (1 spirit stone)

effects.log: You carry the jar home. When you open it at dusk, a sunset spills out, warm and rose, and for a quarter hour your whole house glows.

choices.text: Watch {npc} catch one at dusk

effects.log: The net swings out and comes back full of coral light. It is the finest thing you have seen in a century.

choices.text: Admire the stock of jars and leave

effects.log: Each glows faintly, each a different colour. You stand there a long time.

events.text: The watchman asks a favour. "There is a sunset I have not yet caught," {he} says. "A green one. It happens perhaps once in a thousand years, at the exact moment the sun touches the cloud sea. I have been waiting for three hundred. I am not quick any more. Would you hold the second net?"
events.arc: The Seller of Sunsets at the Edge

choices.text: Hold the second net at the edge

effects.log: You stand with a net in the wind, patient, until the sun nears the horizon. Your arms ache.

choices.text: Watch and shout when the green appears

effects.log: You are the spotter. When the green flash comes, you shout, too late.

choices.text: Bring {npc} dinner and keep company

effects.log: The old watchman eats slowly, eyes on the horizon. It is a good evening.

events.text: The green flash comes. For a single heartbeat the whole sea of clouds goes emerald and the edge of the sky glows like a held breath. {npc} swings the net with all {his} old strength. It catches, or does not. The light is gone before either of you can tell.
events.arc: The Seller of Sunsets at the Edge

choices.text: Close the jar as the light comes in

ok.log: You slap the lid on. Inside, a tiny emerald sunset glows like a firefly. {npc} is quiet for a long time. Then {he} weeps.

fail.log: The lid falls late. A thread of green lingers on the net, fading. {npc} sighs, and then laughs, a rueful rusty sound.

choices.text: Take the net and cast it yourself

effects.log: It is clumsy but sure. Half a thread of green is yours.

choices.text: Let the sunset go unjarred

effects.log: You watch it fade with {npc}. Some sunsets are best uncaught.

events.text: {npc} gives you the green jar. "Open it when you are very old," {he} says, "on a night you have not liked. It will not fix anything. It will only be green." You carry it for a thousand years. When you open it, finally, it is.
events.arc: The Seller of Sunsets at the Edge

choices.text: Open the jar on a hard night

effects.log: The green fills your small room, quiet and cool. It does not fix anything. It is, however, very green.

choices.text: Pass the jar to someone else in need

effects.log: They open it on their own bad night. You never hear, but you know.

events.text: The watchman grows old at the edge, and you visit each year with a jar. The two of you open a sunset together, one for each, and watch them fill the sky. Neither of you speaks. The green was never caught. Perhaps, {npc} says, that is better, for now there is still something to wait for.
events.arc: The Seller of Sunsets at the Edge

choices.text: Bring a jar next year, too

effects.log: You do. The edge is quiet and rose and endless.

choices.text: Learn to catch a sunset yourself

effects.log: You buy a net and borrow a patience. In a century or two you will have a jar of your own.

events.text: Immortals die rarely, but they die. When one does, the ashes are carried from isle to isle to the place they asked for. {npc} has been the Ash Ferry's skipper for three hundred years. "People think it is a grim job," {he} says. "It is the kindest. Everyone is glad to see me, in the end. Come aboard for a trip. I need a second pair of hands."
events.arc: The Ferry That Carries the Ashes Home

choices.text: Take the oars for the first leg

effects.log: The ferry slides over the cloud like a thought. The jar of ashes in the bow is warm.

choices.text: Keep the logbook of the passage

effects.log: It is a long list of names and wishes. Each wish is a small, specific tenderness.

choices.text: Sit with the jar for company

effects.log: It feels odd to say hello to ashes. You say it anyway.

events.text: The jar's owner wished to be scattered at the Wind Gate, on the one day of the year the winds turn. The skiff reaches it in a storm. The skipper holds the jar to the sky, and sings a wordless song. The wind takes the ashes up in a spiral of pale gold, and the storm, for a moment, falls silent.
events.arc: The Ferry That Carries the Ashes Home

choices.text: Sing the second verse

effects.log: Your voice cracks, but the wind hears. The ashes rise higher, slow and golden, and then are gone.

choices.text: Hold the skiff steady as the ashes rise

effects.log: The skiff bucks. You hold on. When the gold is gone you are soaked, cold and quiet.

choices.text: Bow your head in the wind

effects.log: {npc} nods. The storm picks up again as soon as the song is done.

events.text: A letter arrives at your door from a family you have never met. The deceased wished to be scattered over a garden on an isle that has since drifted out of reach. "Can you find it?" it asks. {npc} is unsure. "We have a chart of the old route," {he} says. "But isles move. It could be anywhere."
events.arc: The Ferry That Carries the Ashes Home

choices.text: Take the chart and search for the lost garden

effects.log: You follow the old route for a season. The garden is on a distant isle, overgrown and sweet. You scatter the ashes among its roses.

choices.text: Ask the Ministry of Fog to trace the isle

effects.log: It takes two years. The isle is found at last, a speck on a faint chart.

choices.text: Write the family honestly that the garden is lost

effects.log: The reply is kind. They ask that the ashes be scattered over any garden.

events.text: The skipper retires. {npc} sits on the dock, and the new skipper, a nervous young apprentice, waits beside. "Take the ashes where they ask," {he} says. "And if they cannot ask, take them where they would have asked. Do it kindly. That is all." The apprentice nods. The old ferry rocks.
events.arc: The Ferry That Carries the Ashes Home

choices.text: Offer to crew the first run for the apprentice

effects.log: You take the oars. The new skipper sings off-key. The ashes rise anyway.

choices.text: Stand on the dock and wave the ferry off

effects.log: It goes, small and bright on the cloud. {npc} wipes an eye and takes your arm.

events.text: One day the ferry comes for {npc} itself. The apprentice rows, and you sit in the bow beside the jar. At the Wind Gate the apprentice sings the old song. The ashes rise in spiral gold, and the storm falls quiet. You stand in the quiet a long time.
events.arc: The Ferry That Carries the Ashes Home

choices.text: Sing the second verse again

effects.log: Your voice cracks. The wind hears.

choices.text: Say nothing and watch the gold rise

effects.log: It is the right ending.

events.text: A meteor crater on the Hanbit Shelf grows wheat. The wheat is silver, and ripens every week, and tastes of burned sugar. {npc} farms it with two goats and a rake. "The star left something in the soil," {he} says. "I do not ask what. I plant, I reap, I bake. It is the best bread in the sky."
events.arc: The Crater That Grew Wheat

choices.text: Help with the reaping for a day

effects.log: The sheaves glow in your arms. At dusk you eat a silver loaf, hot, and feel your meridians hum.

choices.text: Study the soil with a jade lens

effects.log: There is a seam of star-iron in the crater floor. Tiny seeds of it float up into the wheat.

choices.text: Buy a loaf and be on your way

effects.log: It is still warm when you reach the next isle. You eat it slowly.

events.text: The Ministry of Fields sends an inspector. The crater is not licensed, the wheat is not classified, the farmer is not registered. {npc} stands in the doorway with the rake. The inspector, who has a sweet tooth, takes a loaf and a bite, and puts away the form. "I will need to see the loaf again," they say, "for evidence."
events.arc: The Crater That Grew Wheat

choices.text: Speak for the farmer in front of the inspector

effects.log: You cite the Statutes of Unclaimed Fields, which you half-remember. The inspector writes: "Provisional".

choices.text: Carry a basket of loaves to the Ministry

effects.log: Three clerks eat their way through it. A new rule appears the next week: Crater Wheat, Exempt.

choices.text: Let the farmer handle it

effects.log: {npc} does, with a loaf and a pot of jam. The inspector leaves, happy.

events.text: The silver wheat fails one year. The ears come up pale and empty, and the crater smells of cold iron. {npc} sits in the field with a handful of chaff. "The star has given all it had," {he} says. "I do not blame it. It was a long way to come." The goats nibble sadly.
events.arc: The Crater That Grew Wheat

choices.text: Offer a seed of your own from a distant orchard

effects.log: You plant it in the pale soil. It does not take at first. Then, over a season, it does.

choices.text: Search the crater for the last of the star-iron

effects.log: You dig for a week. There is a seam of it, running deep. You feed it back into the soil, powdered.

choices.text: Sit with {npc} and share the last loaf

effects.log: It is a silent, grateful meal.

events.text: The wheat returns, thinner than before, greyer than before, but alive. {npc} bakes the first loaf of the new harvest and gives you the heel. It tastes of ash and honey. "That is the star, thanking us," {he} says. The goats look pleased with themselves.
events.arc: The Crater That Grew Wheat

choices.text: Plant a row of your seed beside the crater wheat

effects.log: The two grains grow together, grey and silver. The bread is a little sweeter.

choices.text: Take a loaf to the Ministry and a kind word

effects.log: The clerks eat it with reverence. The rule against crater wheat is quietly repealed.

events.text: The silver wheat comes back in a hundred years, brighter than before. The farmer's great-grandchild runs the crater now, with six goats and a granary. They tell visitors, as {npc} did, that the star left something in the soil. They add: and someone put something back.
events.arc: The Crater That Grew Wheat

choices.text: Smile and buy a loaf

effects.log: It is as good as ever. The goats approve.

choices.text: Leave a handful of seed at the gate

effects.log: It is a small thing. The field takes it.

events.text: On the Sorin Isle there is a lake whose reflection is not your own. Look in, and you see the life you might have led had you made one different choice, long ago. Local custom says to look once, and once only. A guide at the shore says: "It is not cruel. But it is long."
events.arc: The Lake That Shows the Lives You Did Not Lead

choices.text: Look into the lake

effects.log: The water shivers. You see yourself at a table, older, with a spouse and a hearth and a cat. You do not know the face across the table. But you want to.

choices.text: Ask the guide what others have seen

effects.log: "Everything," says the guide. "A farm. A throne. A grave. A garden. A boat. Nobody has seen nothing."

choices.text: Skip stones on the lake instead

effects.log: The ripples scatter every reflection. You have a pleasant afternoon.

events.text: You return to the lake, drawn. The other life is still there, in the water, a little older. You see yourself with white hair, laughing at a joke you cannot hear. The guide says, softly, "They always come back. Do you want to step in?" The water is warm.
events.arc: The Lake That Shows the Lives You Did Not Lead

choices.text: Step into the water to touch the other life

ok.log: The water holds, then lets you through. For an hour you walk in the other life, light and strange, and then step back out, dripping, wiser.

fail.log: The water swirls round you and takes more than an hour. When you climb out, a year has gone from your own life, and the guide offers a blanket.
fail.deathCause: a life that was not hers to lead

choices.text: Watch from the shore a little longer

effects.log: You watch the white-haired self laugh. Then you turn away, and the other life dims.

choices.text: Close your eyes and walk away

effects.log: You carry the other life with you, a faint glow behind the eyes.

events.text: A letter comes from the guide. "Someone looked in your reflection," it says, "and told me the other life was happier. They asked how it could be. I said I did not know. Do you?" There is a pressed flower in the fold, small, blue.
events.arc: The Lake That Shows the Lives You Did Not Lead

choices.text: Write back that no life is the happier

effects.log: It is the truest thing you know. The guide posts it at the lake.

choices.text: Visit the lake with the guide and look together

effects.log: You and the guide look in side by side. Both of you see something. Neither of you tells.

choices.text: Keep the flower and say nothing

effects.log: It is blue and light and presses very well.

events.text: The lake becomes a pilgrimage in time, and the guide builds a bench beside it with a plaque: LOOK ONCE. THEN HELP SOMEONE. You sit on it years later. The lake shows only the sky, today. That is the most honest reflection yet.
events.arc: The Lake That Shows the Lives You Did Not Lead

choices.text: Sit and do nothing

effects.log: A calm falls on you that lasts a year.

choices.text: Add your name to the bench

effects.log: It is carved among a hundred others.

events.text: You never look again. But years on, the guide sends another note, and a drawing of the white-haired self in the lake, laughing. Under it: "I think they were laughing at you." You laugh too, and cannot say what at.
events.arc: The Lake That Shows the Lives You Did Not Lead

choices.text: Keep the drawing on your wall

effects.log: It becomes a friend of sorts.

choices.text: Send a drawing back

effects.log: The two drawings hang in the guide's hut, side by side.

events.text: The Nine Clouds Palace keeps its lamps lit with captured lightning, bottled in jade. {npc}, the palace's senior collector, goes out in each storm with a net of copper thread and a face of perfect calm. "You are not afraid?" {he} asks. "Good. Neither am I. It is respect, not fear, that keeps the bolt in the bottle."
events.arc: The Lightning Collectors of the Nine Clouds

choices.text: Ride out with {npc} into the storm

effects.log: The sky is white and black by turns. Thunder shakes the skiff. {npc} swings the net, laughing.

choices.text: Study the bottling from the palace gallery

effects.log: The jar glows blue-white when a bolt lands. The collector's hands are quick and sure.

choices.text: Wish the collector good luck from the dock

effects.log: A bolt cracks a mile away. {npc} comes back soaked and grinning.

events.text: A bolt in the jar is awake. It will not sleep. {npc} shakes it, taps it, sings to it. The bolt sparks and rattles. "It is a young one," {he} says. "It does not want to be a lamp. It wants to be a storm." The jar glows red with indignation.
events.arc: The Lightning Collectors of the Nine Clouds

choices.text: Open the jar and let the bolt fly in the open

effects.log: It rises like a snake of light, shrieks once, and is gone into the clouds. The collector laughs, shaken.

choices.text: Teach the bolt to sleep with a verse

effects.log: You hum a lullaby. The bolt glows softer, steadier, and settles.

choices.text: Put the jar in the cold cellar for a day

effects.log: It sulks. But it will probably come round.

events.text: The palace holds a festival, and the great lamp must burn with a bolt of the first order. {npc} has none. A storm is promised, but a storm is a risk, and a risk with the whole palace watching. The collector looks at you, and sweat gleams on a calm face. "I cannot do it alone," {he} says.
events.arc: The Lightning Collectors of the Nine Clouds

choices.text: Go with {npc} into the storm and bring back a bolt

ok.log: The two of you bring back a bolt the size of a loaf. It blazes in the great lamp, and the palace cheers.

fail.log: The storm scatters you both. You come home singed, empty-handed and alive. The lamp burns on stored light, dimly, with dignity.

choices.text: Ask the Palace to dim the festival lamp for honesty

effects.log: The festival is held in candlelight. It is, many say, the loveliest in years.

choices.text: Support {npc} from the dock

effects.log: It is not much. But {he} comes home safe.

events.text: {npc} retires to the gallery with a cup of tea and a bandage. "I have caught eleven thousand bolts," {he} says, "and I will be remembered for the one that went free." The palace hangs a jar in the lamp-hall, empty, with a plaque: IT WANTED TO BE A STORM.
events.arc: The Lightning Collectors of the Nine Clouds

choices.text: Add a line to the plaque

effects.log: You write: "Thank you." It is the shortest line on the plaque.

choices.text: Visit the gallery each storm season

effects.log: The two of you watch the lightning from the window.

events.text: The Palace passes its lamps down through the generations, and {npc} trains a new collector, a nervous young apprentice who is not afraid either. The jar of the young bolt that sulked is in the cellar. Sometimes, on stormy nights, it flickers, and the whole cellar smells of ozone and pride.
events.arc: The Lightning Collectors of the Nine Clouds

choices.text: Check on the jar on a stormy night

effects.log: It glows warm, steady, content. You close the door softly.

choices.text: Leave it in peace

effects.log: It was always meant to be.

events.text: At the great gate of the Jade Court a line of petitioners shows seals, one by one. You have none. {npc}, the gatekeeper, looks at your empty hands and sighs. "No seal, no entry," {he} says. "That is the rule. I did not make it. I enforce it, and I hate it, a little, every day."
events.arc: The Seal You Cannot Show at the Gate

choices.text: Ask politely if a rogue may file a petition elsewhere

effects.log: "The Hall of Petitions has a side door," says {npc}. "It is not on the map. It has a bell."

choices.text: Wait at the gate until the gatekeeper changes shift

effects.log: Seven hours later a younger guard lets you through with a shrug. It is not a victory, but it is a door.

choices.text: Turn away and find another way

effects.log: The rule stays. You will not be the one to break it today.

events.text: {npc} shows you the side door. The bell rings thin and slow. A clerk lets you in, without seal and without question, and charges double the filing fee. "It is the house rule for rogues," the clerk says apologetically. "I did not make it."
events.arc: The Seal You Cannot Show at the Gate

choices.text: Pay the double fee (2 spirit stones)

effects.log: The clerk files your petition. The ink dries. It is not a pleasant thing to be charged double, but it is done.

choices.text: Protest the fee in writing

effects.log: The clerk accepts the note, stamps it, files it. In a year, the fee is, quietly, one and a half.

choices.text: Withdraw the petition and leave

effects.log: You were not that keen on the filing. You are keener, now, on the unfairness.

events.text: A group of rogues has formed a society at the foot of the Court: the Unsealed. They meet in a tea-shop and draft petitions to the Court about fees, gates and doors. {npc} comes, in plain clothes, off shift, and sits at the back. "I am not here as a guard," {he} says. "I am here as someone who is ashamed."
events.arc: The Seal You Cannot Show at the Gate

choices.text: Join the Unsealed as a speaker

effects.log: You speak. The room is hot with fellow-feeling. A petition is drafted, with nine hundred signatures and one pseudonym.

choices.text: Help {npc} draft a letter from the inside

effects.log: It takes three drafts. The final one is signed by forty gatekeepers, quietly.

choices.text: Listen at the back with a cup of tea

effects.log: It is a quiet, hopeful evening.

events.text: The Court issues a modest reform: rogues may enter the Hall of Petitions by the front door, with a plain stamp in place of a seal. The fee is the same as anyone else's. {npc} stands at the gate, and when you pass {he} stamps your hand with great ceremony, and says: "Welcome."
events.arc: The Seal You Cannot Show at the Gate

choices.text: Return the bow, deeply

effects.log: It is a small victory, and you bow like it is a large one.

choices.text: Walk through with your head high

effects.log: The doors are enormous. You are not, on this day, small.

events.text: Nothing changes at the gate. But {npc} resigns {his} post, and takes up a stall of tea near the side door, serving every petitioner free. "I am a worse gatekeeper," {he} says, "and a better neighbour." The stall has a sign: ALL SEALS WELCOME. NO SEALS ALSO WELCOME.
events.arc: The Seal You Cannot Show at the Gate

choices.text: Drink the tea and spread the word

effects.log: It becomes a haven for rogues and clerks alike. The Court pretends not to notice.

choices.text: Leave a spirit stone in the tip jar

effects.log: It is accepted with grace.

events.text: Once in a century a jade qilin sheds a horn, and the horn is said to be a seed of luck. {npc} is a tracker who finds them. The horn will be in a high meadow, hidden under moss. The qilin does not hide it. It forgets it. "My job," {he} says, "is to take it before anyone else does, and to take it to the right person."
events.arc: The Tracker of the Shed Qilin Horn

choices.text: Help search the meadows

effects.log: You comb the grass for a week. The moss is deep. Your fingers are numb.

choices.text: Ask the qilin's herder where it last grazed

effects.log: The herder points to a hill. "There," they say, "by the white stone."

choices.text: Wait at the stone and watch

effects.log: You see a dozen others come and go. None of them find it.

events.text: The horn is found, under a drift of pale moss: long, jade-green, humming softly. {npc} lifts it with both hands. "Seed of luck," {he} whispers. "A hundred years of fortune in one horn. And now the question: who shall have it?" The meadow is silent. A rival tracker appears at the ridge.
events.arc: The Tracker of the Shed Qilin Horn

choices.text: Keep the horn from the rival tracker

effects.log: A tense hour. The rival is armed with a rope and a good argument. You say no, three times, calmly. They leave.

choices.text: Offer the rival a share of the finding

effects.log: They accept, wryly. The luck-seed is cut in two, and each half still hums.

choices.text: Hand the horn to {npc} and step back

effects.log: {npc} wraps it in silk and says nothing. Your hands are shaking.

events.text: {npc} carries the horn to the Moonlit Isle, where a fever has gone round the children. The horn is set on a pillow in the sick-ward. By morning the fever has broken. Across the isle people wake smiling, unsure why. The horn is warm, and humming, and a little smaller.
events.arc: The Tracker of the Shed Qilin Horn

choices.text: Stay and tend the children

effects.log: You spend a week nursing. All recover. The horn is thinner, but still hums.

choices.text: Ask {npc} whether the horn should be rationed

effects.log: The tracker shakes {his} head. "It is a luck-seed," {he} says. "Use it all, or it sours."

choices.text: Walk the wards quietly with a lantern

effects.log: The children sleep. The horn glows. It is the best night of your year.

events.text: What is left of the horn, a little stub, is set into the lintel of the sick-ward as a charm. The children of the Moonlit Isle grow up with unusual luck and unusual manners. {npc} returns to the high meadows, tracking the next horn. "A hundred years," {he} says. "I will find it."
events.arc: The Tracker of the Shed Qilin Horn

choices.text: Offer to help find the next one

effects.log: You will wait a century. You have time.

choices.text: Visit the ward each year

effects.log: The stub hums when you come. It remembers.

events.text: The horn is gone by the next spring, used and spent. {npc} says that was the right thing and tracks the next. The Moonlit Isle has one fewer fever. A child there remembers a green light and a hush. It will be enough, perhaps, to carry them through a long life.
events.arc: The Tracker of the Shed Qilin Horn

choices.text: Wish the tracker well and wait for the next one

effects.log: The wait is long. You spend it well.

choices.text: Light a candle at the ward door

effects.log: The flame bends toward the lintel, as if bowing.

events.text: Beyond the black cloud-reefs of the Demon Realm there is a garden where nothing dies. Flowers bloom forever, leaves never fall, and insects grow old and do not die. {npc} has tended it for two thousand years. "It is a curse, of a sort," {he} says. "A garden without autumn is a garden with no endings. I am so tired of the roses."
events.arc: The Garden Where Nothing Dies

choices.text: Walk the garden with {npc}

effects.log: Every flower is perfect and fixed. Nothing changes, nothing ripens, nothing rots. You find it hard to breathe.

choices.text: Pick a single flower and see what happens

effects.log: It does not wilt. It does not need water. It lies in your hand like a stone made of silk.

choices.text: Sit with the gardener and drink tea

effects.log: {npc} talks of roses for an hour. The tea is excellent.

events.text: {npc} shows you the source of the garden's deathlessness: a seed-pearl in a stone basin, glowing white. "I stole it from a dying star," {he} says. "I wanted to make a place where nothing would be lost. I did not think about what it would mean to never lose anything." The pearl hums, warm and heavy.
events.arc: The Garden Where Nothing Dies

choices.text: Offer to take the pearl away

effects.log: {npc} hesitates. The garden stills. "I would be sorry to see the roses go," {he} says. "But I would be glad."

choices.text: Study the pearl for a way to loosen its grip

effects.log: You read the pearl for a month. It is bound with a thread of qi that could, in time, be teased apart.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the garden is beautiful

effects.log: {He} nods slowly. "Beautiful," {he} says, "and so very tired."

events.text: The day comes to let the garden go. {npc} and you stand at the stone basin, and the old gardener lifts the pearl. The roses tremble. Every leaf in the garden is waiting to fall. "Last chance," {he} says. "If I put this down, they all wither. If I keep it, they all stay."
events.arc: The Garden Where Nothing Dies

choices.text: Urge {npc} to put the pearl down

effects.log: The pearl drops into the basin. The garden exhales. A single leaf falls, golden, and the gardener weeps for joy.

choices.text: Suggest keeping one tree deathless and letting the rest go

effects.log: The compromise is odd and tender. One apple tree stays green forever. The rest rot gently into mulch.

choices.text: Say nothing; it is the gardener's garden

effects.log: {npc} stands there a long time, and then, with a long breath, sets the pearl down.

events.text: The garden ages, finally. Leaves turn, fruit ripens and drops, an old rose blackens and curls. {npc} walks among them with tears running down. "It is so much work," {he} says, laughing. "I have not raked in two thousand years." {He} picks up the rake. You pick up another.
events.arc: The Garden Where Nothing Dies

choices.text: Rake the garden together

effects.log: Autumn in the Demon Realm smells of smoke and apples. It is the most beautiful you have ever seen.

choices.text: Leave the gardener to the rake and the sun

effects.log: {He} is humming. It is the first tune you have heard from {him}.

events.text: In the garden an apple tree stays green forever, and the rest of the garden does what gardens do. {npc} sits under the deathless tree every year at harvest and eats one apple, and says it is the best {he} has ever had. The apple never changes. {He} does.
events.arc: The Garden Where Nothing Dies

choices.text: Bring a seed from a dying tree to plant beside it

effects.log: It grows, ripens, falls. The deathless tree watches with unusual patience.

choices.text: Share a silent apple with the gardener

effects.log: It tastes of two thousand years, and of tomorrow.

events.text: Once in a long while the isles drift apart: a season when the cloud currents split and the fleet loses itself. Friends stand on opposite shores of widening gaps and wave. {npc} steers the Ganghwa Isle, and wants a messenger. "I have a cousin on the next isle," {he} says. "Before the gap grows, I would like to say goodbye properly."
events.arc: The Season the Isles Drift Apart

choices.text: Carry the message across by skiff

effects.log: The gap is a mile wide and growing. You cross it with a breath to spare.

choices.text: Send a kite across with a message

effects.log: It flaps over the widening gap and catches on a cousin's window. A pale hand takes it in.

choices.text: Wave from the edge with the rest

effects.log: The two isles wave until they are too small to see. A lump rises in your throat.

events.text: The isles drift for months. {npc} grows quiet, and then restless. Your isle is no longer near any neighbour. Food stores run low. A rumour spreads of an isle to the north with plenty. {npc} wants to chase it. The steersmen of the other isles disagree, and the council is loud.
events.arc: The Season the Isles Drift Apart

choices.text: Speak for a steady course and rationing

effects.log: The council grumbles but agrees. The isle holds. The rumour proves to be a mirage.

choices.text: Offer to scout the northern rumour yourself

effects.log: You find a ragged shelf of fruit-bushes, far smaller than rumoured, but real. You bring back a boat of berries.

choices.text: Share your own stores with neighbours

effects.log: Everyone gives a little. Everyone is hungry together, which is a kind of company.

events.text: The currents turn again. The isles begin to drift back together. {npc} is at the bow, hands white on the rail. As the gap closes, a figure on the opposite shore waves, and {npc} laughs aloud and weeps. The cousin has not been lost. The moment the two isles touch, there is a cheer across the whole fleet.
events.arc: The Season the Isles Drift Apart

choices.text: Help moor the two isles together

effects.log: Ropes fly. A hundred hands pull. The isles bump, creak, and settle side by side with a shudder of joy.

choices.text: Cross the bridge first to greet the cousin

effects.log: The cousin hugs you hard, then looks past you for {npc}. The two embrace on the gangway.

choices.text: Stand back and let the isles meet

effects.log: You watch the two isles press together like old friends. The reunion is long.

events.text: The steersman calls a feast on the reunited isles. Hundreds crowd the long tables. Someone sings a song of the drift. {npc} stands on a chair and says: "We were far, and now we are near. The sky is wide. We are not." The whole table cheers.
events.arc: The Season the Isles Drift Apart

choices.text: Raise a toast to the drift

effects.log: The whole feast drinks. Somewhere, a child falls asleep on a coat.

choices.text: Sit quietly and listen to the songs

effects.log: A hundred voices, a thousand years. You do not mind a minute of it.

events.text: The season of drift ends, and the isles learn to keep a ledger of their neighbours: who is on which shore, who waved, who answered. {npc} keeps the ledger of your isle and lets you add a line. You write: "A good drifting." It is entered.
events.arc: The Season the Isles Drift Apart

choices.text: Check the ledger at the next drift

effects.log: The entry is still there. It will be, for a thousand years.

choices.text: Close the ledger and go on with the day

effects.log: It is a good ledger.

events.text: In the Nine Clouds Palace there is a loom older than the palace, and on it the weather is woven. {npc}, the senior weaver, sets the shuttle for the week: a warm front in thread of dawn, a shower in silver. "It is not a machine," {he} says. "It is a conversation. The loom suggests, I answer. Sit. Try a row."
events.arc: The Loom That Wove the Weather

choices.text: Sit at the loom and weave a row

effects.log: The thread is cool. When you lift the shuttle, a small cloud curls up from the cloth.

choices.text: Watch the loom for a day

effects.log: It clatters softly. The weather it makes is better than any you have ever seen.

choices.text: Admire the weaver's hands

effects.log: Quick as birds. You would not dare to touch the shuttle.

events.text: The loom jams. A knot of grey thread has twisted into the pattern, and the week's weather is frozen: a dull, windless cloud. {npc} tugs at the knot. It will not yield. "Someone has woven a secret into the weather," {he} says. "A message, from someone who wanted to be heard."
events.arc: The Loom That Wove the Weather

choices.text: Cut the knot and release the weather

effects.log: The shuttle runs free. The week's weather bursts out in a sudden spring, and the knot lies on the floor, curling.

choices.text: Untie the knot and read the message

effects.log: It is a prayer, woven in grey: a request for rain on a drought-struck valley far below. It is old. It was never answered.

choices.text: Let {npc} untangle it alone

effects.log: {He} works at the knot for three days. At the end, {he} weeps and laughs and does not say why.

events.text: The weaver asks you to take the message down to the valley. "A prayer unanswered is a debt," {he} says. "The loom wove it into a knot because the Ministry would not hear it. Let it fall as rain, where it was asked." You take the grey thread and the quiet skiff, down toward the world below.
events.arc: The Loom That Wove the Weather

choices.text: Carry the thread to the valley and let it rain

effects.log: The thread unspools in the wind. By the next morning, clouds gather, and the valley drinks.

choices.text: Bring the thread back and weave it into the loom, properly

effects.log: The pattern is redone. The Palace's next week of weather brings a rain to the valley, as asked.

choices.text: Hold the thread and decide later

effects.log: It sits in your sleeve, grey and faintly warm, a weight on the conscience.

events.text: A letter, years on, comes up through the clouds from the valley: a smudged scrap in a child's hand. "Thank you for the rain." {npc} reads it twice and sets it on the loom as a bookmark. "The weather is a conversation," {he} says. "It is nice to be answered."
events.arc: The Loom That Wove the Weather

choices.text: Weave the letter into the next cloth

effects.log: It becomes a single silver thread in the spring pattern. The valley has a fine year.

choices.text: Keep the letter as a talisman

effects.log: You carry it for a thousand years.

events.text: The loom is not jammed again. {npc} grows old at the shuttle, and teaches you the knack of weaving a conversation. Rows of weather unfurl, season after season. Somewhere in the valley, a child looks at the sky and says: "Wow. Look at the clouds."
events.arc: The Loom That Wove the Weather

choices.text: Weave a row for that child

effects.log: It is a small cloud, shaped like a rabbit. The child laughs.

choices.text: Weave on without a name

effects.log: The loom makes the weather it needs.

events.text: A fox the size of a cat sits on the Cheongun Ridge each dawn, drinking dew from the grass. It has nine small tails, each a different shade of white. Locals call it a nuisance. It watches you with an expression of mild amusement.

choices.text: Offer it a bowl of dew from the high leaves

effects.log: It drinks, and sits close, and does not leave for an hour. Its tails sway like ferns.

choices.text: Trace its path across the ridge

effects.log: It loops, doubles, and cuts across, laying a trail like a map. You follow it to a bench with a view.

events.text: A vault hangs from the underside of an isle, sealed with a door of plain cloud-pine and a lock of ice. A sign says: OPEN WHEN THE ISLE IS HAPPY. The isle has not been happy in a century. Tonight, a festival is under way, and the lock is dripping.

choices.text: Wait by the door until the ice melts

effects.log: It melts at midnight. Inside is a single jar of honey, labelled "Sweet." You take one spoon.

choices.text: Leave the vault closed, in case the happiness is a coincidence

effects.log: The ice refreezes by dawn. Some doors are better left until sure.

events.text: A great tail rises from the cloud sea at dawn and slaps the surface once. A column of spray reaches the isle's edge, soaking the early walkers. Somewhere deep below, a whale grunts, satisfied. It does this every morning, for no reason anyone has discovered.

choices.text: Stand at the edge and get soaked on purpose

effects.log: The spray is cold and salty and smells of ancient things. You laugh, soaked, delighted.

choices.text: Time the slap with a sand-glass

effects.log: Every day at the same minute, give or take. You write it in a ledger.

events.text: A toppled gate of black stone lies across a small isle, grown over with moss and bracken. Its lintel is carved with a poem, in a script you half know. The first line reads: "I built this so that no one could pass." The last: "I forgot to shut it."

choices.text: Copy the poem into a notebook

effects.log: It is a joke, a tender one, and four thousand years old.

choices.text: Walk through the broken gate in both directions

effects.log: It is a minor victory, in a minor way.

events.text: A cloud-bridge between two isles hums in the wind. It is the old kind, strung with silk and woven of vapour, and each plank rings a note under the foot. Crossing it is playing it. Children cross it back and forth all day, composing.

choices.text: Cross it slowly and listen

effects.log: The notes come in a gentle scale. You find a chord, and hold it, and the bridge hums with you.

choices.text: Cross it at a run with the children

effects.log: It is a gallop, a laugh, a jumble. You fall into a heap at the far side, happy.

events.text: A small pond fills a star-crater, so clear that the stars at night seem to be in it, not above it. A heron stands in the shallows, still as a post. The water is perfectly warm. Not a leaf floats on it. No one owns it.

choices.text: Wade in up to your knees

effects.log: The warmth climbs your legs. Your meridians loosen like old rope.

choices.text: Sit on the bank and watch the stars

effects.log: The heron looks at you, and at the stars, and back, as if comparing.

events.text: A small wind-snake lives in a bamboo flute on the market stall of a tinker. When the tinker plays, it coils out of the end and sways. The notes it likes are the low ones. The tinker has been paid in coins and in snake-shed. Both are cheap.

choices.text: Ask the tinker to play a tune for the snake

effects.log: It uncoils and sways. Its eyes are pale as wax. The tune is a ballad about the weather.

choices.text: Buy a length of snake-shed for a keepsake (nothing)

effects.log: The tinker presses a dry strand into your hand for free. It hums faintly when you walk.

events.text: A goat trail winds down the face of a hanging cliff, no wider than a hand. At the bottom, a single flat rock holds a cup of tea, steaming, left by someone who has just gone. The trail above is empty, and the tea is still hot.

choices.text: Drink the tea and climb back

effects.log: It tastes of mountain mint. Your muscles buzz. At the top, a goat looks pleased.

choices.text: Leave the tea and note the trail on a map

effects.log: You record the path, not to follow, but to remember.

events.text: The steersmen of the Ninth Fleet call one wind Old Hwan, and it has moods. On good days it is warm and behind them. On bad days it is cold and in their face. Today it sulks in the north, and every skiff leans away from it.

choices.text: Greet Old Hwan formally and ask for fair passage

effects.log: The wind eddies round you once. The steersmen look at you with new respect.

choices.text: Offer a spirit stone of tribute (nothing but a bow)

effects.log: The wind lifts your sleeve and, for a moment, goes still.

events.text: One isle in the Ninth Fleet never moves. It is moored to nothing, and the winds go round it. It has a lighthouse, a small harbour and a population of eleven, who say they are not stuck, merely devoted. They do not mind visitors. They do not expect them.

choices.text: Stay a week as a guest

effects.log: You mend a fence, trade a recipe, and play at cards. You leave warmer than you came.

choices.text: Ask them how it feels to stay still

effects.log: They say: "Quiet." They say it together, and then, again, in different keys.

events.text: The night sky over the Hwarang Isle is a star short. The old map shows it plain, a small blue one, low in the east. Tonight there is nothing there. The isle's astronomers are thrilled, appalled and, strangely, a little shy.

choices.text: Join the astronomers on the roof and watch for it

effects.log: The star does not return. But you spend the night under a sky that is, for once, utterly honest.

choices.text: Light a small lantern where the star should be

effects.log: The astronomers approve. The lantern burns till dawn.

events.text: The night fishers of the Reef of Lamps hang lanterns over the water and wait. Silver fish, drawn by the glow, rise to take a nibble of light. The fishers do not catch them. They watch, and in the morning they eat porridge, and are fat and content.

choices.text: Hang a lantern and watch with them

effects.log: A silver fish rises, nibbles your lantern, and sinks. You spend the night waiting for another.

choices.text: Learn the knack of the lantern-hang

effects.log: It is a way of holding a pole, nothing more. It takes six hours.

events.text: On a ledge no wider than a plate, someone has left a tea-set: a pot, two cups, a tin of leaves. A card reads: MAKE IT FOR A STRANGER. You are alone on the ledge. The wind pulls at your sleeve. No stranger comes.

choices.text: Brew the tea and wait for a stranger

effects.log: An hour later a pilgrim in a grey cloak arrives, accepts a cup, and says nothing. You both drink in perfect contentment.

choices.text: Brew it and drink both cups yourself

effects.log: It is a good pot. You leave a card of your own: THANK YOU, STRANGER.

events.text: An orchard of stone trees stands on a high plateau, each with stone fruit, each fruit a little different: a peach, a pear, a plum. Birds of stone perch in the branches. It is very quiet. A wind passes, and the whole orchard chimes like a bell.

choices.text: Listen to the orchard chime

effects.log: The chime is long, slow, mournful. You feel unusually calm.

choices.text: Pick a stone peach and carry it home

effects.log: It is heavy, cold, perfectly formed. It sits on your shelf and, now and then, hums.

events.text: A stall at the night market sells nothing. A sign reads: I LISTEN. Behind the counter an old man sits with his hands folded. A queue of immortals waits, each with a thing to say, each leaving lighter. The price is a quiet word of thanks.

choices.text: Wait in the queue and say what is on your mind

effects.log: The old man hears you. He says nothing. You feel the weight lift, a little.

choices.text: Sit beside him for an hour and listen too

effects.log: He nods. The two of you hear a great many things. You leave with a few of them.

events.text: In the Thirsty Reach, fishers hunt cloud-eels with nets of woven starlight. The eels are long, glassy and furious. When a net closes, they sing a thin high note, and the fishers sing back. It is said the eels give up more quickly to a good voice.

choices.text: Sing back to the eel in your best voice

effects.log: The eel relaxes, goes slack, and is released with a bow. The fishers cheer.

choices.text: Help haul the net, and hum under your breath

effects.log: The eel is heavy and angry. By dusk you have a bruise and a story.

events.text: A spiral stair of white stone drops through a hole in the cloud-floor, down into the white. It has no rail. Moss grows on every step. A bell rope hangs at the top. A sign says: RING IF YOU WISH TO BE EXPECTED.

choices.text: Ring the bell and descend

effects.log: The bell tolls once. At the bottom, a lamp is lit for you, and a bench, and a window onto the sea of clouds.

choices.text: Descend without ringing, quietly

effects.log: The stair is deep. At the bottom is a dark empty room. You turn back, and the bell rings, behind you, on its own.

events.text: At the summit of a cloud-peak there is a cairn, built stone by stone by passing travellers over a thousand years. Each stone has a name painted on the underside, hidden. The wind wears at the cairn, and it holds.

choices.text: Add a stone of your own, name down

effects.log: You paint the name of someone you love underneath. The wind passes round it. The cairn stays.

choices.text: Walk once round the cairn and take in the view

effects.log: The sky spreads out in all directions. You have never felt so small, or so comfortable.

events.text: A kitchen on a quiet isle serves one soup a day. The soup changes with the weather and the cook's mood. Today it is grey and thick and smells of rain. Everyone at the long table eats in silence, and then, one by one, in great content.

choices.text: Eat the soup and ask for a second bowl

effects.log: The cook beams. The second bowl is richer than the first.

choices.text: Ask the cook the secret of the soup

effects.log: "Whatever the weather wants," they say. "I only listen."

events.text: Cloud-berries grow in thick drifts on the underside of a low cloud-bank, pale blue and tart. Pickers go out at dawn with baskets tied to their waists, hanging from ropes. It is cold and quiet. The berries glow faintly in the baskets.

choices.text: Pick a basket of berries on a rope

effects.log: Your arms ache and your fingers sting. The berries are the best you have tasted.

choices.text: Help the pickers sort the harvest on the quay

effects.log: You sort them by shade. A picker gives you a handful as thanks.

events.text: A grey cat sits on the sill of every house in the Hollow Isle at midnight, in a line. They do not mew, nor stretch, nor groom. They sit, and they look at the moon. At the first cockcrow, they all vanish. The people of the isle say the cats are paying their respects.

choices.text: Sit on a sill with them for an hour

effects.log: The cat beside you does not move. After an hour, it leans, ever so slightly, into your side.

choices.text: Leave out a saucer of milk and go to bed

effects.log: In the morning it is empty, and the saucer is warm.

events.text: The Jade Court's gardener is the only one in the whole Court who greets everyone by name. A junior clerk says it is the most important job in the building, because nobody else has the time. The gardener hears this and goes on pruning, smiling.

choices.text: Ask the gardener to teach you a few names

effects.log: You learn twelve by heart. The next morning, three clerks look at you in surprise.

choices.text: Help prune the hedge by the gate

effects.log: It takes an hour. At the end, the gardener hands you a clipped sprig of jasmine.

events.text: At the Edge of Heaven, on certain nights, a faint chorus rises from the white. It is thin, wordless, a thousand voices singing one long note. Pilgrims gather to hear it. None can say whose voices, or what the song is for. All go home quieter.

choices.text: Listen at the very edge until the note fades

effects.log: It lasts the whole night. At dawn you feel carried.

choices.text: Hum a note back into the white

effects.log: The chorus shifts a quarter-tone. It is the most intimate thing you have ever done at a distance.

events.text: A thundercloud has drifted across a hilltop picnic, and the picnic party, stubborn, has opened umbrellas of oiled silk and carried on. They are eating dumplings in a downpour and singing. A grey-haired host shouts: "Join us, we have room!"

choices.text: Join the party and share a dumpling

effects.log: The rain is warm. The singing is bad. You laugh more than you have in decades.

choices.text: Watch from a dry porch and toast them

effects.log: They wave their cups. It is a pleasant way to see a storm.

events.text: A bell rings at midnight over a still sky-lake, though no one has hung one there. Ripples spread from the centre. A small boat is moored at the shore, with an oar, a lantern and a note: IF YOU HEAR IT, GO AND SEE. The bell rings again, softly.

choices.text: Row to the middle of the lake

effects.log: The bell rings once more, directly beneath you. You wait. A silver fish rises with a small bell in its mouth, and sinks.

choices.text: Light the lantern and wait on the shore

effects.log: The ripples spread and fade. In the morning, the boat is gone, and a faint bell hangs on the willow.

events.text: A hot spring on a quiet ledge belongs to a hermit who, in a note on the door, has gone on pilgrimage. "Please bathe," it reads, "and leave the water as you found it." Steam curls over the pool. Snow falls upward in slow white threads.

choices.text: Bathe in the spring and rest your bones

effects.log: The water is hot and mineral. You emerge three centuries lighter in spirit.

choices.text: Clean the spring and leave a flower

effects.log: The hermit will not be back for a long time, but the spring is ready.

events.text: A grove of cloud-bamboo carries messages. Pilgrims tie ribbons to the stalks, and the wind blows the ribbons toward their recipient. On a still day the grove is silent. On a windy day, it is a post office in a gale.

choices.text: Tie a ribbon to a stalk, with a short message

effects.log: The wind lifts it and carries it off. You never learn where.

choices.text: Stand in the grove and read the ribbons as they blow

effects.log: Some are love, some are grief, some are shopping lists. You smile at them all.
